incidents.name: bZx BZxOracle sUSD marginal-rate collateral valuation
incidents.summary: BZxOracle 0xaa6198fe597dfc331471ae7deba026fb299297fc is the price source that bZx's getBorrowAmount() and takeOrderFromiToken() paths use to size a loan against its collateral. Its getTradeData(sourceToken, destToken, sourceTokenAmount) ignores the amount it is asked about - the protocol passes 2**256-1 - and instead STATICCALLs KyberNetworkProxy 0x818e6fecd516ecc3849daf6845e3ec868087b755 getExpectedRate with srcQty 2**255 + 1e16, that is the marginal rate for a 0.01-unit trade with permissionless reserves disabled, then returns that rate verbatim as the collateral price. There is no time averaging, no deviation bound against an independent reference, no check that the quoted marginal rate is achievable at the size being valued, and nothing stopping a borrow in the same transaction that moved the quoting market. The attacker flash-borrowed 7,500 WETH through iETH LoanToken 0x77f973fcaf871459aa58cd81881ce453759281bc, bought sUSD from the Synthetix depot and then ran eighteen consecutive 20-ETH buys through the Uniswap V1 sUSD exchange 0x2157a7894439191e520825fe9399ab8655e0f708 that Kyber's reserve quotes; the same eth_call that returns a sUSD/WETH rate of 0.003613877057815960 at block 9504626 returned 0.009297067356545891 inside the exploit, 2.5726 times higher. getBorrowAmount therefore authorised up to 6,816.866335916617112493 WETH against 1,099,841.392100433025126219 sUSD at the 150 percent initial margin, and takeOrderFromiToken opened a 6,799.272741673360528371 WETH loan of which 6,796.012817135270528952 WETH was paid out.

loss.notes: Measured as the attacker's exact realised proceeds: attack contract 0x360f85f0b74326cddff33a812b05353bc537747b holds 0 wei at block 9504626 and 2,378.153715421627764132 ETH at block 9504627, and moved that whole balance to the attacker EOA in withdraw() transaction 0x2e05b36f4e1afd92366dfded4f7fb7a11eab4d681e313caab6068b1a5879067f at block 9504634. All of the attacker's campaign capital was the 7,500 WETH bZx flash loan, which was repaid inside the same transaction, so no attacker-supplied input is counted. This is a conservative floor on the lender's economic loss rather than a gross depletion: the iETH pool's WETH balance fell from 18,586.276356627435240969 to 11,787.018373071280837922, a 6,799.257983556154403047 WETH outflow worth 1,823,163.10 USD, against 1,099,841.392100433025126219 sUSD of collateral taken into BZxVault worth 1,074,683.79 USD at DefiLlama's incident-time sUSD price of 0.9771261517396886, implying a shortfall near 748,479 USD; the difference between that and the figure recorded here is slippage the attacker paid to the Kyber, Uniswap and Synthetix markets, not value retained by bZx. Disjoint from the two other bZx incidents in this dataset: eip155:1:0xb5c8bd9430b6cc87a0e2fe110ece6bf527fa4f170a4bc8cd032f768fc5219838 (2020-02-15, 1,193 ETH) and eip155:1:0x85dc2a433fd9eaadaf56fd8156c956da23fc17e5ef83955c7e2c4c37efa20bb5 (2020-09-13, 8.1 million USD).

incidents.name: TrustPad LaunchpadLockableStaking reward accounting
incidents.summary: receiveUpPool accepts arbitrary callers and trusts their reported lock history. It computes reward debt before increasing the stake, so an attacker supplies an old lock date, repeatedly deposits and withdraws, then compounds unearned historical rewards with stakePendingRewards.

loss.notes: Victim balanceOf before/after each of 26 exploit blocks totals 29587378.247454806 TPAD depletion, excluding recycled deposits. The victim is reflection-excluded and fee-exempt; the two unrelated token transactions in final block 33262748 cannot affect its balance. Value uses disposal VWAP: 19 sales debit 30162599.532230174 TPAD including the 1% transfer fee, producing 615.682669599467334517 BNB, valued at $251.70828244452184/BNB. Sale inputs are exact transferFrom calldata amounts; Transfer logs omit the reflection fee. Apply that effective price to victim depletion, not the larger sold quantity, which also includes reflections and the initial 0.02 BNB token purchase. The remaining 251.336528056 TPAD is included in victim depletion at that same estimated VWAP; gas and later recoveries are not deducted.

incidents.name: Inuko bond prices LP from the pair's raw USDT balance
incidents.summary: The Inuko bond contract sizes a bond by LpToToken, which values LP as 2 x IBEP20(USDT).balanceOf(pair) x lpAmount / totalSupply, then quotes that USDT amount in INUKO with the router's getAmountsIn. In one transaction the attacker flash-borrowed USDT, sent 5,181,964.88 USDT to the INUKO/USDT pair, bought three bonds with 2,231.06 LP while the balance was inflated, and skimmed the USDT back. Two days later, when the lock expired, the three bonds paid 172,923.21 INUKO, which the attacker sold into the pair.

loss.notes: The bond contract paid 172,923.209469637221781689 INUKO on the three manipulated bonds. The attacker's disposal moved the price, so it is valued at realised proceeds: 64,834.400411031142494522 USDT reached the attacker EOA from the pair in the claim transaction, 0.37493 USDT per INUKO paid out, with DefiLlama coingecko:tether at 1. From that the attacker-supplied consideration is netted: 2,231.061260442558263531 INUKO-USDT LP delivered to the bond vault, worth 3,103.035475642067368147 USDT at the pair's pre-exploit reserves. The pair's net USDT outflow of 71,238.505050452932003552 in the claim transaction also includes the INUKO token's own tax swap, and is not used. The seed row and the Ancilia report give 64,834 USD, the attacker's USDT proceeds.

incidents.name: LotteryTicketSwap50 live-reserve redemption misprices LP
incidents.summary: LotteryTicketSwap50 sized each ticket redemption's LP burn from the NATA/USDC pair's live reserves. A flash-financed reserve skew let one helper mint 2,600 tickets and redeem them in 130 calls while destroying too much protocol-owned LP, depleting the protocol entity's native Base USDC.

loss.notes: The victim entity is LotteryTicketSwap50 0x172119155a48de766b126de95c2cb331d3a5c7c2, its NATA/USDC pair 0xadcaab077f636d74fd50fda7f44ad41e20a21fee and the owner/deployer's LP position. At anchor-1 the pair had 170.154260915765325861 LP outstanding: 99.415567080707983861 (58.42672792%) held by LotteryTicketSwap50 and 70.738693835057341000 (41.57327207%) held by its owner/deployer 0x66d9748e58f3bbfb4e400b3c6991bd578dabbeb2. Exhaustive LP Transfer history leaves no external holder. The pair sent 3037219.668858 and received 2929805 USDC, losing 107414.668858, while the swap contract received 259219.668858 and sent 259025, recovering 194.668858 internally. Entity loss is therefore exactly 107220 USDC: 105470 reached the attacker EOA and 1750 was the fee paid to external Uniswap V3 WETH/USDC 0.05% pool 0xd0b53d9277642d899df5c87a3966a349a798f224. Archive USDC balances agree: pair 291143.873072 -> 183729.204214 and swap 413.324943 -> 607.993801. Base USDC returns name USD Coin, symbol USDC and 6 decimals at anchor-1. DefiLlama observed $0.999946 29 seconds before the receipt; exact decimal multiplication is $107214.21012.

incidents.name: CashCowCoin trading proxy sell() burns CCC from the pair and syncs
incidents.summary: CashCowCoin's public trading proxy sell() swaps the caller's CCC for WBNB through the CCC/WBNB PancakeSwap pair. It then calls the token's proxy-only function 0xb20a0b6f to burn the CCC that just arrived in the pair to 0xdead, and calls pair.sync(). Each sell therefore takes WBNB while the pair's CCC reserve stays flat. With a Moolah flash loan the attacker bought 8.8M CCC and ran 80 sells, draining the pair's WBNB reserve from 165.49 to 0.018.

loss.notes: WBNB depletion of the CCC/WBNB pair 0x1dbe9458a6840784d5defd62c6b71386100097c0 across the exploit transaction; the attacker's 13,999.89 WBNB donation and flash-loaned buy are returned within the same transaction and cancel out. It equals the attacker's net 165.4719 WBNB. The pair's CCC is not valued because the drained pair was its market.

incidents.name: NewFreeDAO reward contract repeatable claim
incidents.summary: The NFD reward contract pays its bonus, selector 0x6811e3b9, to any caller in proportion to that caller’s NFD balance and records the claim only against the caller’s own address. The attacker looped: deploy a fresh claimer contract, move the same NFD into it, claim again. The payout multiplied without limit, and the accumulated NFD was sold into the NFD/WBNB pair for its WBNB.

loss.notes: Three of the attacker’s transactions call the reward contract, at blocks 21140435, 21140481 and 21140498; netting them gives the attacker exactly 4481.324982360678881755 WBNB, which is what the NFD/WBNB pair lost to the dumping. The seven earlier transactions the attacker sent to other contracts of its own between blocks 21139097 and 21140296 never touch the reward contract and are excluded. The nominal NFD the claims minted is not valued: it only had worth to the extent the pair absorbed it, which the WBNB figure already measures. Nothing was recovered.

incidents.name: GROKD deposit contract unauthenticated updatePool
incidents.summary: The GROKD LP-staking deposit contract (UUPS proxy 0x31d3231c, implementation 0xec61196d) exposes updatePool(uint256 pid, (startBlock, endBlock, rewardPerBlock)) without any caller check: it only requires pid < pool count and overwrites the pool's reward schedule. After staking 1 LP through the ordinary deposit() one transaction earlier, the attacker contract set pool 0's rewardPerBlock from 0.1875 to 969,437,458 GROKD and called reward() in the same transaction, collecting 1,346,001.9 GROKD, almost the contract's entire GROKD reward balance, which it sold for 157.67 BNB.

loss.notes: Exact victim depletion: GROKD balanceOf(deposit proxy) falls from 1346594.907093285618305585 to 592.991783799382637245 across source-1, equal to the reward() transfer of 1346001.91530948623566834 GROKD to the attack contract. GROKD has no DefiLlama quote and the attacker's own sales moved the GROKD/WBNB pair, so it is valued at realised proceeds: five sells (source-8..source-12, blocks 37622485..37622533) disposed of exactly that amount (4 x 300000 + 146001.91530948623566834 GROKD) and paid the attacker EOA 157.669066410511957157 BNB, valued at the DefiLlama WBNB quote 582.04 at the anchor (source-7). The GROKD transfer tax (3.5% of each sell, swapped by the token contract for its own recipients) is not in the attacker's proceeds, so the realised value is conservative. The attacker's 0.2 BNB LP purchase and 1 LP stake in 0x383dbb44 are attacker inputs and are not subtracted.

incidents.name: BTC20 presale proxy claim exploit
incidents.summary: The presale priced BTC20 from a manipulable Uniswap spot quote, allowing a flash-loan-funded price manipulation to buy the remaining presale inventory below its market value.

loss.notes: The exploit trace ends with exactly 18.348059243787394323 ETH transferred from the attack contract to the attacker after the 300 WETH flash loan was repaid.

incidents.name: YuliAI sell inventory live V3 quotation
incidents.summary: YuliAI's sellToken path valued incoming YULIAI by forwarding the requested quantity to a QuoterV2 against the live YULIAI/USDT Pancake V3 pool, then paid that quote from protocol USDT inventory. One bounded receipt moved the pool before repeatedly exercising the path; this review nets protocol-controlled sell fees and the fair prestate value of the retained YULIAI consideration.

loss.notes: The victim entity is sell contract 0x8262325bf1d8c3be83eb99f5a74b8458ebb96282 plus its creator, owner and configured receiverFee EOA 0x078f3f917c7355027a8388b7083b2199910c8a9a. Archive balances at blocks 57,432,055 and 57,432,056 move from 101,443.782000000000000000 + 663.393732000000000000 = 102,107.175732000000000000 USDT to 1,605.747295468511420520 + 5,655.295467226574428960 = 7,261.042762695085849480 USDT. The exact entity-level stable depletion is therefore 94,846.132969304914150520 USDT: the contract's 99,838.034704531488579480-USDT outflow less the owner's internal 4,991.901735226574428960-USDT five-percent fee recovery. In the same boundary, the sell contract gains exactly 3,347,358.354974243185076585 YULIAI and the owner balance is unchanged. Immediately before the receipt, Pancake V3 fee-10,000 pool 0xa687c7b3c2cf6adaef0c4edab234c55b88e01333 has token0 canonical 18-decimal Binance-Peg USDT, token1 18-decimal YULIAI, sqrtPriceX96 1,334,846,821,531,167,810,533,929,326,840, active liquidity 1,721,008,515,508,744,595,598,029, and balances 102,203.563337554348779303 USDT and 29,004,603.501598146291084966 YULIAI. Correct token orientation gives 0.003522867459496474822898258515289302553283462544060329020695 USDT per YULIAI. At that recorded 60-decimal price, retained consideration is $11,792.299824012411246321659065323531459767412921239379420208798892 to 60 decimal places, leaving net loss $83,053.833145292502904198340934676468540232587078760620579791201108 to 60 decimal places. The only other factory-discovered prestate YULIAI market is a dust V2 pair with 0.029203095562343651 USDT and 7.986386893235572202 YULIAI, so it is not a competing price anchor. The V3 pool gains 16,046.200892423232810268 USDT while providing the retained YULIAI, and flash proxy 0x8f73b65b4caaf64fba2af91cc5d4a2a1318e5d8c sends and receives exactly 200,000 USDT with zero fee. The campaign EOA realizes 78,799.932076881681340252 USDT; proceeds are not substituted for entity loss. EOA nonce 2 creates the helper and nonce 3 is the sole loss. Nonce 4 approves a downstream aggregator; nonce 5 plus three permissioned relayer receipts dispose of all proceeds; nonce 6 withdraws only the helper's native balance, leaving it at zero USDT and YULIAI. Nonce 7 is a later unrelated native deposit. These disposal and withdrawal receipts contain no transfer to the victim contract or owner, and the bounded attacker/helper scan finds no later USDT or YULIAI return or recovery.

incidents.name: BYToken permissionless auto-burn of the pair reserve
incidents.summary: BYToken._autoBurn, callable by anyone through triggerAutoBurn(), burns DAILY_BURN_RATE of totalSupply (1% per elapsed interval) from the pool address whenever the token contract holds too little BY, then calls pair.sync(). The amount is independent of the pair's own reserve, so a caller who first shrinks the pair's BY reserve can have the burn remove all but 1 wei of it. With a flash-borrowed 422,497 WBNB the attacker bought 6.31M BY to the router (the from == pool && to == router liquidity-removal branch skips the trading gate), donated WBNB and synced to reach the 40,000 WBNB auto-enable threshold, bought exactly 62,868 BY so 67,800 BY + 1 wei remained, called triggerAutoBurn() the second the first interval elapsed, then sold dust BY for the pair's entire 146.6 WBNB.

loss.notes: Exact WBNB depletion of BY/WBNB PancakeSwap pair 0x1f358e18e0db68ff33c2319c8dad328edf9b7059, whose liquidity the deployer seeded before trading opened: WBNB balanceOf(pair) 146602850775618057371 at block 102329718 and 2 at block 102329719, equal to the attacker contract's net WBNB gain (withdrawn in receipt log 60). The 422,497 WBNB flash loan and every WBNB swap and donation leg are attacker inputs returned within the transaction and are netted out. The pair's BY loss (6,441,732.97 to 62,868 BY, 67,800 BY burned) is not added: it is the same liquidity already realised as WBNB. The 7 BNB builder payment is not deducted. Later pair activity is dust trading; no second AutoBurn exists.

incidents.name: AIDC pair-side accumulated burn
incidents.summary: AIDC's transfer accounting could burn an accumulated sell-side amount from its own AIDC/WBNB pair, breaking reserve accounting and depleting the pair's WBNB reserve.

loss.notes: Gross loss is the exact net WBNB depletion of AIDC/WBNB pair 0x2725033282b3bd4be8873b7f0f622c18e3b7cbd8 in the single successful incident receipt. The pair receives 100.000034165547162792 WBNB and sends 321.225837525258000289 WBNB, for 221.225803359710837497 WBNB net depletion. Archive balances fall from 221.225824586427689773 WBNB immediately before the incident block to 0.000021226716852276 WBNB after it, reproducing the same difference. The sender's three bounded pre-incident transactions 0x36d7b9d2...7228, 0x75f6e0ba...ab96, and 0x555b8f07...7423 have no AIDC or WBNB transfer to or from the pair and are excluded. The incident credits 220.125803359710837497 WBNB to the attacker; financing fees and downstream routing effects do not reduce gross pair depletion. The closest preceding DefiLlama BNB observation is $550.4782257918903 at 1782675299, 54 seconds before the incident.

incidents.name: BCE deferred burn against the PancakeSwap pair
incidents.summary: BCE accrued a scheduledDestruction amount on sells and settled it during a later ordinary transfer by burning that amount out of the PancakeSwap pair's own balance and calling sync(), collapsing the BCE reserve so the attacker's remaining BCE could be sold into the distorted pair for its USDT side.

loss.notes: Gross defect-caused loss is the exploit transaction's exact net USDT outflow from PancakeSwap pair 0xca23e8d408d769661cb480a3fd45d6be370c45f7: 1,368,537.151371370971397343 plus 36,575,519.358323350250156783 USDT out, less 2,222,765.758031675244035783 plus 34,921,281.427495645469740320 USDT in, equals 800,009.324167400507778023 USDT. This also equals the 680,007.925542290431611320 USDT paid to the attacker EOA plus 120,001.398625110076166703 USDT swapped into WBNB for the attack's 15% builder payment. It does not count flash-loan principal as loss and supersedes the rounded $679,000 report, which tracks the attacker's retained USDT after the builder payment rather than the LP's gross loss.

incidents.name: LeetSwap WETH/axlUSDC pair fee-transfer drain
incidents.summary: LeetSwapV2Pair exposed its fee-transfer helper publicly without caller, token, or amount authorization. An unprivileged caller could move a pair's counterpart-token balance into its fees contract, synchronize the depleted reserve, and drain WETH through the resulting reserve distortion.

loss.notes: The pair sent 119.447582023779038288 WETH to the attack helper. Excluding the helper's identifiable 0.001 WETH setup-swap input leaves exact pre-recovery victim depletion of 119.446582023779038288 WETH, valued at DefiLlama's nearest observation of $1,863.01. The public fee-transfer call also moved the counterpart token into the pair's fees contract; that internal transfer is excluded because claim allocation and recoverability cannot be isolated from the receipts, so no speculative counterpart-token value is assigned.

incidents.name: D3x.ai exchange spot-price manipulation
incidents.summary: The exchange implementation priced USDT/D3XAT conversions by calling D3XAT.price(), which read the current PancakeSwap reserves through Router.getAmountsOut. It imposed no time-weighting or manipulation bound, so one transaction could buy D3XAT, move the same pool's spot price through transient accounts, and redeem D3XAT against the exchange's USDT inventory at the manipulated quote.

loss.notes: The exchange proxy and protocol controller 0x13342140a62cb51c052b5a70eb186f40a1725ebf form the victim entity. Two initial exchange buys put 24627.150187372155949310 USDT into the proxy. Nineteen later redemptions send 224790.352174233336041807 USDT to the seller helper and 39668.885677805882830887 USDT to the controller; the next redemption reverts. The controller is the proxy and active-implementation deployer and the sender of the last upgrade, and its archive USDT balance rises by exactly the fee amount and retains it through the bounded window. That internal transfer cancels, leaving 224790.352174233336041807 - 24627.150187372155949310 = 200163.201986861180092497 USDT of external protocol depletion. The proxy's archive balance change independently equals its receipt net of -239832.087664667062923384 USDT. The victim union gains 21680.158448278855196476 D3XAT overall because controller transfer-tax receipts more than offset the proxy's D3XAT decrease, so D3XAT is not a loss component. The reported 190 BNB is downstream realization: the D3XAT/WBNB pair sends 190.553117446131167874 WBNB to the router, which unwraps it; it is not native depletion from the exchange. The 20 million USDT flash principal plus 2000 USDT fee is repaid in full. Nothing was returned to the victim union.

incidents.name: SVT pool marginal-price quote without an invariant
incidents.summary: The SVT pool 0x2120f8f305347b6aa5e5dbb347230a8234eb3379 quotes both sides of the market at its instantaneous spot ratio and applies no constant-product or any other invariant to the trade being executed. buy(uint256) (selector 0xd96a094a) takes a 1.5 percent USDT fee and pays out (amount - fee) * 1e18 / price SVT, and sell(uint256) (selector 0xe4849b32) pays out amount * price / 1e18 USDT less a 10 percent fee, where in both cases price = USDT.balanceOf(pool) * 1e18 / SVT.balanceOf(pool) read from the live balances before the transfer. Because the quote ignores the trade's own effect on those balances, a buy moves the ratio without charging for the move, and the SVT just bought redeems immediately at the new, higher ratio. I reproduced all four legs of the anchor transaction to the wei with that formula. The invariant broken is that an automated market maker must price a trade against the reserve curve it will end on, not against the marginal price it starts from. No parameter repairs it: for any fee below 100 percent an attacker sizes the buy so that the ratio distortion exceeds the fees, and as the USDT input approaches the pool's USDT balance the payout approaches the pool's whole SVT inventory.

loss.notes: Exact BSC-USD depletion of the pool across the three-transaction campaign, taken from the receipts: 1,119,165.577404063032213426 left the pool and 600,296.101490916296932929 of attacker-supplied buy input went in, leaving 518,869.475913146788810743. Of that, 398,848.920802613110227784 is the attacker's realised take, which is exactly the balance its EOA 0x4b44b52ef15f7aab9a0a6cfdfa8d2c5eeeb6d8c3 holds after the campaign having started at zero, and 120,020.555110533678582959 accrued to the pool's own fee wallet 0xf037a9f7e7ee68a011ab3e4fa8667dd350370b04, which is stored in pool slot 1 from deployment and is not attacker-controlled; it is counted because it left the drained pool and is not a recovery to the reserve backing SVT. The DODO flash loan of 600,296.101490916296932929 BSC-USD was repaid in full in each transaction and is not loss. The SVT leg is not separately valued: the pool's SVT inventory is its own token, and the 2,068,867.337245240376360201 SVT the attacker still held after the anchor transaction was sold back into the same pool in the two follow-up transactions for a combined 1,066.459898994375177222 BSC-USD, which is already inside the figure above and shows the residual had no independent value. The seed row's figure of 397,782 is the attacker's take in the anchor transaction alone. A block-boundary check gives 521,020.643056518743156196 BSC-USD in the pool at block 31178237 and 2,153.137734371954345453 at block 31178423; the 2.000600000000000000 difference from the receipt sum is unrelated user trading in the 185 intervening blocks.

incidents.name: Zeed Finance YEED reflection skim drain
incidents.summary: The YEED token distributes a reflection fee to every holder on each transfer, including the PancakeSwap pairs it trades in, without those pairs resyncing. The attacker cycled skim() between the three YEED pairs so each cycle credited the pairs more YEED than their recorded reserves, then swapped the accumulated YEED out for the pools’ USDT.

loss.notes: The whole loss is in the single exploit transaction. Three YEED pairs pay out 187555.556168947981908342, 711623.947354811699369548 and 142848.961548294074132861 USDT and the attacker contract 0x05e55d051ac0a5fb744e71704a8fa4ee3b103374 receives exactly their sum. The YEED the attacker was left holding is not counted. Nothing was recovered.

incidents.name: Bazaar Balancer-fork exitPool without sender validation
incidents.summary: The Bazaar vault is a Balancer fork whose exitPool() never checks that the caller is the position holder or an approved relayer of it. The attacker called exitPool naming another holder as the sender, burning 850,000,000 of that holder’s BZR pool tokens and receiving the corresponding 392.37 WETH and 880,539,680 rYOLO.

loss.notes: The whole loss is in the single exploit transaction, which is a contract creation whose constructor performs the exit. The vault 0xefb4e3cc438ef2854727a7df0d0baf844484edab pays out exactly 392.368916281212373207 WETH and 880539680.680963671973966099 rYOLO to the attacker contract while 850,000,000 BZR pool tokens are burned from the holder 0xb66585c4e460d49154d50325ce60adc44bc900e9. DefiLlama has no price series for rYOLO, so that component is recorded in quantity only and the USD total counts the WETH leg alone, which makes the figure a floor. WETH on Blast is priced through the DefiLlama ETH series. The attacker, self-described as a whitehat, forwarded the ETH to 0xfb72b2b32740de44488db791d83125ce39a53d91, which returned 353.13201 ETH to 0xde4d48f64687888d112b653c8fab4f0f67c37dbb in 0x5fc22cab25e0d9cf436718a040893550c266789ebd58c7ab5936634c762a70dd (block 4623649); the rYOLO never left the attacker contract. Recoveries do not reduce gross loss.

incidents.name: Will trading zero-margin order forced into public expired settlement
incidents.summary: The WILL short-trading contract's placeSellOrder accepts margin 0, giving closeTime = block.timestamp, and sells contract-held (staked) WILL for USDT. Anyone can then call updateExpiredOrders, which books 1.8x the shorted USDT for buy-back, and settleExpiredPositions, which spends that contract USDT on WILL at the live pool price with a caller-chosen minTokensToReceive. The attacker opened an instantly expired order, pumped WILL, and made the contract buy back at the inflated price before dumping.

loss.notes: Attacker contract net USDT gain across both campaign transactions (source-1 and source-7). The victim's gross depletion is 2,722,729.9 WILL (staked user tokens) against a 13,854.51 USDT net gain (71,306.38 USDT attacker order deposit plus 70,899.62 USDT sale proceeds minus 128,351.49 USDT settlement spend); the dumped WILL crashed the pair price (0.0878 to 0.0077 USDT per WILL), so a pre-exploit spot valuation of that WILL is not realisable and the attacker's realised USDT gain is used instead. The PoC header's ~52,777 USD profit is not reproduced by the receipts.

incidents.name: ATM BlindBox predictable expired-blockhash settlement
incidents.summary: BlindBox bets resolve on blockhash(betBlock+2), but settle(betId) is public and caller-timed and lastUnsettledId auto-settles only one bet per entry. Once that blockhash expires, _trySettle falls back to keccak256(block.prevrandao, betId, block.timestamp), which the settler knows in advance. The attacker queued 1-ATM filler bets to block auto-settlement, settled winners at once and settled losers after expiry in blocks where the fallback made them win, draining the DEAD-address payout pool at 1.95x.

loss.notes: Gross victim depletion in the helper's 38 winning predictable-fallback bets: 66850752.15 ATM paid minus 34282437 ATM deposited for those same bet IDs. Placement time does not exclude a stake: bet 5136 contributes 585000 - 300000 = 285000 ATM although its deposit precedes the incident anchor. Live-blockhash wins are excluded throughout the campaign. Losing and unsettled stakes are attack costs and do not reduce gross theft. The anchor predictor test pays a third-party bettor, not the helper; no theft of that bettor's funds is claimed. USD value allocates the nine disposals' aggregate proceeds proportionally to the attributed ATM quantity, because the sales mix exploit winnings, ordinary winnings and initial capital. BSC-USD is valued at par; later recoveries and the cold wallet's removal of the remaining DEAD balance are not netted.

incidents.name: Unknown BSC swap-bot contract lets anyone swap approved wallets without slippage limits
incidents.summary: Unverified contract 0x16d7c6f4, used by an operator's many EOAs to trade for managed wallets, exposes f8c03cc4(tokenIn, tokenOut, fee, amountIn, buyBack, 0, wallet). It pulls amountIn from any wallet that approved it and sells it on PancakeSwap V3 with no minimum output. It then buys the same amount back with the caller's tokens and sends it to the caller. There is no caller authorization. After draining the pool's other side, the attacker called it for 152 approved wallets in three transactions, receiving their TA, WBNB and USD1 for dust.

loss.notes: Gross debits of the 152 approved wallets named as the wallet argument in the three campaign transactions. The wallets received only dust back (24935602 wei USDT and 0.0083 TA in total), which is not netted. TA is illiquid, and the attacker's same-transaction sale moved its price, so TA is valued at realised proceeds: 282180.028682576245452554 USDT net to attacker contract 0x5b0d9b3c in source-1 (DefiLlama quoted 0.102143 before the sale). WBNB and USD1 are valued at DefiLlama quotes. Flash liquidity and the attacker's buy-back inputs are excluded.

incidents.name: LeetSwap WETH/DEBASED pair fee-transfer drain
incidents.summary: LeetSwapV2Pair exposed its fee-transfer helper publicly without caller, token, or amount authorization. An unprivileged caller could move a pair's counterpart-token balance into its fees contract, synchronize the depleted reserve, and drain WETH through the resulting reserve distortion.

loss.notes: The pair sent 19.363407035463818643 WETH to the attack helper. Excluding the helper's identifiable 0.001 WETH setup-swap input leaves exact pre-recovery victim depletion of 19.362407035463818643 WETH, valued at DefiLlama's nearest observation of $1,863.01. The public fee-transfer call also moved the counterpart token into the pair's fees contract; that internal transfer is excluded because claim allocation and recoverability cannot be isolated from the receipts, so no speculative counterpart-token value is assigned.

incidents.name: CS Token stale sellAmount pair burn
incidents.summary: CS stores the current sell size in a global sellAmount variable, then lets a later qualifying transfer consume that stale value to burn 80% of it directly from the CS/USDT pair before calling pair.sync(). The attacker repeatedly paired a sale with a self-transfer to contract the CS reserve and drain USDT.

loss.notes: The exploit receipt's 515 USDT Transfer logs net to exactly 954,285.001826338883421706 USDT leaving the CS/USDT pair. The flash pair supplied 80,000,000 USDT principal and received 80,240,000 USDT, so the attacker EOA retained exactly 714,285.001826338883421706 USDT after the 240,000 USDT flash fee. Gross victim assets lost, rather than attacker net proceeds, is the comparable loss measure.

incidents.name: MetaWin staking USD reward settled at FCN/USDT pair balance spot price
incidents.summary: The staking contract 0x431abb27dab05f4e7cdeaa18390fe39364197500 accrues each staker a reward denominated in USD and settles it in FCN at a price it derives, inside the paying transaction, from two raw balanceOf reads on the PancakeSwap V2 FCN/BSC-USD pair 0xacb496dd4a8b6b9d1b99d422b8700f6ef932bc10. In the anchor transaction the claim entry point, selector 0xd9574d4c, reads the caller's stored 10e18 USD entitlement from slot 0x9c6375cda627d083cbb712ee89f8748935cee8e2ed0be5ca571a2fdf7ae3eba3, reads BSC-USD.balanceOf(pair) = 0.02 and FCN.balanceOf(pair) = 0.501971077397338362, and pays out 10 / (0.02 / 0.501971077397338362) = 250.985538698669186971 FCN. Those pair balances are what the caller had just set: the same transaction is a PancakeSwap flash swap that removed 512963.341056079475662703 BSC-USD from that exact pair before calling the claim. The invariant violated is that a fixed USD liability may not be settled at an instantaneous, caller-controllable AMM quote; there is no TWAP, no minimum-reserve or deviation guard, no getReserves-versus-balance check and no re-entrancy or flash-loan protection on the read. No parameter value repairs it: the reward rate, the priced pair and the fee split are configuration, and at any non-zero entitlement a claimer who can move the pair's balances within the transaction converts that entitlement into an arbitrary quantity of FCN.

loss.notes: Exact depletion of the PancakeSwap V2 FCN/BSC-USD pair 0xacb496dd4a8b6b9d1b99d422b8700f6ef932bc10 in the anchor transaction: its BSC-USD balance fell from 512963.361056079475662703 to 10000.020000000000000000. The flash swap took 512963.341056079475662703 BSC-USD and was repaid with 10000 BSC-USD and 85 FCN, and the attacker's contract forwarded 503468.345335579475662703 BSC-USD to its EOA in the same transaction, so the realised proceeds and the pool depletion agree to the ~505 BSC-USD the contract already held. BSC-USD is taken at par. The staking contract's whole FCN reward pool was also taken - its balance fell from 252.989548188125072069 to 2.004009489455885098 FCN, 225.886984828802268274 FCN to the attacker and 25.098553869866918697 FCN to the protocol fee address 0x19c4a6b4abfe88161f07c4fa2229a4120acfd7d5 - but that FCN is not valued separately: its only realisable value was the BSC-USD the attacker took out of the same pair, so counting both would double count, and FCN could never have been marked at the pair's pre-attack implied price of about 1,021,900 USD per token against a 0.501971077397338362 FCN reserve. The attacker sold part of the residual FCN back into the same pair over the following two days; that tail is mixed with third-party trading in the pool balance and is not attributed here, so this figure is a lower bound on the campaign total.

incidents.name: OPC trading helper burns sold tokens out of its pair
incidents.summary: Every OPC trade goes through the unverified helper 0xa642e668. On a sell (db3f7000 with flag 1), it swaps 95% of the tokens into the OPC/USDT pair, burns 90% of the sold amount from the pair with burnFrom, and calls sync(), so the pair's OPC reserve barely grows while USDT flows out. Its e3bb6e96 liquidity removal also pays the caller the helper's entire OPC balance. The attacker flash-borrowed 10M USDT and bought OPC with the helper as recipient, then swept it out with e3bb6e96. It made 100 helper sells, each burning OPC from the pair, and dumped the rest, taking 112,750 USDT.

loss.notes: Exact USDT depletion of the OPC/USDT pair 0xa05548891a30bc92b767ca86817a1cd06288bb9a in the exploit transaction. The attacker's 10M USDT flash liquidity is circular and excluded. The deployer's later owner withdrawal of the remaining 15433 USDT (source-6) is a separate privileged action and is not counted.

incidents.name: ZORA community claim allocation to the stateless 0x Settler
incidents.summary: ZoraTokenCommunityClaim pays each account's allocation to any _claimTo chosen by that account. Its allocation setter wrote a 5,500,777.45 ZORA allocation for 0x's BaseSettler, a stateless router whose execute runs arbitrary actions for any caller. Once claims opened, an attacker's constructor had the Settler call claim(attacker) and received the whole allocation.

loss.notes: Exact ZORA transfer from the claim contract to the attacker EOA (source-1 receipt log 147), valued at the DefiLlama ZORA quote.

incidents.name: LeetSwap WETH/SHARE pair fee-transfer drain
incidents.summary: LeetSwapV2Pair exposed its fee-transfer helper publicly without caller, token, or amount authorization. An unprivileged caller could move a pair's counterpart-token balance into its fees contract, synchronize the depleted reserve, and drain WETH through the resulting reserve distortion.

loss.notes: The pair sent 17.173863794881959064 WETH to the attack helper. Excluding the helper's identifiable 0.001 WETH setup-swap input leaves exact pre-recovery victim depletion of 17.172863794881959064 WETH, valued at DefiLlama's nearest observation of $1,860.95. The public fee-transfer call also moved the counterpart token into the pair's fees contract; that internal transfer is excluded because claim allocation and recoverability cannot be isolated from the receipts, so no speculative counterpart-token value is assigned.

incidents.name: NXUSD Cauldron LP-price accounting
incidents.summary: The Cauldron accepted a live reserve-derived LP valuation when checking solvency, allowing one borrower to withdraw 998,000 NXUSD against insufficient JLP collateral.

loss.notes: The sole successful loss receipt transfers exactly 998,000 NXUSD from DegenBox 0x0b1f9c2211f77ec3fa2719671c5646cf6e59b775 to the helper with no NXUSD inflow or return. The DegenBox archive balance falls by exactly that amount, from 60,793,507.532450031356773887 to 59,795,507.532450031356773887 NXUSD. DegenBox receives and retains 0.045330977931305070 USDC/WAVAX JLP collateral, exactly matching its archive increase; this borrower-supplied consideration is not another victim asset loss. The helper's NXUSD, JLP, USDC, USDC.e, WAVAX, and native balances all end at zero. Downstream conversions and the 371,406.644911-USDC transfer to the profit receiver dispose of already-counted NXUSD and are excluded. NXUSD is valued at par; this corrects the seed's attacker-profit-style 50,000 USD estimate to gross victim depletion.

incidents.name: Bedrock uniBTC vault native mint without price conversion
incidents.summary: The uniBTC Vault's payable mint() treats msg.value as "native BTC" and mints uniBTC at _amount / EXCHANGE_RATE_BASE (1e10), i.e. one 8-decimal uniBTC per whole 18-decimal native coin, with no ETH/BTC price conversion. That path is only sound on BTC-gas chains; on Ethereum it minted BTC-denominated uniBTC one-for-one against ETH. The implementation activated at block 20826624 also replaced the native-mint guard require(address(this).balance <= caps[NATIVE_BTC]) with require(ISupplyFeeder(supplyFeeder).totalSupply(NATIVE_BTC) <= caps[NATIVE_BTC]); with caps[NATIVE_BTC] = 0 and the supply feeder reporting 0 for NATIVE_BTC, the check that had previously blocked every native mint on Ethereum passed, opening the path.

loss.notes: Single-transaction extraction. Inside the anchor transaction the attacker contract 0x1e1d02d663228e5d47f1de64030b39632a3b787d flash-borrowed 30.8 WETH from Balancer, unwrapped it, called Vault.mint{value: 30.8 ether}() and received 30.8 uniBTC (3,080,000,000 units, 8 decimals), sold 28.81420431 uniBTC into the Uniswap v3 uniBTC/WBTC 0.05% pool 0x3a32f5040bc4d8417e78e236eb2c48c90e003fda for 27.83925883 WBTC (worth about USD 1,810,471 at the incident timestamp), routed that WBTC through the WBTC/WETH pool 0x4585fe77225b41b697c938b018e2ac67ac5a20c0 for 680.404054576756594919 WETH, repaid the 30.8 WETH flash loan and deposited the remaining 649.604054576756594919 ETH into Aave v3 for 0xee800b1b63893ca1e1b0fa8fefdc10fac9b980f7, which withdrew it 43 blocks later. The measured loss is that 649.604054576756594919 ETH of realised extraction; the 30.8 ETH the attacker paid into the vault stayed with Bedrock and is not added back, and the 1.98579569 uniBTC left unsold in the attacker contract is not counted. Between blocks 20836664 and 20837340 roughly two dozen copycat addresses executed the same native mint for about 6.8 ETH in total; they are not attributed to this attacker and are excluded from the number, which is why contemporaneous reporting of about USD 2 million exceeds the USD 1.71 million measured here. Nothing was recovered: Bedrock's deployer 0x899c284a89e113056a72dc9ade5b60e80dd3c94f sent an onchain whitehat offer to both attacker addresses on 2024-09-27 and got no response, and between 2024-10-01 blocks 20871292 and 20871405 the beneficiary address moved 650.1 ETH into Tornado Cash. Fuzzland disclosed in 2025 that a former employee was the attacker and said it reimbursed affected parties off-chain; that is a third-party reimbursement, not a return of the stolen assets, and it is not netted out.

incidents.name: BitCrown distributor missing caller authorization
incidents.summary: The stateless distributor let any caller choose a token, recipients and amounts for transfers from its own balance. The attacker removed its entire 100,000 BTCn inventory and sold it for USDT.

loss.notes: Entire BTCn inventory valued at actual same-transaction disposal proceeds: 7939.270661176575393032 USDT at par. The token transfer deduction and swap price impact are reflected in the effective value of the stolen 100000 BTCn; gas and recoveries do not reduce gross loss.

incidents.name: Malda Migrator accepted an attacker-supplied Comptroller
incidents.summary: Migrator.migrateAllPositions(MigrationParams) reads the source lending protocol out of caller-supplied calldata: _collectMendiPositions calls getAssetsIn(msg.sender) on params.mendiComptroller and then trusts every returned market's balanceOfUnderlying, borrowBalanceStored and underlying, with no check that the comptroller is Mendi's or that the markets are real cTokens. The only allow-list in the contract, allowedMarkets, constrains the destination Malda mToken, not the source. An attacker therefore deployed a fake comptroller and fake cToken markets that report a borrow position against real Malda underlyings, so step 3 made the allow-listed Malda markets lend the underlying to the Migrator via borrowMigration, and step 4 approved the fake market for that amount and called repayBorrowBehalf on it, letting the fake market pull the tokens straight out of the Migrator.

loss.notes: Two-transaction campaign by one sender: the anchor at 19512428:1 and 0x9f12f7b982ffbd90ac5944b3ab8520f7fb5a9882a0a9acf20d63f6922950e59a at 19513198:2. Each component is the exact sum of the underlying that the eight allow-listed Malda mToken markets paid to the Migrator and that the Migrator then forwarded to the attacker EOA 0x370a8db1f020ce70e8eab2502c739844ca2c2910 in those two receipts. Scanning every ERC-20 Transfer whose sender is the Migrator over its entire life shows exactly these two transactions ever routed a market underlying to an address with no code; the other 66 are ordinary Mendi-to-Malda migrations that move funds into Malda markets. Tracking the attacker EOA and both of its exploit contracts to the present shows no further receipts of these underlyings, so nothing was extracted after 19513198 and no recovery is netted here. The attacker also holds mTokens minted against worthless tokens it deployed; those positions were never redeemed for real underlying and are not counted.

incidents.name: Dexible v2 selfSwap arbitrary router call
incidents.summary: Dexible v2's selfSwap() forwarded a caller-supplied router address and calldata without an allowlist, so the attacker pointed it at ERC20 contracts and had Dexible transferFrom the balances of every wallet still holding an approval to it.

loss.notes: Dexible reported $2,047,635.17 taken from 17 approved wallets across Ethereum and Arbitrum. This is the reported gross incident total.

incidents.name: Alpha Homora v2 HomoraBank zero debt-share borrow
incidents.summary: HomoraBank v2 tracks each bank's debt as totalDebt and totalShare. Two flaws in the implementation active at the time combine. First, the permissionless resolveReserve(address) borrows bank.pendingReserve from the Iron Bank cToken through doBorrow, which adds the borrowed amount to bank.totalDebt while minting no debt share at all, so anyone can raise the debt-per-share ratio without bound. Second, borrow(address,uint256) converts the borrowed amount into shares with truncating division, share = amount.mul(totalShare).div(totalDebt), and neither rounds up nor rejects a zero result, so any borrow smaller than totalDebt/totalShare transfers real tokens and records no debt whatsoever; getBorrowETHValue then values the position's debt at zero and execute()'s require(collateralValue >= borrowValue) passes trivially. Using the unadvertised sUSD bank the attacker borrowed 1,000 sUSD while totalShare was zero, repaid down to totalDebt = totalShare = 1 wei, then called resolveReserve(sUSD) directly on the proxy in this transaction, which borrowed 19,709,787,742,196 wei of accrued reserve and left totalDebt = 19,709,787,742,197 against totalShare = 1. Every subsequent borrow up to that ratio emitted Borrow(..., share 0), and because doBorrow also adds each borrowed amount to totalDebt, the free-borrow ceiling doubled with every iteration until 61,089,765.301487271822120729 sUSD had been drawn from the Iron Bank iSUSD market against one wei of debt share. The attacker redeposited that sUSD as iSUSD collateral and borrowed out the iWETH, iUSDC, iUSDT and iDAI markets. Alpha's own post-mortem names both the borrow rounding error and resolveReserve's share-less totalDebt increase, and the fix replaced div with ceilDiv in borrow and in every debt-valuation path. Only feeBps is configurable and no value of it makes truncating share division correct, so this is a code defect rather than a parameter defect.

loss.notes: Reconstructed from the Compound-style Borrow logs of the Iron Bank markets across the nine campaign transactions listed in source-5. The attacker drew 13,244.630331762545750401 WETH from iWETH 0x41c84c0e2ee0b740cf0d31f63f3b6f627dc6b393, 4,032,014.162771 USDC from iUSDC 0x76eb2fe28b36b3ee97f3adae0c69606eedb2a37c, 5,647,242.107646 USDT from iUSDT 0x48759f220ed983db51fa7a8c0d2aab8f3ce4166a and 4,263,138.929122643119834654 DAI from iDAI 0x8e595470ed749b85c6f7669de83eae304c2ec68f. The 61,089,765.301487271822120729 sUSD drawn from iSUSD is deliberately excluded from the total: it was immediately redeposited into the same market as iSUSD (Mint of 61,085,822.453466168029948973 sUSD), so it left no cash gap in that market; its effect is that HomoraBank now owes it with only one wei of debt share behind it, and it is the collateral the four drains above were taken against. Counting it as well would double count. Netting all ERC-20 Transfer logs over the campaign, the attacker's spell 0x560a8e3b79d23b0a525e15c6f3486c6a293ddad2 finished holding exactly 13,244.630331762545750401 WETH and the attacker EOA 13,532,845.885656673015123177 Curve a3CRV (virtual price 1.027693474457175574 at block 11846617, i.e. about 13.91 million USD), which independently reproduces the same figure. The attacker's own seed capital was 1.5 ETH sent in the setup transaction 0x4441eefe434fbef9d9b3acb169e35eb7b3958763b74c5617b39034decd4dd3ad and is not deducted from gross depletion. The total of 38,393,187.17 USD is within 0.6 percent of the 38,175,295.92 USD Alpha Finance published; press reports of 37.5 million USD use a slightly lower ETH mark.

An unprivileged caller could move a pair's counterpart-token balance into its fees contract, synchronize the depleted reserve, and drain WETH through the resulting reserve distortion.

loss.notes: The pair sent 11.360785525333188388 WETH to the attack helper. Excluding the helper's identifiable 0.001 WETH setup-swap input leaves exact pre-recovery victim depletion of 11.359785525333188388 WETH, valued at DefiLlama's nearest observation of $1,862.36. The public fee-transfer call also moved the counterpart token into the pair's fees contract; that internal transfer is excluded because claim allocation and recoverability cannot be isolated from the receipts, so no speculative counterpart-token value is assigned.

incidents.name: DEI lending sAMM spot-oracle liquidation drain
incidents.summary: The DEI lending contract priced collateral from the sAMM-USDC/DEI pool's spot balances, so the attacker flash-borrowed 24,772,798 DEI out of that same pool to crash the reported collateral value, liquidated the newly insolvent users through helper contract 0xb8f5c9e18abbb21dfa4329586ee74f1e2b685009, burned the seized LP for 5,218,173 USDC plus DEI, and kept 3,001,552.4990983484 DEI after repaying the flash loans.

loss.notes: Exact receipt accounting: net 3001552.4990983484 DEI into the attack contract across the flash-loan, liquidation, LP-burn, and swap steps, with USDC and LP legs netting to zero in-tx. DEI still held its $1 peg at the incident timestamp, and the attacker subsequently bridged 3m USDC via Multichain, converting to 200,000 DAI plus 1,101.8 ETH (about $3.1m) before Tornado Cash, corroborating par. The team reimbursed liquidated users, so the protocol absorbed the loss. No attacker-supplied campaign inputs besides gas.

incidents.name: Stars Arena share-buy reentrancy
incidents.summary: The share-buy entry point (selector 0xe9ccf3a3) sent AVAX back to the caller before finalising share accounting, letting the attacker re-enter the weight-setting function (selector 0x5632b2e4) mid-call so that a single share could then be sold via sellShares() for ~266,000 AVAX.

loss.notes: The exploit trace records exactly 266,103.97278 AVAX transferred from the Stars Arena proxy through the attack contracts and then to the attacker EOA.

incidents.name: DDCoin Marketplace sellItem pays the seller twice
incidents.summary: Marketplace.sellItem transfers the sale amount of escrowed USDT to the seller and also calls usdt.approve(seller, amount), so the seller can pull the same amount again with transferFrom. The attacker placed buy orders from helper contracts to gain sell credit, then repeatedly filled the queued buy orders with cheaply bought DD and pulled each sale's USDT a second time.

loss.notes: Only the second, approval-based payout of each sale is counted; the first payout is the designed exchange for DD delivered to the order's buyer. The reported ~$300k is the attacker's total USDT receipt from the Marketplace.

incidents.name: Warp Finance LP collateral priced from spot reserves
incidents.summary: UniswapLPOracleFactory.getUnderlyingPrice valued a Uniswap V2 LP token as (twapPrice0 * reserve0 + twapPrice1 * reserve1) * 10**decimals / totalSupply, taking the reserves from the pair's instantaneous state through UniswapV2Library.getReserves while taking only the unit prices from a TWAP. Flash-loaned swaps that skewed the DAI/WETH pair raised that sum without changing totalSupply, so WarpControl.getBorrowLimit valued the attacker's LP collateral at 135.470392 USDC per token against a true 58.815427 and authorised 3.86 million DAI and 3.92 million USDC of borrowing. The reserve term is unbounded and none of the contract's parameters bounds or averages it, so no parameter value makes the function correct.

loss.notes: Exact depletion of Warp's two stablecoin lending vaults in the anchor transaction, read from receipt log indices 27 and 32: 3,917,983.816717 USDC left WarpVaultSC 0xae465fd39b519602ee28f062037f7b9c41fdc8cf and 3,862,646.608579660094744528 DAI left WarpVaultSC 0x6046c3ab74e6ce761d218b9117d5c63200f4b406, both to the attacker contract, and neither was repaid. Both assets are valued at par. The 94,349.340516285530671934 UNI-V2 DAI/WETH tokens the attacker posted as collateral stayed in WarpVaultLP 0x13db1cb418573f4c3a2ea36486f0e421bc0d2427 and were recovered by Warp and white-hat helpers on 2020-12-20 at roughly 5.85 million USD; that later recovery does not reduce gross victim depletion. The attacker's flash-loan principal from dYdX and three Uniswap pairs is repaid inside the same transaction and is not counted.

incidents.name: GDCToken sell burn exceeds forwarded amount, with reentrant tax-free exit
incidents.summary: On a taxed GDC sell, swapSellAward forwards only 30% of the sold amount to the pair but _burnSellAgainstPair then burns the full nominal amount out of the pair's reserve and syncs; the sell body runs with swapping = true, and the referral reward is paid mid-body with a raw BNB call, during which transfers into the pair skip the tax branch. Helpers that deposited from their constructors (defeating the extcodesize EOA check) could buy from the pair because the token classifies pair outflows to depositors as liquidity removals. The attacker sold 221.24M GDC to collapse the GDC reserve and, inside the referral callbacks, dumped a pre-bought 1.63B GDC bag tax-free, netting 35.34 WBNB from the GDC/WBNB pair.

loss.notes: WBNB the GDC/WBNB pair 0x9cd8d04c30ed78afef7ed00ab1a2a028d476331c paid to the attacker's contracts net of the WBNB they paid into it, less the attacker's 0.2 BNB of helper deposits into GDC; it equals the 35.33715149597698649 WBNB forwarded to the attacker (Moolah flash loan at 0% fee). The pair's total WBNB drop was 38.136252429986871143; the other 2.799 WBNB are GDC's own tax swap-back routed to the company, referral and liquidity paths and are not attributed to the attacker.

incidents.name: SELLC StakingRewards permissionless token listing and spot-priced sell
incidents.summary: StakingRewards.addLiquidity has no access control and sets listToken[_token]=true for any caller-supplied token. sell(token, token1, amount) then pays any token1 the contract holds, priced from the caller-controlled token/token1 pair. The attacker listed its own token, created a custom pair against SellQILP (the SELLC/QIQI LP that StakingRewards held) and sold worthless tokens for the contract's LP. It burned the LP and dumped the SELLC for WBNB. Copycats repeated the drain within hours.

loss.notes: Components are StakingRewards' exact net depletion in each exploit transaction: Transfer inflows minus outflows of real tokens, so attacker-supplied listing liquidity is netted. Only the first campaign is valued. Its 20712693.906761132 SellQILP (99.96% of the SELLC/QIQI pair supply was held by the victim) is valued at the attacker's realised disposal. Burning the LP yielded 6939399.227733031 SELLC and 58060083.58033396 QIQI; the SELLC plus 33689.818 SELLC the attacker bought with 3 WBNB of its own were sold into Pancake SELLC/WBNB pair 0x358efc593134f99833c66894ccecd41f550051b6 for 303.3264312585738 WBNB. Net of the 3 WBNB input that is 300.3264312585738 WBNB at the DefiLlama WBNB price. QIQI had no liquid market beyond the drained pair and is left unvalued. The pre-exploit spot value of the drained LP (about 1561 BNB of underlying at pair reserves) was not realisable against the 596.48-WBNB SELLC pool, so no spot valuation is used. Later copycat depletion (the second SellQILP, QIQI and SELLC components) is recorded without USD value; its realised proceeds were not isolated, so the USD total is a lower bound.

incidents.name: FPC sell hook drains the pair reserve and syncs
incidents.summary: On every sell the FPC token's _update override calls burnLpToken(value * 65 / 100), which moves 10 percent of the sold amount from the PancakeSwap pair to treasuryAddress and 55 percent from the pair to rewardPoolAddress with super._update(usdtPool, ...), then calls IUniswapV2Pair(usdtPool).sync(). The transfer hook therefore rewrites the counterparty AMM's reserves in the middle of the very swap it is settling: sync() lowers reserve1 to the post-drain FPC balance while reserve0 keeps the full USDT balance, and the router then prices the incoming FPC against that collapsed reserve. In the anchor the attacker first bought 790,178.970489172772916652 FPC so the pair held only 160,836.761063161996185171 FPC, then sold 247,441.170766403071054109 FPC through swapExactTokensForTokensSupportingFeeOnTransferTokens; burnLpToken removed 160,836.761 FPC from the pair and sync() set reserve1 to 65,000,000,000,002 wei, so PancakeRouter computed getAmountOut(235,069.112228082917501404, 0.000065000000000002, 27,693,883.534817151619771979) and the pair paid out 27,693,883.527140201011205321 USDT for the sale.

loss.notes: Exact depletion of the FPC/USDT PancakeSwap pair 0xa1e08e10eb09857a8c6f2ef6cca297c1a081ed6b, whose USDT balance is 4,673,883.534817151619771979 at block 52624700 and 0.007676950608566658 at block 52624701; the difference is the liquidity providers' loss and is measured net of the 23,020,001 USDT the attacker paid into the pair on the preceding buy, so no attacker-supplied capital is counted. The 23,020,000 USDT PancakeSwap v3 flash loan and its 2,302 USDT fee are financing, not loss: the attacker's realised take is 4,671,581.527140201011205321 USDT, 2,302 USDT less than the gross depletion recorded here. DefiLlama prices BSC-USD at exactly 1.0 at the incident timestamp. The pair additionally lost 160,836.761063161996185171 FPC that burnLpToken moved to the project's own treasury 0x0fa6c0bd9704a7a45b16e0487549b10218a82baa and reward pool 0xcea188c6bb0db78fd17904c03e28f43ae4e46d5a; that component is not valued because the same transaction destroyed the only FPC market. Nothing was recovered.

incidents.name: P719 internal AMM mints its swap output and burns its swap input
incidents.summary: P719 is its own market maker: sending BNB to the token buys, and transferring the token to the token sells. Both legs quote a constant-product price from the token's own two balances, tokenOut = balanceOf(token) * bnbIn / (address(token).balance + bnbIn) and bnbOut = address(token).balance * tokenIn / (balanceOf(token) + tokenIn), but neither leg settles against the reserve it just priced. The buy leg mints 1.55x the quoted output instead of debiting balanceOf(token), paying the quote to the buyer, 10 percent and 5 percent of it to two fee sinks and retaining 40 percent, so the token reserve rises when it should fall. The sell leg takes 95 percent of the incoming tokens as the swap input and then burns exactly that amount, forwarding the remaining 5 percent to the fee sinks, so the token reserve does not rise while the BNB reserve is paid out. The product of the two reserves is therefore not preserved by a swap: over the exploit transaction it collapsed from 4.3015e43 to 1.3229e42, 3.1 percent of its starting value, and 3,440 BNB of buys were redeemed for 3,987.799074208829188341 BNB of sells.

loss.notes: Exact victim depletion from chain state: the P719 token contract's native BNB reserve, which backs every holder, fell from 675.766160064604403325 BNB to 99.967085855775214984 BNB inside the anchor transaction, a decrease of 575.799074208829188341 BNB. Reconstructed from the call trace, the attacker paid in 3,440 BNB over 47 buys and the contract paid out 4,015.799074208829188341 BNB over 142 payouts, of which 3,987.799074208829188341 BNB went to the attacker's helper contracts and 28 BNB to the token's own fee wallets on the small buy legs. Attacker-supplied inputs are therefore already netted out; the 4,000 BNB PancakeSwap V3 flash loan and its 0.4 BNB fee are financing and are excluded, leaving the attacker 547.399074208829188341 BNB better off, close to the 547.18 BNB the DeFiHackLabs proof of concept reports after it unwinds the attacker's own liquidity position. The residual 99.97 BNB left in the contract drained away over the following days through ordinary holder sells at the now-broken price and is not attributed to this incident.

incidents.name: Brahma TOPG zapper unvalidated call
incidents.summary: The Brahma TOPG zapper executed a caller-supplied swap target and calldata without validation, allowing one transaction to transfer USDC from three accounts that had approved the zapper.

loss.notes: Gross victim depletion is the exact sum of three USDC transfers in the sole loss receipt: 5,364.965317 from 0x392472c4369d6cdea89e2bddfd8144eecfdc032c, 4,299.130227 from 0x140713bbd82113e104c3a45661134f9764807922, and 79,679.661825 from 0xa19789f57d0e0225a82eeff0fecb9f3776f276a3. Each victim's archive balance moves from that amount to zero. The helper receives and forwards the exact 89,343.757369 USDC, ending with zero, while the attacker moves from zero to the same amount. There are no victim inputs or returns. The attacker's nonce-0 helper deployment has no USDC loss; nonce 1 is the loss receipt; nonce 2 disposes of the already-counted USDC downstream and does not touch the victims or zapper. USDC is valued at par.

incidents.name: NGFS public proxy initialization
incidents.summary: NGFSToken left its single-use proxy initializer public, letting the attacker appoint its own contract as both privileged proxy and library, credit itself an unbacked NGFS balance, and sell it against the NGFS/USDT pool.

loss.notes: The NGFS/USDT pair's USDT balance fell from 192,044.910952619638111430 to 1,906.152962308879782744 in the exploit transaction. Its only USDT transfer was the exact 190,138.757990310758328686 payout to the attacker contract, which began with zero USDT and retained the full amount. Stablecoin-par valuation therefore equals the exact gross LP depletion.

incidents.name: Pike Finance uninitialized upgrade implementation
incidents.summary: The implementation Pike installed on 2024-04-28 to fix an earlier incident left initialize() reachable on the proxy, so the first caller could set every privileged role. The attacker called initialize() to make itself owner and upgrader, then called upgradeToAndCall() through the same implementation to install its own logic and sweep the proxy’s 479.39 ETH in the same transaction.

loss.notes: The exploit transaction sends 479.393838338750964434 ETH from the proxy to the attacker EOA and is the only transaction the attacker sent against Pike; the other three transactions in that EOA’s history are the exploit-contract creation and two disposal swaps. Pike was hit on Arbitrum and Optimism in the same campaign at different addresses; this record covers the Ethereum leg only and does not carry those amounts. DefiLlama’s nearest ETH observation is 57 seconds after the incident timestamp. Nothing was recovered.

incidents.name: CrowdRingCircle pair-reserve burn
incidents.summary: CRC's sell hook burned CRC from the receiving AMM pair before crediting the seller, then called sync() on the reduced balance. Repeated dust sells ratcheted down the recorded CRC reserve, inflated CRC's pool price, and let the attacker drain USDT.

loss.notes: The exploit receipt shows the CRC/USDT pair receiving 184,995,877.105807691589020575 USDT and transferring out 185,204,938.738075562615076319 USDT, for exact net victim depletion of 209,061.632267871026055744 USDT. This subtracts the attacker's swap input but does not deduct financing fees; the final 201,359.472267252045095696 USDT transfer to the attacker EOA is net proceeds, not gross loss. USDT is valued at par.

incidents.name: RANT pair-reserve burn and sync
incidents.summary: A transfer of RANT to the token contract invoked _sellBurnLiquidityPairTokens(amount), which removed an attacker-sized amount of RANT directly from the RANT/WBNB pair and called sync() without removing WBNB. The resulting reserve collapse let rant_center sell the attacker's remaining RANT into the manipulated pair and extract its WBNB reserve.

loss.notes: The exploit transaction's WBNB transfer logs show 2,813.769505544453342436 WBNB entering the RANT/WBNB pair and 3,125.628310019077706276 WBNB leaving it across the manipulated swaps. The pair's exact transaction-local depletion was therefore 311.858804474624363840 WBNB. This gross loss exceeds the attacker's final BNB because the attacker separately paid the flash fee and a validator transfer. DefiLlama observed BNB at $655.15 at timestamp 1751728497, 99 seconds before the exploit.

incidents.name: Scroll Network token unchecked router transfer underflow
incidents.summary: SCROLL's transfer(address,uint256) blocks ordinary holder-to-holder transfers with a bare "Err" revert but exempts the Uniswap UniversalRouter, and on that exempt path it debits the sender without any balance-sufficiency check. Because UniversalRouter.execute is permissionless and its TRANSFER command (0x05) moves the router's own token balance, the attacker made the zero-balance router send 1 wei of SCROLL, underflowing the router's SCROLL balance to 2^256-1, then routed 136,275,915 SCROLL from that fabricated balance into the SCROLL/WETH Uniswap V2 pair and swapped it out for the pair's entire WETH reserve.

loss.notes: Exact victim depletion: the Uniswap V2 pair 0xa718aa1b3f61c2b90a01ab244597816a7ee69fd2 transferred 76.360109345510532175 WETH out in the single Swap of the anchor transaction, leaving a 0.076589 WETH reserve. The attacker unwrapped that WETH and forwarded 76.361109345510532175 ETH to the sender EOA, the extra 999999 wei being the value the sender supplied with the deployment; only the pair's WETH is victim loss. WETH is valued at the DefiLlama WETH price seven seconds before the exploit block; the attacker's own SCROLL selling moved only the SCROLL leg, which is worthless fabricated supply and is not counted. Six later transactions by five unrelated senders reproduced the same underflow between blocks 19973774 and 19989190, but the pair was already empty and they removed 0.0406 WETH in total, so they are copycat follow-ons rather than part of this campaign and are not included.

incidents.name: DCF Token sell-side burnPair reserve destruction
incidents.summary: DCF._transfer gives the sender authority over the liquidity pool's own balance. On any transfer whose destination is pairAddress it computes deadAmount = (amount - 5% fee) / deadCfg from the sender's transfer size and, if the pair still holds more than that, calls burnPair, which executes _burn(pairAddress, deadAmount) and IUniswapV2Pair.sync(). Destroying reserve tokens that belong to the pool's liquidity providers on the strength of a third party's transfer amount violates the invariant that an ERC-20 transfer may only move the sender's own balance, and the same _transfer path then routes the 5% fee through swapExactTokensForTokensSupportingFeeOnTransferTokens with amountOutMin = 0 against the pool it has just repriced. No deadCfg value repairs this: deadCfg is only a divisor, setCfg requires it to be non-zero, and for any divisor d an attacker sizes the transfer at roughly d times the pair's balance to burn the whole reserve, so the deployed code is wrong at every configuration.

loss.notes: Exact depletion of the exploited PancakeSwap V2 DCF/BSC-USD pool 0x8487f846d59f8fb4f1285c64086b47e2626c01b6, whose BSC-USD balance fell from 698634.425616096796822251 to 0.039351777270094825 across the single exploit transaction; its DCF reserve went from 4074.442371848803073636 to 78.618712756698854301 and is not valued because DCF has no independent price series once the pool is empty. BSC-USD is taken at par. The attacker's 80,435,691.245080307237888143 BSC-USD of flash-loaned buy pressure is an attacker-supplied input and is netted out. Of the 698,634.386264 taken from the pool, the attacker realised 442,028.607465892649035455 BSC-USD, which is its exploit contract's whole end-of-transaction balance and which it withdrew to its EOA in 0xe8cd91d9135d98988b8ab8197d70d7fd0ece57b79c5149e40fbd4e574b7234a0; 118,575.868323 went to the flash-loan pools as premiums, which METHODOLOGY does not deduct from gross depletion; and 138,029.910475542584895976 was re-deposited by DCF's own fee-and-liquidity path into the sibling DCT/BSC-USD pool 0x5aac7375196e9ea76b1598ed4be19b41fa5ba651, which is not a recovery to the drained pool's liquidity providers. The seed row and the DeFiHackLabs header both report ~442k USD, which is the attacker's realised proceeds rather than victim depletion.

incidents.name: wBARL pod flash-loan bond reentrancy
incidents.summary: The wBARL WeightedIndex pod's flash() sent out the pod's entire BARL reserve and only checked the balance after the callback, so the attacker called bond() inside the callback and minted pod shares against the flash-loaned BARL, repeating it before debonding.

loss.notes: Gross loss is exact net WETH depletion from the wBARL pod, BARL/DAI pool, and DAI/WETH pool treated as one incident victim set. In the anchor receipt the union conserves exactly 180,115,268.225698757678458280 BARL and 119,220.660871058657167624 DAI while sending 52.133956080457251524 WETH. The second receipt conserves exactly 34,460,652.829973374255498438 BARL and 15,727.075468297283066862 DAI while sending 6.917002474099534042 WETH. BARL and DAI therefore cancel inside the union, leaving 59.050958554556785566 WETH gross depletion. Four precursor transfers fund the helper with 400 DAI, which it pays as 40 ten-DAI flash fees to separate recipient 0xd719345fe7030aeae8e2e9eb0e00e299f3a1ce15; those funds never enter the victim union and do not offset WETH depletion. After the second receipt the helper holds zero DAI, BARL, and WETH, while the EOA holds exactly the summed WETH. Its later exact unwrap, separate DAI disposal, and native distributions do not return value to the victim set and are outside the gross boundary. Archive union WETH balances reconcile both incident blocks after separately accounting for unrelated pool inputs. The closest preceding DefiLlama ETH observation is $2,268.74 at 1706464495, four seconds before the anchor. Exact loss is $133,971.27171106517, replacing the seed's rounded $130,000 estimate.

incidents.name: JimboController permissionless shift/reset rebalancing
incidents.summary: JimboController.shift() and JimboController.reset() are public, callable by anyone, and gate only on pair.getActiveId() relative to the stored trigger and anchor bins. Both withdraw the protocol-owned Trader Joe v2 liquidity and redeploy it around whatever active bin the pair happens to be on at that instant, with no price reference, no TWAP, and no bound on how far the active bin may have moved; the only slippage guard in _addLiquidity is a 1% amountXmin/amountYmin on the router's own add, which does not constrain the price the liquidity is placed at. An attacker who flash-borrows WETH, pushes the JIMBO/WETH active bin up, calls shift(), pushes it back down and calls reset() therefore makes the contract redeposit the protocol's WETH into a bin range they control and then buys it out with JIMBO.

loss.notes: Aggregating WETH Transfer logs across the four campaign receipts, the JIMBO/WETH Trader Joe v2 pair 0x16a5d28b20a3fddecdcaf02df4b3935734df1a1f, which held Jimbos' protocol-owned liquidity, loses exactly 4046.421534086982319423 WETH and is the only net loser. Of that, 4026.421534086982376266 WETH ends up in the three attacker contracts (3039.463221773209170351 + 625.999745568426533282 + 360.958566745346672633) and 20.000000000000000000 WETH is the Aave v3 flash-loan premium paid to aWETH 0xe50fa9b3c56ffb159cb0fca61f5c9d750e8128c8; the premium is a financing fee and does not reduce gross victim depletion. Aave's flash-loan principal is repaid inside each transaction and is not counted. The JIMBO the pair received in exchange is deliberately not credited against the loss: the attacker's own rebalancing and selling set that price, and the token had no independent market. The attacker later swept the WETH to the EOA and bridged it out; no recovery is netted out.

incidents.name: GymSinglePool depositFromOtherContract missing access control
incidents.summary: GymSinglePool.depositFromOtherContract() is external with no caller authorization and its private _autoDeposit() helper never pulls tokens from anyone: it only credits userInfo/user_deposits for the caller-supplied _from address and makes the pool approve itself for the credited amount. Any address could therefore book an arbitrary GYMNET deposit it never funded and then call withdraw(), which transferFrom's the fabricated principal out of the pool's own GYMNET balance.

loss.notes: Eighteen transactions between blocks 18498635 and 18501349 move 40,190,625.461200003991892805 GYMNET out of the pool proxy 0xa8987285e100a8b557f06a7889f79e0064b359f2 to twelve attacker addresses: six fabricated principals of 8,000,000, 8,000,000, 8,000,000, 8,000,000, 8,000,000 and 180,000 GYMNET, one of 10,000 GYMNET, and eleven small claimAll payouts on the fake positions. The pool's GYMNET balance falls from 40,170,632.720222770254498215 before the campaign to 1,847.531967313247850203 at block 18501360. The attacker unwound essentially all of it through the PancakeSwap GYMNET/WBNB pair in eight transactions and the exploiter EOA received exactly 7,475.416854059780883755 BNB; only 625.251209 GYMNET was left stranded in three spent exploit contracts. Those realised proceeds, valued at the DefiLlama BNB observation nearest the incident timestamp (289.5921948984552 USD), give the USD figure and the implied 0.0538638637668875 USD per GYMNET unit price. Marking the drained tokens at DefiLlama's GYMNET spot of 0.19653195097164186 USD would give 7.90 million USD, but the drained quantity is about 2.6x the pair's entire GYMNET reserve and was not realisable at that price; contemporaneous reporting of roughly 2.1 million USD is the realised figure. The 10 percent GYMNET transfer tax charged on the attacker's sells is already inside the realised proceeds. Nothing was returned by the attacker: the BNB was swapped and bridged out over the following day.

incidents.name: Unibot router unvalidated external call
incidents.summary: The direct Unibot router's externally callable function 0xb2bd16ab accepted an unvalidated external target and calldata without binding the token owner to the caller or an authorized Unibot operator. It therefore made attacker-selected transferFrom calls as the approved router, allowing the original exploiter to pull tokens from wallets that had approved it.

loss.notes: This record covers only the original 0x413e4f... exploiter's Ethereum campaign; later copycats are not added. Its 22 successful drain transactions run from the anchor through 0x3efea1... at block 18468232:28. Receipt and call-trace enumeration finds 299 successful victim-to-attacker transferFrom calls and matching Transfer logs, spanning 254 unique victim addresses and 22 token contracts. The often-reported 364-victim/42-token counts therefore appear to include attempted entries or broader activity and are not used as exact loss components. The attacker sold the stolen tokens through block 18468489 and then made 18 Tornado Cash deposits totaling exactly 355.5 ETH: three 100 ETH, five 10 ETH, five 1 ETH, and five 0.1 ETH deposits. CertiK independently reports 355.5 ETH of realized proceeds. This conservative realized-extraction measure avoids inventing incident prices for 22 mostly illiquid source tokens; swaps, copycat proceeds, and the team's later victim reimbursements are not added or netted against gross loss. DefiLlama's ETH observation 28 seconds before the anchor is 1800.0036569996832 USD, giving 639901.3000633874 USD and explaining the seed row's rounded 640000 USD figure.

incidents.name: MBU deposit() price-scale mint inflation
incidents.summary: The MobiusDAO deposit proxy's deposit(token, amount) values the deposit as amount x oracle token price without dividing out the 18-decimal price scale, then mints value x 1e18 / MBU price, so it mints 1e18 times the correct MBU. A 0.001 WBNB deposit (0.657 USD at the oracle's 656.92 USD/BNB) minted 9731099570720980.659843835099042677 MBU instead of 0.00973 MBU; selling 28,500,000 of them into the MBU/USDT PancakeSwap pair drained 2,157,126 USDT. Copycats repeated the same 0.001 WBNB deposit ten more times.

loss.notes: Gross USDT depletion of the MBU/USDT PancakeSwap V2 pair 0xb5252fcef718f8629f81f1dfcff869594ad478c6 caused by bug-minted MBU. Component 1 is the anchor transaction (attacker 0xb32a53af96f7735d47f4b76c525bd5eb02b42600). Component 2 merges later actors repeating the same deposit(WBNB, 1e15) path between blocks 49470431 and 49475087: 1809.975661133888705413 USDT drained inside seven later deposit transactions plus 634.791782021593824162 USDT from nine separate Universal Router sells by 0x89f4e21c62e0fb52c8445e842781e77fe333f50d of MBU it minted in 0x84674f8b0ac41b8870b79e51abc4ea491ebf97f02f57d45241073d7cac364dee. The 0.001 WBNB inputs are attacker-supplied and not netted; unsold bug-minted MBU and the 1,000,000 bug-minted MBU that 0xa5eabc3b36dba37593352a00ce8b7720da6fc624 staked and later unstaked are not counted. Small later pair outflows to unrelated addresses (12.01 USDT to 0x0fccab6848d59c45b758dc1c9057e618b157231f and multi-hop swaps via 0x16b9a82891338f9ba80e2d6970fdda79d1eb0dae) have unestablished MBU provenance and are excluded. Nothing was recovered.

incidents.name: dForce LPCurveGaugeAggregatorModel read-only reentrancy
incidents.summary: LPCurveBaseAggregatorModel._getPrice(), the code behind dForce's wstETHCRV-gauge vault aggregator, prices the collateral as priceOracle.getUnderlyingPrice(pool.coins(0)) * pool.get_virtual_price(). get_virtual_price() is an unguarded external view on the Curve ETH/wstETH pool 0x6eb2dc694eb516b16dc9fbc678c60052bbdd7d80 and returns D * PRECISION / token_supply, so while remove_liquidity() is paying out native ETH through raw_call the LP supply has already been reduced but the balances have not fully settled and the ratio is wrong. The aggregator performs the read with no reentrancy probe, so re-entering from the pool's ETH refund let the attacker have dForce value the vwstETHCRV-gauge collateral at a distorted price, seize a 1,019.577317265394873995 gauge-token position and mint 1,219,437.439363481229905117 USX of unbacked debt in the same transaction.

loss.notes: Both components are measured from the anchor receipt. The vwstETHCRV-gauge market 0x2ce498b79c499c6bb64934042eba487bd31f75ea held 1,048.408829854823855419 gauge tokens at block 59527633 and 28.831512589428981424 at block 59527634, and its iToken supply falls by the same 1,019.577317265394873995 at an exchange rate of exactly 1e18, all of it taken from depositor 0x916792f7734089470de27297903bed8a4630b26d. The gauge token is valued the way dForce's own aggregator values it outside reentrancy: get_virtual_price 1.011371298035750307 at block 59527633 times the DefiLlama ETH price 1544.78, i.e. 1562.3461537796664 USD, giving 1,031.17 ETH-equivalent, which matches dForce's own public figure of 1,031.42 ETH liquidated on Arbitrum. USX net minted in the transaction is 1,219,437.439363481229905117 (mints minus burns against the zero address) and is valued at par; dForce publicly put the protocol debt created across both chains at 2.3 million USD, of which this Arbitrum leg is 1.22 million. Cross-check on the attacker side: the attacker EOA's native balance rises by exactly 1,236.654369923464 ETH in this transaction and it also keeps 719,437.439363481229905117 USX, the remaining 500,000 USX having been swapped to 493,757.29376 USDC.e and then to WETH inside the transaction; realised proceeds are slightly below gross depletion because of flash-loan and swap costs. Attacker-supplied capital was 0.5 ETH staged in transaction 0x5f238693 and is not deducted from these victim-side figures. Aave, Balancer and Uniswap V3 flash loans are repaid within the transaction and are not loss. The attacker returned 1,237 ETH to dForce on 2023-02-13; per methodology that later recovery does not reduce gross depletion. The same-day Optimism campaign against the mirror deployment (exploit 0x6c19762186c9f32c81eb2a79420fc7ad4485aa916cab37ec278b216757bfba0d) is a separate incident and none of its loss is counted here.

incidents.name: Rugged Art RuggedMarket targetedPurchase arbitrary router call
incidents.summary: RuggedMarket.targetedPurchase() forwarded attacker-supplied UniversalRouter commands and inputs without validating them, letting a flash-loan-funded caller sweep the market's RUGGED balance and NFTs and then unstake against it.

loss.notes: The commit-pinned reproduction reports approximately 5 ETH of net proceeds. The USD amount values that reported quantity at DefiLlama's incident-time ETH price.

incidents.name: GiddyVaultV3 compound signature covers only the swap payload hash
