incidents.summary: GiddyVaultV3.compound() authenticates the caller with an EIP-712 signature whose digest binds only keccak256 of each SwapInfo.data field, leaving the accompanying fromToken, toToken, amount and aggregator addresses outside the signed scope. The attacker replayed a signature the operator had already produced, substituted its own token and aggregator parameters, and had the vault route the strategies’ balances out through an aggregator it controlled.

loss.notes: The exploit transaction credits the attacker with 3.531384449443560254 g(yb-tBTC), 6.935949844931976725 g(yb-cbBTC) and 6.274444990265641146 g(yb-WBTC). Six follow-up transactions redeem those shares into yb-tBTC, yb-cbBTC and yb-WBTC and then unwrap them, ending in exactly the three amounts recorded here; the components are therefore the realised BTC-denominated value of the stolen shares rather than a mark on the share tokens themselves. DefiLlama observations are within 130 seconds of the incident timestamp. Nothing was recovered.

incidents.name: MINER ERC-X self-transfer balance duplication
incidents.summary: The MINER ERC-X token's _transfer rejects only the zero address for sender and receiver, and the _update it calls caches uint256 fromBalance = _balances[from] and uint256 toBalance = _balances[to] before writing _balances[from] = fromBalance - value and _balances[to] = toBalance + value. When from == to the second write restores the pre-transfer balance and adds value on top, so a transfer to one's own address is a pure credit of value out of nothing while _totalSupply is unchanged. The attacker's contract looped this self-transfer 2000 times inside a Uniswap V3 swap callback, minting the MINER it owed the pool and paying for 999.999999999999998 MINER of output it never held. No parameter value repairs this: the write order is wrong for every amount.

loss.notes: Exact depletion of the MINER/WETH Uniswap V3 pool 0x732276168b421d4792e743711e1a48172ea574a2, measured by summing every WETH Transfer from that pool to the exploit contract 0xbff51c9c3d50d6168dfef72133f5dbda453ebf29 across the eleven campaign transactions in blocks 19226600 to 19226707: 168607972696358826905 wei, all of which the contract forwarded to the attacker EOA in two withdrawals. The attacker's only campaign input was 0.1 WETH spent 27 minutes earlier in transaction 0xe9d68078bbee1d5a0fa6ff683d59928828d162d2b4502182f82dcc0d894b6d4c buying the 3.572592720467130237 MINER seed at market price; netting it would give 168.507972696358826905 WETH. Realised WETH proceeds are used rather than any MINER mark: the exploit minted MINER without limit and the pool's MINER reserve rose from 20,760.445641193926256214 to 31,070.707215523730649876 while its WETH reserve fell from 292.675662175650830997 to 8.339688812255084036, so no spot mark on the minted tokens would be realisable. The pool's WETH balance fell by 284.335973363395746961 between blocks 19226599 and 19226717, so a further 115.728000667036920056 WETH net left it over the same span through liquidity withdrawals and unrelated holders selling into the collapse; that is market exit rather than value taken by this campaign and is excluded.

incidents.name: Cream Finance (AMP reentrancy)
incidents.summary: Cream's borrow path transferred hook-enabled AMP before committing the borrower's updated debt, so the AMP recipient hook could re-enter a second market and borrow again against collateral already consumed by the unfinished outer borrow.

loss.notes: Cream's post-mortem reports 462,079,976 AMP and 2,804.96 ETH lost across the main and copycat exploit campaign. The approximately $34 million contemporaneous total replaces the early $18.8 million estimate, which covered only the initially identified 418,311,571 AMP and 1,308.09 ETH.

incidents.name: UvToken Eco Staking pool caller-supplied pledge contract
incidents.summary: The UvTokenWallet Eco Staking pool 0x5ecfda78754ec616ed03241b4ae64a54d6705a1a pays withdrawals from a caller-supplied pledge contract address. Its withdraw function (selector 0xc81daf6e, arguments user and pledge) asks that address for the user's amount through selector 0x95b81c68 and has UVT vault 0x36f277165c8b1b80cc3418719badb1864e2687bc transfer that amount, without checking the address against the pool's registered pledges. The attacker passed its own contract, which reported 100,449,018.65 UVT, received that from the vault and sold it for 5,011.175 WBNB.

loss.notes: Vault 0x36f27716 transferred exactly 100,449,018.652509565091128557 UVT (log 0x16) to attacker contract 0x99d4311f. In the same transaction the contract sold all of it: 5,052,410.919669585 UVT via the UV/USDT pair 0xb33797e8 and USDT/WBNB pair 0x16b9a828, and 95,396,607.732839968 UVT via the UV/WBNB pair 0xc7e067e4, and the EOA received 3,932.977781469900 + 1,078.197229814380 = 5,011.175011284280665818 WBNB (logs 0x21 and 0x27). That disposal moved the UVT price, so the drained UVT is valued at its realised proceeds: 5,011.175011284280665818 WBNB x 290.21 USD (DefiLlama WBNB at 1666846948). The 0.5 WBNB the attacker spent on 313.819 UVT it staked beforehand is not part of the proceeds. SlowMist reports 5,011 BNB moved to Tornado Cash (the EOA forwarded 5,011.641 BNB to 0xbc1ac845e889a8795e7f22569aa073aeb3071ef6, which made 51 Tornado router deposits). DefiLlama lists 1.5M USD.

incidents.name: Four.meme launchpad liquidity migration into pre-initialized pools
incidents.summary: The launchpad's addLiquidity() migration accepted an existing PancakeSwap V3 pool without checking its initialized price, so attackers pre-created pools at manipulated sqrtPriceX96 values and swapped out the WBNB deposited during migration.

loss.notes: Gross depletion is the WBNB transferred out of 68 attacker-preinitialized PancakeSwap V3 pools in their first post-migration drain, summed over 66 transactions. WBNB Transfer, Deposit and Withdrawal logs show no WBNB input to those pools in the selected transactions, so the exact aggregate outflow is also their aggregate transaction-level balance decrease. Eighteen attacker-created pools that never migrated and six migrated pools with no drain during the campaign are excluded. The public 287 BNB / USD 183,000 estimate is not used because it does not reconcile to gross pool depletion. No recovery is netted.

incidents.name: MO Loan borrow burns pair reserves and prices collateral from the manipulated spot
incidents.summary: Loan.borrow pulls MO collateral, pays USDT valued at the MO/USDT pair's spot reserves, then has the pair burn 90% of the borrowed MO amount from its own reserves and sync, raising the MO spot price; a duration-0 order can be redeemed immediately for full collateral with zero interest. The attacker looped borrow/redeem to ratchet the MO price, then borrowed against the inflated price and sold MO into the depleted pair, draining USDT from the Loan contract and the pair.

loss.notes: Two USDT components: net Loan contract depletion (331,860.835974) and net MO/USDT pair depletion (414,331.166143) in extraction transactions source-2 and source-6. MO burned from the pair and MO moved between the parties are not valued (the post-exploit MO price collapsed), so the USD figure is a lower bound on LP loss. Attacker seed funds (2,100 USDT into its contract and small USDT additions to the pair in its getReward calls) are not counted as victim loss.

incidents.name: GlueX callback drains CoW fee buffers
incidents.summary: The GlueX swap helper authenticates uniswapV3SwapCallback against a pool address supplied in the callback data itself. A caller supplies its own address as the pool, the CoW settlement as payer and an approved token, causing transferFrom to pay the caller without an active swap.

loss.notes: Gross CoW settlement fee-buffer depletion across 66 successful drains by seven transaction senders, ending at block 21135610. DRAGONX and TITANX are valued at their complete onchain disposal proceeds. WETH, weETH and wstETH use historical quotes near the first drain, and USDC uses USD parity. Builder payments, gas and later reimbursement do not reduce gross loss. Sale proceeds are not counted again as stolen WETH.

incidents.name: STO pending sell burn removes the previous sale from the STO/WBNB pair, with trading opened by permissionless initializeLiquidity
incidents.summary: While burnEnabled is set, every non-whitelisted sale to the STO/WBNB pair adds its after-tax amount to pendingBurnFromSell, and the next non-pair transfer moves that amount from the pair to DEAD and calls sync(), so a seller can sell and then delete the sold tokens from the reserve. Buying was still disabled, but initializeLiquidity is permissionless and enables buying and selling once the pair holds 2,000 WBNB. The attacker donated flash-loaned WBNB to the pair, called initializeLiquidity with 1 wei of BNB, bought 7.85M STO, and alternated sells with transfers that burned each prior sale from the pair until it held no WBNB.

loss.notes: Net WBNB depletion of the STO/WBNB pair 0x7c404ad6149bc69e07ecd534b9f4243ef289bd00 in the single exploit transaction; the attacker's flash-loaned donation and buy input and its 0.06 WBNB zap liquidity leg are netted as attacker inputs. The pair's STO burned to DEAD is the same liquidity and is not added.

incidents.name: Neko Network MainPool borrow on behalf of any account
incidents.summary: Neko Network's Aave-style MainPool 0x4071ee5eb20ba7352dcf08cabc7da4fa1daa370c implements borrow(asset, amount, onBehalfOf) by minting the variable-debt token to onBehalfOf and paying the borrowed underlying to msg.sender, with no borrow-allowance or delegation check. The debt token's mint(address,uint256) takes no caller argument. Any account could therefore borrow against another depositor's collateral and keep the funds. Six attacker accounts and two attacker contracts made 196 such borrows against 16 depositors, taking 3,620,179 USDT, 499,424.04 BUSD, 2,792.84 USDC and 1 BTCB.

loss.notes: Sum of MainPool Borrow(reserve, user, onBehalfOf, amount, ...) logs (topic0 0x7752d0a9...) with user != onBehalfOf, excluding the 45 WBNB borrows (2,519.06 WBNB, blocks 9895394-9959340) routed through the Neko deployer's helper 0xfd21385c8753a52157dbaebac805c1df1818d5da, where the transaction sender is the debtor. That leaves 196 attacker borrows (blocks 9965527-9971112), whose per-account counts match the Maze post-mortem: 1 + 103 via 0xe4ecb6c4 for hacker 1, 62 for 0x4f5bc386, 14 via 0x52c52cee, 12 for 0x3551fd33, 3 for 0x79391843 and 1 for 0x6666666c. Its per-asset totals equal the post-mortem's 'Total Loss (Debt Added)'. The borrowed underlying left the fTokens to the attackers; the victims were left with the debt. The attackers' later return of about 1.8M USD to the deployer is a recovery and is not deducted. BTCB is valued at the DefiLlama price nearest its borrow (0x28f2b77a, block 9970588); the stablecoins are valued at par.

incidents.name: LEDS chained unguarded deflationary burns collapse the pair reserve
incidents.summary: The LEDS token implementation exposes several independent burn mechanisms that each remove LEDS from the LEDS/WBNB pair and sync: triggerDailyBurnAndMint, a deferred sell-burn accumulated in stor_18, a to==router burn branch, and the public flush 0x17a06174 which burns the whole accumulated stor_18 from the pair with no access control. Inside flash loans the attacker deposited for LP rewards, chained these burns to reduce the pair's LEDS reserve to 2 wei while its WBNB reserve stayed, then reverse-swapped to drain the WBNB.

loss.notes: Net WBNB the attacker's contract 0xe941c0dd forwarded to the attacker EOA 0x1f9b4d11 (104.56119408224858 WBNB), which equals its WBNB balance gain in the transaction; the Moolah/Venus/Aave/PancakeV4 flash-loan legs are repaid in full. The LEDS/WBNB pair 0xd109a84a1afec068e70cdb11a75e14a856a96f3f held 205.529 WBNB before and 1.926 after; its full 203.603 WBNB decrease is not used because the attacker also added and removed liquidity (LP supply rose 20,376 to the attacker) and the token's deflation forwards part of the reserve to project wallets, so the attacker's realised WBNB is the clean victim loss and matches the reported ~$64K. Valued at the DefiLlama WBNB price.

incidents.name: SpiralHookV2 spot-price borrow with tx.origin same-block guard
incidents.summary: SpiralHookV2.borrow values SPIRAL collateral at the live Uniswap V4 slot0 price of its own pool, and its only same-block defence keys lastSwapBlockOf on tx.origin. The attacker pumped the pool with 54 ETH from one EOA, then borrowed against the bought SPIRAL at the inflated spot from six other EOAs through one contract in the same block, withdrawing 64.71 ETH of hook-owned liquidity.

loss.notes: Net loss: the attacker's 54 ETH pump went into the same hook-owned liquidity that the borrows withdrew, so the loss is the attacker's net ETH gain (64.70728098661343541 ETH borrowed minus 54 ETH paid in), equal to the protocol's net ETH depletion because the swap and origination fees stayed with protocol fee recipients. Unrepaid debt is not added and the SPIRAL collateral left behind is not netted.

incidents.name: ATK live-pair reward pricing
incidents.summary: The ATK reward contract sized claimToken1 from the configured pair's live ATK and USDT balances, so a claim inside a pair callback released reward inventory at a transient reserve ratio and the resulting ATK removed USDT from the pair.

loss.notes: Across the bounded nonce-5-through-18 campaign, the ATK/USDT pair sends 130,938.042674581496920399 + 127,677.363775463262166716 + 3,735.200016119348067113 USDT. It receives 134.728431544645009270 and 121.217699044304557015 USDT in the two linked ATK buys, then 131,271.934683401679737546 and 3,744.724776160452404684 USDT in the two flash repayments. The exact net depletion is 127,078.000876013025445713 USDT. Nonce 18 only moves the first helper's remaining 490.475239958895662429 USDT to the campaign EOA and leaves that helper at zero USDT; nonce 19 similarly withdraws the second helper's 166.107991179817182853-USDT remainder. Nonces 19-21 are downstream disposal, not victim flows. The unrelated source-4 swap in the claim block sends 61.384706202020868948 USDT out of the pair and 607.789 ATK in; excluding it reconciles archive balances. The two positions deposit 970.4654 and 971.1491 genuinely purchased ATK. The claim sends 51,066,033.07817472 ATK from the reward contract; the sale routes 46,038,567.993335287573138174 ATK back to the pair and 505,918.329597091072232287 ATK back to the reward contract. This endogenous reward inventory is not independent scarce consideration; its genuine acquisition costs are already netted in USDT.

incidents.name: Pesto self-balance-triggered swapback sandwich
incidents.summary: The PESTO token repeated the DOGGO pattern: its transfer hook sold the token's own accumulated balance on Uniswap with no slippage bound once that self-balance passed a hard-coded threshold, and the attacker topped the balance up by direct transfer to trigger and sandwich the sale inside a Uniswap V3 flash loan.

loss.notes: After the Uniswap V3 flash loan was repaid and 0.023961153697538490 ETH was paid to the block builder, the trace records exactly 0.503881906767766532 ETH transferred from the attack helper to the attacker EOA. Transaction gas is excluded.

incidents.name: SocketGateway wrapped-token swap route arbitrary call
incidents.summary: Socket route 406 (WrappedTokenSwapperImpl 0xcc5fda5e3ca925bd0bb428c8b2669496ee43067e) is delegatecalled by SocketGateway and, in performAction, forwards fully caller-controlled calldata to a caller-controlled address with `fromToken.call(swapExtraData)`. With amount = 0 the surrounding balance-delta and safeTransferFrom checks are satisfied trivially, so the attacker made the gateway execute `USDC.transferFrom(victim, attacker, allowance)` and equivalent calls on WETH, USDT, WBTC, DAI and MATIC, draining every unlimited approval users held on SocketGateway. The route had been registered three days earlier through NewRouteAdded(uint32,address); the gateway itself was never upgraded.

loss.notes: The campaign is exactly two transactions, both contract creations whose constructors run the drain: 0xc6c3331f at block 19021454 and 0x591d054a at block 19021465. Netting every ERC-20 Transfer in the two receipts gives the attacker EOA 0x50df5a2217588772471b84adbbe4194a2ed39066 a gain of 2,569,980.189709 USDC, 347,005.653023 USDT, 13,821.013832088432971148 DAI, 42.475261047009995242 WETH, 2.88962154 WBTC and 165,356.991611426813451965 MATIC, taken from roughly 200 distinct approval-granting victim addresses. All ten other routeId-406 calls to the gateway between installation and the exploit are small legitimate WETH wrap/unwrap swaps and are excluded. Stables are valued at par and the three volatile assets at DefiLlama observations within 95 seconds before the exploit. On 2024-01-22/23 the attacker returned 1,032 ETH to 0xc3a8af8c8bfc263030258afd80eb25afb6ff0820 and the full WETH, WBTC, DAI and MATIC balances plus 106.047775245495926983 ETH to 0xb4a3b6268c306833f75ebe43192c38905c992598, reported by Socket as about 2.3M USD recovered; recovery is not netted out of the exploit-time gross figure.

incidents.name: USDTStakingContract28 public tokenAllowAll()
incidents.summary: tokenAllowAll(token, spender) was public with no owner check, so the attacker had the staking contract approve them for unlimited USDT and then transferred out the whole deposit balance.

loss.notes: Entire preexisting staking balance transferred to attacker, valued at USDT par. No campaign input or recovery adjustment; gas costs do not reduce gross loss.

incidents.name: ChainSwap MappingToken receive() unauthorised signatories
incidents.summary: The bridge's receive(fromChainId,to,nonce,volume,Signature[]) counted the supplied signature entries towards its threshold without checking that each signatory was an authorised bridge signer, so anyone could mint bridged tokens to themselves.

loss.notes: Forty nonzero mint events beginning with the anchored transaction created exactly 20,000,000 WYLD for the attacker. The attacker sold that full amount in transaction 0x6fcc98a9a765ed2fb6992e099a0a13fe65c46901dbbf0401a76c2edb4a70b3e2 for exactly 652.443795985428055167 WBNB, the exact BSC liquidity loss measured by this row.

incidents.name: Origin Dollar Vault mintMultiple reentrancy
incidents.summary: VaultCore.mintMultiple() skipped the supported-asset check that mint() performed, so the attacker passed a self-controlled fake stablecoin whose transferFrom re-entered the vault and triggered a rebase between the first mint's asset transfer and its OUSD supply increase, minting more OUSD than the vault held in assets.

loss.notes: Origin's project post-mortem reports a $7 million loss. PeckShield independently estimated approximately $7.7 million, including 11,809 ETH and 2,249,821 DAI, so the record retains Origin's rounded first-party gross-loss figure without presenting the reported token quantities as exact structured components.

incidents.name: DeltaPrime unvalidated LFJ reward pair
incidents.summary: TraderJoeV2ArbitrumFacet.claimReward() accepted an arbitrary LFJ pair without checking that the factory created it, then trusted that pair's hook and rewarder. The malicious rewarder called back into the Prime Account to wrap its borrowed native ETH between the function's before/after WETH balance checks, causing collateral and debt proceeds to be misclassified and paid out as rewards without a solvency check.

loss.notes: Arbitrum leg only. Components are the exact depletion of DeltaPrime's five Arbitrum lending pools across the thirteen defect-executing campaign transactions and the loot sweep, summed from their ERC-20 Transfer logs: WethPool 0x2e2fe9bc7904649b65b6373baf40f9e2e0b883c5 -66.619545304650988218 WETH (all of it in the anchor transaction), UsdcPool 0x5f3db5899a7937c9abf0a5fc91718e6f813e4195 -271614.819122 USDC, BtcPool 0x275caecf5542bf4a3cf64aa78a3f57dc9939675c -2.96703344 WBTC, ArbPool 0x14c82cfc2c651700a66abdd7dc375c9ceefddd72 -50060.231512018705280417 ARB and DaiPool 0x7dcf909b1e4b280bee72c6a69b3a7ed8adfb63f0 -2769.105063733408190911 DAI. Every unit is accounted for in attacker hands: the sweep 0xac2132626ed42a611cbca336fca7a6cdafabe919ca95f39f80dcb9a2e24103b7 moved 33.209772652325494104 WETH, 271614.819122 USDC, 2.96703344 WBTC, 35749.434643912413610260 ARB and 2769.105063733408190911 DAI to loot address 0x56e7f67211683857ee31a1220827cac5cdaa634c, the attacker-deployed fake LFJ pair 0x52ee5c0ea2e7b38d4b24c09d4d18cba6c293200e kept the 14310.796868106291670157 ARB drained after that sweep, and the rest of the pool WETH left that contract as native ETH: 0.2 unwrapped inside the sweep, 33.200000000000004096 unwrapped in 0xdf0a5c1ae3fd412d565802b2ae542a1d6e4a585a00648181785b1282175a4a64 at block 273283967 and a final 0.009000000000008 at block 273345812, leaving about 0.00077 WETH of dust. The pool WETH is counted once: the attacker recycled the same 66.619545304650988218 WETH out of the fake pair as working capital for each later transaction and returned it every time. Balancer flash loans through vault 0xba12222222228d8ba445958a75a0704d566bf2c8 are repaid inside their transactions and are not loss; no attacker-supplied capital was consumed. The Avalanche leg of the same campaign is carried by its own record eip155:43114:0xece4efbe11e59d457cb1359ebdc4efdffdd310f0a82440be03591f2e27d2b59e and is deliberately not included here. DeltaPrime's rounded 4.75 million USD post-mortem figure and Verichains' analysis cover both chains together and must not be added to a per-chain measurement; CertiK splits the campaign as about 753 thousand USD on Arbitrum and about 4.1 million USD on Avalanche, which matches the two records. DeltaPrime separately lost about 5.98 million USD to a September 16 private-key compromise; that is a different incident. DAI uses stablecoin par because DefiLlama has no observation at or before the campaign end for it.

incidents.name: DeltaPrime Avalanche unvalidated LFJ reward pair
incidents.summary: TraderJoeV2AvalancheFacet.claimReward(address,uint256[]) accepts an arbitrary LFJ pair address without checking that the LFJ factory created it, then trusts that pair's hook and rewarder. It snapshots the Prime Account's WAVAX balance, calls the caller-supplied pair's claim(), and pays out the difference to msg.sender with no solvency check. The malicious rewarder calls back into the Prime Account's wrapped-native facet to wrap borrowed native AVAX between the before and after snapshots, so pool debt drawn through swapDebtParaSwap is reclassified as reward and transferred out.

loss.notes: Components are the exact depletion of DeltaPrime's Avalanche lending pools, summed from the Transfer logs of the six exploit transactions and the loot sweep: WavaxPool 0xd26e504fc642b96751fd55d3e68af295806542f5 -74420.190026835772433671 WAVAX, UsdcPool 0x2323dac85c6ab9bd6a8b5fb75b0581e31232d12b -860088.776389 USDC, BtcPool 0x475589b0ed87591a893df42ec6076d2499bb63d0 -6.34401755 BTC.b, UsdtPool 0xd222e10d7fe6b7f9608f14a8b5cf703c74efbca1 -259926.541496 USDt and WethPool 0xd7feb276ba254cd9b34804a986ce9a8c3e359148 -49.675622190954455477 WETH.e. The attacker's loot address 0xd3d535141831f6bd8b7df92e2ae0463d60af2413 holds 74183.842277799231529158 WAVAX, 860088.776389 USDC, 6.34401755 BTC.b, 259926.541496 USDt and 49.675622190954455477 WETH.e after the sweep, plus 110 native AVAX; a further 110 native AVAX went to the generalised front-runner 0x5135b55b35822d4d4df66deaf52edef613112c8e that landed the sweep, and per methodology that builder-style payment is not deducted. The 220 native AVAX are already inside the WAVAX quantity that left the pool and are not listed separately. All Balancer flash loans are repaid within their transactions and are not loss. This record covers the Avalanche leg only; the Arbitrum leg of the same campaign is the separate incident eip155:42161:0x6a2f989b5493b52ffc078d0a59a3bf9727d134b403aa6e0bf309fd513a728f7f, whose loss is now an independent onchain reconstruction of about 754 thousand USD from its own five Arbitrum pools, so the two records are disjoint and may be summed. CertiK measured about 4.1 million USD on Avalanche and about 753 thousand USD on Arbitrum against DeltaPrime's rounded 4.75 million USD campaign total.

incidents.name: SushiSwap RouteProcessor2 unvalidated route pool
incidents.summary: RouteProcessor2.processRoute() never checked that the pool address encoded in the caller-supplied `route` was a genuine UniswapV3 pool. The router called swap() on that address and then trusted whoever called back into uniswapV3SwapCallback(), whose implementation transfers `tokenIn` from the address recorded in the router's transient `lastCalledPool`/msg.sender state instead of from the caller. An attacker-controlled contract posing as a pool could therefore make the router execute transferFrom against any wallet that had granted RouteProcessor2 an ERC20 allowance.

loss.notes: The depleted assets were not protocol-held funds. RouteProcessor2 custodies nothing; every wei taken came out of an external wallet that had previously granted the router an ERC20 allowance. Reconstructed from WETH Transfer receipts rather than from the post-mortem estimate: across eleven successful transactions between blocks 17007838 and 17007856, exactly eighteen 100 WETH transferFrom calls left the single approving wallet 0x31d3243cfb54b34fc9c73e1cb1137124bd6b13e1 for eight different searcher contracts, totalling exactly 1800.000000000000000000 WETH. Ten transactions moved 100 WETH each; 0x04b166e7b4ab5105a8e9c85f08f6346de1c66368687215b0e0b58d6e5002bc32 batched eight callbacks for 800 WETH. Sweeping every WETH inflow of all eight receiving contracts over blocks 16990000-17020000 turns up no other victim wallet, so the campaign's gross depletion is exactly the 1800 WETH the post-mortem approximates. Financing, gas, builder payments and any later whitehat returns are not netted.

incidents.name: NOVO transferFrom without allowance check drains the NOVO/WBNB pair
incidents.summary: NOVO's transferFrom moves tokens from any sender without spending an allowance (the _approve deduction is commented out). The attacker bought NOVO with flash-swapped WBNB, called transferFrom to move most of the NOVO/WBNB pair's NOVO to the token contract, synced the pair, and sold NOVO into the collapsed reserve for the pair's WBNB, then repeated five blocks later.

loss.notes: Net WBNB depletion of the NOVO/WBNB pair across both attacker transactions; the attacker's own 17.2 WBNB buys each time are netted by measuring from the pre-transaction reserve.

incidents.name: RWT privileged sell reserve burn
incidents.summary: The role-authorized RWT sell contract exposed sell() without caller authorization and each call burned tokens from the AMM pair before sync, letting anyone repeatedly inflate the pool price and drain USDT.

loss.notes: Gross loss is exact net USDT depletion from RWT/USDT PancakePair 0xc1c2ef25372f12ce18d35044446064b720c4aa27 in the single successful incident receipt. The pair receives 371,491.198973571309200329 USDT and sends 530,107.673365310624346545 USDT, losing 158,616.474391739315146216 USDT. Archive balances fall from 158,742.652464146663510787 to 126.178072407348364571 USDT across block 110827952, reproducing the receipt arithmetic exactly. All seven other transactions in the sender's complete nonce history have zero pair-USDT flow and are excluded. USDT is valued at par; financing and downstream proceeds do not reduce gross pair depletion.

incidents.name: Midas Capital fsAMM-HAY-BUSD cToken rounding loss
incidents.summary: Midas CToken.redeemFresh converted an exact requested underlying amount to the cTokens to burn with divScalarByExpTruncate, rounding the burn down. After reducing the fsAMM-HAY-BUSD market to 1,001 wei of cToken supply and donating underlying to inflate its exchange rate, the attacker repeatedly requested about 1.998 wei of underlying while burning only 1 wei; the remaining-supply guard did not activate because each redemption left exactly 1,000 wei. The inflated collateral position was then used to borrow and liquidate cash from three other Midas markets.

loss.notes: Gross loss is the exact pre-recovery depletion of external token balances in the three victim debt markets over the 17 value-bearing campaign transactions: fANKR 0x13ae975c5a1198e4f47c68c31c1230694dc44a57 lost 685999.702783572563751254 ANKR, fankrBNB 0xb2b01d6f953a28ba6c8f9e22986f5bddb7653aea lost 1148.264532617591819152 ankrBNB, and fHAY 0x10b6f851225c203ee74c369ce876beb56379fca3 lost 25296.116863562095022654 HAY. This excludes the attacker's flash liquidity and donated fsAMM-HAY-BUSD collateral rather than treating those circular inputs as victim loss. It also excludes later swaps and proceeds handling, and nets no recovery. The project post-mortem's approximately USD 340,000 pool-drain estimate corroborates this USD 332,253.20 component valuation; the seed row's USD 600,000 figure described attacker proceeds/profit and is not a comparable victim-depletion measure.

incidents.name: ChaingeFinance second arbitrary-call allowance drain
incidents.summary: MinterProxyV2.swap() accepted a caller-selected target and calldata. By supplying a fake input/output token that satisfied the router's balance checks, the attacker made the approved router call transferFrom(victim, attacker, amount) on 29 real token contracts.

loss.notes: The receipt contains 29 direct transfers from victim 0x8a4aa176007196d48d39c89402d3753c39ae64c1 to attacker EOA 0xacdbe7b770a14ca3bc34865ac3986c0ce771fd68. Exact token quantities are valued with DefiLlama observations from 1713184001 through 1713184292, all before the exploit at 1713184439. Eight Binance-bridged assets without address-level quotes use the corresponding CoinGecko underlying identifiers in the same response. This $133,020.54221111373 measurement covers only this second attacker cluster; the three earlier transactions by a different attacker are a separate campaign and are not included.

incidents.name: AROS claim flow zeroed its own AMM pair reserve
incidents.summary: The AROS token's claim flow pays users out of the project's own PancakeSwap V2 AROS/USDT pair and then force-syncs it: claimPrincipal calls _pullFromLP and claimYield calls _drainFromLPTo three times, each moving AROS out of lpPair, and both end with IUniswapV2Pair.sync(). Nothing floors the remaining reserve. Holding an ordinary claim signature for 910,060.523010163297636200 AROS, the attacker first bought the pair down to exactly that balance with 206,410,902.218 flash-loaned USDT (routing the purchased AROS to the whitelisted feeRecipient so the tradingRestricted (R1) hook let the outflow through), then executed the two claims. The trailing sync() wrote the pair's AROS reserve to zero, so PancakeV2 swap()'s invariant check balance0Adjusted*balance1Adjusted >= reserve0*reserve1*1e6 degenerated to >= 0 and 729,507.137147434919290830 AROS bought the pair's entire 206,712,181.771544840545053791 USDT balance.

loss.notes: Victim depletion is measured on the AROS/USDT PancakeSwap V2 pair 0x3104d26ae74b49eec61675a873b38414329c5edd. Its USDT balance fell from 301279.552818728952544597 to 0.000002841360035403 across the single exploit transaction, so 301279.552815887592509194 USDT left the pair; USDT on BSC is valued at par. The attacker's own 206410902.218537 USDT purchase leg and the flash-loan principals from Moolah, Venus, Aave and Balancer are attacker-supplied inputs and are netted out, and the flash-loan fees that reduced his realised take to 295314.043814755023404189 USDT do not reduce gross depletion. The pair also lost 622117209.361571546199176230 AROS (622846716.498718981118467060 to 729507.137147434919290830), almost all of it forwarded to the AROS feeRecipient 0xecbf62c834a09559ffd044a75f4e46e53df62eed; that leg is left unvalued because this pair was AROS's only market and the same transaction destroyed it, so no pre-attack spot price was realisable for that quantity.

incidents.name: edel-xStock mutable ERC-4626 share-rate oracle
incidents.summary: The wGOOGLx price source multiplied an independent stock price by wGOOGLx's same-transaction convertToAssets rate, so an underlying donation could atomically inflate collateral value and support reserve borrowing.

loss.notes: The seven lending reserve holders lose exactly 204,215.572188 USDC, 1.414889025557658614 wGOOGLx, 122.196850288612833306 wSPYx, 62.969726160938091585 wQQQx, 293.123092617121394703 wMSTRx, 99.854367795581762710 wNVDAx, and 37.589277017463227843 wTSLAx. Every archive balance falls from that exact amount to zero. The USDC reserve receives 180,000 flash-financed USDC and sends 384,215.572188, so the financing input and return cancel to the declared net depletion. Repeated wGOOGLx borrows and supplies, plus their eToken and debt-token representations, cancel inside the lending system; only the final 1.414889025557658614 wGOOGLx reserve outflow remains. It is redeemed and its underlying is donated to the wrapper, which capitalizes the borrower's retained collateral claim but does not return an asset to the lending reserves. The five other wrapped-stock reserves transfer directly to the attacker. Independently preceding DefiLlama observations value all six non-stables 686 seconds before the receipt. Exact decimal multiplication totals $406,564.79737383849000188598741420094817; the JSON number is its nearest IEEE-754 representation. The seed's approximately $204,216 figure counted only USDC proceeds.

incidents.name: Sonne Finance
incidents.summary: The Compound-v2 exchange-rate calculation let a direct VELO donation inflate the value of two wei of soVELO in an almost-empty market, which the attacker used as collateral to borrow assets from other Sonne markets.

loss.notes: Sonne Finance reported an approximately $20 million gross loss from the coherent two-transaction donation-attack campaign. The report does not publish a complete asset-by-asset valuation ledger.

incidents.name: Lodestar GLPOracle donatable plvGLP exchange rate
incidents.summary: Lodestar's GLPOracle.getPlutusExchangeRate() prices plvGLP as plvGLP.totalAssets() * 1e18 / plvGLP.totalSupply(), an instantaneous read of an ERC-4626 vault whose totalAssets() is the vault's plsGLP balance. Any transfer of plsGLP into the vault raises the numerator without minting shares, and getPlvGLPPrice() multiplies that ratio by the GLP price with no moving average, deviation bound, or same-block change guard. Within one transaction the attacker donated 5,620,813.918834889782579953 plsGLP into the vault, lifting the rate from 1.079668824382448539 to 1.822433552033092528, and PriceOracleProxyETH.getUnderlyingPrice(lplvGLP) relayed the inflated price to the Compound-fork Comptroller, letting a looped plvGLP position borrow out every other Lodestar market.

loss.notes: Components are the exact net underlying depletion of Lodestar's Compound-fork markets, summed from the Transfer logs of the four campaign transactions (the anchor plus 0xa9a12d1f, 0xb91ef85f and 0x752547f7, which took the lMAGIC and lDPX markets). Attacker deposits are already netted: in the anchor the lUSDC market pays out 71,775,069.474207 USDC.e against 70,096,512.99552 supplied back by the attacker, and the lplvGLP market pays out 64,845,499.745667204 plvGLP against 61,031,058.58415737 supplied back, leaving the 1,678,556.478687 USDC.e and 3,814,441.161509835687601554 plvGLP recorded here. Every market except lLODE was left at exactly its 10-unit seed dust. Native ETH is the lETH market's balance change from 124.693719452169514630 to 0.1. plvGLP has no DefiLlama observation; it is valued at 0.917512181012688097 USD, the value Lodestar's own GLPOracle.getPlvGLPPrice() returned at block 45121903, i.e. before the donation inflated the rate to 1.548720260621492204. All other assets use DefiLlama historical prices at the anchor timestamp. PlutusDAO later returned about 2.72 million GLP that the attacker had stranded in the plvGLP vault, and 750,000 LODE was distributed to affected wallets; per methodology those recoveries do not reduce gross depletion. Reported figures range from 5.8 to 7 million USD, with CertiK giving about 6.5 million attacker profit and DefiLlama 6.9 million; the reconstruction here is larger mainly because it counts the plvGLP at pre-attack net asset value and includes the later lMAGIC and lDPX drains.

incidents.name: OneRing OShare vault share price from spot strategy valuation
incidents.summary: The OShare vault implementation prices its shares from IStrategyManager.investedBalanceInUSD(), an aggregate mark that each MasterChef strategy derives from the live token balances of the stable pools it farms via getUSDBalanceFromUnderlyingBalance(). depositSafe() reads that mark before pulling the deposit, routes the deposit into the same pools through assetToUnderlying(), and mints shares from the USD figure the strategies report after the pools have moved; withdraw() reads the same mark again and then settles by removing the caller's pro-rata share of the strategies' LP positions. Both legs of a deposit-then-withdraw round trip therefore read a quantity the deposit itself controls inside one transaction. With an 80,000,000 USDC Solidly flash loan the attacker deposited 79,999,997 USDC into a vault whose pre-deposit mark was 4,448,686.168049134972760253 USD on 4,185,979.962653993796224466 shares, was credited an under-reported 44,599,205.960575506514590319 USD and minted 41,965,509.691846094312718922 shares, and then burned them for 47,696,475.292371545217068603 marked USD which settled as 81,534,750.101089 USDC out of the still-imbalanced pools. Boundary test: the mark is read unconditionally in the executed deposit and withdraw paths with no time average, invariant-based valuation or deviation bound, and the only caller-facing guard is the depositor's own _minAmount argument, so no configured value makes the deployed code correct.

loss.notes: Exact victim depletion from the anchor receipt's USDC Transfer logs. The vault and its five strategies received 79,999,997 USDC from the attacker and paid 81,534,750.101089 USDC back to it, a net 1,534,753.101089 USDC funded out of the pre-existing OneRing LP positions: against the three farmed pools the strategy set is net positive by 437,413.252303, 839,621.868989 and 257,678.197053 USDC and collects 39.782744 USDC of harvested rewards, which sums to the same 1,534,753.101089. The attacker-supplied 80,000,000 USDC Solidly flash-loan principal is netted inside the same measurement and is not counted as loss; the 80,080.080081 USDC flash-loan fee is a financing cost that does not reduce gross victim depletion, so the attacker's own retained proceeds are the smaller 1,454,672.244369 USDC that the commonly reported 1.45 million figure describes. As corroboration the strategy manager's investedBalanceInUSD() falls from 4,448,686.168141524586181482 to 2,806,491.940626862259327592 across the exploit block, a 1,642,194.227514662326853890 USD drop, but that mark is itself spot-derived and still reflects the imbalance the attack left in the pools, so the receipt-derived USDC figure is used. USDC is valued at par.

incidents.name: Astrid unvalidated restaked-token withdrawal
incidents.summary: AstridProtocol.withdraw accepted any caller-supplied restaked-token contract without requiring it to match a whitelisted stakedTokens entry. Fake tokens reported attacker-chosen stakedTokenAddress and scaledBalanceToBalance values, so withdrawal processing recorded the protocol's real stETH, rETH and cbETH reserves as claimable and claim transferred them to the attacker.

loss.notes: The receipt shows 64.176037513415148812 stETH, 39.165842900855519099 rETH and 20.000407064566313222 cbETH leaving Astrid. The attack contract liquidated all three inside its constructor and forwarded exactly 127.797499079942863577 ETH to the attacker EOA. At the nearest pre-incident DefiLlama ETH price of 1,789.94 USD, those exact realised proceeds are worth 228,749.85550315292923101538 USD. Gas is not deducted and no recovery is netted.

incidents.name: Value DeFi MultiStables vault share value from manipulable Curve 3pool quote
incidents.summary: MultiStablesVault prices a share against IMultiVaultController.balanceOf(3CRV, _sell), which converts every non-3CRV strategy holding through ShareConverter.convert_shares_rate. That function quotes the holding as StableSwap3Pool.calc_token_amount([0, usdc, 0], true), a spot, fee-free, single-transaction-manipulable pool quantity. Because mint uses balance() before the transfer and redemption uses balance_to_sell() computed at the same instant, an attacker who deposits, imbalances the Curve 3pool and redeems inside one transaction is paid at an inflated share price. In the anchor the identical BUSD-pool holding of 1,988,683.965709684903991584 BCrv quoted 2,100,754.566072978362359769 3CRV before the imbalance and 11,140,592.572211842856711915 3CRV after it, so 24,923,202.990614843737795018 shares redeemed for 33,089,069.045892566308558644 3CRV. withdrawFor carries no contract-depositor guard at all, and the deposit-side checkContract guard was satisfied because the whitelisted ValueVaultBank 0x8764f2c305b79680cfcc3398a96aedea9260f7ff forwards any caller's deposit.

loss.notes: Exact victim depletion measured as the change in 3CRV backing the vault across the single exploit block. Immediately before block 11256673 the vault proxy held 15,481.012004745341988972 3CRV and its Curve 3pool strategy 0x467e9f2caa9b7678ddc29b248cb9fb181907bf3e held 8,907,642.635740816269236890 3CRV in gauge 0xbfcf63294ad7105dea65aa58f8ae5be2d9d0952a, a total of 8,923,123.647745561611225862 3CRV; immediately after, the totals are 0 and 790,129.681897256182811860 3CRV. Vault share totalSupply is unchanged at 11,306,867.172450486840394244 because the attacker burned exactly the shares it minted, and the BUSD-pool and sUSD-pool strategy holdings are unchanged, so the entire delta of 8,132,993.965848305428414002 3CRV is uncompensated depletion. The attacker's own 25,000,000 DAI deposit is an attacker-supplied input and is already netted out by this measurement, as is the 24,956,075.080044260880144642 3CRV the vault received for it. The attacker's realised proceeds were smaller than the depletion: 5,410,161.951405400704050092 DAI was sent to the attacker EOA and 2,000,000 DAI was sent back to Value DeFi deployer 0x7be4d5a99c903c437ec77a20cb6d0688cbb73c7f inside the same transaction, with the remaining difference consumed by Curve and Uniswap slippage and the 72 ETH Aave flash-loan fee. Under the gross-depletion rule the same-transaction 2,000,000 DAI return is a recovery and does not reduce this figure; Value DeFi's post-mortem quotes roughly 6,000,000 USD, which is this depletion net of that return. 3Crv is valued at the DefiLlama observation nearest the exploit, 1.0043459842762914 USD, which matches the pool's own pre-exploit get_virtual_price of 1.004346861769940042.

incidents.name: BTC24H Lock claim() without beneficiary check
incidents.summary: The BTC24H token Lock 0x968e1c98 holds the owner's 110,000 BTC24H until releaseDate 1734220800, but claim() is guarded only by onlyOnOrAfter(releaseDate) and the claimed flag: it has no onlyOwner or beneficiary check and pays claims.amount to msg.sender. About 41.5 hours after release, before the owner claimed, the attacker contract called claim(), received all 110,000 BTC24H and sold them through the Uniswap universal router for 4,953.29 USDT and 0.76433089 WBTC.

loss.notes: Exact victim depletion: the Lock's entire 110000 BTC24H balance (its only inflow was the owner's deposit) moved to the attack contract in receipt log 0. The attacker sold all of it in the same transaction into two thin Uniswap V3 pools, so BTC24H has no reliable spot quote (none on DefiLlama) and is valued at realised proceeds: 10000 BTC24H for 4953.287533 USDT (log 2), valued at par, and 100000 BTC24H for 0.76433089 WBTC (log 6), valued at the DefiLlama WBTC quote 106541 (source-6). Both proceeds went straight to the attacker EOA. No attacker input exists.

incidents.name: MonoX Monoswap self-swap price inflation
incidents.summary: Monoswap's swap path never rejected tokenIn == tokenOut and updated the tokenIn price before the tokenOut price, so repeatedly swapping MONO for MONO ratcheted MONO's recorded price up until the attacker could buy out the pools' other assets.

loss.notes: SlowMist reports more than $31 million lost across the Ethereum and Polygon executions of the same self-swap price-inflation defect. The seven structured components reproduce $12.13 million of exact Ethereum MonoXPool outflows in the code-age anchor transaction and provide an onchain cross-check.

incidents.name: DKP exchange live-pair valuation
incidents.summary: The direct DKP exchange valued its DKP inventory from the configured pair's live token balances. A two-receipt campaign caused the exchange to release DKP at a transient balance ratio and then removed canonical USDT from the same pair.

loss.notes: The canonical 18-decimal BSC USDT balance of pair 0xbe654 falls from 259,605.445236391899433885 before source-1 to 181,045.896092434246591772 after source-2. Receipt arithmetic agrees: source-1 sends 259,390 USDT to the helper, receives the 259,390 principal plus a 674.414 fee, and source-2 sends 79,233.963143957652842113 USDT to the EOA, for exact pair depletion of 78,559.549143957652842113 USDT. The helper also pays 100 USDT through 0xb24fc to constructor-fixed specifyusdtAddr 0xb6df; that address is the DKP protocol's recurring exchange-revenue and distribution account and retains the amount, so entity-level loss is 78,459.549143957652842113 USDT. DKP moves internally across the harmed entity set: exchange -17,115.243270155346986000, pair +16,178.183701114341738517, DKP token fee inventory +851.483352690228512552, and constructor-fixed connectionAddr +85.576216350776734930. Their one-wei shortfall is the token's integer fee truncation, not attacker-held consideration; helper DKP starts and ends at zero. At the pre-incident block, pair total supply is 97,597.498194969607267275 LP: owner-linked UsdtTokenPool holds 68,040.736000000000010000 (69.7156558911%), constructor-bound lpAddress holds 28,714.702564796886292017 (29.4215559782%), and the other 230 holders jointly hold 842.059630172720965258 (0.8627881305%). The pair inventory therefore represents the complete LP-holder victim set while the exchange, token-fee inventory and fixed revenue recipients conserve internal DKP. Source-3 bounds EOA nonces 131-139: helper creation, 932.745305403783296414-USDT funding, the two incident receipts, downstream approval and disposal of 78,000 USDT, and withdrawal of the helper's remaining 158.331305403783296414 USDT to the EOA. No later DKP or USDT returns to the exchange, pair or protocol recipients occur in the same-day actor/helper scan.

incidents.name: MIC public swapManual()
incidents.summary: MIC's unrestricted swapManual() paid LP fees according only to msg.sender's current LP-token balance and reduced a global fee pool without recording which LP position had already claimed. Transferring the same LP position between addresses therefore allowed repeated claims against the remaining accrued fees.

loss.notes: Exact pre-recovery depletion of the accrued LP-fee allocation is the sum of eleven swapAndSendLPFeeEvent amounts: 178.988781874161943857 MIC. The pre-transaction PancakeSwap V2 MIC/BSC-USD pool held 1,774,999.9281271318376792 BSC-USD and 88,921.274156593938885675 MIC, implying $19.961476541612367 per MIC at stablecoin par and $3,572.8803705928563 gross loss. The fee swaps paid 2,445.239989071637839369 BSC-USD to attacker-controlled callers after execution slippage. Flash liquidity and the attacker's trading inputs are excluded. The migrated approximately $500,000 estimate is not retained because it does not reconcile with the exact fee events, pool state, or stablecoin payouts.

incidents.name: Zoomer buyback spot-price accounting
incidents.summary: The buyback contract valued incoming ZOOMER at the current pool spot price, allowing one transaction to exchange attacker-supplied tokens for most of the contract's ETH inventory.

loss.notes: Within the sole loss receipt, the buyback sends 17.248371112617906458 ETH in five calls and receives five 0.02 ETH inputs, so gross victim depletion net of external input is 17.248371112617906458 - 0.1 = 17.148371112617906458 ETH. Its archive balance falls by exactly the same amount, from 17.300097602045297868 to 0.151726489427391410 ETH. It receives and retains 145,108,836 ZOOMER (four transfers of 30,265,400 plus one of 24,047,236), exactly matching its archive token increase; that attacker-supplied consideration is not a victim asset loss. The 90-second-preceding ETH price is 2,927.14 USD.

incidents.name: Umbrella StakingRewards unchecked withdrawal accounting
incidents.summary: StakingRewards.withdraw() subtracted the caller-supplied amount from total supply and the caller's zero balance without checked arithmetic. Under Solidity 0.7 the values wrapped instead of reverting, so an unstaked caller could withdraw the pool's entire UNI-V2 balance.

loss.notes: The selected Ethereum transaction transfers the target's exact entire balance of 8,792.873290680252648282 UMB/WETH UNI-V2 tokens. USD is immediate pre-transaction pool NAV: the stolen share represented 2,235,385.212219056057355257 UMB and 92.244534420912291405 WETH; both reserve sides are marked at the pool spot ratio and WETH uses the incident-time price.

incidents.name: FoxLpBondsPool pre-swap spot pricing over-mints FOX
incidents.summary: stake() prices the entire USDT bond from the FOX/USDT pair before swapping half of that same deposit through the shallow pair. It then mints FOX-denominated bond and referral inventory from the stale pre-swap quote. One financed call minted endogenous FOX and sold it back into the pair, depleting its liquid USDT reserve.

loss.notes: The FOX/USDT pair 0xaab18bcdee287aea288c0560612caadf7c328803 sent 482652334.587313528253588625 USDT and received 240987392.768398210827166510 plus 240987392.768398210827166511 USDT in the loss receipt, so its gross scarce-asset depletion is 677549.050517106599255604 USDT. Archive balances agree exactly: 2786697.198864505157273333 before and 2109148.148347398558017729 after the block; no other transaction in the block touches the pair's USDT or FOX. The pair received net 2108546.337965754947092948 FOX, principally from FOX minted during the same call, so that endogenous inventory is consideration but not an independently scarce loss offset. Thirty-one external financing pools supplied 481974785.536796421654333021 USDT and received 482539358.468560385626356388, an aggregate 564572.931763963972023367-USDT gain outside the Fox victim entity. The attacker retained 112976.118753142627232237 USDT, explaining the smaller proceeds-based seed figure. The canonical BNB Chain bridge list identifies this 18-decimal contract as BSC USDT; DefiLlama observed $0.9984824445632876 nine seconds before the receipt. Exact decimal multiplication is $676520.8322718550395813237978550269637104.

incidents.name: ULME arbitrary approved-user spending
incidents.summary: buyMiner(user, usdt) was public and passed its caller-supplied user directly to USDT.transferFrom without requiring user == msg.sender or another authorization. The attacker invoked it for 100 holders who had approved ULME, forcing their USDT through the ULME/USDT pair while sandwiching those trades.

loss.notes: The exploit receipt contains 100 USDT transfers from distinct approved users to ULME totaling 250,817.770742650963321153 USDT, followed by the same total from ULME to the pair. The users received no asset in return. The pair's 200,170.825418687386914428 USDT transaction-local net inflow and the attacker's roughly $50,000 sandwich profit are consequences of these forced trades, not alternative measures of the users' gross loss.

incidents.name: EvoDeFi MasterChef updatePower raises power without settling rewardDebt
incidents.summary: MasterChef.updatePower(pid) is public and recomputes user.power from the staked amount and the caller's current NFT/proxy bonus without paying pending rewards or resetting rewardDebt. A staker whose bonus rises can call updatePower and the next claim pays the new power times the whole accumulated reward per power minus the old debt. The first exercise (April 2021, a staker whose bonus rose 9%) paid about 0.0039 GEN extra; on 2021-06-10 an attacker flash-borrowed GEN, and six helper contracts each deposited, raised their NFT bonus, called updatePower and withdrew, draining 456,262 GEN from the MasterChef.

loss.notes: Net GEN depletion of the MasterChef in the 2021-06-10 transaction source-2 (other stakers' deposits and reward reserves). Valued at the attacker's realised sale price: 455,576.854326181275474802 GEN sold in 21 transactions (blocks 8169292..8169627) returned 334,616.733764492976012720 BUSD from the GEN/BUSD pair and 421.633957188326703176 WBNB from the GEN/WBNB pair (WBNB at 365.646 USD), about 1.07 USD per GEN; the sale drove GEN from about 2.1 USD down, so this is a lower bound (reported loss about 1,000,000 USD). The April anchor sequence paid about 0.0039 GEN of unearned reward (source-9), which is not added.

incidents.name: Onyx Protocol empty-market rounding
incidents.summary: The freshly listed oPEPE market could be redeemed down to two wei of supply, while direct PEPE transfers increased cash without minting shares. This inflated the exchange rate used for collateral, and redeemUnderlying's integer division then burned only one wei to recover the donation, allowing the attacker to borrow the other Onyx markets nearly empty and recycle the manipulated collateral.

loss.notes: MetaTrust reports approximately 1,156.9 ETH-equivalent ($2.088 million) from the anchor transaction and another $60,000 of MATIC, UNI, APE, USDP, and WETH in the follow-up transaction, for approximately $2.14 million gross across the incident. The structured WETH component records the anchor transaction's post-swap profit; exact per-token amounts for the follow-up are not published.

incidents.name: GROK token pair-balance accounting
incidents.summary: GROK's transfer logic let the attacker shrink the Uniswap V3 pool's own GROK balance during a flash swap, so the position could be closed against a manipulated pool balance and the pool's WETH extracted.

loss.notes: After the 30 WETH Uniswap V3 flash loan and 0.003 WETH fee were repaid, the trace records exactly 26.382963431285374891 ETH transferred from the attack helper to the attacker EOA. Transaction gas is excluded.

incidents.name: BH farm redeems LP from the pair's spot token balances
incidents.summary: The BH farm 0x8ca7835aa30b025b38a59309dd1479d2f452623a holds the protocol's whole BUSDT/BH PancakeSwap LP position and lets anyone redeem it by burning BH. Its withdraw function 0x4e290832(uint256 bhAmount) burns the caller's BH and then computes the LP it removes as bhAmount * sqrt(BUSDT.balanceOf(pair) * BH.balanceOf(pair)) / BH.balanceOf(pair), i.e. it derives the redemption share from the pair's live token balances instead of from its own share ledger. Both balances are freely movable by the caller inside the same transaction. The attacker pushed 22,000,000 flash-loaned BUSDT through the pair, cutting BH.balanceOf(pair) from 251,272,454 to 42,011,431 and raising BUSDT.balanceOf(pair) from 4,405,698 to 26,405,698, and then called the withdraw function ten times, each time redeeming ~55% of the whole LP position for BH that was worth a fraction of it, until the pair held 47,126 BUSDT.

loss.notes: The BUSDT/BH PancakeSwap pair 0x2371e4ad771020ce3d8252f1db3e5559fba8eeb5 holds 1393467.010169397021655925 BUSDT at block 32512073 and 47126.187809646349435225 BUSDT at block 32512074; the 1346340.822359750672220700 BUSDT difference is the loss, and the farm 0x8ca7835aa30b025b38a59309dd1479d2f452623a held 13628344.132032127262454971 of the pair's 13630848.563049281529836047 LP tokens (99.98%) before the exploit. The outflow reconciles exactly: 1275981.822359750672220700 BUSDT to the attacker EOA 0xfdbfceea1de360364084a6f37c9cdb7aaea63464, 60000 BUSDT of PancakeSwap V2 flash-swap fee to 0x16b9a82891338f9ba80e2d6970fdda79d1eb0dae, 9000 BUSDT of PancakeSwap V3 flash fee to 0x4f31fa980a675570939b737ebdde0471a4be40eb, and 1359 BUSDT to the project's own fee contract 0xc9fc938bcf691affa79c9fec3d1719f6297fa20e. The widely reported ~$1.27M is the attacker EOA's net take alone. All of it is in the single exploit transaction; the DODO flash loans that funded it were repaid interest-free in the same transaction. BUSDT (BSC-USD) is valued at par; DefiLlama has no bsc:0x55d398326f99059ff775485246999027b3197955 observation at this timestamp and prices Tether at 0.999384 at the nearest observation 1697033700. The residual BH left in the pair is not counted. Nothing was recovered.

incidents.name: MoonHacker vault unauthenticated Aave flash-loan callback
incidents.summary: MoonHacker.executeOperation, the Aave V3 flash-loan callback of each MoonHacker leverage vault, is declared external with no check that msg.sender is the Aave pool and no check that initiator is the vault, and it takes the money-market address out of the caller-supplied params blob. Any address can therefore call it directly: with SmartOperation.REDEEM and mToken set to the real Moonwell mUSDC market the vault repays its own borrow with USDC the caller pushed in and redeems its entire collateral, and with SmartOperation.SUPPLY and mToken set to an attacker contract whose mint() and borrow() return 0 the vault executes IERC20(token).approve(mToken, amountBorrowed + amountToSupplyOrReedem), handing the caller an allowance over the redeemed balance, which the caller then pulls with transferFrom.

loss.notes: Single-transaction campaign. From the USDC Transfer logs of the anchor transaction, three of the four vaults held a position: 0xd9b45e2c389b6ad55dd3631abc1de6f2d2229847 received 485,984.781792 USDC to clear its Moonwell borrow and gave up 595,813.435803 USDC of redeemed collateral; 0x24592ed1ccf9e5ae235e24a932b378891313fb75 received 43,831.723102 and gave up 53,721.818789; 0x80472c6848015146fdc3d15cdf6dc11ca3cb3513 received 883,978.188337 and gave up 1,083,688.969991; 0xce5e0e2bcf40a049a6e148f411a19419d0443607 was empty and moved 0. The 1,413,794.693231 USDC used to repay the vaults' debts came from the attacker's 883,917.967954 USDC Aave flash loan recycled across the vaults and is an attacker-supplied campaign input, so it is excluded rather than counted as depletion; the vault owners' destroyed equity is 1,733,224.224583 minus 1,413,794.693231 = 319,429.531352 USDC. The 441.958984 USDC Aave premium is a financing fee and is not deducted: the attacker ended the transaction with 318,987.572368 USDC. No recovery reduced this figure. The attacker swapped the proceeds to 319,206.5985 DAI in the next block and bridged them out through the Across SpokePool 0x6f26bf09b1c792e3228e5467807a900a503c0281 on 2025-01-27, having sent 'whitehat here, please contact me' messages to the three vault owners on 2024-12-24.

incidents.name: Carson custom pair sell-side reserve burn
incidents.summary: The closed-source Carson/USDT pair, after each swap's constant-product check, transfers a factory-configured share of the input token out of its own balance and then syncs. Its factory configured 30% to 0xdead plus 30% to a fee wallet for Carson input, so every sell removed 60% of the sold Carson from reserves and cut k by about 6.7%. The attacker bought Carson with flash-loaned USDT and sold it back in 51 chunks, draining the pair's USDT.

loss.notes: Net USDT debit of pair 0xe0a3e0f7e4c789747eb29a212ea915a7a1e1ac69 across the four successful attacker calls to 0x9cffc95e742d22c1446a3d22e656bb23835a38ac: USDT sent out of the pair minus the flash-loaned USDT the attacker swapped in. The pair's concurrent loss of 411,566.919752722008226380 Carson (part burned to 0xdead, part to the fee wallet, rest bought back by the attacker and resold) is not valued: the drained pair was that token's market, so its value is endogenous to the USDT reserve counted here. DeFiHackLabs reports ~150K USD.

incidents.name: dTRINITY dLEND empty cbBTC reserve liquidity-index inflation
incidents.summary: dLEND, an Aave v3 fork, listed cbBTC as flash-loanable collateral (LTV 73%) with no supply. The attacker left one scaled share in the empty reserve, donated cbBTC to the aToken and ran 150 flash loans whose premiums, spread over that single share, raised the cbBTC liquidity index from 1e27 to 6.2e33. At that index deposit/withdraw rounding let it keep aToken collateral while withdrawing its cbBTC, and two blocks later it borrowed the entire dUSD reserve against the phantom collateral.

loss.notes: Exact dUSD depletion of the dLEND dUSD reserve (aToken 0x5cc741931d01cb1adde193222dfb1ad75930fd60) in the profit transaction, borrowed against cbBTC collateral that has no backing and never repaid. The cbBTC reserve held no third-party funds: the index transaction and the profit transaction return all flash-loaned and deposited cbBTC to the attacker, so no cbBTC component is added. dUSD is valued at the DefiLlama quote nearest the profit transaction.

incidents.name: bZx Fulcrum ETHDenver flash-loan margin trade
incidents.summary: iTokens_loanOpeningFunctions.takeOrderFromiToken guarded the collateral check with a short-circuiting OR - require((loanDataBytes.length == 0 && sentAmounts[6] == sentAmounts[1]) || !OracleInterface(oracle).shouldLiquidate(...)) - so with empty loanDataBytes the left operand was true and shouldLiquidate() was never called, letting a 5x short open against the iETH pool that was instantly underwater after 5,637 ETH was swapped into 51 WBTC on Uniswap V1.

loss.notes: The 1,193 ETH amount is the attacker's realized net profit after unwinding the Compound position. The earlier 1,271 ETH estimate valued that position before the unwind.

incidents.name: BXH TokenStakingPoolDelegate pays USDT bonus at the live BXH/USDT spot quote
incidents.summary: TokenStakingPoolDelegate converts a staker's pending BXH reward into the pool's USDT bonus token with getITokenBonusAmount, which applies the constant-product formula to the BXH/USDT pair's live getReserves and pays the result from the contract's USDT balance. The attacker flash-borrowed 3.18M USDT, bought BXH to inflate the pair's USDT per BXH, then harvested about 15 BXH of pending reward from a prior vUSDT stake as 40,085.62 USDT, draining the bonus balance.

loss.notes: Net USDT depletion of the staking contract in the anchor: 40,085.623577085020521681 USDT paid out minus the 200 USDT the attack contract sent in first so the balance covered the payout. USDT (BSC-peg) valued at par. The honest value of the harvested reward at the pre-attack reserve ratio was about 2.6 USDT and is not deducted. The PancakeSwap flash-loan fee and the round-trip swap cost are attacker costs and are not netted.

incidents.name: APC TransSwap swaps inventory at the live APC/USDT spot quote
incidents.summary: The TransSwap proxy's swap(tokenA, tokenB, amount) prices APC against MUSD from the APC/USDT PancakeSwap pair's live reserves (getReserves then router getAmountOut of 1 APC) and pays the output from its own inventory. A flash-loan buy pumped APC, the attacker swapped APC into MUSD at the inflated quote, dumped APC, swapped the MUSD back into more APC at the depressed quote and sold it, draining TransSwap's APC inventory in two transactions.

loss.notes: Gross depletion of the TransSwap proxy's APC inventory in the two campaign transactions; its MUSD leg nets to zero in each. Each component is valued at what the attacker realised selling it into the APC/USDT pair: the pair's net USDT outflow in that transaction, with USDT at par. The attackers' own dumping moved APC from a pre-attack spot of about 0.789 USDT, so spot-marking the drained APC is not used. DODO flash-loan fees (3,600 and 1,500 USDT) are financing costs and are not deducted; attacker EOAs netted 40,477.142 and 6,126.987 USDT. The second transaction was sent by a different EOA and contract 2,471 seconds later against the same implementation, before the proxy was upgraded.

incidents.name: Harvest Finance Vault share price from manipulable Curve y-pool mark
incidents.summary: The Harvest Vault implementation 0x9b3be0cc5dd26fd0254088d03d8206792715588b, shared by the fUSDC and fUSDT vault proxies, converts between shares and underlying at both ends using underlyingBalanceWithInvestment(), which is underlyingBalanceInVault() plus IStrategy(strategy()).investedUnderlyingBalance(). For the CRVStrategyStableMainnet strategies that number is the strategy's yCRV position marked through IPriceConvertor.yCrvToUnderlying, i.e. the Curve yDAI/yUSDC/yUSDT/yTUSD pool's instantaneous calc_withdraw_one_coin. _deposit therefore mints amount.mul(totalSupply()).div(underlyingBalanceWithInvestment()) and withdraw pays underlyingBalanceWithInvestment().mul(numberOfShares).div(totalSupply) off a quantity any caller can move inside a single transaction by swapping through that pool. The only mitigation is the strategy's depositArbCheck(), which compares the same manipulable mark against curvePriceCheckpoint, a lagged copy of itself refreshed at doHardWork, with a three percent arbTolerance; withdraw() consults no check at all, so no value of arbTolerance makes the deployed code correct and the defect is not a parameter choice. Inside each of thirty transactions the attacker flash-swapped USDC and USDT out of Uniswap V2, pushed the y-pool off balance so the vault's underlying mark fell, deposited to mint shares at the depressed price, restored the pool and withdrew at the recovered price, repeating seventeen rounds against fUSDC and thirteen against fUSDT.

loss.notes: Exact victim depletion, obtained by netting every ERC-20 Transfer log across the thirty-two campaign transactions in source-5: the fUSDC vault 0xf0358e8c3cd5fa238a29301d0bea3d63a17bedbe ends 18,636,750.636105 USDC lighter and the fUSDT vault 0x053c80ea73dc6941f518a68e2fc52ac45bde7c9c ends 14,975,169.350940 USDT lighter. Attacker-supplied inputs are the Uniswap V2 flash swaps, which are repaid inside each transaction and therefore net to zero. Of that depletion the attacker forwarded exactly 13,000,000 USDC and 11,000,000 USDT to 0x3811765a53c3188c24d412daec3f60faad5f119b, which is the 24 million USD figure most reporting quotes, and returned 1,761,898.396474 USDC and 718,914.048541 USDT (2,480,812.44 USD) to the Harvest deployer 0xf00dd244228f51547f0563e60bca65a30fbf5f7f in the same campaign. The remaining roughly 7.1 million USD was consumed by Curve y-pool imbalance fees and Uniswap swap fees and accrued to those pools' other liquidity providers; per methodology neither the financing costs nor the partial return reduces gross victim depletion, so the total is 33,611,919.99 USD, consistent with the 33.8 million USD figure Harvest published. Both stablecoins are valued at par.

incidents.name: Unnamed Base Compound fork uSUI slot0 spot price feed
incidents.summary: The price feed the fork's oracle 0x93d619623abc60a22ee71a15db62eede3ef4dd5a serves for market cSUI is the immutable adapter 0xc112e41c1094ff7fbf9e5dc0d1026103542e7e0c. Its latestAnswer() reads the instantaneous slot0().sqrtPriceX96 of Uniswap-V3-style pool 0x5c45b0f48c326f79b56709d8f63ce2bee7697106 and returns chainlinkEthUsd * 2**192 / sqrtPriceX96**2, reproduced to the unit in the anchor trace: 253253757616 * 2**192 / 2858318274747956646160580417568**2 = 194578070. The runtime contains the slot0 selector and no observe/observations selector, so there is no time-weighted observation, no minimum-liquidity floor, no deviation cap against the previous answer and no staleness bound; the only bound in the code clamps the ratio at 1e16, sixteen orders of magnitude above any plausible uSUI price. One 500 WETH exactInputSingle into the pool inside the same transaction drove sqrtPriceX96 from 2858318274747956646160580417568 to the 1e21 limit, lifting getUnderlyingPrice(cSUI) from 1.9457807e18 to 2.5325375761e37, after which 50 uSUI of collateral supported borrowing every market of the fork to zero. No parameter value makes this code correct: the priced token, the Chainlink ETH/USD wrapper and the pool address are storage configuration, but an unaveraged slot0 read is manipulable under every configuration of them.

loss.notes: Every component is the exact pre-exploit underlying balance of one cToken market of the fork, taken from eth_call at block 21512062 and confirmed zero at block 21512063; all fourteen markets were emptied inside the anchor transaction. The 15 WETH the attacker minted into cWETH from its 800 WETH Morpho flash loan is an attacker-supplied campaign input and is excluded, so the WETH component is the 247.435971398571237348 WETH the market held before the mint rather than the 262.435971398571237348 WETH borrowed. The 50 uSUI deposited as the inflated collateral is likewise excluded, so the uSUI component is 13982.866550395379924780 minus 50. uSUI is valued at realised proceeds because the attacker's own swaps moved its price: the two Uniswap V3 swaps in the anchor transaction net exactly 13932.866550395379924780 uSUI into the pool and 8.618646200019168827 WETH out of it (357.947060332568731027 out minus 349.328414132549562200 in), which at 2533.49 USD/WETH is 21835.25 USD, or 1.5672 USD per uSUI against a 1.95 pre-manipulation mark. Every other component uses a DefiLlama price at the anchor timestamp, or par for USD+ and USDT. The marks are corroborated by the attacker's own disposals: the nine Universal Router sales in source-7 sent out precisely the drained quantities of USD+, Mog, DEGEN, cbBTC, wstETH, uSOL, MIGGLES, USDT and BRETT and returned 134.113530821806791107 ETH, which with the 256.054617598590495000 ETH unwrapped from the WETH proceeds totals 390.168148420397286107 ETH or 988487.10 USD - 0.10 percent below the 989451.69 USD marked here. USDz, WIF and PEPE were dust markets holding 6.9e-11, 5.3e-14 and 2.8e-17 tokens and contribute nothing. No recovery was identified. The seed row's 1,000,000 USD figure is a round report; this reconstruction supersedes it.

incidents.name: DEI lender Solidex LP oracle balance-based collateral valuation
incidents.summary: The deployed contract that computes the collateral price is the Solidex DEI/USDC LP oracle at 0x8129026c585bcfa530445a6267f9389057761a00, which DeiLenderSolidex 0x8d643d954798392403eea19db8108f595bb8b730 consults for every solvency decision. Its getOnChainPrice() (selector 0xbd2a9d2c) values one LP unit as (IERC20(USDC).balanceOf(pair) + IERC20(DEI).balanceOf(pair) * pair.getAmountOut(1e18, DEI)) / pair.totalSupply() against the Solidly stable pair 0x5821573d8f04947952e76d94f3abc6d7b43bf8d0, and getPrice() (selector 0x51a0fd38) accepts a Muon-signed price only after cross-checking it against that same quantity. Every input is the pair's instantaneous raw token balance, not a synced reserve, a cumulative-price observation, or an independent feed, so a plain token transfer into the pair inflates the price and the donation is recoverable in the same transaction. The oracle validates nothing about manipulability: no TWAP window, no reserve/balance reconciliation, no deviation bound, and no bound on how far the quote may move within one block. In the anchor transaction the attacker flash-borrowed roughly 143 million USDC from about twenty Solidly pairs, pushed the DEI/USDC pair from 9,965,063.905675 USDC and 9,556,010.307554660495240937 DEI to 153,146,534.178753 USDC and 5,045.910201204745134760 DEI, which lifted the oracle's LP unit price from 2,000,822.763556768631327287 to 20,936,736.548805047505034720 USD, and borrowed 17,246,885.701212305622476302 DEI against 0.929182265419947290 Solidex deposit tokens genuinely worth about 1.86 million USD. No parameter value makes this code correct: the pair, token and Muon-verifier addresses are configuration, but every configuration of them still prices the LP from balances the caller can move inside the transaction.

loss.notes: The anchor minted 17,246,885.701212305622476302 unbacked DEI to the attacker. Because that quantity is larger than the entire DEI/USDC pool and the attacker's own selling set the price, the loss is measured as realised proceeds rather than a spot mark on DEI: within 66 minutes the attacker sold 15,818,000 DEI into the Solidly pair 0x5821573d8f04947952e76d94f3abc6d7b43bf8d0 for 4,748,593.702757 + 4,258,677.329129 + 2,811,448.853343 + 1,928,951.245729 + 803,884.255646 = 14,551,555.386604 USDC, and redeemed 1,501,091.6098773733 DEI through the DEUS redemption contract 0x9bd5cc542bc922e95ba41c0702555e830f2c1cb4 for 792,000.0 + 396,864.555022 = 1,188,864.555022 USDC, a total of 15,740,419.941626 USDC valued at par. A 500,322.5909182056 DEI round trip through 0xfa9eacdc763500ba4ab6ba2bfcf154d5a4b19ed7 returned 495,601.431539 USDC against 496,363.193858 USDC sent and is excluded as a wash. Flash-loan fees of roughly 329,148.62 USDC paid to the lending Solidly pairs inside the anchor are financing cost and do not reduce gross depletion. The lender keeps the attacker's 0.929182265419947290 Solidex deposit tokens, worth 1,859,129.03 USD at the unmanipulated oracle price of 2,000,822.763556768631327287 USD per unit that the same oracle returned 43 minutes earlier in transaction 0xdb5c3a873ae601eeec0a83d015f90d6e58858945df31372cf940bad7ee20194a; that retained collateral is a recovery and is not netted here, which is why published estimates of about 13.0 to 13.4 million USD sit below this gross figure.

incidents.name: OSN LP dividend weights not reduced on LP transfer
incidents.summary: OSN's _transfer hook sets an account's LP-dividend weight only on router liquidity adds (lpAmount += estimated liquidity) and on liquidity removals, where it overwrites lpAmount with the recipient's full current pair-token balance and pushes it to the dividend tracker. Plain LP-token transfers never reduce the sender's weight. LP moved to another address that then makes a tiny add and remove is therefore counted twice, and one LP position can register full weight in any number of accounts. The first such duplication is a probe: 0xf003ffa9 sends 1 LP to 0x71940b72, which adds and then removes dust liquidity. The May 2024 campaign by 0x835b45 cycled flash-loaned LP through 100 helper contracts, withdrew the LP, generated taxed swaps and collected the dividends.

loss.notes: The attacker's realised net USDT: attack contract 0x4a5acac3 paid its EOA 109,682.365414208009944720 USDT across 16 campaign transactions, less the EOA's 10-USDT funding. All flash loans are repaid within each receipt, and the contract ends with zero USDT, OSN and LP. Every unit of that gain was extracted from third parties: pair LPs, drained by the tax sales that fund the tracker, and holders whose tracker dividends were diverted. Victim depletion is therefore at least this amount. The same receipts also pay the marketing wallet 0xea1f5740 and PancakeV3 flash fees, which are not added because gross third-party depletion cannot be separated from the attacker's own swap taxes. Excluded as unrealised or immaterial: 14.030326252660469 USDT of tracker dividends paid to the helper contracts after the campaign (to block 45000000), and at most 0.47 USDT of dividends to the probe addresses.

incidents.name: FH sell path burns the sold amount from the FH/USDT pair before the sale
incidents.summary: On a sale to the FH/USDT pair, FHToken._transfer burns 80% of the seller's after-fee amount from the pair's own balance, moves another 20% from the pair to the treasury, and calls sync() before the seller's tokens arrive. Buys are only allowed to whitelisted recipients, but the constructor whitelists PancakeSwap router 0x1b81d678ffb9c0263b24a97847620c99d213eb14, whose public sweepToken releases tokens held for any caller. Four minutes after the community wallet added 19,999.5 USDT of liquidity, a generic exploit bot looped 25 times with flash-loaned USDT: buy to that router, sweep, sell. It took the pair's USDT.

loss.notes: Exact USDT depletion of the FH/USDT pair 0x8f2d1a3992856a860304f1b86534b6b129cc4df7, all of which reached the attacker EOA; the flash-loaned USDT buy legs are attacker inputs. The pair's FH burned to DEAD or moved to the treasury and slippage wallets is the same liquidity and is not added.

incidents.name: unverified_0x452E25 unauthenticated uniswapV3SwapCallback
incidents.summary: The contract's uniswapV3SwapCallback() paid out the requested amount to msg.sender without verifying that the caller was a genuine Uniswap V3 pool, so a direct call with a fabricated delta and token address transferred 27.3 WETH out.

loss.notes: The exploit receipt records exactly 27.349 WETH leaving the victim and then being forwarded unchanged to the attacker EOA.

incidents.name: ParaSwap Augustus V6 arbitrary-call approval drain
incidents.summary: AugustusV6.uniswapV3SwapCallback() did not verify that msg.sender was a genuine Uniswap V3 pool and trusted the caller-supplied data for the payer and token, so anyone could invoke it directly and make the router transferFrom any wallet that had approved it.

loss.notes: ParaSwap reports approximately $24,000 lost in the initial malicious incident across four affected wallets and multiple EVM networks. Per-asset quantities are not published.

incidents.name: ShadowFi SDF unauthenticated burn(address,uint256)
incidents.summary: ShadowFi's SDF token declares burn(address account, uint256 _amount) public with no owner check, no allowance check and no msg.sender == account check; it simply calls _transferFrom(account, DEAD, _amount). The attacker deployed a one-shot contract that bought 0.010354936721195452 SDF from the PancakeSwap SDF/WBNB pair 0xf9e3151e813cd6729d52d9a0c3ee69f22cce650a with 0.001 WBNB, called SDF.burn(pair, 10354936721195451) to destroy the pair's entire SDF reserve except one wei, called pair.sync() so the reserves became 1 wei SDF against 1,078.615699417903036883 WBNB, and then swapped 8.461538283 SDF for 1,078.616699290110670619 WBNB before selfdestructing.

loss.notes: Single-transaction exploit. The victim is the PancakeSwap SDF/WBNB pair 0xf9e3151e813cd6729d52d9a0c3ee69f22cce650a and its liquidity providers. Its WBNB balance went from 1,078.615699417903036883 before the transaction to 127,792,366,264 wei after, a depletion of 1,078.615699290110670619 WBNB, which is also exactly the 1,078.616699290110670619 WBNB the attacker received minus the 0.001 WBNB he seeded, so the attacker-supplied input is excluded. The 10,354,936.721195451 SDF burned out of the same pair is not valued separately: its only market was this pool, so pricing it would double-count the WBNB leg, and the burn made it unsellable. Gas is not deducted and there was no recovery; the attacker unwrapped the WBNB in the next block and moved it out in 26 transactions to 0x0d5550d52428e7e3175bfc9550207e4ad3859b17.

incidents.name: EST delayed sell-burn drained by skim loop
incidents.summary: ESTToken records every taxed transfer into the pair as a sell in _pendingSellBurn. The next non-pair transfer then burns that amount, capped at 10% of the pair's EST balance, directly from the pair and calls sync(). Nothing ties that burn to tokens that stayed in the pair. The attacker bought EST through fee-excluded BNBDeposit and claimed EST from it. It then looped 'transfer EST to pair, skim() to BNBDeposit' about 150 times.
