Each iteration burned 10% of the pair's real EST reserve and synced, shrinking it to 0.1045 EST, and the attacker sold 18.74M EST for all of the pair's WBNB.

loss.notes: Exact net WBNB depletion of the EST/WBNB Pancake pair 0x74986cd86caf54961dd70eedcaf7cb3fe813c0b9 in the exploit transaction. The attacker's own WBNB, which enters the pair through BNBDeposit deposits and the 245400-WBNB round-trip buy, is netted as inflow. The Moolah flash loan is repaid in the same tx. The pair's EST side (moved to BNBDeposit or burned) is not valued separately. The attacker's net WBNB gain is 160.889451187958247246, which includes its own unwrapped BNB, so it is not used.

incidents.name: LeverageUsingSiloFlashloanWithGeneralSwap unvalidated swap target
incidents.summary: openLeveragePosition() on the unreleased leverage helper accepted a caller-supplied flashloan target and swap calldata without constraining them to the selected Silo market, so a fake flash lender's onFlashLoan callback made the helper call the real WETH Silo's borrow() on behalf of a third party that had granted it debt-receive approval.

loss.notes: The exploit receipt records exactly 224 WETH transferred from Silo 0x160287e2d3fdcde9e91317982fc1cc01c1f94085 to the attacker EOA while debt shares were assigned to the approved third-party borrower.

incidents.name: Vee Finance leveraged-trade swap without a valid price bound
incidents.summary: When a Vee lending market opens a leveraged position it hands control to the trading proxy 0xd1f855cef146d36cc5851e2139c54524420797f2, which resolves its execution venue with PangolinFactory.getPair(collateral, target) and then swaps the borrowed principal through PangolinRouter.swapExactTokensForTokens. The deployed code applies no liquidity floor to the pair it receives, no comparison against an independent price, and the amountOutMin it supplies is computed wrongly (Halborn attributes the miscalculation to dropped token decimals). In the anchor transaction it swaps 1.551393710318664115 WETH.e into a WETH.e/QI pair that the attacker had created 21 minutes earlier and seeded with 0.000003118379317223 WETH.e and 0.059871635214100967 QI, with amountOutMin set to 10649908 wei of QI, and accepts 0.059871514507227568 QI as the whole position. The attacker immediately bought the WETH.e back out of their own pair for the same dust, leaving Vee's market holding worthless collateral against the borrow. Repeating this 1,232 times emptied Vee's WETH.e and WBTC.e markets.

loss.notes: Measured as the complete drain of the two Vee market contracts. veWETH.e 0x024fdf9702c5ed031defeb380ca4d198435b305d holds 8918.152004900399986930 WETH.e at block 4622794 and 0.000000000000000001 WETH.e at block 4628953; veWBTC.e 0x60655668622b81f2a48b2095f593a8b5690aa1bd holds 207.18590825 WBTC.e and then exactly 0. Aggregating every WETH.e and WBTC.e Transfer log over blocks 4622795-4628960 reproduces those two addresses as the only large net losers, at exactly -8918.152004900399986929 WETH.e and -207.18590825 WBTC.e; their recorded totalBorrows rise from 3177.145372797417598036 to 9711.788308072086 WETH.e and from 185.48532883 to 392.66226447 WBTC.e over the same window, so the removed cash is not recoverable debt. The attacker's own collateral deposits are already netted inside these balance deltas because each iteration mints and then redeems the same 0.962462752229458474 WETH.e. A small unquantified part of the outflow may be contemporaneous legitimate redemptions in the same two-hour window; the reported team figures of 8804.7 ETH and 213.93 BTC bracket the measured quantities within a few per cent. WETH.e and WBTC.e are 1:1 Avalanche-Bridge representations of ETH and BTC and are valued with the DefiLlama ETH and BTC datapoints closest to the campaign. Later recoveries are not netted out.

incidents.name: Makina DUSD manipulable Curve accounting instruction
incidents.summary: Makina approved a permissionlessly callable accounting instruction that valued its Curve MIM/3CRV position through the pool's manipulable calc_withdraw_one_coin quote. A MEV searcher flash-manipulated that pool, invoked the approved instruction to inflate Caliber and Machine AUM, and synchronously propagated the false DUSD exchange rate into the DUSD/USDC Curve pool. Two cycles then removed nearly all of that pool's USDC.

loss.notes: Gross pre-recovery depletion of the DUSD/USDC Curve pool in the anchored transaction. USDC.balanceOf(pool) fell from 5,127,936.124721 at block 24273361 to 18,962.782093 at block 24273362, an exact 5,108,973.342628 USDC. The pool's DUSD token balance was unchanged. This measures victim assets rather than the searcher's smaller proceeds after flash-loan fees, manipulation costs and builder payment; later recoveries do not reduce gross loss.

incidents.name: IPC sells burn the pair's balance
incidents.summary: IPC's transfer hook implemented a sell by subtracting destroyNum from the IPC/USDT pair's IPC balance and immediately syncing the lower reserve, rather than charging the seller. Repeated permitted swaps therefore ratcheted down the pair's IPC reserve and let the attacker deplete its USDT side.

loss.notes: Gross pre-recovery loss is the IPC/USDT PancakeSwap pair 0xde3595a72f35d587e96d5c7b6f3e6c02ed2900ab's exact net USDT outflow in the single successful exploit transaction; the attacker EOA receives the same amount. USDT is valued at par. The pair's IPC balance reduction is the defect's mechanism and is not added as a second loss component. A transaction three seconds earlier, cited in technical reproductions as an earlier attempt, failed with no logs or loss and is excluded. No recovery was identified.

incidents.name: Rodeo Finance OracleTWAP samples an AMM spot price on a predictable schedule
incidents.summary: OracleTWAP is Rodeo's price feed for unshETH, but it does not compute a time-weighted average. latestAnswer() returns the unweighted mean of four stored slots, and update() fills one slot per call with a single instantaneous sample of OracleUniswapV2Eth.latestAnswer(), which is the spot reserve ratio of the thin Camelot unshETH/WETH pair 0x29fc01f04032c76ca40f353c7df685f4444c15ed times the Chainlink ETH/USD answer. No price accumulator, deviation bound, outlier rejection or same-block guard exists anywhere in the contract, and update() is rate-limited to one call per 30 minutes, so the sample instants are public and predictable. Rodeo's keeper 0x3b1f14068fa2af4b08b578e80834bc031a52363d called update() on a fixed clock, and the attacker sandwiched three consecutive samples with a swap into and out of the pair, lifting slots 1 to 3 from 2,639.236641922531347490 to 4,973.350465837606916071, 4,994.765044571862817590 and 4,269.731359394042641877 USD. At the anchor block latestAnswer() therefore returned 4,219.270877931510930757 USD while the contract's own currentPrice() read 2,642.426353532527916618. Every guard that should have stopped the leveraged open reads that same number: StrategyHelper.swap derives its slippage floor as convert(ast0, ast1, amt) * (10000 - slp) / 10000, so an inflated unshETH price lowers the minimum unshETH the swap must return, and InvestorActor's health check values the resulting position with the same feed. The violated invariant is that a collateral price used to authorise borrowing must not be settable by the borrower's own trades; no value of any parameter this deployed contract exposes restores it, because the only settable state is the exec keeper set and the sampling source is fixed in the constructor with no setter.

loss.notes: Gross cash depletion of the Rodeo USDC Pool 0x0032f5e1520a66c6e572e96a11fbf54aea26f9be is exact: its USDC balance falls 1,741,376.033697 -> 1,341,376.033697 -> 861,376.033697 -> 421,376.033697 -> 1,376.033697 across the four exploit transactions, 1,740,000 USDC in total, and Pool.getTotalBorrow() rises from 2,258,548.055219 to 3,998,555.547057 over the same blocks. That gross figure overstates victim loss because the borrowed USDC was spent buying unshETH that stayed inside Rodeo: StrategyLong 0x9e058177a854336d962d5ae576e9a46cfd8374d7 holds 0.005545436473013793 unshETH at block 110043452 and 430.845556549435845898 unshETH at block 110048300, and unshETH has no third-party historical price, so the offset cannot be valued to a defensible number. The reported loss is therefore the attacker's exactly reconstructed net realised proceeds: the attacker EOA 0x2f3788f2396127061c46fc07bd0fcb91faace328 was funded with 1 + 49.1 = 50.1 ETH from 0x404888f2396127061c46fc07bd0fcb91faacf439 and, at the end of the campaign, bridged 520.516760848238480749 ETH out through the Across Arbitrum_SpokePool 0xe35e9842fceaca96570b734083f4a58e8f7c5f2a in transaction 0x11230dea0b883e0e57f8090928d5f984e8d43c4f53ef33139f632bed44cd9300, leaving 0.0000219395 ETH behind. Every other native movement is an internal round trip: 55 ETH wrapped to WETH and returned, 192.470830773420532027 ETH spent minting unshETH through SgSender 0x5ba96b2be2b4e88fa51506198ccfaae57fb6f246, and 290 ETH bridged out and returned as 285 unshETH. Net 520.516760848238480749 - 50.1 = 470.416760848238480749 ETH, 885,272.60 USD at the DefiLlama ETH price of 1,881.89 at the anchor timestamp, which matches Rodeo's own post-mortem figure of about 472 ETH / 888,000 USD; press reports quoting 1.5 million USD used the gross size of the borrow rather than the realised take. Because third parties (Camelot liquidity providers and swap fees) also absorbed part of the 1,740,000 USDC, this net figure is a lower bound on Rodeo's own loss and the upper bound is 1,740,000 USDC less the value of the retained unshETH. Attacker-supplied capital, the 50.1 ETH of seed funding, is excluded.

incidents.name: ACP PaymentManager releasePayment double release (claim tracked in memory)
incidents.summary: PaymentManager.releasePayment loads the job into memory, increments amountClaimed on that copy only and has its escrow-sufficiency check commented out, so every call pays the full job budget again out of the pooled escrow. ACPRouter releases payment automatically when a job reaches COMPLETED and also lets anyone call claimBudget on a completed job. From block 37590595 one EOA's claimBudget calls re-paid 1,408 already-settled jobs; on 2026-03-02 an attacker created a 97,000 USDC job with its own provider, completed it and claimed it a second time, and copycats followed until the implementation was replaced.

loss.notes: Each component is the USDC that PaymentManager transferred out (platform fee, evaluator fee and provider amount) in releases of a job beyond its first release: 1,865 re-releases before the attack (1,408 jobs, all sent by 0x7346dc42102b5cdba321d587564612d1f3878ad2), the attack's second 97,000 USDC release, and 49 re-releases in 7 transactions by four senders afterwards. Fees paid to the platform treasury are not deducted; the attacker's own 97,000 USDC budget, which funded the first release of its job, is not counted. USDC valued at par.

incidents.name: Punk Protocol pool re-initialization
incidents.summary: The three Punk CompoundModel pools exposed initialize() without access control or a one-time initialization guard. The extraction contract reinitialized each pool with itself as forge_, invested the pool's stablecoins into Compound, and called withdrawToForge() to redeem and sweep the funds.

loss.notes: Gross victim depletion is the three exact pool outflows in the anchor transaction: 2,995,824.696852 USDC + 3,000,022.7862 USDT + 2,954,191.544042759328963399 DAI = $8,950,039.027094759 at stablecoin par. The frontrun anchor split the proceeds: its copied payload forwarded the full USDC leg to the original attacker EOA 0x1d5a5640 (hardcoded recipient in the copied calldata), while the USDT and DAI legs went to the frontrunner EOA 0x3aa27ab. The frontrunner later returned 3,000,058.381173 USDT and 1,954,191.5440427593 DAI ($4,954,249.925 total, matching Punk's reported approximately $4,954,250 recovery) to Punk deployer 0xe36cc043 and moved 1,000,000 DAI to 0xc176761d; the attacker swapped the USDC via 1inch and deposited it into Tornado Cash. Recoveries are not subtracted from gross loss.

incidents.name: RWC deferred sell burn removes pair RWC and syncs on demand
incidents.summary: RWC._transfer queues 40% of every sold amount (first 100M-token tier) as pendingPoolBurn and, on the next sell or through the permissionless executePendingPoolBurn(), subtracts that amount from the PancakeSwap pair's own RWC balance, credits DEAD and calls pair.sync(). The burn is paid by the pool's reserve rather than by the seller and can be triggered by anyone at any time, including by a zero-amount transfer to the pair. A flash-loan attacker looped buy, sell and executePendingPoolBurn 29 times, burning 38657.98 of the pair's 52156.45 RWC, ratcheting the RWC price up and selling back, and drained 109460.85 USDT from the RWC/USDT pair in one transaction.

loss.notes: Exact USDT depletion of the RWC/USDT pair 0x053207705669538a2b3851bcd1279572c0f55e40 in the single exploit transaction (pair balance 155361.577596537419707755 at block 123134629, 45900.722835311826818098 at block 123134630). Destination split from the receipt: 39964.071600905055157624 USDT to the attacker EOA, 62547.104844288483958918 to companyWallet 0xde2f6153f49e3134b88e98e3e86c0ae0411cc11b and 6949.678316032053773115 to platformWallet/deployer 0x911ea5a98fb8f238ffcb86c8a531d69afc7b4cde through the token's own sell-fee swap. The fee-routed part is counted because it left the pool only through the attacker's manipulated sells; the pool's liquidity had been added by 0x3aefe6c935131e6b853deacad9e566603eec0223 and its LP tokens sent to DEAD, so the depleted USDT was the backing of RWC holders. The 2495286.020489131224935440 USDT flash loan from 0x8f73b65b4caaf64fba2af91cc5d4a2a1318e5d8c was repaid within the transaction and is not loss.

incidents.name: Prisma MigrateTroveZap flash-loan callback injection
incidents.summary: MigrateTroveZap: onFlashLoan did not validate initiator/params, letting anyone migrate (and re-open with attacker params) other users' troves.

loss.notes: The incident post-mortem reports 3,479.24 wstETH lost across the primary and copycat exploit transactions, worth approximately $12 million.

incidents.name: BSC swap router unauthenticated uniswapV3SwapCallback pays any approver
incidents.summary: The unverified UUPS swap router 0xa331fde0 (implementation 0x241f743e) has a public swap entry, selector 0x33411b5e, that calls swap() on any caller-named V3 route pool. Its uniswapV3SwapCallback (0xfa461e33) accepts a call from any msg.sender and runs transferFrom(payer, msg.sender, amount), with the payer decoded from the callback data. It neither checks that the caller is a factory-deployed pool nor binds the payer to the swap initiator. An attacker-deployed fake pool re-entered the callback with victims as payer, pulling 29 approvers' tokens through their standing router allowances. Four later actors repeated the path before the router was paused.

loss.notes: Components are victims' tokens pulled by router transferFrom calls in which the payer is outside the attacker's addresses. Each is valued at the attacker's same-transaction disposal of that token: WBNB (plus USDT at par) received from the token's sale counterparties, minus the WBNB the attacker spent on that token's seed purchase. Seed round trips and the 1 WBNB flash-swap fee are attacker inputs. The main campaign, source-1, has 59 callbacks across 29 victims, 32 victim-token pairs and 8 tokens. Its components sum to 46.643086 WBNB plus 11550.468529943177031310 USDT, plus 6.924275 USDC at par. The attacker EOA received 62.284129499372716328 BNB. Copycat campaigns (source-7): 0x8d5b56cc (pDOG, FLORK, plus the "1" token, whose loot was returned to its pair unsold and is valued at DefiLlama), 0x1cac5af9 (b-money, Priceless, 淘公仔, Q币) and 0x8cc42905. De minimis copycat loot not added: 0x8cc42905's two transactions netted 0.009574 and 0.002442 WBNB, and the PONKE, SPCXB and CDL residues are under 1 USD. Loot kept unsold and unpriced is not valued, so the total is a lower bound for those transactions: 0x8d5b56cc's 0x3fa0fbbe (BEE, 黑马, GALIA) and 0xfa20e2bd's four transactions (13 low-cap tokens held in 0x9a9eb282). Unit values from realised disposals are below DefiLlama spot where available (Max 0.01346 vs 0.01490, OCEAN 9.59e-10 vs 1.37e-9 USD).

incidents.name: Super Sushi Samurai stale-balance self-transfer inflation
incidents.summary: The token's custom _update() read the recipient balance before reducing the sender balance. When sender and recipient were equal, its final recipient write overwrote the reduction with the stale balance plus the transfer amount, so every self-transfer minted the transferred amount out of nothing. The first exercise, on 2024-03-17, was a self-transfer of an entire 272,222,222,222.22195 SSS balance whose minted duplicate was sold into the SSS/WETH pair two minutes later; from 2024-03-21 game players, a whitehat that emptied the pair, and two later actors who self-transferred the pair's own balance through skim() repeated it.

loss.notes: Four campaigns against pair 0x92f32553cc465583d432846955198f0ddcbcafa1 (token0 WETH, UniswapV2-style 0.3% fee) are merged. (1) 2024-03-17 first exercise: 0x3dd45687042335a753e69f930ee0a5c3d6d01235 self-transferred its whole 272,222,222,222.22195 SSS balance (anchor), which minted an equal duplicate, then sold its entire 7,621,950,000,000.2146 SSS balance in 0xd576deeed7619498d71a33eeae6bd22eb08790b7d134ca81e00757ad7d7f8071 for 28.384109665566404476 WETH. The component is the WETH attributable to the minted 272,222,222,222.22195 SSS: actual output minus the output the same swap gives for the balance without it (7,202,733,222,222.432797 SSS after the 2% sell tax) at the pre-swap reserves 762.343906020378814326 WETH / 192,568,090,897,129.908987 SSS, i.e. 28.384109665566404476 - 27.406800442796240454 = 0.977309222770164022 WETH; the 997/1000 formula reproduces the actual output to the wei. (2) 2024-03-21 whitehat campaign of 0x6a89a8c67b5066d59bf4d81d59f70c3976facd0a: it first paid 0.010000000000000000 WETH into the SSS/WETH pair, then the cash-out receipt transferred 1,310.040494988573740722 WETH from that pair with zero WETH returned. Gross victim depletion net of the linked input is therefore 1,310.040494988573740722 - 0.010000000000000000 = 1,310.030494988573740722 WETH. The cash-out also delivered 4,954,444,444,444,439 SSS to the pair, exactly matching its same-block archive increase; this unbacked consideration is retained by the victim and is not a second loss component. Other pair activity between the setup purchase and cash-out reduced pair WETH by 109.408357782325449417; it is not attributed to this campaign (see the incident limitation). (3) 2024-03-21 blackhat 0xd0203f15af5ccc7e22966b31ef7a37316b6fab56: one transaction from its freshly created contract 0x71f759457568b9c1e5010d5587bae20dc572e0a5 called pair.skim(pair) 72 times, each a pair-to-pair self-transfer that doubled the pair's SSS balance, and swapped the inflated balance out, netting 40.278322289118611961 WETH out of the pair (1 wei WETH input already deducted). (4) Four seconds later 0xc0ffeebabe5d496b2dde509f9fa189c25cf29671 repeated the same pair-balance route in seven transactions (blocks 1116275-1116297), netting 7.100269482163580044 WETH. The remaining 29.086743612218663948 WETH left the pair at block 1116976 as a liquidity removal by LP 0x2836ca71fd966aa08024869d0c6bb72ab55e93c9 and is not loss. Players who self-transferred from 2024-03-21 13:13 UTC (0x05f43bfe..., 0x82a95827..., 0x9b96c9ac..., 0xa875a98d..., 0x65db5f6b...) moved the inflated SSS into the game contract 0x3028ea87ba570f7e3b4ddb96da94f455fa8f400c or to other wallets and made no net pair WETH withdrawal of their own (0x82a95827 was a net 0.1 WETH buyer); the 129 other transaction senders that first self-transferred after the whitehat drain likewise withdrew no pair WETH. ETH prices: 3,627.08 USD 143 s before campaign 1's sale, 3,526.16 USD for campaign 2 as before, 3,496.9 USD 153 s before campaign 3. The later 1,244.66 WETH whitehat return is recovery and is not netted.

incidents.name: bZx iETH self-transfer duplication
incidents.summary: LoanTokenLogic's _internalTransferFrom cached the sender and receiver balances before writing them and never rejected _from == _to, so each self-transfer of iETH credited the receiver without debiting the sender and doubled the attacker's iETH before burnToEther().

loss.notes: The approximately $8.1 million gross campaign loss covers the reported LINK, ETH, USDT, USDC, and DAI drained through duplicated iToken balances. The attacker later returned the assets; recovery is separate from exploit-time gross loss.

incidents.name: Seneca Chamber arbitrary-call approval drain
incidents.summary: Chamber's public performOperations exposed an OPERATION_CALL action with attacker-controlled target and calldata. Because users had standing token allowances to their Chamber, an attacker could make the Chamber call token.transferFrom(victim, attacker, balance) and drain approved wallet assets.

loss.notes: The reported $6.4 million gross campaign loss covers repeated approval drains from Seneca users on Ethereum and Arbitrum. Approximately $5.3 million was later returned under a 20% bounty; recovery is separate from exploit-time gross loss.

incidents.name: LW buyback trigger counted from a spot-balance price
incidents.summary: LW (GGGTOKEN) increments thanPrice whenever a sell is worth more than 2,500 USDT at getTokenPrice(), a ratio of the pair's USDT and LW balances, and its public receive() spends 3,000 USDT from the market wallet on an LW buyback per unit of thanPrice. The attacker skewed the pair balances with flash-loaned funds so that repeated sells counted as large, then sent BNB to the token to fire the buybacks and sold LW into the USDT they added to the pair.

loss.notes: USDT pulled from the LW market wallet by the forced buybacks in both attack transactions. The attacker contract kept 48,415.97 USDT; the rest went into the LW/USDT pair and fee recipients. The reported ~$50k is the attacker's take.

incidents.name: Blueberry PriceOracleProxy unscaled price adapter
incidents.summary: The money market's PriceOracleProxy implemented getUnderlyingPrice() by returning the CoreOracle's uniformly 18-decimal price unchanged, without the underlying-token decimal normalization required by the lending market, severely undervaluing OHM, USDC, and WBTC borrow balances.

loss.notes: Immunefi reports $1.35 million stolen and $1.08 million recovered, yielding approximately $270,000 net. Blueberry reports that the project replenished the remainder so users ultimately realized no loss.

incidents.name: ATM transfer-triggered fee auto-swap manipulation
incidents.summary: ATM synchronously sold its own token inventory into the ATM/WBNB pair before each non-whitelisted transfer to that pair. The sell amount followed the triggering transfer, the threshold was zero, and both internal swaps accepted zero minimum output, so a flash-funded attacker repeatedly transferred ATM to the pair and skimmed it back to trigger 34 protocol dumps before unwinding against the depleted pool.

loss.notes: The exploit receipt records 148.244121844478847692 WBNB entering and 549.190328414293175920 WBNB leaving the ATM/WBNB pair, for an exact 400.946206569814328228 WBNB net LP depletion. This excludes the attacker's pair inputs. The USD value uses the nearest DefiLlama BNB observation preceding the transaction.

incidents.name: EGD Finance claimAllReward prices rewards from live pair balances
incidents.summary: EGD_Finance.claimAllReward converts each stake's USDT-denominated reward quota into EGD as quota * 1e18 / getEGDPrice(), and getEGDPrice divides the EGD/USDT pair's live USDT balance by its EGD balance. Inside a flash swap that removed 99.99999925% of the pair's USDT, the attacker claimed the reward of an 18-block-old 100 USDT stake, received 5.61M EGD (99% of the contract's EGD) and sold it for about 36k USDT.

loss.notes: The EGD Finance proxy paid 5,614,105.648378533801366233 EGD to the attack contract. Its disposal in the same transaction realised 36,054.121156865234135946 USDT, the EGD/USDT pair's net USDT outflow; EGD's 10% transfer tax withheld 561,410.56 EGD for token fee recipients, and that share is included in the quantity but realised nothing, so the effective unit value is below the pre-attack spot of 0.008094 USDT per EGD. USDT at par. The attacker's 100 USDT stake (transaction 0x4a66d01a017158ff38d6a88db98ba78435c606be57ca6df36033db4d9514f9f8) and the 10 USDT flash-swap fee are not netted; the honest reward due was about 0.0003 USDT.

incidents.name: NGP transfer hook drains the pair reserve and syncs
incidents.summary: On every sell the NGP token’s _update hook moves treasury and reward fees out of the PancakeSwap pair itself, with super._update(mainPair, treasuryAddress, ...) and super._update(mainPair, rewardPoolAddress, ...), and then calls IUniswapV2Pair(mainPair).sync(). Each sell therefore permanently shrinks the pair’s NGP reserve and raises the NGP price. The attacker repeated small sells behind a flash loan until the price was inflated, then sold a large NGP position and took almost the whole USDT reserve.

loss.notes: The NGP/USDT PancakeSwap pair 0x20cab54946d070de7cc7228b62f213fccf3ffb1e holds 2212887.451145128834721055 USDT at block 61515894 and 9.156136012843449018 USDT at block 61515895; the difference is the loss to the pair’s liquidity providers, who are left holding NGP. The whole loss is in the one exploit transaction. Of that outflow, 1896191.720695873504350698 USDT reaches 0x8618314270528e245fbbb6fba54e245bb61a8d47 and the remainder goes to the token’s own fee recipients. DefiLlama prices USDT at exactly 1 at the incident timestamp. Nothing was recovered.

incidents.name: LAXO_Token
incidents.summary: LAXO's transfer and liquidity accounting reduced the token-side balance of its own LAXO/USDT pair, breaking reserve accounting across a two-transaction campaign and depleting the pair's USDT reserve.

loss.notes: Gross loss is the sum of exact net USDT depletion from LAXO/USDT pair 0xf05a6361e6f851bbff39c4f1d9ad4b661d3180b3 in two successful campaign receipts. In the anchor, the pair receives 350,000 USDT and sends 613,903.599313881523062936 USDT, losing 263,903.599313881523062936 USDT. In the second transaction, it receives 110,000 USDT and sends 180,408.492159940780730341 USDT, losing 70,408.492159940780730341 USDT. Their sum is 334,312.091473822303793277 USDT. Archive balances reproduce each component: 420,327.567509178068063660 to 156,423.968195296545000724 USDT across the anchor block, then 156,428.270808909321478144 to 86,019.778648968540747803 USDT across the second block. An unrelated 4.302613612776477420-USDT pair inflow between the two blocks is excluded. The two bounded precursors have no LAXO or USDT pair flow, and the sender has no later transaction through block 83,000,000. Campaign proceeds split into 182,381.343308214995028383 USDT sent to the payout address, 151,700.748165607308764894 USDT routed through LAXO to token fee recipients, and 230 USDT of financing fees. All are direct consequences of pair outflow, while all value returned to the pair is already netted; recipient and financing treatment therefore do not reduce gross LP depletion. USDT is valued at par.

incidents.name: Unknown batch executor unauthenticated execute(actions)
incidents.summary: EOA 0x98289e90 deployed an unverified batch executor and gave it an unlimited yvWETH allowance. Its execute((address,uint256,bytes)[]) runs arbitrary calls for any caller. An attacker's constructor had it transferFrom the owner's entire 384.667 yvWETH balance to itself, withdraw the underlying from the Yearn vault, and send the 429.21 WETH to the attacker.

loss.notes: Exact yvWETH debit from owner 0x98289e90d6fc92a8769bc892d006a2baa7705afe, valued at the vault's pricePerShare() at block 24981716 (1.118358035811806430 WETH per share, 430.1957 WETH) times the DefiLlama WETH price. The attacker's withdraw accepted maxLoss 10000 bps and realised 429.210570004163139885 WETH; the 0.985 WETH shortfall is strategy loss borne by the stolen shares and is included. No attacker input is involved.

incidents.name: CoW Protocol solver SwapGuard unprotected call
incidents.summary: A whitelisted solver's SwapGuard helper exposed an entry point that executed caller-supplied interactions with no access control, so the attacker routed a settlement through it and moved GPv2Settlement's DAI buffer to itself.

loss.notes: Gross loss is the exact DAI Transfer from GPv2Settlement to the attacker in the exploit receipt, valued at stablecoin par. This record does not substitute the larger contemporary headline estimate for the reproduced onchain amount.

incidents.name: DODO DVM re-callable init()
incidents.summary: DVM.init() is a plain external function with no initializer guard and no access control. Inside a flashLoan callback the attacker called it again to repoint _BASE_TOKEN_ and _QUOTE_TOKEN_ at worthless tokens of their own, so the pool’s repayment check measured the fake balances and passed while the real wCRES and USDT had already left.

loss.notes: Netting the exploit receipt shows this pool paying out 1139456.204397 USDT and 133548.938584725046782716 wCRES and receiving only the attacker’s own FDO and FUSDT. DefiLlama has no price series for wCRES, so that component carries quantity only and the USD figure is the USDT leg at par, which makes it a floor. The headline figures of USD 2 to 3.8 million for the DODO incident aggregate several pools and value the wCRES leg; this record covers the wCRES-USDT pool alone. Part of the proceeds was returned to DODO by searchers who front-ran the attacker; that is a recovery and is not netted here.

incidents.name: VerusBridge duplicate-proof-root parser divergence
incidents.summary: NotarizationSerializer used the last Verus proof-root entry when duplicate system IDs were present, while Verus consensus kept the first. Two signed notarizations therefore installed and confirmed an attacker-chosen root that authorized a later unbacked import.

loss.notes: The failure-finalizing notarization is anchored 252 seconds before the payout transaction. The drain receipt and call trace establish the exact eight asset quantities; the USD total uses incident-time DefiLlama prices for ETH, tBTC, MKR and scrvUSD and par for DAI, USDC, USDT and EURC.

incidents.name: NblNftStake withdrawNft reentrancy
incidents.summary: NblNftStake.withdrawNft() returned the staked ERC-721 with safeTransferFrom before paying NBL and clearing the slot, despite inheriting a reentrancy guard that the function did not use. The receiver callback re-entered the same slot, so two nested withdrawals each paid its unchanged NBL amount and emptied the staking contract.

loss.notes: NblNftStake held exactly 1,773,100,000 NBL before the exploit and zero afterwards. The attacker supplied a separate 1,773,100,000 NBL flash-loan deposit, which is excluded, then received 3,546,200,000 NBL through two identical withdrawals. After repaying 1,778,419,300 NBL principal and fee, the attacker sold the remaining 1,767,780,700 NBL for 164,967.658585 USDT and 6.900257340231423430 WETH. At $2,227.59/WETH those proceeds are $180,338.60283352611651843370, an effective realised price of $0.0001020141258661360634372994908/NBL. Applying that price to the exact gross victim depletion values it at $180,881.2465732458540806757271 without subtracting the attacker's flash-loan fee.

incidents.name: MetaPoint user contract unrestricted approve
incidents.summary: Each MetaPoint per-user contract exposes a public approve() that grants the caller an unlimited POT allowance, so an attacker can authorize itself and transferFrom the contract's entire POT balance.

loss.notes: Seventeen drain receipts contain 466 unique victim-to-pool POT transfers totaling exactly 209,431.616898011367571955 POT. Those transfers produced exactly 823,417.781370262268552996 USDT from the POT/USDT pool, used here at stablecoin par as the campaign-realized value; the attacker immediately converted the same USDT quantity to 2,515.786571418808574992 WBNB.

incidents.name: BT.Finance Curve aave-pool strategies unbounded slippage
incidents.summary: BT.Finance's StrategyUSDTCurve and StrategyUSDCCurve value their Curve aave-pool LP at get_virtual_price() but enter and exit the pool with add_liquidity(..., 0, true) and remove_liquidity_one_coin(..., 0, true), with no slippage bound, and the strategy deposit() and vault earn() that push vault funds into the pool are callable by anyone. With flash-loaned DAI the attacker unbalanced the pool, pushed its own and the vault's idle USDT/USDC into it at the distorted rate, restored the pool and redeemed its vault shares through freshly created helper contracts, so the slippage fell on existing depositors. Five transactions cut the USDT vault's balance() from 1,415,603.715775 to 525,985.069294 and the USDC vault's from 2,625,707.869159 to 882,227.990952 while share supplies stayed unchanged.

loss.notes: Depositor loss measured by each vault's own balance() (idle token plus strategy want plus gauge-staked a3CRV at get_virtual_price) between block 11817851 and block 11817869 with totalSupply unchanged: bUSDT vault 0x3ec4a6cfe803ee84009ce6e1ecf419c9cb1e8af0 1,415,603.715775 -> 525,985.069294 USDT (getPricePerFullShare 1.004921 -> 0.373391), USDC vault 0x8d702f8c5304c9d233a8a23fd3a22155e15bb357 2,625,707.869159 -> 882,227.990952 USDC (1.033299 -> 0.347185). The strategies' a3CRV-gauge balances fall by 667,796.22 (USDT) and 1,732,938.27 (USDC) over the five legs. The attacker's net proceeds are 1,381,896.996183609 DAI (0x66c7a0c6 sweep to the EOA); the remainder of the depositor loss stayed in the Curve aave pool as imbalance value (get_virtual_price 1.015670 -> 1.025644). DefiLlama dates the event 2021-02-12 at 1.5M USD, which is the attacker's proceeds; the onchain campaign is 2021-02-08.

incidents.name: CloberDEX
incidents.summary: Rebalancer invoked an untrusted strategy burnHook before reducing its recorded pool reserves. A callback could reenter burn while the stale reserves remained available, causing the same WETH liquidity to be counted and withdrawn twice.

loss.notes: Exact pre-recovery victim depletion is 133.7 WETH: Rebalancer's WETH balance fell from 133.707875556674808577 immediately before the anchor transaction to 0.007875556674808577 afterward. The receipt records 267.4 WETH supplied to Rebalancer from flash-loan proceeds, 401.1 WETH returned across the nested burns, repayment of the 267.4 WETH principal, and retention of the 133.7 WETH victim depletion. Published analysis values 133.7 WETH at approximately $501,279; the USD total is therefore reported rather than independently price-reproduced.

incidents.name: Maestro Router 2 unvalidated external call
incidents.summary: Maestro Router 2 implementation 0x8eae9827b45bcc6570c4e82b9e4fe76692b2ff7a exposed function 0x9239127f without caller authorization or target/calldata constraints. Through the proxy, an unprivileged caller could make the router execute token transferFrom calls as the spender and remove tokens from users who had approved the router.

loss.notes: The 12 successful campaign receipts show exactly 270.505159823556961290 WETH transferred from liquidation pools to the attack helper and immediately withdrawn to ETH. This is the exact common-asset value realized from the stolen tokens before any recovery, rather than the rounded 280-ETH public estimate. It is recorded as net loss because the gross victim depletion comprised 11 different volatile or illiquid tokens; separately adding those token quantities to their sale proceeds would double count the same loss. Receipt logs establish exact stolen quantities of 565463522794.182597666471533996 MOG, 48547556.581675106888722181 LMI, 36699014.396393139889031068 JOE, 9347.142332543648356945 BANANA, 4988293193.069537666 OGGY, 210000848.249795702514222702 jim, 240800.995682007751449462 ETF, 16597.430949033 LP, 6444188221.913920492320455870 APU, 102061241.618795802640566220 шайлушай, and 10685.567762358287885017 PROPHET. PROPHET_Dividends mirror-transfer logs are accounting shares and are not a twelfth asset. Later Maestro reimbursements do not reduce this pre-recovery measurement. DefiLlama's nearest WETH observation was $1,782.36 at 2023-10-24T23:30:00Z, 59 seconds before campaign end.

incidents.name: MOKE manipulable spot-price settlement
incidents.summary: MokeRelease.settle() allowed any EOA to overwrite settledMokePrice with the instantaneous MOKE/WBNB and WBNB/USDT AMM spot price. The attacker distorted the WBNB/USDT reserve ratio, settled the manipulated price, and then claimed 43.86 million MOKE against genuine stored release quotas; claim()'s deviation check compared the live price to the just-manipulated settled price and therefore did not protect the reserve.

loss.notes: The MOKE/WBNB PancakeSwap pair 0xba6a49a97cc725b3c39d6c5ea6deffddb64fe6b8 paid 1664.616180024096154954 WBNB in the exploit's MOKE sale: its Swap event at log 209 records 43860308.980417278429035188 MOKE in and exactly that WBNB amount out. This is the defect-caused gross loss to liquidity providers. The pair's end-of-block WBNB reserve fell by the larger 1692.745266365074783560 WBNB, from 1849.174363661815743493 at block 113652608 to 156.429097296740959933 at block 113652609, but the other 28.129086340978628606 WBNB was paid in the separate Burn event at log 108 against LP tokens the attacker already owned, so it was a withdrawal of pre-positioned liquidity rather than loss caused by the defect. DefiLlama prices BNB at 588.2809941793458 USD seven seconds before the incident. The seed row's USD 907,700 estimate tracks the attacker's lower post-financing proceeds rather than the pair's gross loss.

incidents.name: FlooringPeriphery extMulticall arbitrary call
incidents.summary: Multicall.extMulticall() in the FlooringPeriphery implementation is an unguarded external function that loops over caller-supplied (target, callData) pairs and executes calli.target.call(calli.callData) from the periphery proxy's own context, with no access control, no target allowlist and no calldata filtering. Because users grant the periphery setApprovalForAll on their NFT collections and ERC-20 allowances, any caller could make the proxy invoke safeTransferFrom or transferFrom on an approval-holding victim and move the asset to itself.

loss.notes: The campaign is exactly three transactions from 0x4d0d746e0f66bf825418e6b3def1a46ec3c0b847 through its contract 0x7e5433f02f4bf07c4f2a2d341c450e07d7531428, all driving extMulticall on the periphery proxy: block 18802261 pulled 14 Bored Ape Yacht Club tokens (ids 638, 4112, 4523, 5271, 5864, 5914, 5986, 6019, 6074, 6255, 6517, 6936, 8272, 9488) from five approval holders, block 18802289 pulled 36 Pudgy Penguins (ids 1024, 1338, 1349, 1715, 2079, 2341, 2375, 2503, 2567, 3279, 3309, 4212, 4605, 4778, 4953, 5092, 5365, 5382, 5584, 5606, 5866, 5927, 6197, 6472, 6679, 6693, 6827, 7228, 7258, 7484, 7821, 7912, 7983, 8239, 8325, 8723) from 0xe5442ae87e0fef3f7cc43e507adf786c311a0529, and block 18802297 pulled 12.063212894780222877 WETH from five further approval holders. Token counts come from a trace_filter enumeration of every transferFrom/safeTransferFrom call made by the proxy 0x49ad262c49c7aa708cc2df262ed53b64a17dd5ee between blocks 18341948 and 18830000 whose token owner is neither the transaction sender nor its entry contract. The NFT unit prices are the median arm's-length onchain sale price for each collection over blocks 18795000-18809000, taken from Seaport 1.1/1.4/1.5 OrderFulfilled and Blur v2 packed executions and excluding every transaction involving a campaign address: BAYC 26.683 ETH from 64 sales, Pudgy Penguins 9.525 ETH from 84 sales, converted at the DefiLlama ETH price for the incident timestamp. The medians are corroborated by the attacker's own disposal: he sold all 14 BAYC into Blur bids for 367.11 ETH (26.22 ETH average) and all 36 Pudgy Penguins for 391.04 ETH (10.86 ETH average) within 25 minutes. Excluded: 15 Azuki (ids 1657, 1892, 2230, 2480, 2583, 2953, 4313, 4371, 4406, 7230, 7371, 7689, 8305, 8561, 9627) pulled through the same defect between blocks 18802605 and 18802671 by 0x4526250a2e18dbd7fdd2dd0e49d58d88dc25da4c and 0x0171837c6461f551ab1eb5937374f52d6cefe7bb, because every one of them was returned to its original owner by block 18824263. Nothing taken by the exploiter was recovered: the 754.36 ETH of Blur proceeds plus the 12.06 ETH of unwrapped WETH left the exploiter address in two transfers at blocks 18802638 and 18802712.

incidents.name: BetterBank FavorRouterWrapper unvalidated-pair ESTEEM bonus minting
incidents.summary: FavorRouterWrapper.swapExactTokensForFavorAndTrackBonus only checks that the swap path ends in a registered FAVOR token, so any input token and any PulseX pair qualifies, and the FAVOR token's logBuy then credits an ESTEEM bonus on the bought amount. FAVOR's 50% sell tax applies only to whitelisted market pairs. The attacker created a worthless token, paired it with FAVOR, wash-traded 25 untaxed round trips to farm ESTEEM, redeemed it for freshly minted FAVOR, and sold that FAVOR into the official pairs, draining pDAI, PLSX and WPLS.

loss.notes: Quantities are exact gross depletion of the three official FAVOR market pairs, netted from each campaign receipt's Transfer logs, and include the 25,000-unit flash-loan premium paid out of each drain. pDAI/PDAIF pair 0xa0126ac1364606bafb150653c7bc9f1af4283dfa loses 890,899,504.360636360162048223 pDAI in the anchor; its balanceOf falls from 1,135,797,919.86 at block 24343024 to 244,898,415.50 at block 24343025. PLSX/PLSXF pair 0x24264d580711474526e8f2a8ccb184f6438bb95c loses 9,051,562,270.599955394519949325 PLSX in source-2, and WPLS/PLSF pair 0xdca85efdce177b24de8b17811cec007fe5098586 loses 7,409,355,692.988930176285433904 WPLS in source-3. The attacker supplied no value: flash loans were repaid in-transaction, and the FAVOR sold into the pairs was minted from farmed ESTEEM. That FAVOR is not netted against the drained reserves. Valuation is realised proceeds wherever the attacker sold, because every sale filled well below the pre-exploit DefiLlama quote. Of 890,874,504.36 pDAI received, 190,874,504.36 were sold for 396,945.3679 Ethereum-bridged DAI and 150,000,000 for 431,748.410207 bridged USDT, both taken at par. That is 0.00243 USD per pDAI against the 0.00501604 quote. All PLSX received sold for 263,979.344321 bridged USDC, and all WPLS for 70.078649042369470052 bridged WETH (4,472.85 USD/ETH, source-13). The realised unit rates are applied to the full depleted quantities, which include the unsold premiums. The remaining 550,000,000.000000000000000001 pDAI was never sold: the attacker transferred it to 0xce04c590344c2bd8e2bfe49a280c1d501dc8c000 in 0x51d91f4974ac5a152e2fda0a854f645826dc6efff4fabf325480718c305a0ff5 (block 24349712), the reported negotiated return. With the 25,000 pDAI premium it is valued at the pre-exploit quote 0.00501604, and the return does not reduce gross loss. The sales ran from block 24343052 to 24348986, after the last campaign transaction; their valuation timestamps are pinned to the anchor, as in other realised-proceeds records. Cross-checks: pricing every quantity at the pre-exploit DefiLlama quotes gives 5,119,420.82 USD, matching the reported ~$5M. Realised proceeds alone total 1,406,124.30 USD, matching Securelist's ~$1.4M net-profit figure. ESTEEM minted to the attacker and the treasury is not counted as loss.

incidents.name: Uranium Finance v2 pair k-check miscalculation
incidents.summary: The v2 UraniumPair.swap() scaled its balance adjustment by 10000 for the new fee but kept Uniswap's 1000**2 factor on the reserve side of the constant-product require, making the post-swap invariant check 100x too weak and letting the attacker take ~99% of each pair's reserves for a token dust input.

loss.notes: The U.S. Department of Justice reports that the attacker obtained approximately $53.3 million across 26 Uranium liquidity pools by exploiting this error. This is the reported gross campaign total rather than a reconstruction of each asset's incident-time price.

incidents.name: ARK public liquidity-pair burn and reserve collapse
incidents.summary: ARK exposed an unrestricted function that burned tokens held by its ARK/WBNB pair and synchronized the reduced reserve. The attacker repeated it 6,794 times, then swapped against the collapsed ARK reserve and withdrew the pair's WBNB.

loss.notes: The exploit receipt contains the only two WBNB transfers: 0.000000000000000100 WBNB from the attack helper to the pair and 348.147268515623217950 WBNB from the pair to the attacker EOA. Their net is the exact pair loss. The USD value uses the nearest DefiLlama BNB observation preceding the transaction.

incidents.name: LocalTrader price-manager missing access control
incidents.summary: The LocalTrader price-manager implementation exposed ownership and token-price setters without effective access control. A fresh EOA changed both values, acquired the exchange's LCT inventory for a negligible BNB payment, and exchanged the LCT against the protocol's LCT/WBNB liquidity.

loss.notes: Gross loss uses the LocalTrader exchange 0xce3e12bd77dd54e20a18cb1b94667f3e697bea06 and LCT/WBNB pair 0x64b266cd63ff3239e6491d6c2c58a5b8552c8724 as one victim set. The exchange receives 0.000000000032650797 BNB and sends 32,650,797 LCT; the final swap sends exactly the same LCT into the pair and removes 379.322744715267840729 WBNB. LCT is internal to the victim set and cancels rather than requiring an illiquid-token valuation. Subtracting the linked BNB input gives 379.322744715235189932 BNB of exact underlying depletion. Archive exchange balances reproduce its leg. The final receipt reproduces the pair leg; unrelated transactions in the same block supply 117.026153119475717607 WBNB net, so the pair's archive balance reconciles as 835.992277421314929535 + 117.026153119475717607 - 379.322744715267840729 = 573.695685825522806413 WBNB. The three approval transactions have zero victim flow but remain inside the complete consecutive-nonce campaign. The closest preceding DefiLlama BNB observation is $313.66 at 1684841863, 79 seconds before the anchor. Exact loss is $118,978.37210738067, replacing the seed's rounded $120,445 estimate.

incidents.name: Palmswap PLP AUM ignores collateral bought as USDP
incidents.summary: Palmswap's PlpManager prices the PLP liquidity token off PlpManager.getAum(), which credits the whole of Vault.poolAmount() to PLP holders and deducts only permanentPoolAmount, aumDeduction and open-trader profit. It never deducts the vault's own Vault.usdpAmount() liability, so BUSDT deposited through Vault.buyUSDP by an account that is not the PlpManager raises the PLP redemption rate even though the depositor keeps a fully redeemable USDP claim on the same pool. With inManagerMode false, buyUSDP and sellUSDP were callable by anyone. The attacker flash-loaned 3,000,000 BUSDT, minted 996,324.456826157454206069 PLP at an AUM of 1,060,591.303897471446528544 USDP against a supply of 1,060,117.814431969258921599 PLP, then sent 2,000,000 BUSDT straight to the vault and called buyUSDP for itself, lifting AUM to 4,050,654.353532854041808248 USDP against 2,056,442.271258126713127668 PLP, and redeemed its PLP at the inflated 1.9697 rate before selling the USDP it had just bought back for BUSDT.

loss.notes: The Palmswap vault proxy 0x806f709558cdbba39699fbf323c8fda4e364ac7a holds 1073754.395280771243426859 BUSDT at block 30248637 and 169598.473733068075688988 BUSDT at block 30248638; the 904155.921547703167737871 BUSDT difference is the loss and it all occurs in the single exploit transaction. It reconciles exactly against the transaction's BUSDT transfers: 901455.921547703167737871 BUSDT to the attacker EOA 0xf84efa8a9f7e68855cf17eaac9c2f97a9d131366 and 2700 BUSDT of Radiant flash-loan premium to the aToken 0x4ff2dd7c6435789e0bb56b0553142ad00878a004 on a 3,000,000 BUSDT loan. The widely reported ~$900k is the attacker EOA's net take alone. BUSDT is valued at par; DefiLlama has no bsc:0x55d398326f99059ff775485246999027b3197955 observation at this timestamp and prices Tether at 0.999825 at the nearest observation 1690219500. The vault held no other token at the exploit block. Not netted out: the attacker moved the full 901455.921547703167737871 BUSDT to 0x0fe7457f5909778b15d8e46768678abbf0c98329, negotiated onchain with the Palmswap team, and on 2023-07-27 returned 721450 BUSDT to the Palmswap deployer 0xa237d6b4bdf35ba51b732577260154849b4eff20, keeping the remainder as a bounty.

incidents.name: HB reward claim refills PROOF by pulling HB from the HB/USDT pair
incidents.summary: A PROOF reward claim (a plain call to the PROOF proxy from a registered wallet) calls MAIN.swapBack, which has HB.swapBack move up to 200,000 HB straight from the HB/USDT pair to PROOF and sync() whenever PROOF's balance is short. The attacker, an EIP-7702-delegated EOA that passes PROOF's msg.sender == tx.origin check inside its own flash-loan batch, bought the pair down to 200,000 HB for a whitelisted wallet, claimed a 612.83 HB reward so the refill took the pair's last 200,000 HB, and sold dust HB into the resulting 0.002 HB reserve for the pair's USDT.

loss.notes: Exact USDT depletion of the HB/USDT pair 0x67a63609cf1c317196724666cc39b2da63545a96 in the single exploit transaction. The 72.1M USDT buy and every later USDT deposit into the pair came from the Moolah WBNB flash loan and Venus borrows, all repaid within the transaction. The 73.6M HB bought for the whitelisted wallet and the 200,000 HB moved to PROOF are the same liquidity and are not added. About 1,510 USDT left in the pair was sold out by various holders over the next 14,000 blocks and is not counted.

incidents.name: Themis live LP-collateral valuation
incidents.summary: The lending pool valued Balancer gauge collateral from live pool state, allowing unsupported borrowing against a transient LP valuation.

loss.notes: The sole loss receipt empties six Themis market reserves. Gross depletion is 44,758.273451813505008435 DAI, 85,753.783607 USDC, 58,824.329320 USDT, 85,149.641487792003679412 ARB, 1.08947859 WBTC, and 97.620373410593518825 WETH. The WETH market transfers 317.620373410593518825 WETH out after receiving 220 WETH of same-receipt borrower collateral, so only the exact net reserve depletion is counted. Each reserve's archive balance falls by the declared net amount and ends at zero. LP and gauge tokens are borrower-supplied collateral, not additional victim depletion; flash liquidity and later conversions dispose of or finance already-counted assets and are excluded. The seed's approximately $370,000 proceeds estimate is replaced by exact reserve depletion. Exact decimal component arithmetic totals $512,004.35786888399426448664; the JSON number is its nearest IEEE-754 representation.

incidents.name: Nimbus fixed-APY staking rewards priced from spot swap feed
incidents.summary: Nimbus StakingRewardFixedAPY and LockStakingRewardFixedAPY convert NIMB-denominated accrued rewards into GNIMB with PriceFeeds.queryRate. On 2022-12-01 the owner rewired PriceFeeds' NIMB and GNIMB feeds from owner-set static NimbusPriceFeed contracts to PriceFeedSwap contracts that return the live NimbusRouter getAmountsOut spot quote. The attacker staked through three helper contracts, and 8.6 days later flash-borrowed about 75,477 BNB, bought NIMB in the NBU_WBNB/NIMB pair to raise the NIMB/GNIMB rate about 42,000-fold, and claimed rewards that emptied all three staking contracts.

loss.notes: Other stakers' GNIMB taken from the three staking contracts. Their combined pre-exploit GNIMB balance of 16,480,792.579260974757935462 fell to zero. Excluded from loss: the attacker's own principal of 187,100.345016290273752920 GNIMB staked in 0x7d2d8d2c, and the 424.966629926279399044 GNIMB of legitimately accrued rewards returned by earned() at block 23886614. The attacker's GNIMB top-ups sent to the contracts in the same transaction cancel out in the balance difference. In the same transaction the attacker sold exactly 16,480,792.579260974757935462 GNIMB for 546.826074786203541275 NBU_WBNB (Nimbus-wrapped BNB, redeemed 1:1 for BNB), and that sale moved the price. The unit value is those proceeds per GNIMB sold, at the DefiLlama WBNB price. Attacker net profit was only 278.03 WBNB, because the NIMB pump round trip and flash-swap fees ate the rest. DeFiHackLabs reports ~76K USD.

incidents.name: APIG token business-logic flaw
incidents.summary: APIG's transfer accounting credits a self-transfer without preserving the sender debit. The attack helper doubled its APIG balance with 28 self-transfers, then spent the inflated balance into two PancakeSwap pairs and removed their USDT and BETH reserves.

loss.notes: The receipt shows APIG/USDT pair 0xefbf31b0ca397d29e9ba3fb37fe3c013ee32871d receive the attacker's 500-USDT input and pay 72,628.575425255057150292 USDT, for 72,128.575425255057150292 USDT of net depletion; APIG/BETH pair 0xb920456aec6e88c68c16c8294688b2b63c81b2ce pays 59.5 BETH. Archive pair balances at the surrounding block boundary reproduce both amounts. The USDT loss includes the 1.5-USDT financing fee paid from victim depletion. BETH uses the closest preceding DefiLlama ETH price point, $1,625.46 at 1694174103.

incidents.name: PearlDriver NLAMM unchecked buy() cost overflow
incidents.summary: NLAMM.buy(token,index,amount) runs inside an unchecked block and charges amount * currentPrice in USDT, then mints amount * 1e18 game tokens. Choosing amount so the product wraps let the attacker pay fractions of a cent for up to 1e63 tokens of five craft resources, which it sold into their PearlDEX USDT pairs in the same transaction; two later actors repeated the overflow before the implementation was replaced.

loss.notes: USDT paid out of PearlDEX pairs (factory 0x73a0ba8bac1b6ae00de1e9cf767cdb98075ab92e) for overflow-minted tokens, per campaign; no USDT flowed into those pairs from the attackers in these transactions. The fractional USDT paid to NLAMM for the mints is attacker input and is not subtracted. BSC-USD valued at par.

incidents.name: ApeStaking NFT ownership accounting
incidents.summary: ApeStaking's deposit path could attribute an already-staked NFT position and caller-supplied stake amounts to a temporary NFT holder without receiving corresponding ApeCoin, allowing repeated withdrawApeCoin calls to drain APE and support cross-market borrowing.

loss.notes: Assets extracted into attacker-controlled accounts across the successful Pawnfi exploit calls from block 17496620 through 17496648, after APE flash-loan repayment. ETH is the gross protocol payout before gas; token amounts are final attacker balances. Values use DefiLlama's closest incident-time observations and stablecoin par.

incidents.name: Hyperdrive Router unrestricted CALL action abuses user operator approvals
incidents.summary: RouterUpgradeable.execute dispatches CALL actions (kind 15) through RouterLib.call to any AddressRegistry-resolved target with caller-supplied calldata, without binding the call to the caller's own account. Users make the Router their market operator and share/WHYPE spender, so any caller could make the Router invoke market.withdrawCollateral, market.borrow or transferFrom naming another user, stealing collateral, borrowing against victims' positions and sweeping approved balances.

loss.notes: Gross victim depletion over three merged campaigns of the same Router CALL defect against implementation 0x8c3c47cd: (A) 2025-09-18 by 0x11181b7d via 0xe253c916, withdrawing zero-debt users' collateral from markets 1 and 2 (unreported publicly); (B) 2025-09-27 by 0x9bb54e91, borrowing 672,934 USDT0 against victims' positions in market 3 and withdrawing 110,244.895039 thBILL collateral from market 7 (the publicly reported ~$782k); (C) 2025-09-27 by MEV EOA 0x0000000000004f3d8a, borrowing 42,700.736036 USDT0 in market 3 and sweeping users' approved WHYPE and market shares. Components are priced with DefiLlama at each campaign's first leg; share components carry unit prices derived from convertToAssets at block-1 of each sweep tx times the underlying price. Hyperdrive's later compensation and its reclaim of campaign-C shares do not reduce gross loss. Tiny UBTC (3 base units) and PT-kHYPE collateral are included at DefiLlama prices.

incidents.name: Level Finance LevelReferralControllerV2 claimMultiple duplicate-epoch claimed overwrite
incidents.summary: LevelReferralControllerV2.claimMultiple() iterates a caller-supplied epoch array without rejecting duplicates and overwrites the claim ledger with an assignment, users[epoch][msg.sender].claimed = reward, where claim() correctly accumulates with +=. Because claimable() returns fullReward - claimed, repeating one epoch makes claimed oscillate between c and fullReward - c and pays out the full epoch reward every two iterations forever. The attacker first earned epoch-13 referral points with self-referred flash-loan swaps, called claim() once to make claimed non-zero, then called claimMultiple() with the same epoch thousands of times per transaction and drained the controller's LVL reward reserve.

loss.notes: The LevelReferralController proxy 0x977087422c008233615b572fbc3f209ed300063a paid 214084.756853317598928554 LVL to the attacker contract 0xf08a01d2cace301ae69f07af5fdfb2336da2f629 across the 16 campaign transactions in source-5: 0.354509432724078554 LVL in the two honest claim() calls of 0xcb2c525c and 214084.402343884874850000 LVL in the fifteen duplicate-epoch claimMultiple() transactions. The controller's LVL balance falls from 217433.524803252160217421 at block 27835717 to 2168.819242105662540105 at block 27837770; the 1180.30 LVL difference is unrelated user claims in the same window. Valuation uses realised proceeds, not spot. The attacker forwarded every stolen LVL to 0x70319d1c09e1373fc7b10403c852909e5b20a9d5, which held 0 BNB and 0 LVL before the campaign, was seeded with exactly 1 BNB, sold the entire position through the PancakeSwap SmartRouter in the ten successful transactions of source-6, and ended with 3345.095796628300937646 BNB and 1 wei of LVL at block 27837906. Net realised proceeds are therefore 3344.095796628300937646 BNB (gas paid out of the same balance makes this a slight underestimate), worth USD 1102113.65 at the DefiLlama BNB price of 329.57 in source-7, an effective 5.148 USD per LVL. Marking the same 214084.76 LVL at the DefiLlama LVL spot price of 8.44 (1682946678) or 8.50 (1682963538) would give USD 1.81 million, but the stolen amount is 0.43 percent of the 49838881.9 LVL supply and the sale itself moved that price, so spot marking is not a usable valuation here; the realised figure also matches the contemporaneous USD 1.1 million reporting. About 5.91 LVL of the total (roughly USD 30) was the attacker's nominal epoch-13 entitlement and is not netted out. No recovery or return took place.

incidents.name: BNB48 private-tx MEV bot pancakeCall access control
incidents.summary: The bot trusted an unauthenticated swap callback caller, allowing a single transaction to transfer its six-token inventory out of the contract.

loss.notes: Gross loss is the exact net ERC-20 depletion of bot contract 0x64dd59d6c7f09dc05b472ce5cb961b6e10106e1d in the single successful incident receipt. It sends 25,912.948173777791158265 USDT, 22,307.554466878046228172 BUSD, 5,160.324984279773039298 USDC, 327.931283327916980816 WBNB, 0.014990282011559361 BTCB, and 0.097450591261976269 ETH, with zero inbound or returned units of any component. Stablecoins are valued at par. The closest preceding DefiLlama observations are BNB $285.3866866195567 at 1663074301, BTC $21,447.84909779573 at 1663074388, and ETH $1,636.5916335063653 at 1663074373, respectively 139, 52, and 67 seconds before the incident. Gas and later recovery are not deducted from gross victim depletion.

incidents.name: xToken xSNXa and xBNTa unvalidated mint pricing
incidents.summary: xSNX.mint(uint256 minRate) derived the fund's SNX unit value from the caller's own swap execution rate (weiPerOneSnx = ethContributed * 1e18 / snxContributed, where snxContributed is whatever kyberNetworkProxy.swapEtherToToken returned for a caller-supplied minRate) and fed it to TradeAccounting.calculateIssueTokenPrice, so a flash-loan-skewed SNX/ETH market collapsed the computed NAV per token and 0.125 ETH minted 1,282,360,456.05 xSNXa against a 7,567,827.98 xSNXa supply; no deviation check against the Synthetix oracle rate was applied. In the same transaction xBNT.mint(address[] path, uint256 minReturn) forwarded an arbitrary caller-supplied Bancor path to convertByPath and treated the returned amount as incrementalBnt without requiring path[path.length-1] == address(bnt), so four 0.03 ETH conversions ending in the SPD token 0x1dea979ae76f26071870f824088da78979eb91c8 were credited as BNT and minted 3,908,930,748.753742907112776888 xBNTa, half of which was sold through Bancor for 781,673.47 BNT inside the same transaction and half kept.

loss.notes: Components are the exact assets the anchor transaction delivered out of the xToken system: 2,422.004613114626938018 ETH forwarded to the attacker EOA plus the 5 ETH paid to the block miner out of the same extracted balance (builder payments do not reduce gross depletion), and the SNX, BNT and freshly minted xBNTa credited to the attacker EOA. ETH is valued at the DefiLlama incident-time price. SNX, BNT and xBNTa are valued at realised proceeds because the attacker's own liquidation moved those prices: the ten 1inch SNX sales between 13:51 and 15:14 UTC returned 1,948.698205540616982034 ETH in total (per-40,000-SNX proceeds fell from 193.34 to 187.43 ETH as the attacker sold), the single BNT sale returned 1,479.022638776856410914 ETH, and the 1,954,465,374.38 xBNTa returned only 5.365103413152759515 ETH when converted through Bancor on 2021-05-20, so the nominal 1.95 billion xBNTa reported elsewhere is worth about USD 14.6 thousand and is not marked at any xBNTa spot price. Realised ETH proceeds are converted at the incident-time ETH price, except the 2021-05-20 xBNTa conversion which uses the ETH price at that time. The flash-loaned 61,833.227224473099385337 WETH from dYdX SoloMargin was repaid inside the transaction and is not loss. Aggregate depletion spans the xSNX fund contract (which lost its entire 415.643497 ETH reserve) together with the Balancer xSNXa pool and the Bancor xBNTa pools into which the unbacked tokens were sold; the components above are the aggregate value removed and are not attributed to a single victim contract.

incidents.name: Paribus pETH redeem reentrancy
incidents.summary: The Paribus native-ETH market sent ether to the redeemer before the comptroller's collateral bookkeeping was updated, so the receive hook re-entered the protocol and borrowed against collateral that had already been withdrawn.

loss.notes: Gross loss is exact net depletion of the three implicated Paribus markets in the successful anchor receipt. pETH receives 200 ETH and sends 213.075471156453514228 ETH, for 13.075471156453514228 ETH net depletion; its archive balance falls from 13.075471156463824220 ETH to 0.000000000010309992 ETH. pUSDT receives 30,000 USDT and sends 50,122.071155 USDT, for 20,122.071155 USDT net depletion; pWBTC receives no WBTC and sends its full 0.75523112 WBTC balance. Both token archive balances fall exactly to zero. Flash-liquidity inputs are included in the market inflows; repayments and downstream swaps occur outside the victim markets and return no value to them. USDT is valued at par. The closest preceding DefiLlama points are ETH at $1,919.93 at 1681207964, 168 seconds before the anchor, and BTC at $30,072 at 1681207971, 161 seconds before it. Exact component values total $67,937.3707330498, replacing the seed's rounded $86,000 estimate.

incidents.name: SOF sell hook burns the sold amount from the SOF/USDT pair before the sale
incidents.summary: SOF._update handles a sale to the SOF/USDT pair by moving 90% of the sold amount from the pair's own balance to DEAD and calling sync() before the seller's tokens arrive. Buys revert unless the recipient is fee-excluded, so the attacker bought 991,223 SOF with flash-loaned USDT for a fee-excluded mining contract, leaving 787.9 SOF in the pair, then sold 875.45 SOF: the hook burned the remaining 787.9 SOF from the pair, and the sale received all of the pair's USDT.

loss.notes: Exact USDT depletion of the SOF/USDT pair 0x1f3863d274594f25c6203c9272857f0d51b1c010 in the single exploit transaction. The 313,567,718.11 USDT buy leg and the flash loans (fees 22,689.81 USDT to lenders) are attacker inputs or financing and are not netted against gross depletion, so the loss exceeds the attacker's 225,936.43 USDT profit. The 991,223.16 SOF bought for the mining contract and the pair's SOF are the same liquidity and are not added.

incidents.name: Paribus Camelot PNFT instantaneous-position oracle
incidents.summary: Paribus's direct Algebra V1 position oracle valued a Camelot liquidity NFT from the pool's instantaneous globalState without a time-weighted or deviation constraint. Once that oracle, pool and PNFT market were enabled, the lending controller accepted the transient position valuation and released four scarce reserve assets against collateral whose fair pre-event value was much lower.

loss.notes: The four Paribus reserves are the victim entity. At block 296699666 they hold 12.599960598441767978 native ETH, 6,510.273280264926258675 ARB, 0.36729789 WBTC and 3,924.210566 USDT; each balance is zero at block 296699667. The same receipt records helper 0xa8906930 debts in exactly those principal amounts. At the independently preceding marks the four gross products are $41,494.064243182445887469820, $5,041.386361131872006635194450, $37,757.12119833 and $3,924.210566, totalling exactly $88,216.782368644317894105014450. Canonical Arbitrum USDT reports six decimals and is valued at par. NFT 224023, retained by the Paribus PNFT custodian, has ticks -870000/+870000 and liquidity 261501642958000974. Applying the deployed LiquidityAmounts integer floors to the block-minus-one sqrtPriceX96 1993589943807320009052 gives 10,392,455.444702046400702691 PBX plus 6,580.072402 USDT. Camelot pool 0x25874cc60cbf7495b7cd1fa724178d251cfad5a8 then held 32,061,295.168839585435883621 PBX, 12,479.674453 USDT and active liquidity 466540172465242247; its exact spot was 0.00063315858681153637624319371523608944190276287934929122266559846865593598578993264 USDT per PBX. The position's fair pre-event value is therefore exactly $13,160.144804869404522237652225787648445816117581853463500053413592978259905749617, and gross reserve value less that attacker-supplied collateral consideration is $75,056.637563774913371867362224212351554183882418146536499946586407021740094250383. Two Uniswap V3 PBX/USDT pools had zero active liquidity and only dust; this Camelot pool was the only credible active market. DefiLlama's independently preceding $0.00060716 PBX mark at 1737197908 would value the position at $12,889.95564980529449265064586756, a disclosed 2.05% sensitivity, but the immediate onchain block-minus-one market is selected. Later recovery is not netted from exploit-time loss. The attacker swept and returned exactly 12.599 native ETH, all 6,510.273280264926258675 ARB, and the 10,283.193627-USDT final receipt residual to governance address 0x8ad8328166764ad208ae8dfe90ae766a1f0aee65. The residual includes the receipt's sale of all 0.36729789 WBTC for 37,912.265247 USDT, together with the pUSDT draw and PBX round trip, after the 3,093,209.807085-USDT Aave principal and 1,546.604904-USDT premium were repaid; it is not the WBTC proceeds alone. The returned ETH is 0.000960598441767978 below the pETH principal. Governance later withdrew the underlying NFT from the PNFT custodian in transaction 0x9bfa37a9 and burned it in transaction 0x125c5f6a, receiving 17,018,151.157492337382342522 PBX and 4,176.682356 USDT. The helper still owns the wrapper token, but the underlying NFT no longer exists, so that wrapper carries no residual underlying claim. No RepayBorrow event names the helper after the incident; all four reserve cash balances remain zero and the four debts remain outstanding and accrued at head.

incidents.name: PancakeBunny BUNNY minter spot LP valuation
incidents.summary: PriceCalculatorBSCV1.valueOfAsset() prices any Cake-LP whose pair contains WBNB as amount * WBNB.balanceOf(pair) * 2 / pair.totalSupply(), a single spot read of the pair's WBNB reserve with no invariant, TWAP or bound. BunnyMinterV2.mintForV2() zaps the vault performance fee into BUNNY-BNB LP, values that LP through the same call, and mints BUNNY = valueInBNB * performanceFee / feeSum * bunnyPerProfitBNB / 1e18 with no cap or sanity check. Flash-loaning WBNB into the BUNNY-WBNB pair inside the same transaction inflated the reported LP value, so a VaultFlipToFlip.getReward() on a position worth a fraction of a BNB minted 8,018,324 BUNNY, 6,972,455 of it to the attacker.

loss.notes: Valued on realised proceeds, not on a spot mark of the minted token. The single exploit transaction mints 8018324.054007685473386005 BUNNY from the zero address, of which 6972455.699137117802944353 goes to the attacker's contract and 1045868.354870567670441652 to the protocol's BunnyPool. The attacker sells the BUNNY into the two BUNNY/WBNB PancakeSwap pairs, which give up 64350.677479753673535696 and 56270.431537854947410798 WBNB respectively, 120621.109017608620946494 WBNB gross; 5989.566902738969215519 WBNB of that is consumed by PancakeSwap flash-swap fees inside the same transaction, so exactly 114631.542114869651730975 WBNB is transferred out to attacker EOA 0xa0acc61547f6bd066f7c9663c17a312b6ad7e187 after every flash loan is repaid. That WBNB quantity is the measured loss. The 697245.569913711780294436 BUNNY the attacker still holds at the end of the transaction is deliberately excluded: the attacker's own selling had already collapsed the BUNNY/WBNB pairs, so no spot mark on that residue is realisable, and the frequently quoted 45M headline is a mark on the full 6.97M BUNNY that could never have been sold at that price. WBNB is valued with the last DefiLlama datapoint at or before the exploit (1621460291, 364.1902823916861 USD); BNB moved between roughly 364 and 390 USD within minutes of the exploit on that day, and the nearest later datapoint (1621463838, 379.71 USD) would give 43.53M USD, so the USD figure carries a few per cent of price noise that the exact WBNB quantity does not.

incidents.name: TMM deferred sell burn drains the TMM/USDT pair
incidents.summary: While freeTrade is off, TMM accumulates waitBurnTokenAmount from buys and, on the next sell into the pair, transfers that amount from the TMM/USDT pair to 0xdead and calls sync(). The attacker flash-borrowed USDT, bought TMM to grow the pending burn beyond the pair's balance, triggered two pair burns that left a reserve of 1 TMM-wei, and sold a small amount of TMM for almost all of the pair's USDT.

loss.notes: USDT reserve drop of the TMM/USDT pair in the exploit transaction. The reported $1.665m is the attacker's profit after flash-loan costs.

incidents.name: thirdweb legacy Bridge approval misuse
incidents.summary: The active implementation behind an obsolete thirdweb Bridge proxy improperly authorized ERC20 orders, allowing one caller to consume a wallet's prior unlimited USDC approval in three transactions.

loss.notes: Gross victim depletion is 865.989600 + 1,770 + 30,994 = 33,629.989600 USDC across three receipts from one attacker, victim, proxy, and call selector. Receipt transfers have no victim inflow or return, and archive balances reconcile respectively as 865.989600 to zero, 1,770.134760 to 0.134760, and 30,994.049120 to 0.049120 USDC. A preceding victim-initiated bridge transaction transferred 0.015080 USDC as a fee and 5.026752 USDC to the proxy; it is legitimate use, not victim depletion from the incident. Transactions after each loss receipt dispose of already-counted proceeds without touching the victim and are excluded. USDC is valued at par.

incidents.name: SafeDollar reward pool deflationary-token accounting
incidents.summary: SdoRewardPool credited the nominal PLX deposit and returned that nominal amount even though PLX burned 0.15% on transfer. Repeated deposit/withdraw cycles depleted the pool's actual PLX balance to two wei; updatePool() divided newly accrued SDO by that balance, inflating accSdoPerShare and allowing a pre-positioned stake to mint unbacked SDO.

loss.notes: The campaign's final transaction transfers exactly 202,230.248261 USDC and 46,006.739506 USDT from the two SDO liquidity pools to the attacker helper after the helper sells the unbacked reward SDO. Stablecoins are valued at par.

incidents.name: Yearn v1 yDAI loose Curve slippage configuration
incidents.summary: Yearn's controller selected StrategyDAI3pool for the v1 DAI vault while the strategy's slippage allowance was 1% and the vault's earn() function was permissionless. In each exploit round the attacker imbalanced Curve 3pool, deposited DAI into yDAI, called earn() so the strategy added that DAI near the configured minimum, restored the pool, and withdrew. Eleven transactions repeated the loss-making round trip before Yearn disabled further investment.

loss.notes: Gross pre-recovery loss to the shares outstanding before the campaign. Immediately before the anchor, at block 11792183, yDAI totalSupply was 31,494,626.844158695810766902 and getPricePerFullShare was 1.110058316613691736 DAI. After the eleventh and final defect-executing transaction, at block 11792351, getPricePerFullShare was 0.758491538466562243 DAI. Their product, (1.110058316613691736 - 0.758491538466562243) * 31,494,626.844158695810766902, is 11,072,464.488546969286678676 DAI. Using only the opening supply excludes attacker-supplied temporary deposits and later users' shares. The attacker's final Curve unwind at block 11792373 raised the onchain share price by 4.067954716 DAI across the opening supply; gross pre-recovery depletion remains the value before that recovery. DAI is valued at par.

incidents.name: Gym Network LiquidityMigrationV2 migrate() flaw
incidents.summary: LiquidityMigrationV2.migrate() removed caller-supplied GYM/WBNB LP, then reused the raw GYM quantity as the desired quantity of a different asset, GYMNET, spending the contract's own GYMNET reserve and minting the resulting GYMNET/WBNB LP directly to the caller. The attacker skewed the GYM pair and constructed LP whose withdrawal outputs matched the GYMNET pair ratio, forcing the migration to deplete 1.166 million treasury GYMNET without any value-equivalence check.

loss.notes: Exact pre-recovery victim depletion is the LiquidityMigrationV2 GYMNET balance change across the exploit: 1,450,998.605164940945782286 before to 284,261.031699608471293657 after, a loss of 1,166,737.573465332474488629 GYMNET also emitted from the victim in Transfer log 49. The 1,399,999.999999999999999838 GYM left in the migration contract was attacker-supplied campaign input and does not offset gross victim depletion. No earlier transaction in block 16798807 touched the GYMNET/WBNB pair, so its block-16798806 reserves are the exact pre-exploit price state: 7,677,163.643402146827976102 GYMNET and 11,387.586657604004961399 WBNB. Their ratio values the depleted GYMNET at about 1,730.629414932106 WBNB; DefiLlama's incident-time BNB price of $423.1616558171135 gives $732,336.0088284722. The seed row's $561,595 figure instead values the attacker's lower 1,327.140409926955785497 WBNB retained proceeds after repayment and token-transfer fees, so it is not the preferred gross victim-loss boundary.

incidents.name: Beanstalk GovernanceFacet emergencyCommit on unsnapshotted voting power
incidents.summary: GovernanceFacet.emergencyCommit(uint32) executes a BIP's arbitrary LibDiamond.diamondCut once bipVotePercent(bip) = rootsFor(bip) / totalRoots() reaches the two-thirds supermajority. Both terms are read at call time, Silo deposits mint Roots synchronously through recordVote's balanceOfRoots(msg.sender), and the only temporal guard is C.getGovernanceEmergencyPeriod() (86,400 s) measured from BIP submission rather than from the acquisition of voting weight. The facet neither snapshots weight at proposal time nor imposes any holding period between minting Roots and voting them, so the supermajority authorization is satisfiable by state that exists only inside the authorizing transaction. In transaction 0xcd314668 the attacker took roughly USD 1 billion of Aave and Uniswap V3 flash loans, deposited 795,425,740.813818200295323741 BEAN3CRV-f (BDV 789,265,388.807140) and 58,924,887.872471876761750555 BEANLUSD-f (BDV 57,932,975.182545) into the Silo, minted 386,865,631,100,312,806,110,485,288,529 Roots, voted them onto BIP-18 (log 64) and emergency-committed at 387,487,298,354,313,289,142,728,288,490 / 485,851,957,499,334,104,135,968,761,599 = 79.75 percent, delegatecalling the attacker's init contract 0xe5ecf73603d98a0128f05ed30506ac7a663dbb69 to transfer every Silo-held token out of the diamond. The thresholds are private compile-time constants inside the facet runtime, not owner-settable parameters, and no value of the emergency period, the supermajority ratio or the proposal threshold makes the deployed code correct, because none of them constrain when the voting weight was acquired.

loss.notes: Measured from the exploit receipt. Netting every ERC-20 Transfer log, the Beanstalk diamond 0xc1e088fc1323b20bcbee9bd1b9fc9546db5624c5 lost 79,238,241.423601190873232684 BEAN3CRV-f, 1,637,956.191657208904972868 BEANLUSD-f, 36,084,584.376516 BEAN and 0.540716100968756904 BEAN:ETH Uniswap V2 LP after the attacker's own same-transaction Silo deposits (795,425,740.813818200295323741 BEAN3CRV-f and 58,924,887.872471876761750555 BEANLUSD-f, both flash-loan funded and therefore attacker-supplied inputs) are removed. Redeeming those positions took 10,883.105341079068109889 WETH and 32,414,493.174334 BEAN out of the BEAN:ETH pair, 43,043,401.256710036550983795 3CRV net out of the BEAN:3CRV metapool and 1,255,121.165448307654022661 LUSD net out of the BEAN:LUSD pool. The structured components are instead the attack contract 0x79224bc0bf70ec34f0ef56ed8251619499a59def's exact end-of-transaction net position (24,830.116910462326232315 WETH and 36,398,226.924163 BEAN) plus the 250,000 USDC it sent to the Ukraine donation address 0x165cd37b4c644c2921454429e7f9358d18a45e14 inside the same transaction; this avoids marking BEAN or BEAN-paired LP at the pre-attack quote. The measurement is therefore net: the 315,000 DAI, 450,000 USDC and 135,000 USDT Aave premiums and the Curve/Uniswap slippage were paid out of the extracted assets and are not added back; adding the 900,000 USD of premiums reconciles to Beanstalk's own figure of about 77 million USD of non-Beanstalk user assets stolen. BEAN carries a 1.0142914155592448 USD DefiLlama quote at the incident timestamp, but that quote is the pre-collapse peg: BEAN fell roughly 75-90 percent within hours, the attacker never sold the 36.4 million BEAN, and the quantity could not have been sold at spot, so it is recorded without a USD value. The widely reported 182 million USD figure is Beanstalk's total value locked with BEAN and BEAN-denominated LP marked at peg, not the value of assets that left the system.

incidents.name: KyberSwap Elastic
