incidents.summary: A double-rounding edge case let the swap result price pass a tick boundary while the Pool logic treated the tick as uncrossed, leaving currentTick inconsistent with base liquidity and enabling an overpaying reverse swap.

loss.notes: KyberSwap reports $55,234,535.17 taken from affected pools across the multi-chain exploit campaign: $48,671,786.84 by the primary exploiter and $6,562,748.33 by mimicking bots, valued at exploit time. This gross figure precedes later recoveries and excludes assets that were temporarily inaccessible rather than stolen.

incidents.name: Bamboo AI spoofable sale activation and pair-burn drain
incidents.summary: BambooAI._transfer sets sale = block.number whenever sender == addressDev and recipient == the pair, and once sale > 0 every transfer from a non-pair sender runs updatePool, which moves amount/100 of the pair's BAMBOO balance to a hardcoded address and calls sync. transferFrom(addressDev, pair, 0) needs no allowance, so anyone could activate the pair burn; repeated self-transfers or transfer-and-skim loops then shrank the pair's BAMBOO reserve and sold into the inflated price, draining the WBNB side.

loss.notes: Net WBNB depletion of the BAMBOO/WBNB pair 0x0557713d02a15a69dea5dd4116047e50f521c1b1 in the six drain transactions of source-7 (blocks 29668035..29668055, four actors), each netting its flash-loan legs within the transaction. The first drain (216.3359 WBNB) came from 0x16c4da1afe64634ab72968d8f7f9a80518b84e61, one block after trading opened; the anchor account's own drain (source-7 third hash) took 11.9136 WBNB. The BAMBOO moved from the pair to the hardcoded address is excluded as the token was worthless after the drain. WBNB is valued at the last DefiLlama point before the first drain.

incidents.name: XSURGE SurgeBNB sell() reentrancy
incidents.summary: SurgeToken.sell() sent BNB to the seller before updating the token supply and reserve, so the attacker's receive() hook re-entered purchase()/sell() repeatedly and drained the contract's BNB backing at a stale price.

loss.notes: The campaign report attributes five transactions and 13,112 BNB (about $5.57 million) to the same reentrancy campaign. It reports no recovery; the figure is gross and does not net any later compensation funded by the project.

incidents.name: Shezmu permissionless collateral mint
incidents.summary: A WBTC collateral input token exposed mint(address,uint256) without caller authorization. The attacker minted arbitrary collateral, deposited it into the vault, and borrowed unbacked ShezUSD.

loss.notes: Two receipts in the bounded seven-nonce campaign depleted the ShezUSD/USDC pool by exactly 639,740.960319 + 42,926.569474 = 682,667.529793 USDC, with no campaign USDC input or return. The first receipt's same-block MEV transaction returned 76,500.771328 USDC to the pool while removing 122,736.557154824572663770 ShezUSD; those unrelated flows explain the block-level archive residual and are excluded from this campaign. The attacker-created 18-decimal pseudo-WBTC and freshly issued ShezUSD are unbacked consideration retained by the protocol or pool, not additional priceable victim outflows. Downstream WETH/ETH disposal and later negotiated recovery are excluded from exploit-time gross loss. Same-day recurrence by a second actor (USDC and sDAI components): Four disposal receipts depleted the Curve ShezUSD/USDC pool by 962.224781 + 118.616729 + 142.949383 = 1,223.790893 USDC and the Balancer ShezUSD/sDAI pool by 771.270672279107347817 + 92.720177612173316782 = 863.990849891280664599 sDAI. Each receipt exactly matches the corresponding archive pool-balance delta, with no same-block residual. The two sDAI components are valued at their closest-preceding ERC-4626 DAI conversion values and DAI par. The freely minted pseudo-WBTC and ShezUSD are unbacked pool consideration, not additional scarce-asset loss. Downstream WETH/ETH disposal, retained unbacked ShezUSD, and later return activity are excluded.

incidents.name: Conic ETH omnipool Curve reentrancy guard skipped for WETH-listed pools
incidents.summary: ConicEthPool guards its Curve interactions by calling CurveHandlerV3.reentrancyCheck(pool) at the end of deposit and withdraw. That function returns immediately unless _isETH(pool) holds, and _isETH asks the CurveRegistryCache whether the pool lists the 0xEeee ETH sentinel directly. For the Curve v2 rETH and cbETH pools in the omnipool the meta-registry reports WETH instead, so the check returned early even though those pools transfer native ETH on withdrawal. The attacker re-entered Conic from inside a Curve remove_liquidity ETH callback and had the omnipool value its Curve LP holdings from mid-update pool balances, halving the exchange rate for existing depositors. The violated invariant is that the omnipool must never price or move its Curve positions while a Curve pool it holds is mid-update; the deployed guard could not detect that state for the pools that most needed it.

loss.notes: Measured as the omnipool's own underlying accounting across the single exploit transaction: getTotalAndPerPoolUnderlying() falls from 3,416.508041001657295625 ETH at block 17740954 to 1,536.655180883092422805 ETH at block 17740955 while cncETH total supply is unchanged at 3,408.790292193721163119, so all 1,879.852860118564872820 ETH is depletion of existing depositors rather than a redemption. The attacker realised 1,723.726595625401118794 ETH net of gas, the widely reported 1,724 ETH / 3.2M USD; the roughly 156 ETH gap is Curve and Balancer slippage and fees paid to third parties, which does not reduce gross victim depletion. The Balancer flash loan principal is an attacker-supplied input and is excluded. The separate crvUSD omnipool loss later the same day belongs to its own incident and is not included.

incidents.name: CvxRewardDistributor claimMultipleStaking
incidents.summary: claimMultipleStaking() did not check that entries of the claimContracts array were registered staking contracts, so a caller-supplied fake contract was invoked as a staking service and returned reward amounts that minted 58M CVG to the attacker.

loss.notes: Gross swap proceeds transferred to the attacker in the exploit transaction. Asset amounts are exact token Transfer events; the aggregate USD value is reported by Verichains.

incidents.name: vETH virtual-liquidity factory unbacked mint
incidents.summary: The vETH virtual-liquidity factory 0x62f250cf7021e1cf76c765dec8ec623fe173a1b5 exposed a permissionless addVirtualLiquidity(address,address,uint256,uint256) (selector 0x6c0472da) that called VirtualToken.takeLoan to mint up to the 300 ether per-block limit of unbacked vETH straight into a caller-named Uniswap V2 vETH/token pair, pulled only the matching amount of the counter token at the pair's live spot ratio, burned the resulting LP to address(0), and never called repayLoan. Because vETH is redeemable one-for-one for ETH through the whitelisted router, the caller could first push the pair's spot ratio with a flash loan so that 300 vETH required almost no counter token, then sell the counter token back and withdraw more ETH from VirtualToken than had been deposited. No parameter value fixes this: the loan is never repaid at any limit, so the deployed factory code mints an unbacked redeemable claim on every call.

loss.notes: Exact victim depletion measured as the native-ETH balance of the VirtualToken backing contract 0x280a8955a11fcd81d72ba1f99d265a48ce39ac2e, which fell from 493.212272163562760008 ETH at block 21184777 to 352.727119496848597852 ETH at block 21184796 with no other account activity in that window: 140.485152666714162156 ETH across the three campaign transactions (132.513467878004258374 + 4.846141416396402693 + 3.125543372313501089). The Balancer flash-loan principal is attacker-supplied and repaid inside each transaction, so it is not loss. The residual token inventory the attacker kept (BIF, Cowbo and BOVIN, plus 0.680685122899160147 leftover vETH) is deliberately not marked: the meme tokens were made illiquid by the attacker's own selling and the whole residue liquidated for about 1.35 ETH in transactions 0xfd6d05e7329526b72fd9ac5e24082fb74c9bc03bd2650a4b783cbbc309fc7a07 and 0x6391004ac335f7fd8e1e0986038ea46b0221a6138e4180019916bff4cd8c4e13, so counting spot marks would overstate the loss. The campaign minted 900 unbacked vETH in total; the 759.5 vETH not withdrawn as ETH remains an unrealised undercollateralisation of the same contract and is excluded from this figure.

incidents.name: Akropolis Delphi SavingsModule fake-token reentrancy
incidents.summary: SavingsModule.deposit(address,address[],uint256[]) accepts any token address the caller names: it never checks the token against the pool's registered token set, and its amount normalisation falls through to an identity case for tokens it does not know. It then calls that token's transferFrom while the caller's pool-token balance is still unadjusted, with no reentrancy guard. An attacker-controlled ERC20 could therefore reenter deposit() from inside its own transferFrom and deposit real DAI in the inner frame, so the outer frame credited the fake token's nominal amount on top of the real deposit and minted roughly twice the pool tokens the DAI justified; withdrawing them returned real DAI for value that was never delivered.

loss.notes: Measured as the net DAI the two Delphi pool adapters paid the attacker contract 0xe2307837524db8961c4541f943598654240bd62f over the whole campaign, by summing every DAI Transfer log in blocks 11242620-11242700 in which that contract is a party and netting per counterparty: 1276753.689692559845800164 DAI out of the sUSD pool 0x91d7b9a8d2314110d4018c88dbfdcf5e2ba4772e and 764051.328033013301747370 DAI out of the yCurve pool 0x7967ada2a32a633d5c055e2e075a83023b632b4e, so 2040805.017725573147547534 DAI net. The dYdX flash loans are attacker-supplied inputs and net to a 2 wei fee; the attacker's own 45.51280861515868 DAI of seed and the 9954.487191384842 DAI he spent buying gas on Uniswap are already inside those nets, which is why the amount finally swept to the attacker EOA in 0xf15623567231c67df2b8bcc5540236fbda2c3ac11ecbec427048f11b582cb869 is the smaller 2030850.530534188306235972 DAI. DAI is par-valued. Nothing was recovered.

incidents.name: Conic crvUSD omnipool mints and redeems against manipulable Curve LP marks
incidents.summary: ConicPoolV2.depositFor() and withdraw() convert between cncCRVUSD shares and underlying with _getTotalAndPerPoolUnderlying(), which values every Curve position at CurveLPOracleV2.getUSDPrice(lpToken) = sum(pool.balances(i) * price(coin i)) / lpToken.totalSupply(), i.e. from the Curve pools' instantaneous balances. The Curve add_liquidity and remove_liquidity_one_coin calls that back those conversions are executed by the delegatecalled CurveHandlerV3 with a hardcoded minimum of 0, and the only slippage bound in the whole path is the caller-supplied minLpReceived / minUnderlyingReceived, which an attacker sets to zero. The violated invariant is that the omnipool must not mint or redeem shares against marks that the same transaction can move, and must not trade its own Curve positions at an unbounded price. The attacker flash-borrowed 12M USDC, 9M USDT and 80,000 WETH, minted 93M crvUSD from the crvUSD controller, pushed the crvUSD/USDT and crvUSD/USDC pools off balance, made the omnipool deposit about 47M crvUSD single-sided into the pool it then considered least balanced, unwound the swap, and made the omnipool withdraw single-sided again, repeating the sandwich four times per transaction.

loss.notes: Measured as the mark-independent depletion of the omnipool's Curve positions: for each of its four Curve pools, (idle LP + Convex-staked LP) * get_virtual_price() at the block boundaries of the defect-executing transactions. The sum falls from 49,553,618.830634864627661493 at block 17743469 to 48,682,039.404766238059398496 at 17743480 (871,579.425868626568262997) and from 40,924,481.223378674223457560 at 17743530 to 40,863,219.664732509374336713 at 17743531 (61,261.558646164849120847), total 932,840.984514791417383844 crvUSD of pool D-value. The omnipool's own accounting agrees: getTotalAndPerPoolUnderlying() falls 49,551,067.132383105461785002 -> 48,678,526.665747486728361172 and 40,922,092.636477872837352137 -> 40,860,757.486433788902539284, 933,875.616679702668236683 crvUSD in total, a 0.11 percent difference, and cncCRVUSD total supply is unchanged at 49,529,983.483468799349940419 across blocks 17743469-17743491, so none of the depletion is a redemption. Twelve successful transactions execute the defect. The anchored attacker takes 76,615.444126 crvUSD in the anchor transaction and 61,261.558646 in transaction 0xc08bfee8... at block 17743531; a second actor, 0xfde0d1575ed8e06fbf36256bcdfa1f359281455a through 0xd050e0a4838d74769228b49dff97241b4ef3805d, copies the same four-cycle sandwich once per block for the next ten blocks and takes 794,963.981743 crvUSD. All twelve hit the same execution context with the same defect inside 62 seconds and no other record counts them, so they are one campaign here; the split is stated so a reviewer can restrict the figure to the anchored attacker's 137,877.002772 crvUSD if that scope is preferred. Ordinary user withdrawals between blocks 17743480 and 17743530 reduce holdings by 7,891,877.914274652257975570 shares at an unchanged 0.9828 exchange rate and are excluded. The Balancer flash loan principal, the 93M crvUSD minted against the attacker's own WETH collateral, and the Curve and crvUSD-controller fees paid to third parties are attacker-supplied inputs or third-party receipts and are not netted. The separate ETH omnipool loss earlier the same day is its own incident and is not included.

incidents.name: DN404
incidents.summary: The proxy remained uninitialized, allowing the attacker to call its public initializer and then use the resulting authority to withdraw all FLIX held by the proxy.

loss.notes: The receipt records exactly 685,000 FLIX leaving the victim and the immediate FLIX/USDT swap returning 169,577.736489 USDT; the realized stablecoin proceeds provide the onchain valuation.

incidents.name: Predy Finance PredyPool lock settlement credits a supply() as repayment of take()
incidents.summary: PredyPool settles a trade lock by comparing raw ERC20 balances. TradeLogic.callTradeAfterCallback() runs GlobalDataLibrary.initializeLock(), which snapshots the pool's quote and base token balances, then hands control to the caller's predyTradeAfterCallback, then runs finalizeLock(), whose settle() computes paid = balanceOf(this) - snapshot. PredyPool.take() is guarded only by onlyByLocker and sends any amount to any address without recording a debt, and PredyPool.supply() is reachable from inside that callback because trade() carries no reentrancy guard. The attacker registered its own pair through the permissionless registerPair(), acquired the lock with a zero-size trade(), and inside the callback called take() for the pool's entire WETH and USDC balances and then supply() to put the same tokens back. settle() saw both balances restored and reported paid = 0, so the lock finalised and the empty vault passed PositionCalculator.checkSafe(), while supply() had minted the attacker supply tokens for the whole pool. Two withdraw() calls after the lock closed burned those supply tokens and removed everything. The violated invariant is that a locker's take() must be repaid with assets that create no offsetting claim; a balance delta cannot distinguish repayment from a new deposit that mints its own LP position.

loss.notes: Exact victim depletion in the single exploit transaction: PredyPool 0x9215748657319b17fecb2b5d086a3147bfbc8613 holds 219,585.737814 USDC and 83.910994929830029848 WETH at block 211107441 and zero of both at block 211107442. The attacker contract 0xb79714634895f52a4f6a75eceb58c96246370149 is created inside the exploit transaction and holds no USDC or WETH beforehand, so none of the drained amount is attacker-supplied capital; the take() and supply() legs inside the lock net to zero and are not double counted. The pool's USDC balance is still zero at blocks 211200000, 212000000 and 215000000, so no onchain restitution reached the pool. Priced with DefiLlama at the exploit timestamp, 0.999782 for Arbitrum USDC and 2912.04 for WETH, the total is 463,890.04 USD, which reproduces the 464k USD commonly reported.

incidents.name: LpdFi sizes an interest-bearing principal from the LPD spot pair price
incidents.summary: LpdFi.buy(uint256 uAmount) lets the caller name the USDC principal that will accrue interest and charges for it in LPD at `tokenAmount = uAmount * 1e18 / token.price()`, where Lpd.price() returns the instantaneous reserve ratio of the immutable PancakeSwap LPD/USDC pair 0x85346d31743796f7d00d675629e32783a968f210 with no TWAP, liquidity floor or deviation bound. Interest then accrues from the discrete issue index in getOrder as `interestRate * uAmount * (issue - lastIssue) / BASE`, so crossing an issue boundary credits a whole 0.5 percent period regardless of elapsed time, and claimInterest funds the entitlement through removeLp, which burns protocol-owned Cake-LP with both PancakeRouter minimum outputs set to zero. The attacker swapped 43,714,602.618935976563910532 USDC into the pair to lift Lpd.price() from 0.126899043811789644 to 655.1979230244382 USDC per LPD, called buy(140324732e18) for only 214,171.515306781626633142 LPD, reversed the swap, and one second later, once getIssue() rolled from 18 to 19, claimed 701,623.66 USDC of interest, which removed the protocol's entire Cake-LP position.

loss.notes: The fraudulent interest claim burned the whole protocol-owned liquidity position: LpdFi's Cake-LP balance fell from 1678049359669752344366456 to 1 wei between blocks 113613923 and 113613924, and the pair returned 700535.142132506110424513 USDC and 4059427.508747598805052053 LPD to LpdFi. The LPD leg stayed with the contract, so the depletion measured here is the USDC leg, all of which left LpdFi in the same transaction: 693529.790711181049320267 USDC to the attacker's executor 0x7f5ad0a998dcb3f5006f0d152bebc055979ef711 and 7005.351421325061104246 USDC to the contract's configured feeAddress 0x4c0c86041013a3883d9b6331054df7ca9c977242, matching the ClaimInterest event's receivedAmount and feeAmount fields. Attacker-supplied inputs are excluded: the executor was staked with 116495 USDC by EOA 0x5d289266d85ef671561ba3f253fb79327c193f33 and consumed it in the price manipulation, and the flash liquidity used for the 43.7M USDC swap was repaid inside the setup transaction, so the attacker's own realised gain is the smaller 573034.793138448987344168 USDC that the seed row and public write-ups quote, being the EOA's 689529.793138448987344168 USDC terminal balance less its 116495 USDC stake. Not valued: the residual damage to the LPD/USDC pair and to the 4,059,427.5 LPD LpdFi retained, whose pair-implied value collapsed once the protocol's own liquidity was withdrawn.

incidents.name: DEI token burnFrom reversed allowance lookup
incidents.summary: The DEI implementation selected on 2023-04-16 wrote the allowance update inside burnFrom() with the owner and spender arguments transposed, so calling burnFrom(victim, 0) granted the caller an unlimited allowance over the victim and let the attacker transferFrom every DEI holder that had ever approved the token.

loss.notes: Halborn and CertiK report about $6.5 million drained across Arbitrum ($5 million), BNB Chain ($1.3 million), and Ethereum ($135,000) through the same DEI defect. Halborn reports roughly 10% was returned; the gross loss is retained and recovery is not netted.

incidents.name: XCarnival XNFT withdrawn-collateral order reuse
incidents.summary: XNFT.withdrawNFT() returned a pledged NFT without closing or invalidating the pledge order, so getOrderDetail kept reporting the collateral and P2Controller.borrowAllowed kept approving borrows against it. The attacker pledged one BAYC, withdrew it, re-pledged it into a new order, and repeated the cycle to open 83 simultaneously borrowable orders backed by the same token.

loss.notes: Six borrow transactions moved 2,988 ETH out of the xETH pool 0xb38707e31c813f832ef71c70731ed80b45b85b2d, whose balance falls from 3,014.418576385059098519 ETH at block 15028860 to 26.418576385059098519 ETH at block 15029010; the four attacker exploit contracts forward exactly 1,980 + 540 + 288 + 180 = 2,988 ETH to the attacker EOA. Widely reported figures of 3,087 ETH are the attacker EOA balance after the campaign, which also contains pre-attack funds. DefiLlama's nearest ETH observation to the incident timestamp is at 1656244505. The attacker returned 1,467 ETH to the XCarnival deployer the following day; recovery is not netted out of the exploit-time loss.

incidents.name: Galaxy Fox claim contract unprotected setMerkleRoot
incidents.summary: The unverified GFOX airdrop/claim contract's setMerkleRoot(bytes32) writes the Merkle root to storage slot 3 without any caller check. The attacker set a root equal to its own leaf and called claim with an empty proof, withdrawing 1.34B GFOX and selling it into the GFOX/WETH Uniswap V2 pair; three copycat transactions by two other actors repeated the same calls within about two hours and emptied the contract.

loss.notes: The claim contract's entire GFOX balance (1,780,453,099.185 GFOX) was taken in four transactions: the anchor (1,335,339,824.38875), copycat bot 0xcc3a5dc003b3a58621745a39f706ef9646d5c481 in source-6 and source-7 (333,834,956.0971875 and 83,458,739.024296875) and 0x14b362d2e38250604f21a334d71c13e2ed478467 in source-8 (27,819,579.674765625, sold in source-9). GFOX is valued by realised proceeds: the GFOX/WETH pair 0x92ee0df7f6b0674cabc9bfc64873786fa7be82d0 paid out 108.744009594558929771 + 5.081096386975926775 + 1.344190519511096579 + 2.329061044327335573 = 117.498357545373288698 WETH for the dumped tokens, valued at the WETH quote at the anchor time (3035.7 USD; all legs within 2h16m). Token transfer tax taken from the stolen GFOX is not counted, so this is a lower bound.

incidents.name: LavaLending UniV3Wrapper one-sided unclaimed-fee inflation
incidents.summary: LiquidityProviderBase._limitFees() caps a Uniswap V3 position's pending fees only when BOTH token fee amounts exceed their max-APR budget (`if (totalFees0 > max0 && totalFees1 > max1)`), so fees accrued in a single token are returned uncapped. UniV3Wrapper.getAssetsBasedOnPrice() adds those uncapped fees to the oracle-priced fair reserves, and Lava's WrapperOracle divides that sum by totalSupply to price the USDC/USDC.e wrapper LP token. The attacker minted a dust LP position, drove one-directional swaps through the 0x8e295789 USDC/USDC.e pool to accrue ~100k of token0-only fees against a 0.000999-share supply, and borrowed the Lava market out against the inflated collateral. The Chainlink-derived sqrtPriceX96 in WrapperOracle defends only the getAmountsForLiquidity() leg; the unclaimed-fee addend bypasses it entirely.

loss.notes: Components are exact ERC-20 Transfer nettings from the single anchor receipt, summed over the depleted victim addresses: the Lava aToken reserves aUSDC 0x16cb622cae7ad9fd2b0780b2026ed301414781fe, aUSDC.e 0x16cba9a6a9bb38e339d4250da0afd919c6bdbdfe, aUSDT 0x8da6bc74b2534030cd38c996c395b914990fa684, aWETH 0xec9b99c8262b72d846f0f80fce76af7d3c7c6af6 and awstETH 0xcb1332663a39f238bcd1cc7621e3e24a50251b94, plus the wrapper's own Uniswap V3 position in pool 0x8e295789c9465487074a65b1ae9ce0351172393f (25,644.648649 USDC and 49,038.308971 USDC.e) and the wrapper contract balance (1.278268 USDC), which the attacker redeemed with the LP shares he borrowed uncollateralised. Every one of the five reserves was drained to exactly zero. The 923.684256 USDC and 1,350.185377 USDC.e retained by the Uniswap V3 flash pools are financing fees paid out of the stolen funds and are therefore included in gross depletion rather than netted off; the attacker's own end balances were 77,477.425666 USDC, 96,215.533581 USDC.e, 60,349.016947 USDT, 8.525476552027716376 wstETH and 20.332763573538003060 ETH after gas. Flash-loan principals from Balancer, Aave V3 and the Uniswap V3 pools were repaid inside the transaction and are not counted. Stables are valued at par; WETH uses the DefiLlama ETH price and wstETH the DefiLlama mainnet wstETH price at the incident timestamp, both transferred in kind rather than sold, so no price impact applies.

incidents.name: MEV bot 0x05f0 unprotected swap entry point
incidents.summary: The MEV bot contract exposed selector 0xf6ebebbb, an internal swap-execution entry point, with no caller check and no output validation. A flash-loan-funded attacker called it directly with pool and amount parameters of their own choosing and moved the contract’s whole USDC, USDT, WETH and WBTC balance out through the pools it was told to trade against.

loss.notes: Components are the victim contract’s net ERC-20 balance deltas in the single exploit transaction, which is the first transaction of block 18523344. The attacker’s later transaction to the same exploit contract at block 18537100 does not touch the victim. BlockSec’s contemporaneous alert put the loss near USD 2 million; this exact netting at DefiLlama prices for the incident timestamp is higher. Nothing was recovered.

incidents.name: LML staking rewards sized at a stale stored price
incidents.summary: The LML staking implementation converts USDT-denominated rewards into LML at a stored LML/USDT price that updatePrice() refreshes at most once per 3600 seconds, while the LML paid out is sold at the live pair price with no deviation check. The token's swapBack() refills the reward source by moving LML straight out of the LML/USDT pair and calling sync(). The attacker pumped the pair with flash-loaned USDT, claimed rewards for 11 pre-staked EIP-7702 accounts at the stale price, and sold the LML back into the drained pair.

loss.notes: Net USDT depletion of the LML/USDT pair in the single exploit transaction, equal to its reserve drop. The reported ~$950k is the attacker's profit after flash-loan and swap costs. Burned and redistributed LML is not valued.

incidents.name: Cheese Bank LP oracle priced from spot pair reserves
incidents.summary: CheesePriceOracle.fetchLPAnchorPrice() values a Uniswap V2 LP token as `wETH.balanceOf(pair) * 2 * ethPrice / pair.totalSupply()`, a single-block spot read of the pair's WETH balance. Every non-LP asset in the same contract is priced through fetchAnchorPrice(), which reads Uniswap's cumulative-price accumulator over a TWAP window; the LP branch has no accumulator, no window and no sanity band. refresh() is permissionless, so an attacker could swap 20,000 ETH into the CHEESE/WETH pair, call refresh in the same transaction to write the inflated LP price into `prices`, and then borrow against LP collateral through the Comptroller's ordinary borrow() checks.

loss.notes: Reconstructed from the exploit receipt, not from reporting. Logs 193, 197 and 201 are the three Cheese Bank markets paying the attacker contract: 2068252649482 USDC units from 0x5e181bdde2fa8af7265cb3124735e9a13779c021, 1237995403809 USDT units from 0x4c2a8a820940003cfe4a16294b239c8c55f29695 and 87586864453785145669360 DAI wei from 0xa80e737ded94e8d2483ec8d2e52892d9eb94cf1f. All three are par-valued dollar stablecoins. The 21000 ETH dYdX flash loan and the 50 ETH used to buy CHEESE are attacker-supplied inputs and are not loss. Cheese Bank retained the 2833.226849227665 CHEESE/WETH UNI-V2 LP tokens the attacker had deposited into market 0x7e4956688367fb28de3c0a62193f59b1526a00e7 at log 180, but that collateral was itself attacker-supplied and, once the 20000 ETH manipulation swap was unwound inside the same transaction, worth a small fraction of the stablecoins removed, so the gross depletion is reported without netting it. No ETH-denominated market paid out in this transaction.

incidents.name: Inverse Finance YVCrv3CryptoFeed spot-balance LP valuation
incidents.summary: YVCrv3CryptoFeed.latestAnswer(), the price feed the Anchor Oracle used for the anYvCrv3Crypto collateral market, prices the Yearn share as (WBTC.balanceOf(tricrypto2) * BTC/USD + WETH.balanceOf(tricrypto2) * ETH/USD + USDT.balanceOf(tricrypto2) * USDT/USD) * 1e18 / crv3crypto.totalSupply() * vault.pricePerShare(). Every Chainlink component is sound, but the pool composition is read live, so the aggregate is whatever an imbalanced trade leaves in the pool at that instant. The contract even declares an ICurvePool interface whose only member is get_virtual_price(), the manipulation-resistant alternative, and never calls it; CRV3CRYPTO is used solely for address(). In the anchor transaction the attacker flash-borrowed 27,000 WBTC from Aave V2, added 225 WBTC as liquidity for 5,375.596969399930881565 crv3crypto, wrapped it into 4,906.754677503974414310 yvCurve-3Crypto and minted anYvCrv3Crypto, then pushed the remaining 26,775 WBTC through tricrypto2 for 75,403,376.186072 USDT. The feed answer moved from 979.618562315051433272 USD at block 14972418 to 2,831.510989208155228660 USD inside the exploit, a 2.89x inflation, and borrowAllowed let the attacker draw 10,133,949.192393802606886848 DOLA against collateral worth a fraction of it. The violated invariant is that collateral pricing used for borrow authorization must not be atomically manipulable by a market participant. The boundary test finds no parameter: the feed has no owner, no setter and no constructor argument, every address is a hardcoded constant or an inline-initialised literal, so no configured value of the deployed contract would have rejected the manipulated composition.

loss.notes: The component is the exact Borrow amount in the anchor receipt: anDOLA 0x7fcb7dac61ee35b3d4a51117a7c58d53f0a8a670 sent 10,133,949.192393802606886848 DOLA to the attack contract, and the attacker immediately swapped all of it for 9,881,355.040729892287779421 3CRV, so a near-par DOLA mark is realisable rather than a spot mark. Following the treatment used for this protocol's April 2022 record, the 4,906.754677503974414310 yvCurve-3Crypto the attacker posted as collateral is an attacker-supplied input that stayed with the protocol and is not netted from this gross figure; Inverse later liquidated it and reported the resulting net protocol loss as 5.83 million USD in DOLA. The attacker's own realised end-of-transaction proceeds, after the 27,000 WBTC Aave V2 flash loan was repaid with the 27,024.3 WBTC premium, are 53.24446541 WBTC and 99,976.294967 USDT, about 1.259 million USD at the DefiLlama WBTC price of 21,760.665102437866, which is the figure contemporaneous reporting quotes as 1.2 to 1.3 million. Nothing else in the block re-executes the defect: the attacker's only earlier transaction is the attack-contract creation one block before, and the two later calls with selector 0xc7e42b1b merely sweep the proceeds.

incidents.name: Hinkal legacy-note nullifier double-spend
incidents.summary: The legacy note circuit constrained the shielded secret only through a product involving the note scalar while deriving the public nullifier from that secret independently. An attacker could change both private factors while preserving the proved relation, obtain a fresh nullifier for the same note, and make the selected verifier accept repeated spends.

loss.notes: The loss is the exact Hinkal pool balance delta over the coherent onchain campaign, from immediately before block 25447059 through the final defect-enabled outflow in block 25448366: USDC fell from 773,098.032506 to 798.032506 and ETH fell from 10.891509399221825937 to 10.591509399221825937. This nets the attacker's 27,900 USDC and 0.02 ETH proofless deposits against 800,200 USDC and 0.32 ETH withdrawn; those deposits are campaign inputs, not later recovery. It corrects both the seed row's 797,000 USD gross-withdrawal figure and published 772,000 USDC reconciliations that omit the earlier 300 USDC and 0.3 ETH net drain.

incidents.name: WGPT sell hook burns treasury LP before crediting the deposit
incidents.summary: AiWGPTToken.transferFrom executes its treasury-funded LP removal and exact-output WGPT purchase before crediting the caller’s deposit to the pair. The hook updates pool reserves, then credits an unconsumed deposit that the caller can reclaim with skim. Repeated calls consume treasury LP and raise the WGPT price, allowing the caller to sell the retained tokens for USDT.

loss.notes: Net USDT depletion of the token contract and its WGPT/USDT pool, measured from all receipt Transfer events. Pool net change is -105212.230996130493027690 USDT and token-contract change is +22636.034519356989903313 USDT. This offsets all campaign inflows, including the attacker’s 30000 USDT treasury funding and initial swap inputs. Gross removal of treasury LP cannot be valued separately from the same transaction’s trades. Financing fees, gas and later recoveries are not deducted. Attacker reinvestment in its EXPToken/USDT pool is not another loss component.

incidents.name: Siren MinterAmm withdrawCapital ERC1155 callback reentrancy
incidents.summary: MinterAmm.withdrawCapital burned LP and snapshotted the AMM's collateral, then sent the redeemer's ERC1155 option tokens before paying collateral and had no reentrancy guard. The attacker re-entered withdrawCapital from onERC1155Received, so nested withdrawals were priced against a stale collateral balance, draining six Siren Polygon AMMs.

loss.notes: Net collateral each AMM paid to the attack contract, less collateral the attacker supplied in the same transaction, across six exploit transactions. Liquid assets at DefiLlama quotes before each leg; USDC at par; aggregate method other. ERC1155 option tokens are not valued.

incidents.name: Reaper Farm rfUSDT vault redeem without owner authorisation
incidents.summary: ReaperVaultV2 redeem(shares, receiver, owner) never verifies that the caller is owner or has the owner's share allowance, so the attacker burned a holder's rfUSDT shares and sent the underlying fUSDT to its receiver.

loss.notes: The sole attacker transaction emitted one Withdraw event for exactly 1,002.055460 fUSDT, valued at stablecoin par. A later third-party withdrawal sent the remaining assets to Reaper's rescue safe and is excluded.

incidents.name: Spectra Router arbitrary call
incidents.summary: The Router's command executor did not validate the target/parameters of the commands it dispatched, so the attacker crafted a transferFrom-style call and pulled 188,013 asdCRV out of wallets that had approved the router.

loss.notes: Gross loss in this exploit transaction. The asdCRV amount is the exact Transfer emitted by the token; the USD value is the contemporaneous amount reported by Verichains.

incidents.name: Layer3 USD live spot collateral valuation
incidents.summary: Loan.supply valued deposited BTCB with PancakeSwap Router V2's current two-token quote and minted LUSD from that quote. The successful receipt temporarily displaced the referenced BTCB/USDT reserves, so the LUSD minted against 0.001515366635982742 BTCB exceeded the independently valued collateral retained by the Loan contract.

loss.notes: The LUSD pool's archive USDT balance falls by 9,800.402958646947704433 in the incident block. The receipt decomposes that change exactly: 100.004111822928037800 USDT is paired with endogenous L3 and capitalized into 16.110436463978777246 Cake-LP minted to and retained by the pool, while 9,700.398846824019666633 USDT leaves the victim entity for the attacker helper. The Loan contract simultaneously retains the attacker's exact 0.001515366635982742-BTCB deposit. Immediately before the loss, Pancake pair 0x3f803ec2b816ea7f06ec76aa2b6f2532f9892d62 held 39,642.343651114056995536 USDT and 1.308898664806062396 BTCB, with reserve timestamp 1688739223. The reserve-implied price is the exact ratio 39,642.343651114056995536 / 1.308898664806062396, approximately $30,286.793559368329840326123063709099959686246757061248349441343945552583311207193 per BTCB; DefiLlama independently corroborates it with a preceding $30,277 observation at 1688739768. The exact collateral-credit rational is (0.001515366635982742 × 39,642.343651114056995536) / 1.308898664806062396 dollars, approximately $45.895596470763762791825835613590524256663991716609547910720118830076326619601439. Subtracting that rational from the external USDT outflow gives net loss approximately $9,654.5032503532559038411741643864094757433360082833904520892798811699236733803986. No BTCB was returned to the attacker: the collateral stayed in Loan until protocol manager transaction 0xe5dfbf3d1f27f00efee13b465d877ac7d5bef7c978016659aeb9b3ac8e9c0050 later swept the aggregate 0.001533265791594517-BTCB balance to 0x81f319f3cba6abb3ba555b6e6cf4debb1fd93568. That later protocol disposition does not change the incident-time credit. Five nested flash lenders received their USDT principal back; the six preceding calls reverted; and the next successful EOA transaction forwarded the already measured 9,464.716730420359231245-USDT proceeds without returning assets to the victim.

incidents.name: PolyDEX PLX Locker (vMToken) claimUnlocked ERC777 reentrancy
incidents.summary: vMToken.claimUnlocked (the fPLX token locker) transfers the claimable PLX before increasing _released. PLX is an ERC777-style token that calls the recipient's tokensReceived hook, so an attacker contract re-entered unlockAll()/claimUnlocked 40 times per transaction and was paid the same vested amount repeatedly. Eleven transactions with growing lock sizes drained 59.6M net PLX from the locker, which the attacker sold for USDC and WETH.

loss.notes: Net PLX depletion of the locker across the eleven reentrant transactions (88,158,559.597 out minus 28,525,877.115 locked in by the attacker contracts). Valued by the attacker's disposal: 25 sales of 59,534,251.04 PLX between blocks 15952778 and 15953416 returned 127,336.874416 USDC.e plus 119.239910666 WETH, swapped for 266,831.663730 USDC.e; total 394,168.538146 USD. The disposal crashed the PLX price, so this is a lower bound; PolyDEX reported about 500,000 USD.

incidents.name: TGBS public _burnBlock()
incidents.summary: A public state-changing token function allowed an arbitrary caller to reduce the TGBS balance held by its PancakeSwap pair, breaking the pair's reserve accounting and depleting its WBNB reserve.

loss.notes: The incident receipt shows 1,235.242777623808307005 WBNB entering PancakeSwap TGBS/WBNB pair 0x779a0e4799488d2fcac65f5fb8eb65dbbf08ce43 and 1,612.662433362706533055 WBNB leaving it, for exact net depletion of 377.419655738898226050 WBNB. Archive balances fall from 381.978233513290349616 WBNB before the incident block to 4.558577774392123566 WBNB after it, reproducing the receipt result. The same sender's preceding transaction 0xe02c6f4b38ac1063154bea7fd37ec3b61190b2ed17522dc99eca3e4caecc0827 has no WBNB or TGBS transfer into or out of this pair and is excluded from the single-transaction campaign. Gross pair depletion nets all WBNB inputs in the incident receipt; financing fees, gas, and later recovery are not deducted. The closest preceding DefiLlama BNB observation is $407.71 at 1709709892, 183 seconds before the incident.

incidents.name: DEPUSDT proxy unprotected approval
incidents.summary: The DEPUSDT vault proxy exposed an approval/authorisation entry point with no access control, so the attacker granted itself an allowance over the vault's USDT and transferred the deposits out.

loss.notes: Exact USDT transferred from the DEPUSDT proxy to the attacker, valued at stablecoin par. The separate LEVUSDC transaction is a separate incident and is excluded.

incidents.name: MetaDragon token-id transfer unrestricted minting
incidents.summary: P404Token treated any transfer value below 30,001 as an ERC-721 token ID. When the recipient was the token contract itself, _update skipped ERC-20 balance accounting, called the linked collection's burn without checking that the caller owned the NFT, and minted 9,800 MetaDragon tokens to msg.sender. The attacker repeated this over existing token IDs and sold the unbacked mint into the MetaDragon/WBNB pair in 12 transactions.

loss.notes: The 12 successful campaign receipts each contain exactly one WBNB Transfer: a payout from MetaDragon/WBNB pair 0x0a86a9cc823f8febc1d26f1f880be3c986e7c042 to attack helper 0xdaef6079cb84405dac688a9f6956c6830b7ddbc6. Those exact realised payouts sum to 301.983523984473584116 WBNB; no WBNB enters the pair from the attacker in the transaction set. The USD value uses the nearest DefiLlama BNB observation preceding the anchor.

incidents.name: Reaper Farm rfDAI vault redeem without owner authorisation
incidents.summary: ReaperVaultV2 redeem(shares, receiver, owner) never verifies that the caller is owner or has the owner's share allowance, so the attacker burned arbitrary holders' rfDAI shares and sent the underlying DAI to its receiver.

loss.notes: Two attacker transactions emitted six Withdraw events whose assets sum to exactly 465,578.315235863858364449 DAI, valued at stablecoin par.

incidents.name: DFX Finance Curve flash() reentrancy
incidents.summary: Curve.flash() was the only state-changing entry point without the contract's nonReentrant guard, so the attacker re-entered deposit() inside flashCallback and had the flash-loaned XIDR/USDC counted both as flash repayment and as a new LP deposit, then withdrew the underlying.

loss.notes: Approximate gross protocol loss reported by Numen across the DFX v2 attack.

incidents.name: Reaper Farm rfBTC vault redeem without owner authorisation
incidents.summary: ReaperVaultV2 redeem(shares, receiver, owner) never verifies that the caller is owner or has the owner's share allowance, so the attacker burned arbitrary holders' rfBTC shares and sent the underlying BTC token to its receiver.

loss.notes: Three attacker transactions emitted 11 Withdraw events whose assets sum to exactly 9.69794911 BTC. Later third-party withdrawals sent remaining assets to Reaper's rescue safe and are excluded.

incidents.name: HYPR L1StandardBridge reinitialization
incidents.summary: The HYPR L1StandardBridge implementation cleared the storage used by Initializable, leaving the deployed bridge reinitializable. The incident transaction reinitialized the bridge and released 2.57 million escrowed HYPR.

loss.notes: The transaction and commit-pinned reproduction record exactly 2,570,000 HYPR transferred from bridge custody. Rekt reported the amount as approximately $220,000; no independently reproducible incident-time HYPR price series was retained.

incidents.name: Dough Finance
incidents.summary: ConnectorDeleverageParaswap decoded caller-controlled swap targets and calldata, approved the supplied token-transfer proxy, and called the supplied target without validating either address or the function selector. The attacker therefore made the connector call WETH.transferFrom against Dough accounts that had approved it.

loss.notes: Security analyses report approximately 1.8 million USDC taken by the black-hat attacker across eight Dough account calls. The anchor transaction contains the first 596.844648055377423623 WETH withdrawal; the incident-level amount covers the full repeated attack sequence and excludes later recoveries.

incidents.name: Exactly Protocol DebtManager unvalidated-market impersonation
incidents.summary: DebtManager accepted a caller-supplied market in its permit and leverage path without checking that the Auditor listed it. A malicious market bypassed the permit, set DebtManager's effective sender to a victim, then reentered crossDeleverage with a real market to withdraw the victim's position through an attacker-controlled swap pool.

loss.notes: Exactly's post-mortem reports $7,612,038 lost by 117 accounts. The main attacker caused 97% of the campaign loss and a copycat using the same defect caused the remaining 3%.

incidents.name: SQUID migration self-sale uses manipulable minimum output
incidents.summary: SquidTokenSwap.sellSwappedTokens is public and derives its minimum output from the same PancakeSwap reserves its trade consumes. An attacker repeatedly trades around the SQUID v1-to-v2 conversion and these treasury-funded sales, controlling both legs of the spot quote and extracting WBNB. The nominal 5% slippage check has no independent price reference.

loss.notes: 167.305316006695072569 WBNB extracted across six transactions on April 8 and April 14, 2024. Each component is the combined WBNB depletion of the SQUID v1/WBNB and v2/WBNB pools after all same-transaction WBNB inputs, including attacker-supplied principal. Internal swaps between the two pools cancel. The first two transactions pay 5 WBNB each to an external flash lender, retained in gross loss. SQUID reserve transfers, intermediate purchases and burns are not valued again. Each recurrence uses a preceding BNB/USD quote. Gas, builder payments and later recovery do not reduce the measurement.

incidents.name: Rabby Wallet SwapRouter arbitrary-call allowance drain
incidents.summary: Rabby's swap router accepted caller-selected external-call targets and calldata, so the attacker made it call approved token contracts with transferFrom payloads and drain users' balances.

loss.notes: Gross positive ERC-20 Transfer logs from non-cluster addresses to the attacker EOA or either attack helper across the cited 19-transaction Ethereum campaign: 73 transfers, 19 assets, and no positive cluster outflow in those transactions. Eighteen assets use DefiLlama observations returned for the 1665480000 query; sparse SWIV coverage uses the nearest available pre-campaign-end observation at 1665400072. Every quote precedes campaign completion.

incidents.name: MEV bot 0xa47b unguarded callback
incidents.summary: The MEV bot accepted an unauthenticated Balancer flash-loan callback and delegated execution to addresses supplied through callback calldata. The attacker made that path transfer the bot's WETH to attacker-controlled code and used the proceeds in an arbitrage transaction.

loss.notes: The exploit receipt shows 187.745915823040341329 WETH leaving the bot for attacker-controlled helper 0x2d0037e6e417baef5adc0d521dd127e724279bfe. A 1 WETH Balancer flash-loan transfer into the bot and its 1 WETH repayment cancel, leaving the same exact net bot depletion. No recovery is netted.

incidents.name: Reaper Farm rfETH vault redeem without owner authorisation
incidents.summary: ReaperVaultV2 redeem(shares, receiver, owner) never verifies that the caller is owner or has the owner's share allowance, so the attacker burned arbitrary holders' rfETH shares and sent the underlying ETH to its receiver.

loss.notes: Six attacker transactions emitted 22 Withdraw events whose assets sum to exactly 60.199256562032326281 ETH. Later third-party withdrawals sent remaining assets to Reaper's rescue safe and are excluded.

incidents.name: GDS token business-logic flaw
incidents.summary: GDS transferred liquidity-pair tokens to holders during ordinary transfers without consuming a holder-specific entitlement. The attacker split GDS among 100 helper contracts, repeatedly triggered the transfer path, and redeemed the accumulated pair tokens for USDT.

loss.notes: USDT Transfer logs show the GDS/USDT pair received 3,600 USDT in the setup transaction and lost 40,852.750053127377203615 USDT in the completion transaction. The net pair depletion across the two-transaction campaign is therefore 37,252.750053127377203615 USDT. This replaces the unaudited imported $180,000 estimate.

incidents.name: Value DeFi vStake ProfitSharingRewardPool initializer never sets its initialized flag
incidents.summary: ProfitSharingRewardPool.initialize(address,address,address,address,uint256) is guarded by a notInitialized modifier that requires !initialized, but the function body never writes initialized = true; the flag is declared bool public initialized = false and no other function in the contract assigns it. The guard is therefore inert for the life of the deployment: any caller can re-run initialize at any time, and the body unconditionally sets operator = msg.sender, stakeToken = _stakeToken, reserveFund = _reserveFund and _locked = 0. governanceRecoverUnsupported(IERC20,uint256,address) is onlyOperator and refuses only the token currently stored in stakeToken, so re-initializing with a substitute stakeToken both hands the caller the operator role and lifts the one restriction on the recovery path. In the anchor the attacker EOA calls the vStake proxy 0xed517fde7f36efeab9d52e569c77491ad964f6e6 with _stakeToken set to the attacker-deployed HACKEDMONEY token 0x732126e7ec26416c31b1d89392966bfd7476e2ce and _startRewardBlock 1000000000000000000000 (satisfying require(block.number < _startRewardBlock)); operator moves from the Value DeFi deployer 0x7be4d5a99c903c437ec77a20cb6d0688cbb73c7f to the attacker in that single call, while initialized still reads false afterwards. The violated invariant is that a one-shot initializer must be callable only once on a deployed execution context; no parameter value restores it, because the flag the guard reads is never written by any reachable code path.

loss.notes: The vStake pool proxy 0xed517fde7f36efeab9d52e569c77491ad964f6e6 held exactly 10839.160048651271862327 vBSWAPBUSD ValueLiquidPair LP, 93.680122706081820564 WBNB and 17278.422722300487009949 BUSD immediately before the anchor block and zero of all three afterwards, so this is the complete depletion of the pool and no attacker-supplied input is included. The three governanceRecoverUnsupported calls that moved them are 0x9ba0454c2301ad5780795ae7477e9fa7e38226be16cc282158624479e66389b6 (LP), 0x77e68d369cae24cbac2e87252f192f7a26fd48c77e71e1b1b48803971d4b932d (WBNB) and 0x9ee8d54da43218126171bcb1615032fb692624f2c9b7f82307d1988df75f296a (BUSD). The stolen LP is reported through the underlying it released: burning all 10839.160048651271862327 LP in 0x7d0ac4536e6ff9ffd356889aca1b6c1ebc0fd8630ad2e82c7bd04624020bd29a returned exactly 7342.746839157244509784 vBSWAP and 205659.217053357174168128 BUSD, and the BUSD component here is that leg plus the 17278.422722300487009949 BUSD taken directly. vBSWAP had no DefiLlama price series and a very thin market, so it is valued at realised proceeds rather than a spot mark: the attacker sold the whole 7342.746839157244509784 vBSWAP through 1inch in 0x796fadf34c240906cf19040d9d3ec392433a5811c92c6feecc5c86622b33831e for 8790.771775341623850222 WBNB, which at the DefiLlama WBNB observation nearest the incident (634.1162697996361 USD, timestamp 1620185024) is 5574371.41 USD, an implied 759.17 USD per vBSWAP. Because the aggregate mixes realised proceeds with a spot price and par, the incident-level method is other. BUSD par is corroborated onchain: the attacker's own conversion of 205659.217053357174168128 BUSD to 325.70592941962514 WBNB implies 631.43 BUSD per WBNB against a 634.12 USD WBNB price, and 17278.422722300487009949 BUSD converted to 17275.918319362165 USDT. Value DeFi later compensated the affected stakers in full; under the gross-depletion rule that recovery does not reduce this figure. The separate 2021-05-07 Value DeFi vSafe WBNB vault incident and the 2020-11-14 Ethereum MultiStables incident are different campaigns with their own losses and are not included here.

incidents.name: Pickle Finance ControllerV4 fake-jar swap
incidents.summary: ControllerV4.swapExactJarForJar validated only approvedJarConverters for the call targets and never checked that _fromJar/_toJar were Pickle jars, so an attacker-deployed fake jar turned the controller into an arbitrary-call proxy that withdrew the real DAI strategy's cDAI.

loss.notes: Pickle reported 19,759,355 DAI drained from the pDAI jar; the reported whole-token amount is valued at stablecoin par.

incidents.name: Balancer STA deflationary-token pool drain
incidents.summary: The BPool credited swapExactAmountIn with the requested tokenAmountIn instead of the amount actually received, and exposed a permissionless gulp() that resyncs a token's recorded balance to the real one, so repeatedly swapping the 1%-transfer-fee token STA and calling gulp drove the pool's recorded STA balance to 1 wei and let 1 STA be swapped out for essentially the whole WETH side - the pool's own accounting, not any external price, is what failed.

loss.notes: Gross assets lost are the exact decreases in each token's balance at the affected pool between the block immediately before the exploit and the exploit block. Each asset is valued at CoinGecko's nearest observation before the exploit.

incidents.name: Venus zkSync uncapped wUSDM ERC-4626 oracle
incidents.summary: Venus selected an ERC4626Oracle that priced wUSDM by calling convertToAssets without bounding donation-driven appreciation. The attacker redeemed wUSDM, donated the resulting USDM directly to the vault to raise that conversion from 1.069434091624779268 to 1.763927342727284953, and used the inflated Venus valuation to liquidate one attacker-controlled account against another and extract WETH and wUSDM.

loss.notes: Measured as the exact net assets retained by the attacker-controlled recipients in the focal transaction. The EOA's WETH balance rises from zero by 86.721142851973722607 WETH and the helper's wUSDM balance rises from zero by 55,000.000000215426061874 wUSDM; the receiver retains neither asset. WETH uses the nearest DefiLlama ETH price at or before the incident. wUSDM uses its pre-exploit onchain redemption value of 1.069434091624779268 USDM per share with USDM at stablecoin par. The official later accounting of $902,159 outstanding bad debt and $716,789 net loss includes later users, liquidation fees, virtual debt, and recovery, so it is not added to this transaction-scoped amount.

incidents.name: OCA SwapHelper sellOCA recycles the sold OCA out of the OCA/USDC pair
incidents.summary: The OCA SwapHelper's public sellOCA(amount) sells the caller's OCA into the OCA/USDC PancakeSwap pair with the USDC paid to the caller, then calls OCA.recycle to pull the same OCA amount back out of the pair and sync(), so every sale removes the pair's OCA without USDC coming back in. The attacker obtained OCA untaxed by flash-swapping it directly from the pair, which OCA's liquidity-removal heuristic exempts from its 100% buy tax, then repeated buy/sellOCA cycles to shrink the OCA reserve and sold its remaining OCA for the pair's USDC.

loss.notes: Exact USDC depletion of the OCA/USDC pair 0x5779bf44cd518b05651ae38fcc066247cce21504 in the two exploit transactions: the anchor (all proceeds to the attacker EOA) and a copycat by a different actor 4053 seconds later that took the leftover USDC with the same buy/sellOCA cycle. The 8,704,860.15 USDC Moolah flash loans and every USDC buy leg are attacker inputs returned within each transaction. The pair's OCA loss (977,500.45 OCA in the anchor, recycled to the mining pool and DEAD) is the same liquidity and is not added. Ordinary direct sellOCA sales by holders between the two transactions are not counted.

incidents.name: Goledo PPI collateral priced from Swappi spot reserves
incidents.summary: Goledo (Aave v2 fork) listed PPI as 65%-LTV collateral priced by a custom feed that multiplies Pyth CFX/USD by the instantaneous WCFX/PPI reserve ratio of a Swappi pair. A flash-swapped 11M WCFX buy inflated the PPI oracle price 71x inside one transaction, letting 8.67M deposited PPI borrow the pool's xCFX, WCFX, NUT, WBTC, ETH, USDT, USDC and ABC liquidity.

loss.notes: Exact reserve outflows from the single exploit transaction. A 6,000,000 xCFX deposit made by the attack contract from its own first borrow (onBehalfOf 0xfa6b93b1bfef8bd325d88ffc61d02627505fea86) and re-borrowed in the same transaction is excluded as attacker-supplied input; the attacker's 8.67M PPI collateral left in the pool is not netted. CEX freezes of proceeds do not reduce gross loss. Prices are pre-exploit DefiLlama quotes, consistent with Goledo's own oracle at block 88464094.

incidents.name: Reaper Farm rfUSDC vault redeem without owner authorisation
incidents.summary: ReaperVaultV2 exposes the three-argument ERC-4626 exit path redeem(shares, receiver, owner) (and the matching withdraw) but never checks that msg.sender is owner or holds an allowance from owner, so any caller could burn an arbitrary holder’s vault shares and have the underlying asset paid to an address of their choosing. The attacker contract called redeem with each depositor as owner and its own address as receiver; the three owners drained in the anchor transaction had an allowance of exactly 0 to the attacker contract at block 44045360.

loss.notes: Scoped to the rfUSDC vault 0xcda5dea176f2df95082f4dadb96255bdb2bc7c7d, the only Reaper vault that executes in the anchor transaction. Its Withdraw(caller,receiver,owner,assets,shares) log stream from creation to block 44060000 contains 13 events with caller != owner attributable to the attacker, spread over three transactions at blocks 44045361, 44045487 and 44045900, and their assets sum to exactly 596,685.496653 USDC; the attacker receiver 0x2c177d20b1b1d68cc85d3215904a7bb6629ca954 bridged out that exact amount (596685496653 units) at block 44046708 in transaction 0x73a62117b6b88dc6e8384dce596392f995f1f37a10f6dc05f4bbf881e4be6bc5. The 14 later third-party redeems on the same vault (blocks 44052039-44053339, caller 0x1e71aee6081f62053123140aacc7a06021d77348, receiver the safe 0x539ef36c804e4d735d8cab69e8e441c12d4b88e0, about 25,600 USDC) are a rescue sweep of the remaining balances and are excluded; that receiver has made no outbound transfer. The same campaign also drained the sibling vaults rfETH 0x58c60b6df933ff5615890ddddcdd280bad53f1c1, rfWFTM 0xa6313302b3ceff2727f19aaa30d7240d5b3cd9cd, rfBTC 0xeb7761d05a31769d35073f703dd3a41f3ca9bd3d, rfDAI 0x77dc33dc0278d21398cb9b16cbff99c1b712a87a and rfUSDT 0xa9a9db466685f977f9ecee347958bcef90498177, which brings the widely reported campaign total to about USD 1.7M; those vaults are separate deployments with distinct runtime code hashes, none of them executes in this anchor transaction, and their value is not counted here.

incidents.name: Belt Finance beltBUSD Ellipsis LP mispricing
incidents.summary: StrategyEllipsisImpl.eps3ToWant() values the strategy's staked 3EPS position as the raw sum of the BUSD, USDC and USDT ERC-20 balances held by the Ellipsis StableSwap pool, scaled by the strategy's LP share. That sum is not the pool's StableSwap invariant and moves with any single-transaction swap, so wantLockedTotal() is an attacker-controlled spot quantity. MultiStrategyTokenImpl consumes it unfiltered: _deposit() mints beltBUSD shares from the calcPoolValueInToken() delta and _withdraw() redeems shares at pool * shares / totalSupply, paying out of whichever strategy holds the most assets. Cycling deposit -> Ellipsis exchange() -> withdraw inside one transaction therefore minted shares against a depressed Ellipsis valuation and redeemed them against an inflated one, draining BUSD out of the Venus strategy.

loss.notes: Measured from the victim vault's own accounting. beltBUSD 0x9171bf7c050ac8b4cf7835e51f7b4841dfb2ccd0 reports calcPoolValueInToken() = 221115445.035265077214489032 BUSD on 217103856.217843203380419587 shares at block 7838861 (immediately before the first successful attack transaction) and 174161472.163601099685723562 BUSD on 217091891.155444809406501592 shares at block 7839266 (immediately after the last one), i.e. price per share falls from 1.018477740963737758 to 0.802247708270668928 BUSD. The raw pool drop is 46953972.871663977528765470 BUSD; 9598.943888427119078496 BUSD of that is the value of the 11965.062398393973917995 shares legitimately redeemed by other users inside the same 20-minute window, leaving 46944373.927775550409686974 BUSD of exploit-attributable depletion. Per-strategy, bVenusBUSD 0x53a53a9e10abe9d18d009f6f962f51dc8b1d6edc falls from 66067863.16 to 6063192.61 BUSD while bEllipsisBUSD 0x2ec2ddd12566b66f4da248b1ecdee8619b5c56cd rises from 65923134.14 to 78973831.82 BUSD; the other four strategies are unchanged. The attacker-supplied PancakeSwap flash-loan principal is repaid inside each transaction and is not counted. Of the depletion, 6234753.171048180404312114 BUSD reached attacker address 0x8937dd570e3cb32df77e39c0805d17e88f9d14ae and the remainder was dissipated as Ellipsis imbalance value and PancakeSwap flash-loan fees paid out of vault assets; both are gross victim depletion and are not netted out. BUSD is valued at par. Belt's later user compensation is a recovery and does not reduce the exploit-time gross loss. The 4Belt Vyper pool's 5.51% mark-down is a downstream consequence of this same beltBUSD depletion and is not counted separately.

incidents.name: DAO Maker vesting unprotected init()
incidents.summary: The vesting implementation's init() had no caller authentication or one-time initialization guard, so calling it again made the attacker the proxy's owner. The attacker then used the owner-only emergencyExit() path to sweep the proxy's vested sale tokens.

loss.notes: SlowMist reports nearly $4 million taken across the DeRace, Coinspaid, Capsule Coin, and Showcase vesting proxies. The reported figure is treated as the gross campaign loss.

incidents.name: RADT DAO wrapper unauthenticated withdraw
incidents.summary: The RADT-DAO token (TWN) calls wrapper withdraw(from,to,amount) on every transfer, and the token's fallback lets the wrapper move any holder's balance. The wrapper, a proxy to implementation 0x9122191d7b2ccf11a2600de4eafd6b8cd3d03a62, never checks that withdraw's caller is the token. With cc (slot 0x1a) false, a direct call with to = the RADT/USDT pair and a pair USDT balance above reserve runs the pair-payout branch, which transfers RADT out of the pair to the named LP holder and fee recipients. The attacker stripped the pair's RADT, called sync() and sold RADT into the remaining USDT.

loss.notes: Exact net BSC-USD depletion of the RADT/USDT pair 0xaf8fb60f310dcd8e488e4fa10c48907b7abf115e. Source-1: 95305.580256723571814836 USDT out minus the attacker's 1000 USDT buy and 1 USDT balance nudge = 94304.580256723571814836; the DODO flash loan of 243673.2130680496 USDT is repaid in the same tx. Three later direct wrapper withdraw calls repeated the drain on the depleted pair: 0x2a8b13da919c35f9d50980db02b7af8f0346df313f342393b5bd5178f8f5a795 (block 21581514, 139.947367702162221125 USDT), 0x2e4a4eda9b168e9dfdc6768c75daba7b509b91ab5d5383173f4e4337721427b8 (21581562, 9.813802445018996652) and 0x112c387548f930115fdbe771e93b8030d2280ddaf1ff9422fb23c5f0d121e294 (21617521, 4.979538374436752712); a fourth, 0x35f01ebce53727872ef601d30fcbb73e9f53f62ea8e5a06988a122b643f129ff (21625307), moved no USDT. USDT is at par.

incidents.name: Opyn ETH put double exercise
incidents.summary: oToken.exercise(uint256,address[]) loops over the caller-supplied vault array and calls _exercise() once per vault, and _exercise() settles the ETH underlying leg with require(msg.value == amtUnderlyingToPay) against the same unchanged msg.value on every iteration while crediting vault.underlying to each vault. One ETH payment therefore exercised the put against several vaults, paying out each vault's USDC collateral, and removeUnderlying() then returned the single ETH payment from the attacker's own vault.

loss.notes: Exact gross depletion of third-party vault collateral, summed from the amtCollateralToPay field of every Exercise event whose vaultExercisedFrom is not an attacker helper, across the fourteen defect-executing transactions between blocks 10590876 and 10592517. USDC is valued at par. The victim vaults were credited an equal amount of vault.underlying ETH by the same buggy loop, but that credit is unbacked because each attacker withdrew the single real ETH payment from their own vault with removeUnderlying(), so it does not offset the depletion. oTokens the attackers bought on Uniswap V1 and the collateral of their own vaults are attacker-supplied inputs and are excluded. Opyn's later reimbursement of affected vault owners is a recovery and does not reduce gross depletion. Three independent senders exploited the same defect in the same six-hour window against byte-identical sibling oToken series; they are covered here as one campaign, matching the single 371,260 USDC figure Opyn reported, and no other record claims any part of this loss.

incidents.name: PerpPair same-actor virtual PnL realization
incidents.summary: PerpPair let one economic actor provide leveraged virtual liquidity, trade against that same virtual reserve state, and immediately realize the resulting LP PnL as withdrawable Vault collateral. addLiquidity records the LP's virtual balances and debts, trade moves the shared virtual curve, calcPnL marks the actor's combined LP and trader positions against that moved state, and realizePnL credits the positive result to real collateral without an independent realization price, delay, or separation between the LP and trader. The violated invariant is that a participant must not be able to turn a self-created virtual counterparty loss into a claim on scarce vault collateral.

loss.notes: The Vault receives exactly 30,000 + 15,000 + 10,000 + 5,000 = 60,000 USDC and sends 183,283.399597 + 42,364.335584 = 225,647.735181 USDC in the sole successful loss receipt, for gross depletion of 165,647.735181 USDC. Its archive USDC balance falls from 165,647.735882 to 0.000701, exactly the same net change, so no unrelated same-block adjustment is required. The 60,000 USDC is genuine collateral consideration retained by the victim. The external financing source receives 60,030 USDC after supplying 60,000, leaving 165,617.735181 USDC as attacker proceeds; the 30-USDC financing premium explains why proceeds are lower than gross victim loss and is not subtracted again. Later approval and bridge deposits move all proceeds downstream, do not touch the Vault, and are excluded from the exploit-time boundary.

incidents.name: LULA reward recycle confiscates and re-syncs the LULA/USDT pair reserve
incidents.summary: The LULA token funds its referral reward payouts by confiscating liquidity from its own AMM pair. LULA.recycle(uint256) computes `maxTake = balanceOf[uniswapV2Pair] / 3`, moves `min(amount, maxTake)` LULA from the PancakeSwap LULA/USDT pair 0xf0b36389a12a28be1280c0ec2a4bbc76889d6a96 to the rental contract with an internal `_basicTransfer`, then calls `IUniswapV2Pair.sync()` so the pair adopts the reduced reserve. The pair's constant product is therefore reducible on the token side, at a caller-chosen moment, with no compensating movement on the USDT side, and the rental contract 0x377a015f44c3fdf71060e94648edc9e0316c7f1a exposes it to any account holding reward credit through a permissionless claimTeamReward(). The attacker flash-loaned 197,050,832.75 USDT, bought the entire LULA float out of the pair into the fee-exempt owner address so no buy tax or cooldown was recorded, then drove 41 claimTeamReward/recycle iterations that took the pair's remaining 24,022.132677570768 LULA while its USDT reserve stayed at 197.6M, and finally sold the recycled LULA back into the now token-empty pair, recovering the flash loan plus the pair's whole USDT reserve.

loss.notes: Gross depletion of the victim pair 0xf0b36389a12a28be1280c0ec2a4bbc76889d6a96, measured from its own balances: USDT 591841.327760739761309679 at block 112655389 and 181.576724119654205222 at block 112655390, a fall of exactly 591659.751036620107104457 USDT, which the receipt's Transfer logs confirm as 197050774.696543 USDT in and 197642434.447580 USDT out within the single exploit transaction. Attacker-supplied inputs are excluded by construction: the 197,050,832.75 USDT that entered the pair was flash-loaned campaign input and left again in the same transaction. Financing costs are not netted off, so the attacker's own realised profit is smaller: EOA 0x2677806d48325ced7533c54b86ed5e99b129a4ed went from 107.755447197024975180 to 578403.663035258025501958 USDT, a gain of 578295.907588061000526778 USDT, and the 13363.84 USDT difference is flash-loan and swap cost. Not valued: the 7997208.894795931 LULA the pair also lost, because the same transaction left the pair holding 181.58 USDT against 4749.05 LULA, so that quantity had no realisable value at any price and marking it would inflate the loss.

incidents.name: Reaper Farm rfWFTM vault redeem without owner authorisation
incidents.summary: ReaperVaultV2 redeem(shares, receiver, owner) never verifies that the caller is owner or has the owner's share allowance, so the attacker burned arbitrary holders' rfWFTM shares and sent the underlying WFTM to its receiver.

loss.notes: Three attacker transactions emitted 14 Withdraw events whose assets sum to exactly 1,003,068.399671123969333133 WFTM. Later third-party withdrawals sent remaining assets to Reaper's rescue safe and are excluded.

incidents.name: Olympus BondFixedExpiryTeller unvalidated bond redemption
incidents.summary: BondFixedExpiryTeller.redeem() trusted the caller-supplied bond token's underlying and expiry values without verifying that the token was created by the teller. The attacker supplied a forged bond token, burned its arbitrary balance, and made the teller transfer its real OHM reserves.

loss.notes: The exploit receipt contains one asset outflow: exactly 30,437.077948152 OHM transferred from BondFixedExpiryTeller to the attack helper.

incidents.name: MARA proxy unauthenticated swap entry point
incidents.summary: The MARA proxy exposes an unauthenticated payable entry point (selector 0x5fc985ea) that runs caller-supplied swap paths with the contract's own funds, letting the attacker skew the MARA pair inside a DODO flash loan and sell into it.

loss.notes: The exploit receipt records exactly 8.8 WBNB transferred to the attacker EOA after the 11 WBNB DODO flash loan was repaid.

incidents.name: MinimalForwarder unguarded execute on BSC
incidents.summary: KiloEx's BSC MinimalForwarder exposes a public execute((address,address,uint256,uint256,uint256,bytes),bytes) entry point that relays any request with a valid signature but omits the keeper and approved-router authorization enforced by its other relay entry point. Because the request chooses its own signer and the downstream delegate trusts msg.sender == the forwarder without checking the appended ERC-2771 sender, the attacker used a self-generated signer to reach the privileged price-and-trade path, set artificial prices, and trade against KiloEx's USDT vault.

loss.notes: Three calls using the unguarded forwarder entry point define the BSC campaign. In the first two, KiloEx USDT vault 0xef7af0804aab3885da59a8236fabfa19ddc6cf48 loses a transaction-local net 892947.452212280000000000 and 61974.379910380000000000 USDT. In the third, the attacker directly relays USDT.transfer through the forwarder and removes 4306.800000000000000000 USDT of accumulated KiloEx fees. The resulting gross KiloEx outflow is 959228.632122660000000000 USDT; the attacker EOA receives 959217.079253360000000000 USDT, with the difference going to flash-loan and protocol fees. This record covers BSC only and does not include the separately recorded Base loss or the out-of-scope opBNB leg. Later recovery under the cross-chain bounty agreement is not netted out of the exploit-time gross loss. Base leg of the same campaign (USDC component): Three exploit transactions (blocks 28933730, 28933848, 28935593) net 3,323,209.390248 USDC out of the KiloEx USDC liquidity pool 0xdf5acc616cd3ea9556ec340a11b54859a393ebbb, whose USDC balance falls from 3,323,951.604434 at block 28933729 to 1,555.175358 at block 28935593 (the residual difference is unrelated third-party deposits between the exploit transactions). Of that outflow the attacker EOA 0x00fac92881556a90fdb19eae9f23640b95b4bcbd keeps 3,323,170.888033 USDC; 15 USDC is the Uniswap V3 flash-loan fee and 23.502215 USDC is a KiloEx vault fee. This record covers the Base leg only; the BSC leg is a separate record and opBNB is out of the corpus, so the widely reported ~7.5M campaign figure is not used here. Between 2025-04-15 and 2025-04-18 the attacker returned the proceeds under a 10% bounty deal (on Base: 305.536342416848900260 ETH, 10,551.589691 USDC, 232.193079 USDT and 0.090531 USDbC to 0xd38a22f5330f45162f13086d6ccbde0335c1ae9e). Recovery is not netted out of the exploit-time gross figure.

incidents.name: Popsicle Finance Sorbetto reward-accounting exploit
incidents.summary: SorbettoFragola transferred LP shares without synchronizing the recipient's per-share fee debt. The same shares could therefore be moved through fresh addresses, each credited with historical fees, and the duplicated rewards collected from vault liquidity.

loss.notes: Halborn reports approximately $20.7 million drained from the Sorbetto Fragola pools. BlockSec reports over $20 million and the rounded six-asset basket recorded here. The total is the gross campaign loss across all eight vaults executed in the selected transaction.

incidents.name: Quixotic ExchangeV4 missing buyer authorization
incidents.summary: ExchangeV4.fillSellOrder validates only the seller signature, then pulls ERC-20 payment from the caller-supplied buyer without buyer authorization. The attacker signed sales of a fake ERC-1155 token and named allowance-holding wallets as buyers, draining OP and WETH.

loss.notes: Exact victim debits across 891 successful calls, including the 2.5% marketplace fee. No attacker input is subtracted from victims: payment comes directly from the named buyers. Later recovery, swaps and bridge transfers are excluded. Optimism WETH is valued at the contemporaneous Ethereum WETH quote (1:1 ETH units).

incidents.name: Market.xyz transient Curve LP collateral price
incidents.summary: The miMATIC market accepted a Curve/Beefy LP collateral value read while the Curve pool was inside remove_liquidity, allowing loans against a transiently inflated virtual price.

loss.notes: The sole successful loss receipt sends 249,000 and 66,000 miMATIC from market 0x3dc7e6ff0fb79770fa6fb05d1ea4deacce823943 and returns 65,000 and 15,000 through two linked self-liquidations: exact depletion is 315,000 - 80,000 = 235,000 miMATIC. Its archive balance falls from 250,027.800262910883221624 to 15,027.800262910883221624, and no other transaction in the block touches that reserve. Seized mmooCurvestMATIC-MATIC-4 collateral-market shares remain with the borrower helpers as consideration; the 95,000-miMATIC in-receipt sale and the EOA's retained 140,000 miMATIC are downstream disposition, not separate losses. The imported $180,000 estimate measured proceeds rather than gross victim depletion.

incidents.name: SIR vault uniswapV3SwapCallback caller check on stale transient storage
incidents.summary: The SIR vault authorises uniswapV3SwapCallback by comparing msg.sender against an address it keeps in EIP-1153 transient storage, and that record is not cleared once the swap it was written for has completed. The attacker created a Uniswap V3 pool against a token of its own, drove one mint through the vault so that its own address ended up in the transient record, and then called Vault.uniswapV3SwapCallback directly three times, once per token, making the vault transfer out its USDC, WBTC and WETH.

loss.notes: Components are the vault’s net ERC-20 deltas in the single exploit transaction, and each equals the amount argument of one of the three direct uniswapV3SwapCallback calls. The v1 snapshot carried USD 1,781,486 for this row; that figure is not supported on chain and is about five times the measured loss, which matches the roughly USD 355,000 reported at the time. The attacker EOA sent nine transactions in total; only this one touches the vault, the rest being the exploit-contract creation and the subsequent disposal swaps. Nothing was recovered.

incidents.name: SpankChain LedgerChannel reentrancy
incidents.summary: LCOpenTimeout transferred the channel's ETH and then called an attacker-controlled token before deleting the channel state, so the token's transfer callback could repeatedly re-enter LCOpenTimeout and withdraw the same ETH balance.

loss.notes: SpankChain's post-mortem reports 165.38 ETH drained (about $38,000) and about $4,000 of BOOTY immobilized. This records the loss at exploit time; the attacker's later return of funds does not reduce the incident-time amount.

incidents.name: Cover Protocol Blacksmith stale-cache infinite mint
incidents.summary: Blacksmith copied a Pool struct to memory before updatePool() advanced accRewardsPerToken in storage, then calculated the miner's rewardWriteoff from the stale copy. Leaving a tiny LP balance amplified the gap, and later reward claims minted unbounded COVER.

loss.notes: Rekt reports $9.4 million taken across six exploiters using the same Blacksmith stale-cache defect. The anchored transaction is the campaign's first major loss-finalizing mint. The later $3.2 million recovery is separate from exploit-time gross loss.

incidents.name: RareStakingV1 universal Merkle-root update
incidents.summary: RareStakingV1.updateMerkleRoot() attempted to restrict callers with require(msg.sender != owner() || msg.sender != 0xc2F394a45e994bc81EfF678bDE9172e10f7c8ddc). Because the owner and fixed address were distinct, at least one inequality was true for every possible caller, making Merkle-root replacement permissionless. The attacker deployed a helper, set the root to keccak256(abi.encodePacked(helper, the staking proxy's full RARE balance)), and called claim() with that amount and an empty proof in the same transaction, draining the proxy.

loss.notes: The RARE balance of staking proxy 0x3f4d749675b3e48bccd932033808a7079328eb48 is exactly 11907874.713019104529057960 RARE immediately before the anchor and zero afterward. The claim calldata, TokensClaimed event, and RARE Transfer log all independently record that full amount. This is gross asset loss from the staking proxy; later movement and sale of the same tokens are attacker realization and are not added again. DefiLlama's nearest historical RARE observation is 0.061452 USD at timestamp 1753689540, 1379 seconds before the exploit, valuing the loss at 731762.71686445 USD. The seed row's 730000 USD amount is a rounded estimate.

incidents.name: WiseLending empty-market donation/rounding inflation (second incident)
incidents.summary: The attacker reduced the PLP-stETH-Dec2025 lending market to a tiny share base, donated pool tokens, and repeatedly exercised asymmetric deposit/withdraw rounding to inflate the collateral value of a second position, which then borrowed assets from five other WiseLending markets.

loss.notes: The exploit receipt records the exact gross borrow outflows from WiseLending: 104.066616635764896511 wstETH, 92.012091781801765194 WETH, 9,000 USDC, 2,000 USDT, and 5,000 DAI. The latest CoinGecko WETH and wstETH observations before the transaction plus stablecoin-par valuation produce $565,709.49.

incidents.name: RWAVault ERC-4626 withdraw override without allowance spend
incidents.summary: RWAVault.withdraw(uint256,address,address) overrides OpenZeppelin's ERC4626.withdraw and bypasses ERC4626._withdraw, which is the only place the base implementation performs 'if (caller != owner) _spendAllowance(owner, caller, shares)'. The override reads _depositInfos[owner], computes the share and principal reductions, and then calls _burn(owner, shares) and SafeERC20.safeTransfer(asset, receiver, assets) with no check that msg.sender is the owner or holds an ERC-20 allowance from the owner. Any external caller can therefore name an arbitrary owner and an arbitrary receiver and take that depositor's position out of the vault.
