The invariant broken is that an ERC-4626 vault may only move a share owner's assets on the owner's own authority or against an allowance the owner granted. No parameter restores the check: the allowance spend is absent from the compiled code, and the phase and withdrawalStartTime gates that the override does enforce were satisfied by the vault's normal Matured state. RWAVault.redeem has the same omission.

loss.notes: Exact depositor depletion in the single exploit transaction. The vault clone 0xb9c7c84a1aa0dd40b5b38aae815ad0cdd2e5f88a held 398,656.303037 USDC at block 24979315 and 0.830585 USDC at block 24979316. Of the 398,655.472452 USDC that left it, 392,763.999994 was routed to the attacker's contract 0x50c140c2f705fa9d0bd0f4f253bacf4087588d17 as the receiver of the eight unauthorised withdraw calls, against 392,764.000000 of burned shares, and that is the loss recorded here. The remaining 5,891.472458 USDC is the pending interest that _claimRemainingInterest paid to the eight rightful depositors themselves, so it is not stolen value and is excluded. The attacker's own gross proceeds were the same 392,763.999994 USDC, of which 5,000.000000 was swapped through Uniswap V2 into 2.195959995966763304 WETH paid to the block builder 0x4838b106fce9647bdf1e7877bf73ce8b0bad5f97; that payment is a bribe and METHODOLOGY does not deduct it from gross depletion. The attacker EOA 0x7137804200a073f616d92e87007f1f100100b56a ended the transaction with 387,763.999994 USDC. USDC is valued at par. The seed row's figure of 398,655 and the DeFiHackLabs header's 398,655.47 are the total vault outflow including the interest returned to the owners.

incidents.name: Aperture Finance arbitrary call approval drain
incidents.summary: The closed-source Aperture router forwarded caller-supplied call targets and calldata without validation, letting the attacker make the contract invoke ERC-20 transferFrom() and ERC-721 transfers against the standing token and Uniswap V3 position approvals users had granted it.

loss.notes: BlockSec reports approximately $3.67 million of gross assets lost across the Aperture campaign on Ethereum, Arbitrum, and Base. The structured asset component is the exact WBTC amount transferred from a victim in the selected Ethereum transaction; it is only one component of the reported cross-chain total. No recovery is netted from the exploit-time loss.

incidents.name: Nomad Bridge
incidents.summary: Replica proxy: a beacon upgrade + re-initialization on 2022-06-21T18:39:29Z set committedRoot to 0x00, making every unproven message 'proven'. Nomad's UpgradeBeaconProxy emits no EIP-1967 Upgraded event; the change is the Upgrade(address) event on the hard-coded UpgradeBeacon.

loss.notes: The approximately $190 million gross loss covers the permissionless withdrawal campaign caused by the same Replica authentication defect. Nomad's public hack dataset preserves the campaign transactions and events; Mandiant reports more than $190 million removed. The structured 100 WBTC component is the exact loss in the code-age anchor transaction. Subsequent recoveries are separate from exploit-time gross loss.

incidents.name: LBP addLp hashrate credit from flash-inflated pair reserves
incidents.summary: LBP's add-liquidity mining credit is derived from the live PancakeSwap LBP/USDT pair state inside the same transaction. LBP._settlePendingLpAdd passes the pair's post-mint USDT reserve and LP totalSupply into LBPHashrate.notifyCredit, which mints 2 * userLpDelta * currentRUsdt / currentTotalLp of hashrate, and LBP._stagePending records the credit recipient as whatever address last sent LBP to the pair without excluding the pair itself. The attacker flash-borrowed 41,861,104.64 USDT, swapped 15,000,000 USDT into the pair and then added liquidity with a further 5,790,511.65 USDT, lifting the pair's USDT reserve from 439,363.60 to roughly 21.1 million by settle time, and had 10,737,390.51 hashrate credited to the pair address; the ensuing auto-harvest called LBP.mintReward and minted 115,092.77 fresh LBP straight into the pair's own token balance, an unsynced surplus PancakeSwap accounts as swap input, which the attacker swapped back out for the pair's USDT.

loss.notes: The component is the exact net USDT depletion of the LBP/USDT pair 0x00e3ea08fd8cbad955ec5d2292ad637670c31524 in the single exploit transaction, summed over the receipt's USDT Transfer logs and confirmed by getReserves(): 439,363.604173946711436972 USDT at block 104727183 against 61,721.065999847161634108 at block 104727184. The 41,861,104.641678089199196186 USDT of Moolah and PancakeSwap-Vault flash liquidity was attacker-supplied and repaid in full in the same transaction, so it is not loss. This is realised, not marked: the attacker's residual 377,642.570850 USDT was immediately swapped to 610.555786330933864102 WBNB, of which 5 BNB went to builder 0x4848489f0b2bedd788c696e2d79b6b69d7484848 and 605.555786330933864102 BNB to 0x515788797914cb663114aeb806b3cfb6096f6d1a; the builder payment does not reduce gross depletion. At the DefiLlama WBNB price of USD 601.9086 that proceeds leg marks at USD 367,499, which is the USD 367k figure the seed row and the DeFiHackLabs header carry; the USDT par figure recorded here is the victim-side measurement. Not counted: the attacker also retained 23,218.051024950574782538 LBP/USDT LP tokens, 25.3 percent of the post-exploit LP supply, a dilution claim on the remaining reserves rather than an extraction, and the 131,347.6 LBP the pair received is freshly minted unbacked supply rather than compensation.

incidents.name: 0VIX VGHSTOracle donatable vault share price
incidents.summary: VGHSTOracle.latestRoundData() returns price = convertVGHST(1 ether) * ghstFeed.latestRoundData().answer / 10**vGHSTDecimals, multiplying the Chainlink GHST/USD answer by the vGHST vault's live GHST-per-share rate with no bound, time average or sanity check, and reusing the GHST feed's startedAt and updatedAt for a multiplier that has no update time at all. convertVGHST() divides the GHST the vault controls by its share supply, so a bare GHST transfer into the vault raises it in the same transaction. Inside the anchor the attacker sent 1,656,000 GHST to the vGHST vault 0x51195e21bdae8722b29919db56d95ef51faeca6c and the rate went from 1.038332409239877123 to 1.786527556471688230 GHST per share, so the 0VIX oracle 0x1c312b14c129eabc4796b0165a2c470b659e5f01 reported a 72 percent higher ovGHST collateral value and the Comptroller authorised borrows and liquidations against collateral that did not exist. Boundary test: VGHSTOracle holds no storage at all - both vGHST and ghstFeed are compile-time constants and the contract has no owner, initializer or setter - so there is no parameter value at which the deployed code is correct. This is the same defect shape already admitted for Cream Finance's PriceOracleProxy yVault branch and for Lodestar's plvGLP share price, and unlike a genuine market move the manipulated quantity is a contract-internal accounting ratio the attacker wrote to directly.

loss.notes: Exact victim depletion: for each of the ten 0VIX markets the net movement of that market's own underlying across the single campaign transaction, taken from the receipt's Transfer logs and, for oMATIC, from the non-reverted native value transfers in the callTracer trace. Every market is net negative and the attacker's own flash-loaned USDT and USDC collateral deposits are netted inside the same measurement, so no attacker-supplied input is counted. The ovGHST market's entire 183,870.634805052795710012 vGHST collateral left it and is valued at the unmanipulated pre-attack rate convertVGHST(1e18) = 1.038332409239877123 GHST per share times the DefiLlama GHST price 1.12, not at the 1.786527556471688230 rate the attacker's donation produced. This total exceeds the roughly 2 million USD commonly reported because that figure is the attacker's own realised proceeds - the exploit sender 0x702ef63881b5241ffb412199547bcd0c6910a970 ends the transaction up exactly 1,453,546.066478 USDC, 584,444.536038 USDT and 9,565.867204501279 GHST, about 2,048,704 USD at the same quotes. The gap is the attacker's cost of the manipulation: 1,656,000 GHST bought at heavy slippage and pushed into the vGHST vault, of which the vault retains 824,430.2286398828 GHST that accrued to remaining vGHST holders, plus Aave and Balancer flash-loan fees and swap costs. Financing fees do not reduce gross victim depletion. USDC, USDT and DAI are valued at par; WETH and WBTC use the DefiLlama coingecko series because the Polygon token addresses have no series; every quote is the nearest DefiLlama sample at or before the anchor.

incidents.name: Sperax USDs non-rebasing migration reinterprets credits as tokens
incidents.summary: The USDs implementation keeps two balance representations: rebasing accounts store scaled credits in _creditBalances and divide by rebasingCreditsPerToken, while non-rebasing (contract) accounts are flagged by nonRebasingCreditsPerToken[account] = 1 and have _creditBalances read back as plain token units. The lazy migration that _isNonRebasingAccount() runs the first time a transfer touches an unclassified contract account sets that flag without rescaling the account's stored credit balance, so a balance accumulated while the address was still an EOA is reinterpreted at a factor of rebasingCreditsPerToken/1e18. The attacker sent 11 USDs to a counterfactual Gnosis Safe address, deployed the Safe, and let the first transferFrom() out of it trigger the migration: with rebasingCreditsPerToken = 890714019687982181365620786, the Safe's 11 USDs became 9,797,854,205.567804 USDs of spendable balance, which was then sold into Arbitrum liquidity.

loss.notes: Realised proceeds, not a par valuation of the fabricated USDs. The campaign sold 310,004 USDs out of the Safe's fabricated 9.79785e9 USDs balance across 23 transactions between blocks 57803530 and 57840578; the attacker's own selling moved USDs against USDC.e/USDT/WETH on Camelot, Curve and 1inch routes, so only the assets actually received are counted. Components are the exact ERC-20 and native-value credits to the attacker set (EOA 0x26c1fd9f..., proceeds wallet 0x4afcd19b..., exploit Safe 0x5c978df5...): 149,804.349817 USDT less the 10.999083 USDT realised on the attacker's own 11 USDs seed leg in the anchor transaction, 107,946.413734 USDC.e, and 29.420036549112749275 ETH (24.4887 native ETH unwrapped through 1inch plus 5.931308 WETH). The 10,007.133196 USDT the Safe routed into Stargate (received back as 9,986.758893 S*USDT and staked) is counted once, as USDT. Gas and DEX fees are not deducted. USDs itself is excluded from the components because the fabricated units never had backing.

incidents.name: CUT valuePreservationByRemoveLP pays compensation at the live PancakeSwap spot price
incidents.summary: CUT 0x7057f3b0f4d0649b428f0d8378a8a0e7d21d36a7 routes every transfer through the deal-type logic contract 0x7b2e7cb89824236cb7096cde7a153af30f3ecbaf, whose valuePreservationByRemoveLP(address,uint256) (selector 0x70f88861) tops up a liquidity remover with extra CUT so that the USDT value of the withdrawn position is preserved. It computes that top-up from a USDT-denominated pool value held in registry 0x0917914b0a70ee7f1f2460fcd487696856e31154 and converts it to CUT at the instantaneous reserve ratio of the PancakeSwap USDT/CUT pair 0x83681f67069a154815a0c6c2c97e2daca6ed3249, which it reads through token0(), token1() and getReserves() in the same call, with no averaging, deviation bound, or same-transaction guard. The conversion is therefore algebraically a constant times the pair's live CUT reserve: across all ten invocations inside the anchor transaction the excess paid over the amount passed in equals 0.283287608274 times the CUT reserve read in that same call, constant to twelve significant figures while the reserve grows from 757,225.933923 to 5,083,077.535048 CUT and the spot price falls from 2.3384 to 0.0538 USDT per CUT. The attacker exploits exactly that: inside one transaction it adds liquidity asymmetrically, dumps CUT into the pair to crush the price, and removes liquidity, so a fixed USDT obligation is settled in 4.54 times more CUT than it was worth, and the freshly issued CUT is sold back into the pair for the LPs' USDT. The violated invariant is that a payout denominated in one asset must not be converted at a price the payee can set in the same transaction. No parameter value restores it: an identical eth_call against the same deployed bytecode at block 42131696 returns the amount unchanged, and the defect is the unguarded spot conversion itself, not any configured value.

loss.notes: Loss is the USDT the PancakeSwap USDT/CUT pair 0x83681f67069a154815a0c6c2c97e2daca6ed3249 lost to the campaign, summed over the USDT Transfer logs of the three exploit transactions: 1,271,656.254497 in 0x2c123d08..., 159,616.865472 in 0xce6e474d... and 8,290.512970 in 0x6262c0f1..., total 1,439,563.632938965392877836 USDT, against which the pair received 955,130,899.07835 CUT that the campaign itself created. That is the whole of the USDT that left the pair in those three transactions; 1,416,033.632938965392877836 reached the attacker's beneficiary 0x5766d1f03378f50c7c981c014ed5e5a8124f38a4 and 23,530 was the flash-swap fee retained by the funding pair 0x16b9a82891338f9ba80e2d6970fdda79d1eb0dae, and under the gross-depletion rule the fee is not deducted. No flash-loan principal is included: the loans are borrowed and repaid inside each transaction and net to zero at the lender. The pair's raw USDT balance falls further, from 1,454,183.768693 at block 42131696 to 1,419.854250 at block 42132019, but the extra 13,200.28 is ordinary third-party trading in the intervening blocks and is excluded. Binance-Peg BSC-USD is valued at par.

incidents.name: Morpho Blue PAXG/USDC oracle decimal misconfiguration
incidents.summary: The PAXG/USDC market selected a MorphoChainlinkOracleV2 deployed with both token-decimal constructor arguments set to 8, although PAXG has 18 decimals and USDC has 6. Its scale factor was therefore 1e12 too large. The attacker supplied 0.132577813003136114 PAXG as vastly overvalued collateral and borrowed 230,002.486670 USDC without repayment.

loss.notes: The exploit receipt contains one USDC transfer of exactly 230,002.486670 from Morpho Blue to the attacker. The attacker's 0.132577813003136114 PAXG collateral is campaign input rather than victim loss. The borrowed USDC remained as unbacked market debt; no recovery is netted.

incidents.name: StoneVault permissionless round settlement
incidents.summary: StoneVault's round-advance entry point (selector 0x5069fb57) had no access control, so the attacker could deposit, settle the round themselves at a share price they had just moved, and withdraw at a profit in the same transaction.

loss.notes: The trace records 8,600 ETH deposited into StoneVault and 8,617.073005336909691789 ETH withdrawn after the attacker advanced the round, for an exact vault net loss of 17.073005336909691789 ETH.

incidents.name: Qubit Finance (QBridge)
incidents.summary: Ethereum QBridgeHandler accepted the zero address as an ERC-20 resource: its low-level transferFrom call returned success without moving tokens, yet the bridge emitted a Deposit event. Relayers then minted unbacked qXETH on BSC, which the attacker used to borrow the lending markets' assets.

loss.notes: Campaign gross loss across 20 successful BSC borrow transactions caused by 16 zero-value Ethereum deposits through the same defect-bearing handler runtime. One reverted borrow is excluded. Exact Borrow-event amounts aggregate to the ten asset quantities above; contemporaneous prices value them at $86.93 million.

incidents.name: ZZF burnToHolder pays BNB at a live spot quote
incidents.summary: ZZF.burnToHolder prices the ZongZi a user burns with uniswapRouter.getAmountsOut against WBNB and has the ZongZi token pay that many BNB from its reward pool into ZZF, from which receiveRewards pays the burner. After flash-loan buys pumped the WBNB/ZongZi pair, the attacker burned ZongZi at the inflated spot quote and withdrew nearly all of the pool's BNB in two transactions.

loss.notes: BNB depletion of the ZongZi reward pool across both attacker transactions. The attacker's flash-loan buys left about 656 more WBNB in the WBNB/ZongZi pair, which is not netted; the reported ~$223k is the attacker's net profit after that pump. A 4.32 BNB claim by 0xb89b232238b1bad9f144443960f600ea51cb0418 later in the block is not counted.

incidents.name: NeverFall sell() redeems protocol liquidity pro rata to the pair's spot NF balance
incidents.summary: NeverFall.sell(amount) removes amount * pairTotalSupply / balanceOf(pair) of the protocol-owned USDT/NF liquidity and pays the seller a share of the USDT. After flash-loaned USDT bought most of the NF out of the pair, the pair's NF balance was tiny, so selling NF removed almost all protocol liquidity and paid the attacker far more USDT than the NF was worth.

loss.notes: USDT that left protocol control: the attacker's net gain plus the 4,800 USDT flash-loan fee paid out of the proceeds. The 304,303.10 USDT routed to the protocol's own marketing wallet by the sell fee is not counted.

incidents.name: Unknown Arbitrum LP manager public withdraw swaps user positions with no minimum output
incidents.summary: Two byte-identical, unverified Uniswap V3 WETH/USDC position managers, 0x09c12514 and 0x3b329559, expose withdraw(address user, uint128 liquidity) (0x08fab167) to any caller. It removes and collects the user's position, sells all WETH for USDC via SwapRouter exactInputSingle with amountOutMinimum 0 and no price limit, and sends the USDC to the user. The attacker flash-borrowed 20,000 WETH from Aave and sold 7,825 WETH into the 0.05% pool. It then called withdraw for all 11 open positions in both managers, so the positions' WETH was sold at the depressed price. Finally it swapped back and kept 71.54 WETH.

loss.notes: The 11 positions (tokenIds 4184891, 4184901, 4190157, 4190178, 4192245, 4193097, 4193103, 4193166, 4193167, 4193506, 4193585) were worth 78.611616434521354757 WETH and 23815.920221 USDC, principal plus uncollected fees, at the pre-exploit pool state (block 303809031). Users received 783.590805 USDC back in the same calls, so the USDC component is 23815.920221 - 783.590805. The position value is simulated rather than read from logs, hence medium confidence. The attacker's net gain of 71.543669283808496020 WETH is lower because of pool fees, flash-loan premium and the attacker's own swap costs.

incidents.name: TheDAO splitDAO recursive-call drain
incidents.summary: TheDAO.splitDAO(uint256,address) moved the caller's proportional ether to the child DAO with createTokenProxy.value(fundsToBeMoved) and then called withdrawRewardFor(msg.sender) before zeroing balances[msg.sender], totalSupply and paidOut[msg.sender]. withdrawRewardFor forwards nearly all remaining gas through ManagedAccount.payOut(address,uint256), which performs a value-bearing call to the token holder, so the attacker's fallback re-entered splitDAO while its own DAO-token balance was still intact and fundsToBeMoved was recomputed from the same unburned balance on every recursion. The violated invariant is that a split must pay out a token holder's share at most once per token lot; the deployed code performed the external interaction before the state update that enforces it.

loss.notes: Exact victim depletion: 14,112 internal ether transfers from TheDAO 0xbb9bc244d798123fde783fcc1c72d3bb8c189413 to the attacker's child DAO 0x304a554a310c7e546dfe434669c62820b7d83490 across the 488 successful campaign transactions in blocks 1718497-1720245, summing to 3,641,694.241898506992612617 ETH; the child DAO's balance at block 1720685 equals that figure to the wei. Over the same window TheDAO's own balance fell from 11,599,353.240235775461586204 to 7,929,780.451475795897256723 ETH, and the 27,878.546861472571716864 ETH difference went to nine unrelated child DAOs across 16 transfers, never more than one per recipient per transaction, i.e. ordinary splits, and is excluded. The attacker's own legitimate entitlement was one DAO-token lot of 258.056141471 tokens (258.0565647603817 ETH per split), about 0.007 percent of the drain, and is not deducted from this gross measure. ETH is valued at the DefiLlama 2016-06-17T00:00:00Z daily point of 15.397397817568129 USD, the last price stamp at or before the anchor; ETH fell to 11.197136666677007 USD by 2016-06-18T00:00:00Z, so the same quantity is worth about 40.8M USD one day later - the USD figure is unusually sensitive to valuation time. The drain was reversed offchain: the DAO hard fork at block 1920000 zeroed the child DAO and moved all DAO-related ether into the WithdrawDAO refund contract 0xbf4ed7b27f1d666546e30d74d50d173d20bca754, which the node reports holding 12,001,961.845205763407115004 ETH at block 1920001. METHODOLOGY excludes later recoveries from gross victim depletion, so the recovery does not reduce this number.

incidents.name: Numa donation-manipulable vault price used as lending oracle
incidents.summary: NumaVault prices NUMA from its raw rETH balanceOf divided by circulating supply, and NumaPriceOracleNew feeds that spot price to the Numa lending comptroller for both collateral and debt. Within one flash-loaned transaction the attacker built a looped NUMA short against rETH collateral, sold the borrowed NUMA into the vault, donated 150 rETH to the vault to lift the oracle NUMA debt price from 116.94e12 to 161.23e12 wei, then liquidated its own position 26 times to recover its collateral and borrowed rETH against its remaining cNUMA, draining the vault.

loss.notes: NumaVault rETH depletion across the exploit transaction and the attacker's same-session vault sale (source-2), net of attacker-supplied rETH that stayed in the vault (150 rETH donation, 10 rETH buy) and excluding 3.890749723489182171 rETH of protocol fees paid to Numa's own fee/reward Safe. Recipients: attacker 292.969043721660915071 rETH (matches the project's reported 292.96 rETH), Aave rETH flash-loan premium 1.116841928270578525 rETH. cNUMA lenders' 3,626,482.92 NUMA (bad debt) were burned into the vault for this rETH and are not counted again. Later team/partner recapitalisation does not reduce gross loss.

incidents.name: EGA pond _openAPond unbounded buyback percentage
incidents.summary: The EGA deposit pond 0x67db1b06 exposes payable _openAPond(uint256,uint256). It swaps percent/100 of the remaining deposit into EGA via swapExactETHForTokens with amountOutMin 1, without bounding the caller's percent to 100. With a 1,500 WBNB flash loan, the attacker bought EGA and called _openAPond with 1 wei and a percent of 100 times the pond's balance. The pond then spent its entire 506.67 BNB buying EGA at the inflated price, and the attacker sold its EGA back into the pair.

loss.notes: Exact native-BNB depletion of pond 0x67db1b06e507603d19a27fa128c80969e629a38e: eth_getBalance 506665157500000000038 wei at block 42857880, and 1 wei (the attacker's msg.value) at 42857881. The attacker's net profit was 481.023461112559800467 WBNB; the gap went to swap fees and EGA's transfer-tax recipients. The 1,500 WBNB flash loan and the 1 wei input are attacker-supplied and are not loss. The BNB is valued at the DefiLlama WBNB quote.

incidents.name: Furucombo Proxy delegatecall context hijack
incidents.summary: Proxy._exec() used one registry validity check for both callback callers and delegatecall targets. Because Aave V2's lending-pool proxy was marked valid, the attacker delegatecalled its initialize function in Furucombo's context, wrote a malicious implementation into Furucombo's colliding EIP-1967 slot, and then used that implementation to drain tokens users had approved to Furucombo.

loss.notes: Furucombo reported that 21 assets worth approximately $15 million were stolen from 22 users.

incidents.name: OLPC pair-side burn multiplier collapses the OLPC/LABUBU reserve
incidents.summary: OLPCToken._update() sends every pair-to-user transfer down a branch that burns value * decimalsValue from the pair and then delivers value = 0 to the recipient. decimalsValue is an unbounded owner parameter that was raised from 1 to 7326680472586200649 on 2026-05-05, so any unprivileged caller could make the pair destroy 7.3e18 times the moved amount of its own OLPC. The attacker sent dust to the OLPC/LABUBU PancakePair and called skim() twenty times, collapsing the pair's OLPC balance from 51928294.25 to about 0.375, then pre-funded the pair with 8.1 OLPC and ran a Pancake supporting-fee swap with amountIn = 0, which prices that 8.1 OLPC against the collapsed reserve and released 688380.90 LABUBU.

loss.notes: The OLPC/LABUBU PancakePair 0xedb7dcb4cdfec957f8df5cbf5e94229a6cc9f365 lost 688380.902509080087370095 LABUBU in the single exploit transaction: its LABUBU balance falls from 720372.009849017508169693 at block 105326392 to 31991.107339937420799598 at block 105326393, and the pair's Swap event reports amount0Out 688380902509080087370095 with amount1In 8100000000000000000. Valuation is the realised proceeds of that same transaction rather than a spot price: DefiLlama has no LABUBU or OLPC observation, and both tokens trade only in the thin pools the attack moved. The attacker routed the LABUBU through the LABUBU/WBNB and WBNB/USDT pairs inside the exploit transaction and its BEP20-USDT balance rose from 0.105956839086043429 to 1115903.769368970807600681, a gain of 1115903.663412131721557252 USDT taken at par, which is 1.6210555222330743 USD per LABUBU removed from the pair and matches the 1115903.66 USDT figure in source-2. The attacker realised less than the pair lost because 124252.752903288956770302 LABUBU of the output was burned by LABUBU's own transfer tax on the way out. The pair also lost 51928285.776963524850939528 OLPC, burned to 0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dead by the defective hook, which is not valued: OLPC delivers zero tokens to any non-exempt buyer, so it has no realisable market price. No recovery or return took place.

incidents.name: Orion ExchangeWithOrionPool depositAsset reentrancy
incidents.summary: Exchange.depositAsset() carries no reentrancy guard and credits the caller with the exchange's own token balance delta, while swapThroughOrionPool() settles a caller-supplied token path by crediting the balance delta of the path's output token. The attacker put a fake ERC-20 in the middle of the path whose transfer hook re-entered depositAsset() with flash-loaned USDT, so the same 2.84M USDT was credited twice and withdrawn once.

loss.notes: Net USDT movement of the exchange 0xb5599f568d3f3e6113b286d010d2bca40a7745aa in the exploit receipt: it receives 2,844,766.426326 USDT from the attacker contract through the re-entrant depositAsset call plus 0.000099 USDT from the OrionPool pair, and pays out 5,689,532.852749 USDT in the closing withdraw, for a net loss of 2,844,766.426324 USDT. The 0.4999 USDC the attacker deposited to open the position is an attacker input and is not netted. This record is scoped to the Ethereum leg only. The same defect was executed against the Orion exchange on BNB Chain 0xe9d1d2a27458378dd6c6f0b2c390807aed2217ca in transaction 0xfb153c572e304093023b4f9694ef39135b6ed5b2515453173e81ec02df2e2104 for a further 191,606.635567209086337063 BSC-USDT; no incident record exists for that chain, so it is excluded here rather than folded into this Ethereum measurement. Reported campaign totals near USD 2.9M are the sum of both legs. DefiLlama's nearest USDT observation to the incident timestamp is 1.0031 at 1675353310; par valuation is used, which is 0.31 percent conservative.

incidents.name: Parity multisig wallet reinitialization
incidents.summary: The wallet forwarded unmatched calls to a shared WalletLibrary whose public initWallet function lacked a one-time initialization guard. An attacker could call it again through the wallet, replace the initialized owner set with their own address, and then execute an authorized drain.

loss.notes: OpenZeppelin's contemporaneous analysis reports 153,037 ETH drained from three affected multisigs, worth approximately $30 million. The three drain calls transfer 26,793 ETH, 44,055 ETH, and 82,189 ETH, respectively; the USD figure is the report's rounded incident estimate.

incidents.name: Team Finance arbitrary-pair migration drain
incidents.summary: LockToken.migrate() authorized the caller using one lock ID but accepted a separate caller-supplied Uniswap V2 pair and liquidity amount. The attacker used locks for a worthless self-made token to migrate other users' locked LP balances into attacker-controlled Uniswap V3 positions.

loss.notes: The $14.5 million value is the contemporaneous reported incident aggregate. The listed quantities reproduce the anchor transaction's final attacker-controlled balances: ETH from the attack contract state diff and DAI, CAW, and TSUKA from receipt transfers. The DAI was obtained by swapping the stolen USDC inside the same transaction.

incidents.name: BNO pool stale NFT reward accounting
incidents.summary: The pool's emergency withdrawal cleared ERC-20 stake and reward-debt accounting but left the NFT reward addition active, so a later NFT withdrawal could pay rewards that were no longer backed by stake.

loss.notes: Exact pre-recovery victim depletion is the BNO balance change of pool 0xdca503449899d5649d32175a255a8835a03e4006 across the two successful campaign transactions: 1,563,370.168598147731548146 BNO immediately before the anchor and zero after the second transaction. The second receipt records 504,557.855800853399893084 USDT paid to campaign funds-holder 0xdc109426972ae14d5b3d7e91b47d42ff1fd3c8cc after the depleted BNO was sold; that exact stablecoin realization at par is used instead of the seed row's rounded USD 505,000 headline or a thin-market spot mark. The attacker's flash liquidity and amounts returned to the pool are not counted separately. No recovery is netted.

incidents.name: Sovryn loan-closing cross-contract reentrancy into iToken mint
incidents.summary: Sovryn's LoanClosingsWith protocol module reduced the lender pool's principalTotal in _settleInterest before pulling the repayment (an rUSDT ERC777 transferFrom that calls the payer's tokensToSend hook) or refunding native RBTC to the borrower. From those callbacks the attacker minted iUSDT or iRBTC while the pool's totalAssetSupply omitted the repaid principal, i.e. at a depressed tokenPrice, then burned the iTokens at the corrected price once the close finished. Repeated with flash-swapped collateral, this drained the iUSDT and iRBTC lending pools.

loss.notes: Exact net depletion of the Sovryn victim set {iUSDT 0x849c47f9c259e9d62f289bf1b2729039698d8387, iRBTC 0xa9dcdc63eabb8a2b6f39d7ff9429d88340044a7a, protocol 0x5a0d867e0d70fcc6ade25c3f1b89d618b5b4eaa7} across 110 successful attacker transactions (source-12): 36 setup borrows plus 36 rUSDT-leg exploits through attack contracts 0xe40151f2 (01:37-02:49 UTC) and 0xdaa2e727 (03:02-04:07 UTC), and 38 self-contained RBTC-leg exploits through 0xa893cdcb (06:43-07:37 UTC, last source-13), all on 2022-10-04 from EOA 0xc92ebecda030234c10e149beead6bba61197531a. rUSDT is entirely iUSDT-to-attacker net flow (164,360.168033 to 0xe40151f2, 118,693.860995 to 0xdaa2e727). RBTC combines WRBTC Transfer logs and native value frames: iRBTC to 0xa893cdcb 147.537139 (WRBTC 1139.937139 out and 1095 in, 102.6 native out) and protocol to 0xa893cdcb 0.928868 native, less 103.682768 WRBTC paid into the protocol by the Sovryn AMM when closeWithSwap converted the attacker's own XUSD collateral to repay its 2.7-RBTC loans; that repayment is attacker-supplied input and is netted. Gross treatment: the 2,804.4 XUSD of trading fees the protocol kept from the attacker (38 x 73.8) and the later recoveries in source-9 (17.717 RBTC, 19,511.1505 USDT, ETH and BNB) are not deducted. Excluded: 6,949.589485 SOV trading rebates the protocol sent to LockedSOV 0xb4e4517ca4edf591dcafb702999f04f02e57d978 for the attack contracts (vesting-locked, about 2.8k USD); tx 0x4dda1cc8e7bd813cd136a83dffa6be5d456414684f5351d371d276e7e084325f, whose reentrant iRBTC mint and burn returned exactly the 15 WRBTC deposited and which left an open 2.7-RBTC loan backed by 82,000 XUSD; and setup loans never closed (nonces 91, 104, 108, 130: 1 rUSDT against 0.001 WRBTC each). rUSDT (Sovryn-bridged USDT, 18 decimals) is valued at par (DefiLlama USDT 1.00017 at the anchor). RBTC is pegged 1:1 to BTC by the Powpeg; the whole RBTC depletion falls in 1664865799..1664869002 and DefiLlama's rsk WRBTC series has no sample between 1664847694 and 1664873182, so the BTC quote sampled at 1664866907 inside that window is used. The Sovryn post-mortem (source-9) reports 44.9368 RBTC and 282,351.9644 rUSDT extracted, within 0.35% and 0.25% of these onchain figures.

incidents.name: FFIST predictable airdrop balance overwrite
incidents.summary: FFIST._airdrop assigns one raw token unit to a predictably chosen address. A crafted zero-value transfer overwrote the pair balance; sync and tiny sales then drained its USDT reserves.

loss.notes: USDT realised from pair 0x7a3adf2f6b239e64dab1738c695cf48155b6e152: 53200.841980198574448225 in the anchor plus 2214.672631294872206647 in 65 later tiny sales, less the original attacker-supplied 2.408372926510967280 USDT purchase input. USDT is valued at par. Overwritten and remaining FFIST receive no separate value; gas and later transfers do not reduce gross victim depletion.

incidents.name: Elephant Money Reserve TRUNK redemption spot-price collateral valuation
incidents.summary: The Elephant Money Reserve at 0xd520a3b47e42a1063617a9b6273b206a07bdf834 is the deployed contract that computes the TRUNK exchange rate. Both mint(uint256) (selector 0xa0712d68) and redeem(uint256) (selector 0xdb006a75) price the ELEPHANT collateral by quoting the live PancakeSwap V2 state in the same transaction: mint buys collateral through PancakeRouter02 0x10ed43c718714eb63d5aa57b78b54704e256024e with swapExactTokensForTokens/swapExactTokensForTokensSupportingFeeOnTransferTokens (0x38ed1739, 0x5c11d795), and redeem converts the burned TRUNK notional into an ELEPHANT payout quantity with the router's getAmountsOut/getAmountsIn views (0xd06ca61f, 0x1f00ca74) read straight off the ELEPHANT/WBNB pair 0x1cea83ec5e48d9157fcae27a19807bef79195ce1 and the WBNB/BUSD pair 0x58f876857a02d6762e0101bb5c46a8c1ed44dc16. The code validates only a blacklist lookup on 0x3064cda024b921f83e72c996bc06982a5885ed97 and never checks the quote against a manipulation-resistant reference: there is no TWAP or cumulative-price snapshot, no external oracle, no deviation bound, and no restriction on minting and redeeming inside one transaction, so the redeemer sets the rate the Reserve applies. Buying ELEPHANT with 100,000 flash-loaned BNB, minting TRUNK against flash-loaned BUSD at the inflated collateral price, dumping the ELEPHANT, and then redeeming the TRUNK made the Reserve pay out 196,967,214,123,823.406098696 ELEPHANT from its collateral buffer 0xaf0980a0f52954777c491166e7f40db2b6fbb4fc, roughly five times the whole ELEPHANT/WBNB pair reserve. No parameter value of this deployed code is correct: the router address is stored configuration, but every value of it yields a single-transaction spot quote, so the defect is the valuation logic itself.

loss.notes: Measured from the transaction state diff: the attacker EOA 0xe552133cc829a7f7e98e349763fac7ab0f3828b0 ends the anchor transaction 27,416.299660449196663328 BNB richer after paying 0.16615479 BNB of gas, so it received 27,416.465815239196663328 BNB while both attacker contracts end at a zero native balance and every flash loan is repaid inside the same transaction. Realised proceeds are used rather than a spot mark on the stolen collateral because the attacker's own dumping set the price: the Reserve's ELEPHANT buffer 0xaf0980a0f52954777c491166e7f40db2b6fbb4fc was depleted by 196,967,214,123,823.406098696 ELEPHANT (9 decimals), 171,552,429,480,071.979064221 of which were sold straight into the ELEPHANT/WBNB pair, a quantity many times the pair's entire reserve that could not have been sold at the pre-attack price. Offsetting inflows to the protocol in the same transaction were 1,039,345.062525 BUSD into the collateral buffer 0xcb5a02bb3a38e92e591d323d6824586608ce8ce4 and 10,550.558267717257 BUSD retained by the Reserve. A further 30,414,784,643,751.426 ELEPHANT left stranded in the attacker contract 0xbceda90b2880fea5d511d54716229145508996da is excluded as it was never realised. The gas paid does not reduce the measurement. DefiLlama's nearest BNB datapoint to the anchor timestamp is stamped 1649782177, four seconds later; the valuation timestamp records the anchor time that was queried. The reported approximately $11.2 million figure agrees with this reconstruction.

incidents.name: TLN Protocol spot-reserve reward and collateral manipulation
incidents.summary: TLNProtocolStaking priced VUSD/VOW LP rewards from the live reserves of that pool and the thin USDT/VOW pair. A flash-loan-funded VOW purchase raised lpRate 12,876.67-fold, letting the attacker stake 943.253377026177767815 LP and mint 3,199,510.344301177871795565 TLN. TlnSwap then compounded the failure: lock() lent 3,251,534.902745099463206875 VUSD against the TLN while its second live-reserve calculation reduced required VOW collateral from a pre-transaction 921,120.006996164638490158 to 71.530270655320077627 VOW.

loss.notes: TlnSwap's VUSD balance fell exactly 3,251,534.902745099463206875, but VUSD had no reliable external dollar market, so it is not valued at its nominal peg. The recorded loss is instead the attacker's exact net realised proceeds. On BSC, the two sweep transactions moved 107,881.749956792323205771 USDT and 1,463,280.244257269082062875 VOW from the attack contract to the EOA. The EOA sold all USDT and 3,280.244257269082062875 VOW for 184.838953341954182596 BNB, then bridged exactly 1,460,000 VOW to Ethereum and sold it in 61 transactions for 171.439728226688515854 ETH. The 2 BNB transferred into the attack contract during setup bought the LP position later surrendered to staking and is attacker-supplied capital, so it is removed from the BNB component. Gas and bridge fees are disposal costs and are not subtracted. Incident-time DefiLlama prices value the resulting 182.838953341954182596 BNB and 171.439728226688515854 ETH at $748,229.12. Early reports of approximately $200,000 to $280,000 did not follow the VOW bridge and liquidation.

incidents.name: UwU Lend sUSDe price provider spot-median manipulation
incidents.summary: sUSDePriceProviderBUniCatch.getPrice() takes the median of eleven USDe price observations, but five of them are instantaneous Curve spot quotes read through get_p(0) on five hard-coded pools (FRAX, USDC, DAI, crvUSD, GHO), alongside five price_oracle(0) EMAs and one Uniswap V3 TWAP. Because a single transaction can move all five get_p inputs at once, the sorted median is pushed to whichever end of the honest cluster the attacker chooses; the code applies no deviation, staleness or spot-versus-EMA sanity check before scaling the median by sUSDeScalingFactor and returning it as the sUSDe price. All five pool addresses are compile-time constants, so no parameter value makes the deployed logic sound. Flash-loaned swaps across those pools drove UwU's reported sUSDe price from 1.03040982 to 0.98821237 and then to 1.03183659 inside the anchor transaction while the five EMA inputs stayed byte-identical, and the attacker converted that mispricing into deposits, borrows and self-liquidations that emptied every UwU reserve.

loss.notes: Quantities are the exact underlying balances that left UwU's nine funded uToken reserve contracts during the 2024-06-10 campaign, measured both from receipt Transfer logs and by reading each underlying token's balanceOf(uToken) at block 20061318 and block 20061352: every reserve went from its pre-attack balance to zero. The campaign is the anchor transaction plus 0xb3f067618ce54bc26a960b660cfc28f9ea0315e2e9a1a855ede1508eb4017376 (block 20061322, the CRV reserve) and 0xca1bbf3b320662c89232006f1ec6624b56242850f07e0f1dadbe4f69ba0d6ac3 (block 20061352, the WBTC, WETH, sDAI, crvUSD and UWU reserves); all three call the same defective price provider. Eight components are valued at DefiLlama prices timestamped within about four minutes of the anchor. The protocol's own UWU token has no DefiLlama price and is recorded with an exact quantity and a null USD value, so the total is a floor with respect to that component. The CRV component is the largest and is spot-marked: the attacker moved 23,617,586.25 CRV to 0xafca625321df8d6a068bdd8f1585d489d2acf11b and still holds 13,491,866.08 CRV there, so that quantity was never realised in the market; widely reported totals of about USD 19.4 million are consistent with a lower effective CRV valuation. Second leg, 2024-06-13 (seven further components): the same attacker EOA's transaction 0x9235e0662e230bdfa94f56f4932fd09a95fea17e4b9b44a4f40a59449e216110 (block 20081504) used 60,000,000 of the uSUSDE the anchor transaction had moved into attacker contract 0x4cd6feba837b6944be0b2311b7a21036e86c3354 as collateral and borrowed every remaining reserve; each underlying balanceOf(uToken) falls from its block-20081503 value to exactly zero at block 20081504, matching the receipt's Transfer logs. That uSUSDE was backed by no sUSDe: the reserve held zero sUSDe cash from the end of the 2024-06-10 campaign through block 20081503, and its 173.28 million sUSDe of variable debt sat in three attacker-created debtor contracts that never repaid. The leg does not call the defective provider, which UwU had replaced at block 20075143, but it only cashes out collateral the manipulation created, so its loss belongs to this fault episode. The DAI, USDT, crvUSD and WETH it took had been deposited after 2024-06-10; FRAX and LUSD are balances the first campaign had left. Valued at DefiLlama prices 7 to 279 seconds before the transaction.

incidents.name: Aurellion diamond uninitialized initialize takeover
incidents.summary: The owner's diamondCut registered the SafeOwnable facet's initialize(address) selector without invoking any initializer, leaving the OpenZeppelin guard slot at zero on a diamond whose ownership had never written it. The attacker called initialize() to seize ownership, cut in a malicious facet exposing pullERC20, and swept outstanding user USDC approvals via transferFrom.

loss.notes: Exact attacker receipts in the single anchor transaction: 450999.723188 USDC from 0x2e933518068b1cfc9746d94762ef2eddd39c6048, 3.0 USDC from 0xa90714a15d6e5c0eb3096462de8dc4b22e01589a, and 1.281433 USDC from 0xeced2d37e5edcfc67ffb74c655416f893d20793e via pullERC20 transferFrom, plus 5438.532001 USDC of diamond-held balance, all forwarded to the attacker EOA. No attacker-supplied campaign inputs besides gas.

incidents.name: BonqDAO TellorPriceFeed accepts the latest Tellor report unvalidated
incidents.summary: BonqDAO's TellorPriceFeed.price() is the single expression uint256(bytes32(oracle.getCurrentValue(queryId))). It returns the most recent value any Tellor reporter has submitted for the wALBT query id, with no dispute window, no staleness bound, no deviation limit and no sanity range, even though TellorFlex lets anyone become a reporter by staking 10 TRB and Tellor's own consumer guidance requires reading through getDataBefore() behind a delay buffer. Trove.borrow() sizes the mint from ITokenPriceFeed.tokenPrice(wALBT), which resolves through ConvertedPriceFeed 0x7d4c36c7 to that feed, so a self-submitted price is accepted as collateral valuation. The attacker staked 10 TRB, reported wALBT at 5,000,000,000 USD, and minted 100,514,098.34 BEUR against 0.1 wALBT; 108 seconds later the second leg reported a near-zero price and liquidated 33 third-party wALBT troves. The invariant violated is that collateral valuation must not be settable by the borrower.

loss.notes: Quantities are exact and taken from Transfer logs. WALBT: netting the WALBT transfers of the liquidation transaction 0xa02d0c3d... gives 114,672,341.367535192076347775 WALBT leaving troves, of which 13.259732562723399770 is the attacker's own seed in his trove 0x5343c5d0af82b89df164a9e829a7102c4edb5402 and 858,342.997708983721666464 stayed in the CommunityLiquidationPool 0xeec2266a0ea9d1970fe692273839dbbb6a9ae598; 113,813,985.110093645631281541 WALBT taken from 33 third-party troves reached the attacker, who withdrew 113,813,998.369826208354681311 (that sum plus his seed) in 0x7e292f9b.... BEUR: 100,514,098.340794949900000000 was minted from address zero in the anchor, 514,097.340794949900000000 of it as the borrowing fee to BONQStaking and 100,000,000 to the attacker, against 0.1 WALBT of collateral. USD basis is realised proceeds, not spot: the attacker's own selling moved both prices and neither position could have been sold at the quoted mark. Marking 113.8M WALBT at the DefiLlama observation of 0.10532615800872938 USD would give 11,987,589 USD, and the BEUR headline of 100.5M is the source of the ~120M USD figure in press coverage; neither was realisable. The WALBT component is valued at what the attacker actually got for it: he bridged 113,813,997.369826208354681311 wALBT to Ethereum as ALBT in 0xf2687809... (1 wALBT bridge fee) and sold about 29.8M of it through the 0x Exchange Proxy between blocks 16536020 and 16544037 for exactly 756.020062792199460300 ETH (756.003839783902276312 ETH across 27 successful transfers from the 0x FlashWallet plus 16.223008297183988 WETH; four further attempts reverted and moved nothing) and 20,511.905002 USDT, which at the DefiLlama ETH observation nearest the incident timestamp (1573.1999679714593 USD) is 1,209,882.64 USD. The BEUR component is valued at the 534,535.906877 USDC the attacker realised on Polygon by selling 558,407.700135617870000000 BEUR into the BEUR/DAI and BEUR/USDC pools across five swaps in blocks 38793403-38793555; USDC is taken at par. The unit prices in the components are those realised totals divided by the full stolen quantities, so they are realisation rates, not market prices. The remaining 84,000,000 ALBT and about 98.1M BEUR were never converted; the 84M ALBT moved to attacker wallets 0x9210fa17ae138914fa04a161e694d73c9f3502c7 and 0x9ec88aac7a7735769a86114a6396d67ecaa0bd4e and is excluded because no realisation for it is evidenced onchain. Flash loans were not used; the 10 TRB Tellor stake, the 0.1 WALBT and the 13.259732562723399770 WALBT seeds are attacker-supplied inputs and are excluded. Nothing was recovered.

incidents.name: Rikkei Finance SimplePriceOracle setOracleData access control
incidents.summary: SimplePriceOracle 0xd55f01b4b51b7f48912cd8ca3cdd8070a1a9dba5, the price oracle of the Rikkei Finance Cointroller, declares `function setOracleData(address rToken, oracleChainlink _oracle) external { oracleData[rToken] = _oracle; }` with no owner, admin, or any other caller restriction, so any address can repoint any market's feed. getUnderlyingPrice then reads decimals() and latestRoundData() straight from whatever contract that mapping holds. The attacker deposited 0.0001 BNB into rBNB, called setOracleData(rBNB, ownContract) to make the rBNB feed return 4.16881147930e32 with 18 decimals instead of the Chainlink BNB/USD 416.24753868 with 8 decimals, and borrowed the entire cash of the rUSDC, rBTC, rDAI, rUSDT and rBUSD markets against the resulting 2.918e28 account liquidity, then restored the original feed. A second transaction in the same block repeated the pattern in the opposite direction, repointing the rBNB feed at a second attacker contract so that BNB was priced low enough to borrow the whole rBNB market against a dust rBUSD deposit.

loss.notes: The campaign is two transactions in block 16956475 from the same EOA: 0x93a9b022 at transaction index 3 emptied the rUSDC, rBTC, rDAI, rUSDT and rBUSD markets, and 0x4e067608 at transaction index 118 emptied the rBNB market. Each borrow requested exactly the market's getCash(), and every underlying balance confirms it: rUSDC 0x916e87d16b2f3e097b9a6375dc7393cf3b5c11f5 346199.780826500224370302 -> 0 USDC, rBTC 0x53abf990bf7a37faa783a75fdd75bbcf8bdf11eb 3.032997772596307847 -> 0 BTCB, rDAI 0x9b9006cb01b1f664ac25137d3a3a20b37d8bc078 52275.872910150015513225 -> 0 DAI, rUSDT 0x383598668c025be0798e90e7c5485ff18d311063 297082.798044846109795784 -> 0 USDT, rBUSD 0x6db6a55e57ac8c90477bbf00ce874b988666553a 299822.459019477022693829 -> 0.041669357174238900 BUSD (the attacker's own dust deposit), and rBNB 0x157822ac5fa0efe98daa4b0a55450f4a182c10ca 101.469592805999411776 -> 0 BNB, all measured between block 16956474 and 16956475. Nothing was repaid; the positions were left as bad debt against 0.0001 BNB and 0.041429023913104989 BUSD of attacker collateral. Binance-peg USDC, USDT, BUSD and DAI are valued at par; BTCB and BNB use the DefiLlama observations nearest the incident timestamp (40228.48815584733 at 1649992763 and 416.03796227746824 at 1649992784). The attacker converted the proceeds and moved 2673.2 BNB, about 1.11M USD at the same BNB price, into the Tornado Cash BNB pool 0x0d5550d52428e7e3175bfc9550207e4ad3859b17 over 38 deposits in the following hour, which is the source of the widely reported ~$1.1M; that figure is post-slippage and is not used here. Nothing was recovered.

incidents.name: iVest donation-on-burn double debit
incidents.summary: Transfers to the zero address trigger the token's _MakeDonation path, which debits the sender's balance a second time; repeatedly sending iVest to the PancakeSwap pair and calling skim/sync shrank the pair's token reserve and let the attacker swap the reserve out for WBNB.

loss.notes: The receipt shows 1,200 WBNB entering PancakeSwap iVest/WBNB pair 0x2607118d363789f841d952f02e359bfa483955f9 and 1,538.875088869257198253 WBNB leaving it, for 338.875088869257198253 WBNB of net depletion; archive pair balances at the surrounding block boundary reproduce that amount. The attacker input is netted out; the 0.6-WBNB flash-loan fee is not deducted from victim depletion. The closest preceding DefiLlama BNB price is $508 at 1723438335.

incidents.name: DLMC live-reserve sell pricing
incidents.summary: DLMCToken priced buys and sells from its live USDT reserve, so linked buys could transiently raise the price used by a subsequent sell and remove more USDT than the buys supplied.

loss.notes: DLMCToken receives exactly 420,000 + 1,000,000 = 1,420,000 USDT and sends 1,646,119.118936329868440038 USDT in the sole campaign receipt, for gross victim depletion of 226,119.118936329868440038 USDT. Its archive USDT balance falls from 226,119.118936329868440044 to 0.000000000000000006, exactly the same net change; no unrelated same-block adjustment is required. Of the depleted amount, 3,558.897243107769423559 USDT repays financing and 222,560.221693222099016479 USDT reaches the profit receiver. The seed measured only the latter proceeds. DLMC minted or transferred in exchange for the two buys is consideration, not an additional victim asset. Later movement of proceeds or recovery is outside this exploit-time gross-loss boundary.

incidents.name: Raft InterestRatePositionManager collateral-index inflation with round-up share mint
incidents.summary: InterestRatePositionManager.liquidate() closes the liquidated position and then calls _updateDebtAndCollateralIndex, which resets the raft collateral token index to collateralToken.balanceOf(address(this)) divided by the remaining share supply. The attacker donated 6,001.45 flash-loaned cbETH to the manager and liquidated the only other cbETH position, leaving 89 shares backing 6,003.44 cbETH, so the stored index became 6.745e19 wei of cbETH per share. ERC20Indexable.mint then mints amount.divUp(storedIndex) shares, so each subsequent 1-wei managePosition collateral deposit rounded up to a full share worth 67.45 cbETH. Repeating the 1-wei deposit inside the same transaction inflated the attacker position's collateral claim far past the manager's real cbETH holdings and let it borrow 6,705,028.47 R against it.

loss.notes: Loss is measured as the assets the unbacked R actually pulled out of R liquidity inside the exploit transaction, not as the face value of the 6,701,624.445698 net R the defect minted; R was an undercollateralised stablecoin whose market price collapsed immediately, so par-valuing the mint would overstate what left. In the exploit transaction the attacker swapped 2,100,000 R and 1,200,000 R through Balancer ComposableStablePool 0x20a61b948e33879ce7f23e535cc7baa3bc66c5a9000000000000000000000555 for 2,009,226.625525958210315125 sDAI and 1,159,396.050215284713094612 DAI, redeemed the sDAI for 2,094,243.762271227103719829 DAI (log 383), and swapped 86,567.502077069127313424 R through Uniswap V3 R/USDC pool 0x190ed02adaf1ef8039fcd3f006b42553467d5045 for 86,430.564918 USDC (log 375). The two DAI legs sum to the single 3,253,639.812486511816814441 DAI transfer at log 387. Those stables were then routed to 3,339,766.379985 USDC and 1,575.175928415622483130 WETH, an equivalent view of the same proceeds (1,575.175928 ETH at 2,093.46 USD is 3,297,568 USD). Excluded: the attacker mistakenly sent 1,583.410453811108267443 ETH to the zero address at the end of the same transaction, which is a loss to the attacker and not a recovery for Raft, so it is not netted out; the residual 3,315,056.943449 R the attacker kept was dumped through the same pools over the following weeks for a further 140.324 ETH received by the attacker EOA, which is excluded because it was realised after the incident at post-depeg prices; six earlier ratchet transactions in the same campaign (0xa5233e3b, 0x05d6a951, 0x8c4b1b7b, 0x57ee18b5, 0x28a3afd3, 0xa1378a4d) moved at most 8.54 R and are immaterial. DefiLlama's nearest observations to the incident timestamp are 1699642801 for DAI and 1699642799 for USDC.

incidents.name: Eleven Finance NeverSellVault share-burn omission
incidents.summary: ElevenNeverSellVault.emergencyBurn() returned the caller's underlying LP tokens without burning the corresponding vault shares. The attacker could therefore recover a newly deposited position through emergencyBurn() and withdraw the same shares again through withdrawAll(), taking an equal amount from existing depositors.

loss.notes: The primary EOA's five consecutive receipts deplete four Eleven vaults by exactly 411,515.297079048812211459 NRV/BUSD Cake-LP, 30.836253259057738487 nrvBTC, 284.425940428143699836 nrvETH, and 2,412,442.136735313289865732 plus 7,694.931172793800254712 3NRV-LP. In each receipt, the helper supplies X LP, emergencyBurn returns X without burning shares, and withdrawAll returns the same X again; the vault-plus-strategy union therefore loses net X, and its archive balance falls by exactly X. The NRV/BUSD LP is valued from prestate reserves and total supply; the Nerve LPs use their canonical swap contracts' prestate virtual prices, with independently preceding BTC and ETH prices where required. Exact decimal arithmetic totals $4,638,919.013781618333536313. The later copycat used a different EOA, helper, vault and runtime and is excluded. Subsequent recovery and compensation are not netted from gross loss.

incidents.name: ChainSwap receive() unbound signatory check
incidents.summary: The bridge's receive() logic did not bind each recovered signer to its declared signatory. Unauthorized attestations could therefore satisfy the quota and duplicate-signatory checks and release bridged tokens.

loss.notes: ChainSwap's post-mortem reported an approximately $800,000 incident total. The publication does not provide an auditable asset-by-asset allocation for this Ethereum anchor, so assets remain unexpanded.

incidents.name: ORBCore refund-before-sell reentrancy with pair-reserve burnLP
incidents.summary: ORBToken forwards BNB it receives to ORBCore.addPoolAndSell, whose sell branch refunds the BNB to the caller before selling, and _sellToken pays the caller before calling ORBToken.burnLP, which burns up to 20% of the pair's ORB and syncs; none of this is reentrancy-guarded and Core's own swaps are tax-free. With flash-loaned and Venus-borrowed WBNB the attacker first bought almost all ORB out of the ORB/WBNB pair, then re-entered at the refunds so that 58 nested sells ran their burnLP calls against the emptied reserve on the way out, grinding its ORB side to dust, and a final sell drained the pair's WBNB.

loss.notes: WBNB depletion of the ORB/WBNB pair 0x64fad72e5dde70b2960497744b348fd64cb4788c across the transaction (45.318191861188781185 -> 0.335708357864918575), less the attacker's pre-held 3,483.438204554125976510 ORB valued at the pre-exploit reserve ratio (0.027093460559344606 WBNB). Sell taxes routed to leader2 are not deducted; borrowed legs are repaid in-transaction and excluded.

incidents.name: Impermax V3 permissionless reinvest collateral-value destruction
incidents.summary: TokenizedUniswapV3Position.reinvest(tokenId, bountyTo) is permissionless and hands the position's collected Uniswap V3 fees to the autocompounder module, which mints them back as liquidity at the pool's unvalidated spot price; the only post-condition is newLiquidity > 0. Impermax values the same position with an independent Chainlink-derived oracle price through getPositionData, so a caller who first pushes the pool price far away from the oracle can burn essentially all of a position's fee value in one call. In the anchor transaction the attacker wash-traded a self-owned position to accrue 388,058.868833 USDC plus 0.26990816645136616 WETH of fees, borrowed the borrowable's entire WETH cash of 201.360672 WETH against a position ImpermaxV3Collateral.canBorrow correctly valued at 60.130663332976091010 WETH plus those fees, then called reinvest with the 0.02% pool pushed to tick -102035 against an oracle tick near -201290. The fees became only 1.1615 WETH of extra oracle-valued liquidity, the position's collateral collapsed to 61.292130049975177013 WETH with realY 0, and the equally permissionless ImpermaxV3Collateral.restructureBadDebt then wrote the fresh debt down to 29.847% through ImpermaxV3Borrowable.restructureDebt, socialising the shortfall onto the borrowable's depositors.

loss.notes: Multi-transaction campaign spanning blocks 29437393 to 29628142 (2025-04-26 to 2025-04-30). The six Impermax V3 borrowables that emitted RestructureDebt in that window are cWETH 0x5d93f216f17c225a8b5ffa34e74b7133436281ee and cUSDC 0xbc303acda8b2a0dcd3d17f05adddf854edd6da59 of the WETH/USDC pool, cWETH 0xd9a5628f5d0f95421d70e880c17f174d9ea305e0 and ccbBTC 0x0513d232dfcb378d9cbbcd0827106fa12076b048 of the WETH/cbBTC pool, and cUSDC 0x900370e14093e3508b056c81c7a21e687bc350eb and ccbBTC 0xb362479915f2d24a284dd5e6742c4f619ad0453a of the USDC/cbBTC pool. The written-off notional in those 23 events is not the loss: it includes debt the attacker created against his own manufactured collateral and never funded, for example 1,081.02814389 cbBTC. The measured loss is instead the exact net underlying depletion of those six contracts, obtained by summing every ERC20 Transfer between them and the attacker address set over the campaign window: WETH 5,586.139197377487930567 out against 5,539.246558159865319923 in, USDC 26,569,239.607412 out against 26,513,987.648003 in, cbBTC 1,055.99507805 out against 1,055.28600237 in. Flash-loan principal and the attacker's own deposits are therefore excluded by construction. Confidence is medium on completeness rather than on the arithmetic: the attacker's realised proceeds were 121.0926644 ETH delivered to 0xe9f853d2616ac6b04e5fc2b4be6eb654b9f224cd, about 6.6 ETH more than the 114.49 ETH equivalent of the three components, the remainder plausibly being autocompounder bounties, the 1,344,342 imxB that passed through his contracts, and swap profit; that surplus is not attributed to any victim contract and is not counted.

incidents.name: AFX liquidity intermediary sweeps the whole AFX balance of its swap helper and matches it from a funding wallet
incidents.summary: Function 0xb1a87f2c of unverified contract 0x560d3973ee82a318d381c49fcbf3ce9d6cf1250b swaps half of the user's USDT for AFX into helper 0x671ce4, then withdraws the helper's entire AFX balance instead of the swap output. It pulls an equal amount of AFX, plus matching AHT, from funding wallet 0x146933f2 through standing allowances and adds it to the AFX/AHT pair. The attacker flash-borrowed AFX, donated 511,965 AFX to the helper and front-ran with an AFX->AHT buy. It then called the function with 100 wei of USDT, recovered the donation through the refund, and back-ran, forcing the wallet to supply 511,965 AFX and leaving the attacker 10,699.62 USDT.

loss.notes: The attacker's net USDT gain, which is the value extracted from the victim side. The forced 511,965.516 AFX and 12.604 AHT from funding wallet 0x146933f2692f5ff3b62441ab3c2a65ddcaca753c became liquidity at a manipulated AFX/AHT ratio, with LP minted to project addresses 0x9549204b and 0x0ed943ce, and the attacker sold the extracted AFX into the USDT/AFX pair 0x9d2d5cc00c8cf233aefd8a177b904f8d3abb5d46. The wallet's gross token outflow is not a separable stolen amount, so the realised extraction is used.

incidents.name: Value DeFi vSafe StrategyAlpacaWBNB in-flight ibBNB valuation
incidents.summary: StrategyAlpacaWBNB values its ibBNB position at Alpaca Vault totalToken()/totalSupply(), and the vSafe WBNB vault mints shares against that value. Inside Alpaca Vault.work() the lent BNB has left the vault before the debt is booked, so totalToken() reads about half its true value. The attacker opened an Alpaca position through a strategy that calls an attacker-chosen farming token, re-entered vSafe depositFor() from that token's approve() at the depressed share price, and redeemed the excess shares at the true price in later transactions.

loss.notes: Vault WBNB paid to the attacker in nine redemptions minus the attacker's own WBNB deposits in the nine re-entrant deposits: 24267.906010457069055632 - 18922.591338882848871944 WBNB. The attacker's deposits are campaign inputs, not victim loss. Alpaca's lent BNB was repaid within each work() call and is excluded. Reported totals near $11m combine other Value DeFi pools and incidents and are not used.

incidents.name: TMX Tribe Router-minted USDG inflates TLP AUM
incidents.summary: TMX, a GMX-v1 fork on Arbitrum, made its public Router a manager of the Vault, so any user could mint USDG through Router.swap([token, USDG]). GlpManager prices TLP as pool AUM divided by TLP supply and does not subtract USDG minted outside GlpManager, so each such mint raised the TLP redemption price while the minted USDG stayed redeemable 1:1. The attacker looped mintAndStakeGlp, a Router USDG mint, unstakeAndRedeemGlp at the inflated price and sellUSDG, draining the Vault's USDT0, WBTC, WETH, wSOL and USDC.

loss.notes: Components are the Vault's net ERC-20 outflow to the two attacker EOAs across all 445 successful attacker transactions that touched it (blocks 417530153-418024535): tokens the Vault sent them minus the tokens they deposited, so attacker-supplied loop capital is not counted and fees retained by the Vault reduce the figure. USDG nets to zero (minted and burned). The Jan 3-4 test runs from 0x16ed3aff lost 12.642473 USDT0 to the Vault and drew 0.00010844 WBTC; they are netted into the totals. Prices are DefiLlama historical quotes at the last Vault-touching transaction (timestamp 1767583146). The total matches the ~$1.4M reported by DarkNavy and QuillAudits. Later swaps, bridging and laundering by the attacker are not loss events.

incidents.name: Unverified USDC/WETH liquidity pool credits nested reentrant liquidity additions against one payment
incidents.summary: Unverified pool 0x39ed372f8e9f316029994ca7f73b6683829c6b08 records liquidity and tick reserves in function 0xbe16634e before settlement, then calls back msg.sender without a reentrancy guard and checks payment per call. The attacker re-entered the add path 20 levels deep from the callback, paid once in the deepest frame to satisfy every nested balance check, and then removed the inflated liquidity, taking the pool's entire 7,167.42 USDC and 2.05 WETH.

loss.notes: The pool's full pre-exploit USDC and WETH balances, net of the attacker's own deposits in the transaction. The attacker's separate Uniswap V3 USDC->WETH swap is its own trade and not counted.

incidents.name: SwapNet Router arbitrary call
incidents.summary: The closed-source SwapNet Router's swap entrypoint (selector 0x87395540) performed a low-level call to a caller-supplied target with caller-supplied calldata and no target validation, so passing a token address made the router itself execute transferFrom() against users' standing infinite approvals.

loss.notes: Matcha reports $13.43 million taken from 18 SwapNet users across Base, BNB Chain, and Arbitrum. The selected Base transaction records 13,342,433.169249 USDC transferred from one victim to the attacker; the structured asset is this directly observed component of the reported campaign total.

incidents.name: WiseLending empty-pool share inflation through a direct WBTC donation
incidents.summary: MainHelper._cleanUp, run through the syncPool modifier on every WiseLending entry point, compares IERC20.balanceOf(address(this)) against totalPool plus totalBareToken and credits any surplus to both totalPool and pseudoTotalPool without minting shares, so an unsolicited token transfer is booked as pool income for existing shareholders. MainHelper.calculateLendingShares additionally returns the raw amount when totalDepositShares is at most 1, so the first deposit into an empty pool mints one share per wei. Two one-wei WBTC depositExactAmount calls left the WBTC pool with two shares and a pseudoTotalPool of two, a direct transfer of 49.99999998 WBTC then made _cleanUp value each of those shares at about 25 WBTC, and the inflated collateral let borrowExactAmount take every other asset the protocol held before the flash loan was repaid out of a geometric sequence of WBTC withdrawals.

loss.notes: Quantities are WiseLending's own ERC20 balance deltas between block 18342120 and block 18342121, so the aToken amounts already net out the interest that accrued inside the transaction. The 50 WBTC Balancer flash loan is attacker-supplied and is not loss; WiseLending in fact ended the transaction 0.01503674 WBTC richer than it started, and that surplus is not netted against the depletion. aEthWETH is valued at the ETH price because Aave v3 aTokens are redeemable one for one against their underlying and DefiLlama publishes no separate quote for aEthWETH. The executing searcher's own realised take was 169.402969354568854988 WETH, about 261805 USD at the same ETH price, which is the figure the seed row rounded to 260000; the 262280.51 USD recorded here is the larger victim-side depletion. Every component is valued from a DefiLlama historical query taken at the anchor timestamp 1697207963; the datapoints DefiLlama returned for that query carry their own stamps between 1697207997 and 1697208522, all within ten minutes of the anchor. Recoveries after the fact, if any, do not reduce gross depletion under the methodology.

incidents.name: landNFT permissionless whitelisted minter
incidents.summary: The NFT owner whitelisted a helper whose public batch mint forwards arbitrary recipients and quantities without caller authorization. An unrelated caller minted 876 NFTs in five transactions and redeemed 143 for 28,600 XQJ.

loss.notes: 143 successful redemptions remove exactly 28,600 XQJ (9 decimals) from 0xeab03ad7ea0ac5afb272b592bef88cf93ed190c5. The disposal swaps 28,601 XQJ for 149,616.134251685770252629 Binance-Peg USDT (0x55d398326f99059ff775485246999027b3197955), not BUSD. Subtract 0.01 USDT injected into the pair and apply disposal unit value to only the 28,600 stolen XQJ, excluding one pre-purchased XQJ. USDT valued at $1. Remaining unredeemed NFTs carry no additional valuation; gas and recoveries are not deducted.

incidents.name: Cream Finance yUSD price-per-share collateral inflation
incidents.summary: Cream's PriceOracleProxy priced every registered Yearn-vault collateral as getYvTokenPrice(token) = underlyingPrice * pricePerShare(), reading the vault's live share price with no bound, time-average or sanity check. A bare yCRV transfer into the yUSD vault doubled pricePerShare in the same transaction, so the oracle reported twice the true value for crYUSD collateral and the Comptroller authorised borrows against collateral that did not exist. The contract's own getLPFairPrice and getCrvTokenPrice branches avoid spot quantities for exactly this reason; no value of the only yVault parameters (isYvToken, version) bounds the multiplier, so the defect is in the executed code rather than in a configured value.

loss.notes: Exact victim depletion measured from receipts: for every market in the Cream Comptroller's getAllMarkets() at block 13499797, the net movement of that market's own underlying() token across the nine successful campaign transactions, plus native-ETH flows for crETH. Fifty-seven ERC-20 markets and crETH are net negative and every recipient is one of the two attacker contracts. Attacker-supplied flash-loan principal is excluded because it is netted inside the same measurement; the recursive crYUSD leg therefore contributes only 1,424.188372514512394279 yUSD. Fifty-two components use DefiLlama historical prices for the anchor timestamp; six underlyings with no DefiLlama series (yvCurve-stETH, HBTC, vVSP, yvCurve-IronBank, ibBTC, yUSD) use Cream's own unmanipulated getUnderlyingPrice at block 13499797 converted at the same DefiLlama ETH price and are marked method other. The 144.4 million total exceeds the ~130 million commonly reported; the gap is concentrated in thin-market components (CRETH2 at 39.9 million, RUNE, wNXM, PERP) which are marked at contemporaneous quotes and which the attacker could not have liquidated at those quotes, so realised attacker proceeds were lower than this gross victim depletion.

incidents.name: HopeLend empty-market liquidity index inflation
incidents.summary: The HopeLend pool is an Aave v3 fork whose liquidity index is computed from the reserve balance without a floor on an empty market. With one wei of hEthWBTC supply outstanding the attacker donated WBTC straight to the hEthWBTC reserve, inflating the index so that the rounding on burn returned far more underlying than had been supplied, and used the resulting collateral to borrow the WETH, USDT and USDC markets out.

loss.notes: Netting the exploit receipt across the attacker EOA and its exploit contract leaves exactly one non-zero position, 528.004085822170762393 WETH; the WBTC donation, the USDT and USDC borrows and the flash-loan legs all net to zero because they were repaid inside the transaction. The variable debt the attacker leaves behind against those markets is not additionally counted, since the WETH figure already measures what left. A large share of this was taken by a MEV bot that front-ran the attacker rather than by the attacker; that is a redistribution among third parties and does not change the amount the protocol lost. Nothing was recovered by HopeLend.

incidents.name: RICE BentoBox-fork vault unauthenticated setMasterContractApproval
incidents.summary: The unverified BentoBoxV1-fork vault 0xcfe0de4a's setMasterContractApproval(user, masterContract, approved, v, r, s) performs no authorization: it ignores v, r, s and msg.sender, requires only masterContract != 0, and writes masterContractApproved[masterContract][user]. The attacker contract called registerProtocol() to become its own master contract, approved itself for depositor 0x49876a20 with a zero signature, and withdrew that depositor's entire 22,189,176.5 RICE vault balance through the allowed(from) check.

loss.notes: Exact victim depletion: the vault's LogWithdraw debits depositor 0x49876a20bb86714e98a7e4d0a33d85a4011b3455 of 22189176505973791717313474 RICE base units (18 decimals), its full RICE share, in the single exploit transaction. The attacker sold the whole amount in the same transaction into Uniswap V3 RICE/USDT pool 0xa0213b570dff35a8c826334472e23b9a8a94ef3b for 88232.917196 USDT (log 7), then routed it through USDC to 34.52291421920366 WETH paid to the attacker EOA (log 17). That sale emptied the pool's USDT side, so RICE is valued at realised proceeds: the USDT received times the DefiLlama USDT quote 0.999063 (source-6). A spot mark at DefiLlama's RICE quote (0.077597 USD at 1748103192) would give about 1.72M USD, which the pool's liquidity could not realise. No attacker input is subtracted; no other vault asset was taken.

incidents.name: Kame Aggregator AggregationRouter arbitrary executor call
incidents.summary: AggregationRouter.swap forwards caller-chosen executeParams to a caller-chosen executor without validating either. Attackers set the executor to an ERC-20 and the calldata to transferFrom(victim, attacker, amount), so the router spent the unlimited approvals users had given it. The primary attacker, copycats and a white hat drained approvers of both Kame routers on Sei from 2025-09-12 onward.

loss.notes: Exact victim debits from receipt Transfer logs (plus Etherscan-indexed CW20-pointer transfers) of 4008 legs in 2601 successful drain transactions through both Kame routers, 2025-09-12 to block 234150523. Each debit is valued at its hourly DefiLlama price; only stablecoins, wrapped SEI/BTC/ETH/FRAX and liquid staking tokens are valued. Memecoins (about 116.8k USD at DefiLlama prices, excluded because the attackers' disposal likely moved thin markets) and 26 unpriced tokens are left out, so this is a conservative gross figure. Drains through the prior router 0x1415e8ee... (same defect, same campaign, 3978 USD) are merged. White-hat drains and the attacker's later return of 185 ETH are not deducted. Approvals were never revoked onchain by the protocol, and the campaign was still running at the data cutoff (block 234700000).

incidents.name: ReceiverAxelar spoofed expressExecute EYWA unlock
incidents.summary: ReceiverAxelar.expressExecute skipped Axelar gateway validation and trusted attacker-controlled sourceChain and sourceAddress, so the caller passed a spoofed receiveData payload that routed through PortalV2 into the CLP Portal and unlocked 999,787,453.0325354 EYWA to the caller in a single transaction.

loss.notes: Exact receipt accounting: one EYWA Transfer of 999787453.0325354 from the CLP Portal 0xac8f44ceca92b2a4b30360e5bd3043850a0ffcbe to the caller, priced at the 2026-02-01 CoinGecko daily close. This record anchors the largest single drain of a Nomad-style multi-attacker campaign totaling about $2.9m across chains; the 99,988.74 EYWA dust to fee collector 0x4400671b in the same transaction is not counted. No attacker-supplied campaign inputs besides gas.

incidents.name: bEarn BUSD/ibBUSD withdrawal-unit mismatch
incidents.summary: The BUSD Alpaca strategy's withdraw(address,uint256) passed a BUSD-denominated request to FairLaunch as an ibBUSD amount. Because each ibBUSD was worth more than one BUSD, repeated deposit/emergencyWithdraw cycles withdrew excess BUSD and compounded the attacker's credit.

loss.notes: bEarn reports that 26 attack transactions beginning with the anchored transaction drained 10,859,319 BUSD from the affected single-stake BUSD vault. The campaign-wide amount is valued at stablecoin par; it is not narrowed to the first transaction's proceeds.

incidents.name: Zentra aToken burn clamp lets repayWithATokens clear debt without burning
incidents.summary: Zentra, an Aave V3 fork on Citrea, upgraded its aTokens to an implementation whose _burnScaled caps the scaled burn at the holder's scaled balance with no bound on the difference. Pool.repayWithATokens burns the caller's aTokens and marks the debt repaid, so a caller holding no aTokens repays in full while burning nothing. With 200,000 flash-borrowed USDC.e as collateral, the attacker borrowed 140,000 ctUSD, cleared the debt with repayWithATokens and withdrew the collateral. It repeated this for 30 USDC.e.

loss.notes: Net reserve depletion in the single exploit transaction. The zctUSD reserve paid 140,000 ctUSD in the borrow and received 0.000001 ctUSD net from the attacker's 50 supplied and 49.999999 withdrawn. The zUSDC reserve paid the 30 USDC.e borrow and kept 0.000001 of the 200,000 USDC.e collateral supplied and withdrawn. The debt tokens were burned without repayment. The PoC reports ~140,000 ctUSD + 30 USDC.e (~$143K).

incidents.name: RES token fee settlement against manipulable pair state
incidents.summary: BEP20TokenA (RES) settles its transfer fees against AMM state the caller controls in the same transaction. _distB() pays the fee out of the contract's ALL treasury in an amount computed by _atoB()/_tokenACalcTokenB() from live getReserves() of the RES/USDT and USDT/ALL PancakeSwap pairs, and _isBuySwap()/_isSellSwap() arm that path from the pair's raw balanceOf rather than from any manipulation-resistant price, so donating USDT into the RES/USDT pair turns a negligible buy fee into an arbitrarily large ALL payout. The external thisAToB() has no caller restriction and sells the contract's accumulated RES balance into the same pair, then calls _burn(_swapV2Pair, burnNumber) for the full pre-swap amount before sync(); because that sell is itself fee-charged, the burn destroys more RES than the pair received, so the pair pays out USDT for tokens it does not keep.

loss.notes: Two-transaction campaign by the same sender and the same exploit contract: the anchor at 21948017:2 and 0xef19a4dfd69874d5efda3e38b5a19cae4e0b0bdc95769760bd85ede4d15609ac at 21948032:27. The components are the exact BSC-USD depletion of the two pools the defect drained, measured as balance differences across the campaign: the RES/USDT pair 0x05ba2c512788bd95cd6d61d3109c53a14b01c82a fell from 260,015.849847947963440692 to 2,769.147431623968351181 and the ALL/USDT pair 0x1b214e38c5e861c56e12a69b6baa0b45efe5c8eb from 41,761.128268609605264847 to 7,616.282704591176328845. The attacker's own flash-loaned USDT donations into the RES/USDT pair are attacker-supplied inputs and cancel out of these balance differences. The attacker withdrew 209,203.869337859626567655 and 81,468.554169573186212332 BSC-USD to the sender EOA, 290,672.423507432812779987 in total; the 719.124472909611245526 difference from gross depletion is flash-loan fees retained by the lenders, which do not reduce gross victim depletion. The RES contract's ALL (0x04c0f31c0f59496cf195d2d7f1da908152722de7) treasury was additionally depleted by 14,123.190011430917566372 ALL; 2,178.904310074536854027 of those tokens are the counterpart the ALL/USDT pair received for the USDT already counted, and the remainder cannot be valued because ALL's only market is that same drained pair, so the ALL leg is excluded rather than marked at a pre-attack spot price the attacker could not have realised.

incidents.name: GoodDollar GoodFundManager collectInterest double-count
incidents.summary: GoodFundManager.collectInterest accepted duplicated staking-contract entries and double-counted them to over-claim COMP rewards routed through Compound.

loss.notes: The receipt records 258.031203709042906285 COMP sent to the beneficiary after that address supplied 7.4 COMP, for an exact net increase of 250.631203709042906285 COMP. The commit-pinned reproduction reports this as approximately 250 COMP and $13,000.

incidents.name: NORMIE premarket-flag balance inflation and forced swapback
