incidents.summary: NORMIE's _transfer contains two cooperating defects. _get_premarket_user sets premarket_user[recipient] for any address that receives exactly balanceOf(teamWalletAddress) in a single transfer, so the flag is self-assignable; and for a flagged recipient buying from a market pair, _transfer executes _balances[address(this)] += amount, crediting the token contract the full purchase amount without debiting any account and without changing _totalSupply, so the sum of balances exceeds supply. The same function then sells the contract's balance through swapAndLiquify whenever it exceeds a threshold randomised from block.timestamp and block.difficulty, with no slippage bound and no per-block cap. The attacker flagged their helper by flash-swapping exactly the team wallet's 5,000,000-token balance out of the SushiSwap pair, then shuttled 2,266,628.300256719 NORMIE between the helper and the pair with skim, minting that amount into the contract each round and forcing 51 unbounded swapbacks that dumped 237,150,000 NORMIE into the pair, collapsing the price so the tokens flash-borrowed and sold at the pre-attack price could be repurchased for a fraction of the proceeds. No parameter choice makes this correct: the credit is unbacked at every threshold, and the threshold only sets how often the contract liquidates it.

loss.notes: Realised native-ETH extraction over the 14-transaction campaign between blocks 14952783 and 14959665. The attack contract 0xef0ba56da26b4ddfef0959c1d0fc7a73a908befc paid its operator 224.980662844423876994 ETH in fourteen internal transfers and was funded by that operator with 17.9 ETH of buy capital, all of which it spent through the SushiSwap router; the contract's balance is zero and its complete internal ledger closes at 242.880662844423876994 ETH in and out, so the net extraction is exactly 207.080662844423876994 ETH. Attacker-supplied capital and gas are excluded; nothing was recovered. Realised proceeds are used rather than any NORMIE mark: the token's price collapsed by roughly 99% inside the anchor transaction as a direct result of the forced selling, so no spot mark on the 237,150,000 NORMIE the contract dumped or the 235,936,669.33411148 NORMIE the pair absorbed would be sellable. A further 100.05140219385335 ETH left the SushiSwap pair to the token's own teamWalletAddress 0xd8056b0f8aa2126a8db6f0b3109fe9127617beb2 through the same forced swapbacks in the anchor transaction; that value accrued to the project's designated fee wallet rather than to the attacker and is deliberately excluded, so this figure is a conservative floor on the liquidity destroyed.

incidents.name: Bogged Finance BOG transfer-fee distribution mint
incidents.summary: The original BOG token 0xd7b729ef857aa773f47d37088a1181bb3fbf0099 credits the staker share of every transfer fee by only raising _totalFees in _distribute, while _transferFrom debits the sender just the amount sent plus the burnt part. The distributed share is therefore minted for LP stakers without leaving the sender. The attacker staked BOG/WBNB LP so that it held most of the stake, then made hundreds of transfers to itself per transaction, each paying itself newly created BOG. It sold the inflated BOG into the PancakeSwap V1 WBNB/BOG pair 0x1490c68d0d5e3e7c9d53299824c9bb816639aa66, taking 11,865.986498156644903693 WBNB over 33 transactions.

loss.notes: Exact net WBNB Transfer outflow of the WBNB/BOG pair across the 33 successful calls from EOA 0x4622a1f3 to its contract 0xe576790f (blocks 7633044-7633176); the attacker entered with 2 BNB and supplied no other WBNB, so flash swaps, liquidity adds and removals net out inside the sum. The final call 0xf3a66e59 alone nets 11,358.106750514743826316 WBNB. Pair WBNB reserves fell from 14,729.847493066028204336 (block 7633043) to 1,947.278848679801098223 (block 7633176); the difference beyond the attacker's sum is other traders' sells in the same window. BOG stakers' dilution is not valued. DefiLlama lists 3.0M USD.

incidents.name: Paraluni MasterChef depositByAddLiquidity unvalidated tokens
incidents.summary: MasterChef.depositByAddLiquidity() passes the caller-supplied token addresses straight into _doTransferIn and paraRouter.addLiquidity without checking them against the pool LP pair, and addLiquidityInternal then credits the deposit with the raw increase of the pool LP token balance (newBalance - oldBalance). The attacker supplied two tokens of their own whose transferFrom re-entered deposit(pid, amount) with real LP tokens, so the same real LP deposit was counted twice: once by the reentrant deposit and once as the balance delta measured by depositByAddLiquidity. Two withdraw() calls then removed roughly twice the LP that had been paid in.

loss.notes: Components are the MasterChef 0x633fa755a83b015cccdc451f82c57ea0bd32b4b4 net ERC-20 outflow across the 45 depositByAddLiquidity transactions of the campaign (blocks 16005645-16009258), with the seven Para-LP positions resolved into their underlying tokens at the pre-campaign pair state of block 16005644. Raw LP outflow: 220760.392147321091610368 USDT/BUSD LP (98.81% of supply), 14627.197755208809754584 CAKE/BUSD LP, 1674.617368475105344132 WBNB/BUSD LP, 441.367896732979141899 BTCB/BUSD LP, 422.118760287837538705 ETH/BUSD LP, 44.402791154001324517 ETH/WBNB LP and 34.988011674692057714 BTCB/WBNB LP, plus the single-asset pools' 12.937257935935226619 BTCB, 25.823882791173237295 WBNB and 40.931924021235680678 ETH. The 3,774,958.8 T42 minted into the MasterChef as block reward and the 45 worthless attacker-pair LP tokens deposited are excluded. Cross-check: the attacker EOA 0x94bc1d555e63eea23fe7fdbf937ef3f9ac5fcf8f went from 0.889503956097239466 BNB at block 16002700 to 4638.544756398378995119 BNB at block 16009400 after selling everything, i.e. about USD 1.74M realised against USD 1.78M of gross assets removed, the difference being swap fees and slippage. Nothing was recovered.

incidents.name: BunniHubLogic withdrawal rounding reserve depletion
incidents.summary: BunniHubLogic.withdraw() used imprecise rounding while updating the pool's active balances. Forty-four small withdrawals burned negligible shares but substantially reduced the accounted stablecoin reserves, allowing subsequent swaps and withdrawals to extract more USDC and USDT than the burned shares entitled the attacker to.

loss.notes: Bunni's official post-mortem reports approximately $8.4 million lost from the Ethereum USDC/USDT pool and Unichain weETH/ETH pool through the same withdrawal-rounding defect. The structured stablecoin components reproduce $2.37 million of exact Ethereum proceeds and provide an onchain cross-check.

incidents.name: Penpie Pendle-market reward reentrancy
incidents.summary: PendleStaking's batchHarvestMarketRewards() harvested rewards from a permissionlessly registered Pendle market without a shared reentrancy guard or a trusted-market boundary. The attacker registered a market backed by an attacker-controlled SY token, then re-entered depositMarket() during the harvest callback so pre-deposit reward accounting credited its position with the real markets' pending rewards; it then withdrew Penpie's staked Pendle LP as if it were the attacker's reward entitlement.

loss.notes: Ethereum-only gross victim depletion, measured from the three successful drain receipts (0x56e09abb, 0x42b2ec27, 0x663b55a1). Each drain is an atomic flash-borrow: the attacker contract borrows the SY-underlying from Balancer, mints Pendle LP, deposits it into PendleStaking, re-enters to double-count its LP entitlement, withdraws twice the deposited LP (its own plus an equal amount of Penpie's staked inventory), redeems all of it, and repays the flash loan. The flash loans and the attacker's own LP net to zero within each receipt, so the attack contract's net positive token balance at the end of each drain equals the value extracted from Penpie. Summed across the three drains the attacker contracts (0x4af4c234, 0x4476b6ca, 0xcde2cd6a) netted the SY-underlying: 2722.896986125761481022 wstETH, 2522685.569779116882495579 sUSDe, 4100.512911329222524018 agETH and 2695.125694968916318170 rswETH; the four Pendle markets drained were the wstETH, sUSDe, agETH and rswETH pools (PENDLE-LPT tokens 0xc374f7ec, 0xd1d7d997, 0x6010676b, 0x038c1b03) whose net outflow from proxy 0x6e799758 reconciles with these redemptions. The USD total 27,311,618 values only those four liquid SY-underlying assets at DefiLlama incident prices (wstETH, sUSDe and rswETH direct-token series). agETH has no DefiLlama series with a pre-loss observation, so it is valued at the WETH incident price 2446.82956672678 (source-11, observed 1725387742, before the anchor) times agETH's on-chain convertToAssets rate 0.999221757635697525, i.e. 2444.925340299725; DefiLlama's kelp-gain series (nearest observation 2450.63 at 1725409884, about six hours later) confirms this to within 0.2 percent. The attacker also kept the paired yield tokens (YT-stETH, YT-sUSDE, YT-agETH, YT-rswETH) whose exact quantities are recorded with null USD because they are decaying, thinly traded and lack a clean price series; they are additional extraction, so the measured figure is a slight lower bound. Confidence is medium because agETH and rswETH are large restaked-ETH quantities spot-marked rather than measured at the attacker's realised disposal, and the yield-token leg is unpriced. Zokyo reports about $27M and CUBE3 about $28M for the combined Ethereum and Arbitrum campaign; the Ethereum leg measured here is essentially that headline, and the separate Arbitrum record (eip155:42161:0x67c5400d...) holds the Arbitrum loss so nothing is double-counted. Later Penpie recovery negotiations are not netted.

incidents.name: Trade On Orion stake-release liability desynchronization
incidents.summary: OrionVault.requestReleaseStake() credited locked ORN directly back to the caller's internal asset balance and cleared the stake without reconciling an existing ORN liability. Repeating the stake-release and redeem cycle therefore left duplicate liability entries for the same asset. MarginalFunctionality.calcLiabilities() valued every entry from the same live balance, so a later positive ORN balance was counted several times as collateral and checkPosition() accepted large unsupported debits that the attacker withdrew. The deployed redeemAtomic path did require the recovered signature to equal order.sender; the seed row's signature-bypass classification was incorrect.

loss.notes: The loss is the exact campaign-attributable depletion of the Exchange proxy's external asset balances. In the final drain transaction, the proxy lost 19,844.686077960000000000 USDT net of the 4,000,000 USDT flash-funded deposit made inside that transaction, and sent 498,921.92920826 ORN, 62,444.730331000000000000 XRP and 79.896159740000000000 native BNB to attacker-controlled addresses. Before the drain, the same campaign had externally deposited 1.000000000000000000 USDT and 0.30000000 ORN into the proxy in the three transactions listed in source-7; excluding that attacker-supplied capital leaves the four asset components recorded above. The flash pair retained 10,400 USDT on repayment, so attacker proceeds were lower than victim depletion by that financing fee. No recovery is netted. The USD total uses stablecoin par and DefiLlama's token-specific incident-time prices of USD 1.44/ORN, USD 0.52477/XRP and USD 595.9736912132389/BNB. The widely reported approximately USD 645,000 estimate is not used because it does not reproduce the exact onchain quantities at contemporaneous prices.

incidents.name: GoodDollar GoodFundManager untrusted staking callback accounting
incidents.summary: GoodFundManager.collectInterest accepted arbitrary staking-contract addresses and measured reserve balance changes across calls to those untrusted contracts, so attacker-controlled reserve changes during a callback were misclassified as collected staking interest.

loss.notes: The anchor receipt shows an exact net 625,140.676705135213042766 DAI outflow from Compound's cDAI contract and the same DAI increase at campaign beneficiary 0x6c08f56ff2b15db7ddf2f123f5bffb68e308161b after the reserve's cDAI was redeemed. DAI is valued at stablecoin par. The simultaneously created 14,062,071,177.43 G$ and 10,213,394,244.25 G$X express the accounting failure and inflationary harm but are not added to the DAI reserve loss; later freeze, fee, and burn mitigation is likewise not netted against the transferred DAI.

incidents.name: Sumer Money sdrETH repayBorrowBehalf refund reentrancy
incidents.summary: Sumer Money's CEther market sdrETH implements repayBorrowBehalf(address) by refunding any excess msg.value with a gas-forwarding msg.sender.call before it calls the nonReentrant repayBorrowBehalfInternal. During that callback the repaid ETH is already part of getCashPrior() while totalBorrows still carries the debt it settles, so exchangeRateStoredInternal() = (totalCash + totalBorrows - totalReserves) / totalSupply double-counts the same ETH. The attacker drained the market's cash with borrow(), repaid it with one wei of excess, and inside the refund callback the sdrETH exchange rate stood at 2.000000282255694646 instead of the 1.000000141462699840 the market carried a moment earlier: they redeemed their full 150 ETH deposit for half their sdrETH and, with the other half still valued at the doubled rate as Comptroller collateral, borrowed 310,000 USDC from sdrUSDC and 10.877 cbETH from sdrcbETH that were never repaid.

loss.notes: The two components are the exact net ERC-20 depletion of the Sumer markets in the single exploit transaction: sdrUSDC 0x142017b52c99d3dfe55e49d79df0baf7f4478c0c lost 309,999.999999 USDC and sdrcbETH 0x6345af6da3ebd9df468e37b473128fd3079c4a4b lost 10.877097943908610977 cbETH, both borrowed by 0x13d27a2d66ea33a4bc581d5fefb0b2a8defe9fe7 inside the reentrant frame and both still outstanding at block 13076770. The 150 WETH plus 645,000 USDC Balancer flash loan and the 645,000 USDC of sdrUSDC collateral were attacker-supplied and fully returned, so they are not loss; sdrETH's own ETH balance nets to zero across the transaction. The attacker sold the stolen cbETH twelve minutes later for 11.560845752555412057 WETH, which at the DefiLlama ETH price of USD 3,388.05 is USD 39,168 against the USD 39,249 marked here, so the sale did not move the cbETH market and the incident-price mark is realisable. Not counted: 74.999989365185081199 sdrETH left unredeemed at 0x13d27a2d and still held there, an unbacked residual claim on the sdrETH market rather than an extraction.

incidents.name: Rari Ethereum Pool transient ibETH exchange-rate inflation
incidents.summary: AlphaPoolController.getBalance valued Rari's ibETH shares with ibETH.totalETH()/totalSupply() during an external Alpha Homora Bank.work callback. The attacker transiently donated ETH to inflate totalETH, caused Rari withdrawals to burn too many ibETH shares at the manipulated rate, then removed the donation and repeated the cycle.

loss.notes: Measured onchain as campaign net proceeds before gas. Immediately after the attacker's nonce-7 setup transaction, the EOA and helper jointly hold 1,040.677867052043994188 ETH; after the final successful nonce-191 transaction they hold 4,005.135463694322340589 ETH. Their increase is 2,964.457596642278346401 ETH, and the 184 consecutive successful campaign transactions at nonces 8 through 191 dispose of 23.17274534 ETH as gas. A separate non-campaign transaction sends 2 ETH from 0x0eb791bb0a62baffb28d46dfecfc650b4b82a16c to the EOA during the window, so net exploit proceeds before gas are 2,985.630341982278346401 ETH. Transfers between the two attacker-controlled accounts cancel. This account-based net measure is used because the transient ibETH manipulation makes a simple Rari/Alpha contract-balance delta overstate victim depletion. Rari's contemporaneous post-mortem rounded the extraction to about 2,600 ETH and $10 million.

incidents.name: NewMarketTrading SquidRouterModule unbound delegate
incidents.summary: SquidRouterModule accepted Axelar express execution while treating caller-supplied sourceAddress and delegate values as authority and never binding the delegate to msg.sender. Forged payloads therefore drove victim Safes to approve and swap valuable assets into attacker pools.

loss.notes: Rekt reports a $3.98 million gross campaign across 308 successful drain transactions affecting 88 Safes on Base, Arbitrum, and Ethereum. NMT offered a white-hat bounty, but the cited reporting records no returned proceeds; recovery is not netted.

incidents.name: Platypus pool cash/liability accounting manipulation
incidents.summary: A partial withdrawal reduced the full LP liability despite insufficient cash, allowing repeated coverage-ratio and slippage manipulation across deposits, withdrawals, and swaps.

loss.notes: CertiK reports $2.23 million of WAVAX and sAVAX taken across the three related flash-loan transactions by two attacker EOAs; the figure is the aggregate gross incident loss before recovery.

incidents.name: BelugaDex liability/coverage withdrawal accounting
incidents.summary: The pool applied inconsistent liability and equilibrium-coverage accounting across deposits, swaps, and withdrawals, allowing a repeated 21-transaction campaign to deplete its USDT and USDC.e custody assets.

loss.notes: Gross loss is the exact net ERC-20 outflow across all 21 successful campaign receipts from Beluga's USDT custody contract 0xcff307451e52b7385a7538f4cf4a861c7a60192b and USDC.e custody contract 0x7cc32ee9567b48182e5424a2a782b2aa6cd0b37b. Netting transfers into the same custody contracts excludes campaign financing and returns 65,348.918901 USDT plus 115,368.655450 USDC.e. Both components are valued at par at the incident anchor; later exchange proceeds, fees, gas, and recovery are outside this gross victim-depletion boundary.

incidents.name: Cashverse staking distributor public depositBNB swaps with no minimum output
incidents.summary: Unverified staking/reward distributor 0x2d70d62d held 225.995 BNB. Its public depositBNB() (0x42220f34) swaps the whole BNB balance for ADAcash through PancakeSwap with amountOutMin 0 once any stake exists. The attacker flash-borrowed 12,000 WBNB and pushed up the ADAcash price with 53 maximum-size buys. It then called depositBNB() and sold into the inflated pair, capturing the distributor's BNB.

loss.notes: Exact native BNB depletion of distributor 0x2d70d62deb1cb9918ff6be7bb5d173e8cd4ad854, recorded as the wrapped-BNB address and valued at the DefiLlama WBNB quote. The attacker's flash-loaned WBNB and buys are circular. The EOA's BNB balance rose by 150.36 BNB across the block; the rest went to pools and fees. The candidate figure of USD 107.9k is not this gross measure.

incidents.name: Platypus MasterPlatypusV4 emergencyWithdraw solvency check
incidents.summary: MasterPlatypusV4.emergencyWithdraw() checked solvency before zeroing the user's staked LP balance. The check therefore saw the collateral still present and passed, after which the function returned that collateral without requiring repayment of the USP debt it secured.

loss.notes: Platypus reports $9.19 million lost across three attacks by the same exploiter and defect. The anchored first attack accounted for approximately $8.5 million; the reported gross campaign amount precedes subsequent freezes and recoveries.

incidents.name: MEV bot 0xd61492 router unauthenticated command entry
incidents.summary: The bot's vault 0xd614927a ("BBVault") accepts commands only from its router 0x8db0efee. The router's entry 0x0582f20f runs a caller-supplied command program for any caller, including DELEGATECALL to caller-chosen code. An attacker contract called the router and had the vault take flash loans from a fake Aave-style pool it had just deployed. The vault approved that pool for each repayment, and the pool used the allowances to pull the vault's WBTC, WETH, ARB, DAI, USDT and USDC.e to the attacker.

loss.notes: Exact net depletion of vault 0xd614927acfb9744441180c2525faf4cedb70207f in source-1, equal to the attacker EOA's receipts. The flash-loan legs through the fake pool and router net to zero. WBTC, WETH, DAI and USDT use the contemporaneous Ethereum-mainnet DefiLlama quotes, because DefiLlama has no historical Arbitrum quote for those tokens at this time. The router's 2 base-unit USDC.e debit is omitted as de minimis.

incidents.name: Penpie Pendle-market reward reentrancy (Arbitrum)
incidents.summary: The Arbitrum PendleStakingSideChain (same defect as Ethereum) harvested rewards from a permissionlessly registered Pendle market without a shared reentrancy guard, so the attacker re-entered depositMarket() during batchHarvestMarketRewards() to double-count its LP entitlement and withdrew Penpie's staked gUSDC-market Pendle LP as reward.

loss.notes: Arbitrum-only gross victim depletion, measured from the single successful drain receipt 0x67c5400d. The drain is an atomic flash-borrow: the attacker contract 0x4bc9815b borrows 621667.936099 gUSDC from Balancer (0xba1222...), mints SY-gUSDC and Pendle LP, deposits the LP into PendleStaking proxy 0x6db96bbeb, re-enters depositMarket during harvest to double-count, withdraws twice the deposited LP (its own plus an equal slice of Penpie's inventory), redeems it and repays the flash loan. The flash loan nets to zero within the receipt, so the attack contract's end-of-tx net positive balance is the extraction: 616348.200200 gUSDC plus 114673.157598 YT-gUSDC. Proxy 0x6db96bbeb's net outflow of 330469.756983 gUSDC-market PENDLE-LPT (0xa877a0e1) reconciles with these redemptions. The USD total values only the liquid gUSDC (a Gains Network yield-bearing USDC vault token) at its DefiLlama pre-incident price of 1.10 (observation 1725382691, before the drain); the paired YT-gUSDC is recorded with exact quantity but null USD because it is a decaying, thinly traded yield token, so the figure is a slight lower bound. This Arbitrum leg is separate from and not duplicated in the Ethereum record (eip155:1:0x56e09abb...); together they make up the reported ~$27M-$28M cross-chain campaign. Later Penpie recovery negotiations are not netted.

incidents.name: Cyrus Finance CyrusTreasury spot-priced LP withdrawal
incidents.summary: CyrusTreasury pays every USDT-denominated exit or reward claim through withdrawUSDTFromAny, which sizes the PancakeSwap V3 liquidity to remove from the pool's current slot0 price and then collects both tokens of the removed liquidity to the claimant. The treasury's ETH/USDT position sat out of range as roughly 562k USDT. The attacker flash-borrowed 1,798 ETH, sold it into the pool to move the price into the bottom of the position's range, and exited a Cyrus position owed 1,707.055 USDT; at that price the position showed only about 1,853 USDT, so the treasury removed 92% of its liquidity and sent the attacker 1,289.35 ETH plus 1,707.055 USDT before the attacker bought the ETH price back and repaid the loan.

loss.notes: Victim depletion is the out-of-range USDT backing of the liquidity the attacker's exit removed from PancakeSwap V3 position 6358139 (range ticks 55318 to 64492, where it holds only USDT): 55986950637933606610065 liquidity x (sqrtRatio(64492) - sqrtRatio(55318)) / 2^96 = 517785.322516154202754603 USDT, less the 1707.055 USDT the exit legitimately owed (Exited event data), = 516078.267516154202754603 USDT. The 1289.3536997589956 ETH the position paid out is not valued separately: the position bought it from the attacker's own 1,798-ETH sale in the same transaction with that USDT. The performance-fee leg (47392230286554365003 liquidity, 1.185199890884981 ETH plus 1.445 USDT to the protocol's fee receiver 0x6cd7bbb8a8c0c1b24a449c3ad8f913974de7b009) stayed with the protocol and is excluded. The attacker EOA netted 28.139762187797007 ETH and 454169.2170373848 USDT (about USD 512k at USD 2061.52 per ETH) after swap fees and the 1.0788 ETH flash fee; SlowMist reports USD 516,840. Nothing was recovered.

incidents.name: SynapLogic sale proxy unbounded referral rebates
incidents.summary: The SYP sale implementation paid a per-entry referral rebate without bounding aggregate rebates by the payment received. A bounded pre-remediation campaign depleted the proxy's native ETH and USDC inventory through the affected native and USDC purchase paths.

loss.notes: Gross loss is exact victim-proxy depletion across the bounded 22-transaction campaign. The native anchor sends 13.82328425 ETH into the proxy and pays 41.46985275 ETH from it, depleting 27.6465685 ETH; archive balance falls from exactly 27.6465685 ETH to zero. Nineteen later incident receipts send 1,770.548698 USDC into the proxy and 5,311.097380 USDC from it, for 3,540.548682 USDC receipt-net depletion. Two linked precursor transfers from a campaign EOA supply another 90 USDC and are excluded from victim loss. Archive balances reconcile exactly: 3,450.548686 opening + 90 precursor + 1,770.548698 receipt inflows - 5,311.097380 outflows = 0.000004 ending, so victim inventory depletion is 3,450.548682 USDC. The transaction set includes every proxy USDC outflow from the first linked receipt through the last cleanup receipt before the first post-incident upgrade. USDC is valued at par; the closest preceding DefiLlama ETH observation is $3,189.1171414638065 at 1768866603, 12 seconds before the anchor. Exact component values total $91,618.69418800332, replacing the seed's rounded $144,000 estimate.

incidents.name: JUDAO sell-hook pair-reserve desynchronization
incidents.summary: JUDAO's sell hook removed JUDAO from its own PancakeSwap pair for daily mining and burn/tax accounting, synchronized the lower balance as the AMM reserve, and only then completed the seller-to-pair transfer. The attacker triggered this path and used the resulting balance-over-reserve gap as apparent swap input to withdraw excess USDT.

loss.notes: Within the exploit receipt the JUDAO/USDT pair receives 2,295,723.159642210185991282 USDT and sends 236,331.524657750233556859 USDT during JUDAO's fee processing plus 2,523,596.497552140965784945 USDT in the attacker's direct swap. Net victim-pair depletion is therefore exactly 464,204.862567681013350522 USDT. The attacker used 22,613.847147473753465178 USDT of those proceeds to buy 36 BNB, repaid the 2,295,723.159642210185991282 USDT flash loan, and forwarded 205,259.490762457026328485 residual USDT to the EOA. Those dispositions are already contained in the pair's net USDT loss and are not added again. The exact victim depletion replaces the seed row's $205,259 figure, which recorded only residual attacker USDT and omitted both the BNB conversion and fee-recipient outflows.

incidents.name: Defrost LSWUSDC reentrancy
incidents.summary: LSWUSDC computed deposit shares from its temporarily reduced assets during an ERC-3156 flash loan and allowed deposit() from the borrower callback. The callback therefore minted excess shares before flashLoan() restored the principal through a second accounting deposit, letting the attacker redeem more USDC than supplied.

loss.notes: The exploit receipt gives the attacker cluster a net 173,637.629135 USDC after all LSWUSDC and Trader Joe flash-loan principal and fees are repaid. Transfers between the attacker EOA and helper are internal to the cluster.

incidents.name: Hundred Finance hWBTC exchange-rate inflation
incidents.summary: The Compound-v2 fork derived hWBTC's exchange rate from its raw WBTC balance and rounded redeemUnderlying share amounts down. In the nearly empty market, the attacker retained two wei of hWBTC, donated WBTC to inflate their collateral value, borrowed every other Optimism market, then redeemed the donation while the inflated collateral position remained.

loss.notes: The $7.4 million gross loss is the published campaign total for the two Optimism attack transactions. Hundred Finance separately described the theft as approximately $7 million.

incidents.name: Ploutoz live-reserve collateral pricing
incidents.summary: The DOP collateral oracle valued DOP from live DOP/BUSD pool reserves, so a transient reserve imbalance produced unsupported borrowing power.

loss.notes: Gross depletion of the six pToken reserves, combined with the protocol controller as one victim union, is 85 CAKE, 18,000 DOLLY, 18 WETH, 1.6 BTCB, 89,000 USDT, and 90,000 BUSD. Receipt transfers and archive balances independently reconcile every component; fee transfers between each pToken and the controller cancel inside the union. The controller retains the 8,450 DOP collateral supplied in the receipt. Flash liquidity, helper withdrawals, and later swaps are financing or disposal of already-counted assets and are excluded. The imported approximately $365,000 estimate is replaced by exact asset depletion and independently preceding CAKE, ETH, and BTC prices. Exact decimal component arithmetic totals $363,406.751246242747830; the JSON number is its nearest IEEE-754 representation.

incidents.name: CorkHook beforeSwap missing pool-manager restriction
incidents.summary: The incident combined a rollover-pricing defect that let the attacker acquire an excessive CT position for dust with CorkHook.beforeSwap() lacking the authorization check that restricted calls to the official Uniswap v4 PoolManager. A direct call to the hook abused its callback and refund path to obtain matching DS, and the attacker redeemed the CT/DS pair against the protocol's wstETH reserves.

loss.notes: Cork reports 3,761 wstETH extracted, and the selected transaction records exactly 3,760.885365943909071528 wstETH transferred from ModuleCore to the attack contract. Verichains values the incident at approximately $12 million; the USD amount is the reported rounded valuation of this onchain asset outflow.

incidents.name: UPS sell path burns the pair's reserve
incidents.summary: On every non-whitelisted sale to its USDT pair, the UPS token burns 95% of the sold amount directly from the pair's balance and calls sync() before the swap settles. The attacker used flash-loaned USDT to buy almost all UPS out of the pair, sending it to an address on the public whitelist because ordinary buys revert. It then sold 4,982,240 UPS. The burn cut the pair's UPS reserve to 1 wei, so the swap paid out 560,128 USDT.

loss.notes: Exact USDT depletion of the UPS/USDT PancakeSwap pair 0x5db4604c8952a8c3474e8ac33e0d31814d75f786 in the single exploit transaction; the drained UPS reserve is worthless afterwards and is not counted. Flash-loan principal and fees, and the UPS sent to the whitelisted recipient, are attacker-side flows, not victim loss.

incidents.name: Sharwa margin Hegic option collateral valued by a Uniswap V3 spot quote
incidents.summary: Sharwa's HegicModule values a Hegic option NFT held as margin collateral by passing its USDC.e payoff to UniswapModuleWithoutChainlink.getInputPositionValue, which returns the Uniswap V3 Quoter's live quote through the thin USDC.e/USDC 0.05% pool. Inside a Balancer flash loan the attacker pushed 22,000 USDC into that pool, raising an option with a 0.137528 USDC.e payoff to about 21,223 USDC of collateral value (later 36,584), and borrowed USDC, WETH and WBTC from Sharwa's liquidity pools against it.

loss.notes: Gross depletion of Sharwa's USDC, WETH and WBTC liquidity pools by the three borrows in the anchor, left as debt against margin account 19 whose only collateral is Hegic option 16129 with a 0.137528 USDC.e payoff (about 0.14 USDC), which is not netted. Native USDC at par; WETH and WBTC at DefiLlama marks one to two minutes before the block. The attacker EOA received 32,850.892483 USDC after swapping the borrowed WETH and WBTC to USDC and repaying the 22,000 USDC Balancer loan; the attacker's round trip left the USDC.e/USDC pool about 18.69 USDC richer. No later borrow occurred on MarginTrading.

incidents.name: Libertify LibertiVault deposit swap-callback reentrancy
incidents.summary: LibertiVault.deposit(uint256,address,bytes) snapshots the net asset value with getNavInNumeraire(Rounding.Up) before pulling the caller's assets, then hands control to an untrusted callee: _deposit forwards the caller's raw calldata to the 1inch AggregationRouterV4 through userSwap, and that router calls back into the caller-nominated IAggregationExecutor. Nothing on deposit, _deposit or userSwap holds a reentrancy lock, so the executor reenters deposit. The inner call mints against the vault state it sees, and when the outer call resumes it computes shares = totalSupply().mulDiv(valueDeposited, nav) with totalSupply() read after the inner mint but nav still the stale pre-reentrancy snapshot. The share-price invariant that a mint must be priced against the same NAV whose supply it divides is violated, and the attacker's four nested mints issued 23,397,196.64 shares to itself against a pre-attack totalSupply of 21,062.278834564420093169 before it redeemed them for the vault's reserves. No configured parameter value repairs this: minDeposit, maxDeposit, invariant, entryFee and exitFee only scale the mint, they do not restore the NAV/supply pairing.

loss.notes: Exact victim depletion, measured as the change in the vault 0x9c80a455ecaca7025a45f5fa3b85fd6a462a447b's own token balances across the single exploit transaction: WETH 129.411606107394699466 -> 0.011673447233479552 and USDT 81476.027164 -> 26663.335833. The attacker's two 5,000,000-USDT Aave V2 flash loans and the 0.004 WETH it deposited are attacker-supplied inputs and are netted out; the 9,000 USDT of flash-loan premium it paid is not deducted. WETH and USDT are deep markets on Polygon and the attacker's ~5.56 WETH Uniswap V3 sale did not move them, so a contemporaneous spot mark is used rather than realised proceeds; the DefiLlama WETH quote is the Ethereum WETH series because DefiLlama carries no Polygon WETH series. The seed row and the DeFiHackLabs header both state ~452,000 USD; that figure is not reproducible from the receipt at any contemporaneous price and is not used.

incidents.name: YYDS pair-balance price manipulation
incidents.summary: consumptionReturnPool.getPriceOfUSDT() converted stored USDT-denominated returns to YYDS using the instantaneous ERC-20 balances of the YYDS/USDT pair, with no TWAP or manipulation protection. During a pair flash swap, the attacker reduced the pair's USDT balance from 1186471.120130432957137499 USDT to 1.2 USDT while its YYDS balance remained 1656.938602269843892480. Integer normalization then produced a price of only 0.000603864734299516 USDT per YYDS. Two attacker-controlled callers used genuine matured return records totalling 1.683 USDT to withdraw 2787.048000000004191719 YYDS and sold it into the same pair. The withdrawal functions do index msg.sender's stored entitlement arrays; the defect is the manipulable pair-balance oracle, not missing entitlement checks.

loss.notes: The YYDS/USDT pair 0xd5ca448b06f8eb5acc6921502e33912fa3d63b12 starts the exploit with 1186471.120130432957137499 USDT and 1656.938602269843892480 YYDS. Its Swap event records 1186469.920024032957137499 USDT out, then 444183.647236821385893095 USDT and 2787.048000000004191719 YYDS in, leaving 444184.847343221385893095 USDT. The causal net pair loss is therefore exactly 742286.272787211571244404 USDT, and the receipt transfers that exact remainder from the attacker contract to the attacker EOA. USDT is valued at par. The 2787.048000000004191719 YYDS released from consumptionReturnPool is the instrument sold to create this same recorded USDT loss and is not valued again, avoiding double-counting one economic loss. The seed row's USD amount 742286 is a rounded version of the reproduced pair loss.

incidents.name: TUR Stake spot-priced power and unaccrued referral power
incidents.summary: The TUR Stake contract converts staked TUR into mining power from the spot reserves of the TUR/NOBEL and NOBEL/USDT PancakeSwap pairs, and credits 20% and 5% of that power to the staker's first two referrers by raising their power without adjusting their rewardDebt, so each referrer can immediately claim the new power times the whole accumulated reward per share. The attacker borrowed 1.9M USDT, bought NOBEL and TUR to inflate both spot prices, staked 840,992 TUR from an account bound under its own referrer accounts, and had those referrers claim, draining the contract's entire 18.8M TUR reward balance before selling it back to USDT.

loss.notes: The Stake contract's TUR balance fell from 18797013.727945965666304686 at block 88871541 to 1 wei at 88871542. Of that, 589140.185415031974863037 TUR went as the 3% claim fee to the project fund wallet 0xb3026bdc58c591c1137a1fec9506915e39789923 (logs 20, 24) and is excluded, and the attacker's own 840992.452555100162463228 TUR staked in (log 23) is netted out, leaving 18207873.542530933691441648 TUR taken by the referrer accounts (logs 21 and 25 in, forwarded to the attacker at 22 and 26). The attacker's selling moved the TUR price, so the value is the realised gain: the EOA received 2033398.302560718774502099 USDT from the NOBEL/USDT pair (log 71) against the 1900000 USDT it put in (log 5) and repaid (75), a gain of 133398.302560718774502099 USDT, forwarded with 92.09 USDT of its own balance as 133490.392419136677677840 USDT to 0xef670d9c2e24d1788f39ad35c70f4cc51b4e5898 (log 77). USDT is valued at par; 76303.19 USDT of NOBEL transfer tax paid to 0x972bfaae4093baf00bd5b4db2e11d143adc16f97 during the sale is not counted.

incidents.name: Unknown Base account module unauthenticated execute drains vault
incidents.summary: Account 0xc851e5a0 is an EIP-1167 clone of a router that resolves its logic through a registry to module 0xa2362ea5. That module's ERC725X-style execute(uint256,address,uint256,bytes) performs the call for any caller. Vault 0x36057cb0 lets 0xc851e5a0 withdraw. An attacker's constructor had the account call the vault's withdraw (0xaaa18f86) with itself as recipient and took 300,000 USDC. A second actor repeated the call nine days later and took 100,000 USDC.

loss.notes: Exact USDC debits from vault 0x36057cb08b7c19d8368bcad987484db8184145f6 through the open account execute: 300,000 USDC in source-1 (attacker 0xcccc6400) and 100,000 USDC in source-3 (second actor 0x359e11ab, 2026-05-06). No attacker input is involved. Native USDC on Base is valued at par.

incidents.name: Unknown BSC pool poolWithdraw accepts empty signer and signature lists
incidents.summary: The unverified implementation behind proxy 0x20dbf429 authorizes poolWithdraw(token, amount, to, ..., signers[], deadline, signatures[]) with a multi-signature check that passes when both arrays are empty. From block 83557908 several unrelated callers withdrew the pool's USDT to themselves with empty signer and signature lists until the owner upgraded the implementation at block 83655321.

loss.notes: Exact USDT debits of pool proxy 0x20dbf42970eb3fabe62615534c4ef15fd4d59596 in all 23 successful poolWithdraw transactions between the first exercise and the fix upgrade, all with empty signer and signature lists. Components: the first actor (0x997a283b via 0x77f2601f); two EIP-7702 EOAs sharing delegate 0xa124d3858ab98f75534ad9a2a2fbd1cb1f678b21 (59,781.25 and 59,974.609375); the BlockSec-cited actor 0xc6e8210e; and 19 small withdrawals by other callers. BlockSec's ~$180K corresponds to the last three large transactions.

incidents.name: Parity WalletLibrary unprotected initWallet + kill
incidents.summary: WalletLibrary was deployed uninitialised and its initWallet() was reachable on the library itself, so anyone could take ownership and call kill(), selfdestructing the shared delegatecall target and bricking every Parity multisig pointing at it.

loss.notes: Parity reports 513,774.16 ETH blocked across 587 dependent wallets. The ETH is valued using the retained incident-time DefiLlama price; Parity also reports additional inaccessible tokens, which are excluded because the post-mortem does not provide a complete token inventory or valuation.

incidents.name: Visor Finance RewardsHypervisor unvalidated depositor
incidents.summary: RewardsHypervisor.deposit() trusted a caller-supplied `from` contract both to report its owner and to transfer VISR, without validating the contract or confirming receipt. The attacker hook no-opped the transfer and reentered deposit once, causing two vVISR share mints backed by zero VISR.

loss.notes: The follow-up withdrawal transferred exactly 8,812,958.138426966035592617 VISR from RewardsHypervisor to the attacker. Published analyses value the incident at approximately $8.2 million.

incidents.name: Grim Finance GrimBoostVault depositFor reentrancy
incidents.summary: GrimBoostVault.depositFor(token, amount, user) took the deposit token as a caller-supplied parameter and minted shares around an unguarded external transferFrom call, so the attacker passed its own contract as the token and re-entered depositFor from that callback, minting eight tranches of vault shares against a single SpiritSwap BTC/WFTM LP deposit before burning them all in withdrawAll to drain the vault.

loss.notes: The $30 million figure is the rounded aggregate loss across Grim Finance vaults affected by the same depositFor reentrancy campaign. Rekt reports approximately $30 million and Beefy's incident report estimates $32 million; this record uses the conservative rounded estimate.

incidents.name: Allbridge CCTP phantom deposit
incidents.summary: CCTPTokenMessenger accepted a generic Circle attestation, decoded a token amount from its attacker-authored body, and credited a deposit without verifying that Circle minted USDC.

loss.notes: At block 50157344 the Router held 191,155.976393 USDC; 191,112.338841 USDC had been legitimately minted into it three blocks earlier and the remaining baseline was 43.637552 USDC. The attacker flash-borrowed and deposited 808,844.023607 USDC, then redeemed a phantom 1,000,000 USDC credit for a 999,000 USDC payout. The Router ended with its 1,000 USDC fee, so exact pre-existing victim depletion was 190,155.976393 USDC. The 404.422012 USDC flash-loan premium reduces attacker proceeds, not gross victim loss.

incidents.name: Superfluid IDA forged callAgreement context
incidents.summary: Superfluid agreements decoded the ctx bytes from caller-shaped call data without checking the host's ctx stamp. Through Host.callAgreement the attacker passed a forged context naming victims as msgSender, created and updated IDA indexes as those accounts, distributed their super-token balances to itself and downgraded them.

loss.notes: Victim super-token depletion measured by the attacker's downgrades in source-2 across 24 victim (token, account) pairs. Illiquid tokens whose disposal moved the market (QI, MOCA, SDT, STACK) and sdam3CRV use realised proceeds; USDC.e at par; WETH and MATIC at DefiLlama quotes. The aggregate combines bases, hence method other. The theft completed in source-2 at 1644301024; realizedAt is the last attacker disposal used for the realised-proceeds valuation (second MOCA sale, block 24766896).

incidents.name: Sturdy LendingPool setUserUseReserveAsCollateral skips the oracle reentrancy probe
incidents.summary: Sturdy's LendingPool implementation carries an internal _validateOracle(user) that runs Balancer's reentrancy probe (BALWSTETHWETHOracle.check(), a WITHDRAW_INTERNAL manageUserBalance call that reverts inside a Vault context) over every reserve the user holds as collateral. deposit, _withdraw, repay, liquidationCall, finalizeTransfer and _executeBorrow all call it; setUserUseReserveAsCollateral does not, yet its ValidationLogic.validateSetUseReserveAsCollateral path reaches GenericLogic.balanceDecreaseAllowed and prices every collateral through SturdyOracle. The attacker re-entered that one entry point from inside a Balancer exitPool ETH callback, so the cB-stETH-STABLE collateral was valued from mid-exit pool balances: BALWSTETHWETHOracle.latestAnswer() returned 3.008 ETH instead of 1.034 ETH per unit. The invariant violated is that collateral valuation must never be computed while the Balancer Vault is mid-update; the deployed pool enforced it on every oracle-consuming entry point except this one.

loss.notes: Measured from Sturdy's own reserve accounting across the single exploit transaction. The WETH aToken 0xb1ebf8f77ae002d487e7bde22c6180be0af6a3d4 holds 513.367301825658717226 WETH at block 17460609 and 10.697994384645101142 at block 17460610, a fall of exactly 502.669307441013616084 WETH, while variableDebtWETH 0xe1ee5b789ba4ea5287999034fdf293361b53e024 total supply rises by the same 502.669307441013616084 and aWETH total supply is unchanged at 2317.920159523297738032, so no depositor share was minted or burned and the whole amount left the reserve as new debt. getUserAccountData at block 17460610 returns totalCollateralETH 0 for all five borrowing attacker contracts, so the debt is entirely uncollateralised; their variableDebtWETH balances are still outstanding and accruing at blocks 17470000, 17600000 and 18000000, so nothing was recovered. The attacker's own realised take was smaller, 442.455138966650236044 ETH net to the EOA in the same transaction, the widely reported 442 ETH; the roughly 60 WETH difference is Balancer and Curve slippage and a 1 ETH transfer to 0x690b9a9e9aa1c9db991c7721a92d351db4fac990, which does not reduce gross victim depletion. The 285,000 WETH Balancer flash loan and the Aave v3 flash loan are attacker-supplied inputs and are excluded.

incidents.name: Unknown Base MEV bot unvalidated uniswapV3SwapCallback
incidents.summary: Bot contract 0xe143b486's uniswapV3SwapCallback(int256,int256,bytes) pays the positive delta by transferFrom from a payer named in the callback data to msg.sender. The token comes from msg.sender.token0(), and nothing checks that the caller is a genuine pool. The operator EOA 0xc0ffee47 had approved the bot for WETH. The attacker's contract, posing as a pool, called the callback 219 times with the operator as payer and pulled 55.42 WETH.

loss.notes: Exact WETH depletion of operator EOA 0xc0ffee479e4cd49eafba87449225e17c53251226, which approved the bot: 219 transferFrom legs of 0.253043800616667712 WETH, then forwarded to the attacker EOA. Valued at the DefiLlama WETH quote.

incidents.name: RubicProxy routerCallNative executes an arbitrary whitelisted call
incidents.summary: RubicProxy.routerCallNative() forwards caller-supplied calldata to a caller-supplied router address, checking only that the router is in availableRouters. The contract makes no distinction between a swap router and an ERC-20, so once USDC was added to that list any caller could pass USDC as the router and transferFrom(victim, attacker, amount) as the calldata, spending the unlimited approvals users had granted the proxy.

loss.notes: The exploiter’s two transactions, at blocks 16260581 and 16260623, pull 1508457.385172 USDC from 49 distinct approval-holding addresses into the exploit contract 0x253dd81d642220267ccac1d8202c0b96a92b299e. Four further transactions in the same fifteen minutes drive the same defect from other senders against other collector contracts; several are consistent with whitehat rescue rather than theft, so they are not counted here and their amounts are not in this figure. Losses fall on individual approval holders, not on protocol-held funds. DefiLlama prices USDC at 1.00033 at the incident timestamp, so par is marginally conservative. Nothing was recovered by the protocol itself.

incidents.name: Startale smart-account initializer accepts any caller while the transaction-scoped deployment flag is set
incidents.summary: StartaleAccountFactory deploys each ERC-7579 account as an AccountProxy whose constructor sets an EIP-1153 transient flag, and StartaleSmartAccount.initializeAccount lets any external caller in once that flag is set. Transient storage lasts for the whole transaction, not the constructor frame. So a contract that calls createAccount for a counterfactual account that users had already funded can call initializeAccount again in the same transaction. It passes a malicious bootstrap that runs by DELEGATECALL in the account and sweeps its tokens and ETH. From 2026-09-15 at least 16 senders drained 1,052 pre-funded accounts this way in 255 transactions.

loss.notes: Sum over every re-initialization transaction through block 26080663 (2026-09-29T04:14:35Z) of ERC-20 Transfer logs whose sender is an account created by the factory in that same transaction, plus value-bearing CALL frames out of those accounts (callTracer). Nothing the attackers sent in is included. The campaign was still running at the cutoff. The last value-bearing transaction is 0x0a38150204b61699b24c941fe00354152888df64061d8ca27e3c1c81ce4cb47e (block 26080133). ETH was valued at the anchor price because 0.66911 of the 0.74924 ETH left on the anchor day. SHIB was valued at the time of its single drain (26004701).

incidents.name: LavaLending borrowable WETH/USDC.e wrapper LP priced from dust residual supply
incidents.summary: Lava listed the WETH/USDC.e UniV3 wrapper LP 0x6700b021 as a collateral and variable-borrow reserve and priced it with WrapperOracle: wrapper getAssetsBasedOnPrice(Chainlink-derived sqrtPrice) valued at Chainlink prices, divided by the wrapper's live totalSupply, guarded only by totalSupply >= 1e9 raw. A borrower could borrow the LP out of the reserve and redeem it, leaving aLP collateral claims far larger than the wrapper's residual supply. The per-share price of that dust residual could then be raised cheaply by fee donation, and the inflated price applied to every aLP claim. The attacker minted 430,623.99 LP and supplied it. A helper borrowed it all back and the attacker withdrew the other suppliers' 30.93 LP, then redeemed everything, cutting supply from 33.08 to 2.14 LP. After fee payments into the in-range pool, the oracle price rose from 14.25 to 19.88 USD, and the attacker borrowed every Lava reserve's cash.

loss.notes: Gross depletion of third-party cash in the five Lava reserves the receipt drains to zero. The attacker's own campaign inputs are excluded: the helper's 6,492,300.768118 USDC deposit and the attacker's 430,623.991193131340 LP deposit, both recovered within the receipt. Their abandoned cross-positions (helper: USDC collateral against LP debt; attacker: aLP collateral against the reserve borrows) are not counted as consideration. The LP component is other suppliers' LP withdrawn and redeemed by the attacker. It is valued at the pre-exploit WrapperOracle price (Chainlink-derived fair reserves, block 259645907), not at the manipulated price. Attacker proceeds of about 125,795.6 USDC, 1 USDC.e, 0.00679208 WBTC and 2.25 WETH (the PoC's ~$130k) are not substituted for victim depletion.

incidents.name: Pro Token unrestricted executor campaign
incidents.summary: The Pro executor implementation exposed exec() without the caller allowlist added by the post-incident replacement and without a cadence or batch limit, allowing an untrusted caller to force repeated Pro sales under attacker-controlled pool conditions and extract USDT.

loss.notes: Across the 11 successful transactions from the first defect execution through 0xaaea183b...84d0, receipt-level Transfer logs show 57,969.169891681606435859 USDT paid directly by the Pro/USDT pair to attacker EOA 0x427671b2c8e91034a91fe698f9b7259b2345f45d. USDT is valued at stablecoin par. The executor also supplied 167,500 Pro to the forced swaps, while 7,404,304.727660184073717188 USDT went to its three preconfigured receivers; GoPlus identifies those receivers as protocol-designated rather than attacker addresses, so their balances and the exchanged Pro are not counted again. SlowMist's approximately $52,000 figure reflects reported attacker profit rather than this exact gross stablecoin receipt. The later 0x4baf136b...49a50 transaction came from a different EOA and helper and is outside this campaign.

incidents.name: Allbridge Core pool withdraw removes equal token and vUsd amounts and resets the pool price
incidents.summary: Allbridge Core's Pool holds a real tokenBalance and a virtual vUsdBalance on a stableswap curve of amplification a = 20, and swapToVUsd/swapFromVUsd price a trade by solving getY on those two balances. Pool.withdraw(amountLp) computes the withdrawer's payout from their pro-rata share of both balances, but then applies it with the source's own comment 'Always equal amounts removed from actual and virtual tokens': tokenBalance -= amountSP and vUsdBalance -= amountSP. Subtracting the same absolute amount from both legs preserves the pool's price only when the two legs are equal; on an imbalanced pool it drives the ratio away from parity without limit, and neither deposit nor withdraw charges any fee for doing so. A correct proportional withdrawal removes tokenBalance*share and vUsdBalance*share and leaves the price unchanged. In the anchor the attacker flash-borrows 7,500,000 BUSD, becomes the dominant LP of the BUSD pool 0x179aad597399b9ae078acfe2b746c09117799ca0 with a 5,000,000 BUSD deposit, bridges 492,669.980 vUsd into it so it pays out 491,586.447 BUSD and its state becomes tokenBalance 4,831,042,798 / vUsdBalance 5,799,131,313 in system precision, a ratio of only 1.2004, and then withdraws 4,830,262,616 LP. That single withdrawal removes 4,830,999,074 from each leg and leaves tokenBalance 43,724 against vUsdBalance 968,132,239, a ratio of 22,142. Swapping 40,000 BUSD into that state then mints 789,378,078 vUsd, which swapFromVUsd on the USDT pool 0xb19cd6ab3890f18b662904fd7a40c003703d2554 settles for 789,632.117482500000000000 real USDT. The violated invariant is that a proportional liquidity withdrawal must not move the pool's exchange rate. No parameter value restores it: the equal-amount reduction is unconditional, deposit and withdraw take no fee, and every amplification a leaves the same defect, so the 15 bp swap fee the attacker paid is two orders of magnitude below the extraction.

loss.notes: Both figures are the net change in the two Allbridge pools' own token balances across the single exploit transaction, computed from its ERC-20 Transfer logs, so the attacker's 5,000,000 BUSD and 2,000,000 USDT deposits are already netted against the withdrawals they funded and no flash-loan principal is included. The BUSD pool 0x179aad597399b9ae078acfe2b746c09117799ca0 ends 282,403.115457925324692409 BUSD lighter and the USDT pool 0xb19cd6ab3890f18b662904fd7a40c003703d2554 ends 290,278.553842307020179247 USDT lighter, a total of 572,681.669300232344871656 units of stablecoin taken from the remaining liquidity providers. The books close: attacker EOA 0xc578d755cd56255d3ff6e92e1b6371ba945e3984 finishes 549,874.391584307393758024 BUSD up, the PancakeSwap pair 0x7efaef62fddcca950418312c6c91aef321375a00 keeps 22,500 BUSD of flash-swap fee, and the rest is the Wombat swap spread; under the gross-depletion rule the financing fee is not deducted. Allbridge later recovered most of the funds and compensated affected liquidity providers, which likewise does not reduce this figure. BUSD and Binance-Peg BSC-USD are valued at par.

incidents.name: xWin referral reward paid on subscription notional that is redeemed in the same transaction
incidents.summary: xWinDefi credits XWIN rewards along two paths that disagree. The subscriber's own reward, in _storeRewardQty, is time weighted: it multiplies the accumulated base by the number of blocks the position has been held, so an instantly redeemed subscription earns nothing. The referral and manager rewards, in _updateReferralReward, are a flat fraction of _tradeParams.amount credited at subscription time with no holding period, and Redeem's _updateRewardBal only unwinds the subscriber's accumulators, never the referral's. The only guard against self dealing is require(msg.sender != _tradeParams.referral), an address-equality test that a second attacker-controlled contract defeats. Subscribing 76,000 flash-loaned BNB while naming a second attacker contract as referral, then redeeming in the same call frame, therefore mints 15,200 XWIN to the attacker for a round-trip cost of about 0.03 BNB in fund slippage, and the loop is repeatable until the protocol's rewardRemaining budget runs out.

loss.notes: Realised proceeds, not a spot valuation of the stolen governance token. The two-transaction campaign drained 607,998.621764708 XWIN from xWinDefi's reward pool, whose XWIN balance fell from 60,003,368.098 to 59,699,369.230 in the anchor transaction and to 59,395,369.476 in the follow-up 0xda1016b2...7643 fourteen blocks later. That entire quantity was dumped into the PancakeSwap XWIN pair 0xd4a3dcf47887636b19ed1b54aab722bd620e5fb4 inside the same transactions, which collapsed the price: the first round realised 842.512651433088883142 BNB for 303,998.868 XWIN and the second only 43.590521552845251585 BNB for a near-identical 303,999.754 XWIN, so no part of the quantity could have been sold at the pre-exploit price. The components are the attacker EOA 0xb63f0d8b9aa0c4e68d5630f54bfefc6cf2c2ad19's native balance increase in each transaction with its own gas cost added back, 886.103172985934134727 BNB in total. The 76,000 BNB flash loan is attacker-supplied and is repaid inside the transaction. The xWin fund's own slippage cost of roughly 0.03 BNB per subscribe-redeem round trip is an additional loss to fund investors that is not isolated here, so this figure is a lower bound on total protocol damage.

incidents.name: Payy verifier accepted zero-hash USDC burns
incidents.summary: Payy L2 admitted UTXO burns of USDC with a zero burn hash, which the UTXO circuit binds to the first input-note commitment and permits only for zero-kind padding notes. The registered recursive Honk verifier accepted the aggregated statements, and two settlement batches depleted the bridge through direct payouts and a reimbursed fast withdrawal.

loss.notes: Three zero-commitment burns depleted 1,918,793.198148 USDC, including the 1-USDC substitutor reimbursement. Subtract 5 USDC of outstanding attacker-supplied deposits. The earlier 5-USDC deposit/withdrawal cancels. No financing costs or subsequent recoveries are deducted.

incidents.name: TempleDAO StaxLPStaking unrestricted migrateStake
incidents.summary: StaxLPStaking.migrateStake(address oldStaking, uint256 amount) took the migration source as a caller-supplied address and called oldStaking.migrateWithdraw() without checking that the caller was an authorised migrator or that the source was a known staking contract. The attacker passed a contract of their own, was credited a stake equal to the whole StaxLP balance held by the staking contract, and withdrew it.

loss.notes: The exploit transaction moves the staking contract’s entire StaxLP balance, 321154.865567124596801893 xFraxTempleLP, to the attacker. Within 41 blocks the attacker unwound that position through three further transactions and ended holding 1830.122796124022576955 WETH and nothing else, so the realised proceeds are used as the unit valuation, priced at the DefiLlama ETH observation nearest the incident timestamp. That is a realisation value including the attacker’s own market impact, not a mark-to-model LP value. Nothing was recovered.

incidents.name: SNK retroactive referral reward accounting
incidents.summary: SNKMiner.dynamicEarned() multiplied a parent's accumulated reward-per-token delta by its children's current staked balance. A newly bound child could therefore stake after the delta accrued and retroactively increase the parent's reward; repeating that sequence produced excess SNK that the attacker sold into the SNK/USDT pool.

loss.notes: The exploit receipt contains one USDT transfer involving the SNK/USDT pair: exactly 197,725.727895542134092738 USDT leaves the pair for attacker beneficiary 0x7738b2f18d994c7c8fa10e1fe456069624740f3e. The attacker financed and repaid the separate SNK leg; there is no attacker-supplied USDT pair inflow to subtract. USDT is valued at par.

incidents.name: Uniswap V1 ERC-777 sender-hook reserve reentrancy
incidents.summary: Uniswap V1 tokenToEthInput pays ETH before collecting tokens and has no reentrancy lock. An ERC-777 tokensToSend callback can sell again before the first transfer updates the token reserve, overpaying ETH against a stale reserve.

loss.notes: The components are ETH reserve depletion in the imBTC exchange (519 transactions) and eINV exchange (six transactions). For each campaign transaction, sum ETH calls out of its exchange minus ETH calls into it; this excludes recycled attacker inputs and flash-loan principal without subtracting gas or later recoveries. The eINV total exceeds the attacker payout column in the Horus table by 2,193 wei retained in the helper. Both components use the same incident-time ETH price. Unvalued residual token depletion is 0.00000245 imBTC and 0.000000000000000003 eINV.

incidents.name: Likwid MarginPosition leverage-0 borrow reuses an unbooked AMM quote
incidents.summary: LikwidMarginPosition.addMargin with leverage 0 routes to _executeAddCollateralAndBorrow. That function caps the borrow at SwapMath.getAmountOut(pairReserves, marginAmount), the proceeds of selling the collateral into the pool, divided by minBorrowLevel 1.4 and limited to 20% of real reserves. It never books that sale: unlike _executeAddLeverage it sets no pairDelta, so pairReserves do not move. Every further position is quoted against the same reserves. Any caller can split collateral across many freshly minted positions in one transaction and borrow far more BNB than the collateral could fetch. Attackers bought pool tokens from the same vault, pledged them across 16 to 40 positions per transaction and left the BNB debt unpaid.

loss.notes: Each component is one exploit cycle's net BNB depletion of LikwidVault 0x065d449ec9d139740343990b7e1cf05fa830e4ba. A cycle is the attacker contract's 8-10 pool buys, its multi-position leverage-0 borrow and any sale of leftover pool tokens back to the vault. The buys are attacker-supplied BNB that bought the collateral from this same vault. Every bought token went back into the vault as collateral or was sold back (net token change 0, within 12 wei), so the buys are subtracted and the net BNB is the only loss. Gross BNB leaving the vault in the eight exploit transactions is 130.870694119056799425 BNB. PoC transaction 0x83cbd07d alone paid 74.310377809898883696 BNB against 55 BNB of prior buys. Cycles in order are A 0x98b9f2df (anchor), B1-B3 0x053d984e, E 0x76ae4040, and G, H (PoC), I 0x90bde1e0. The debt is recorded against attacker positions whose only backing is the pledged tokens, which the attackers abandoned. Excluded because they returned value to the vault: 0x90bde1e0's buy-and-sell round trip without borrowing (122514216-122515310, vault +20.436914341249654115 BNB), and 0x98b9f2df's single-position pump-and-borrow attempts at 121416022 (vault +8.372128916444106395) and 121431431/121432300 (+11.362576729994412261). Later liquidations or recoveries are not netted. BNB is valued at DefiLlama WBNB spot at each exploit transaction's timestamp.

incidents.name: ParticleExchange onERC721Received forged lien
incidents.summary: ParticleExchange trusted caller-supplied ERC721 callback and lien data, letting a malicious collection fabricate NFT ownership and credit an unbacked ETH balance.

loss.notes: The exploit changes the attack contract's ParticleExchange accountBalance from zero to exactly 50.126827091960426151 ETH, equal to the exchange's full ETH balance at that block.

incidents.name: Saddle sUSD metapool stale MetaSwapUtils library
incidents.summary: The sUSDv2 metapool was linked to a stale MetaSwapUtils whose _calculateSwap path omitted baseVirtualPrice scaling when saddleUSD-V2 was the input or output token. Repeated sUSD/saddleUSD-V2 round trips therefore shifted the invariant and price curve in the attacker's favor until both sides of the metapool were drained.

loss.notes: The receipt's transfer deltas show the metapool losing exactly 5,288,082.139740971886935251 sUSD and 5,016,537.096730963109713838 saddleUSD-V2. The latter is burned in the same transaction for 1,810,723.455638732389504479 DAI, 1,691,981.791323 USDC, and 1,530,488.975938 USDT, establishing an exact stablecoin-par value of $5,033,194.222899732389504479 without double counting those redemption assets.

incidents.name: EFLeverVault flash-loan balance inflation
incidents.summary: EFLeverVault authenticated receiveFlashLoan() only by requiring Balancer as caller, so anyone could ask Balancer to invoke its withdrawal branch and release leveraged collateral as ETH. withdraw() then sent the vault's entire ETH balance to one share holder instead of that holder's proportional amount.

loss.notes: The reported incident total is 750 ETH across the two same-block transactions using the same vault defect, valued at $996,846.76 with the incident-time ETH price. The selected front-run transaction independently establishes 480.008083265872754211 ETH of net vault loss onchain.

incidents.name: Sentiment WeightedBalancerLPOracle Balancer vault read-only reentrancy
incidents.summary: WeightedBalancerLPOracle.getPrice(token) values a Balancer weighted-pool BPT as the weighted-geometric invariant of vault.getPoolTokens(poolId) balances divided by IPool(token).totalSupply(). Both reads are unguarded external views on the Balancer Vault and the pool token, and the oracle never probes the vault's reentrancy lock. Inside Vault.exitPool the BPT is burned before the pool's native-ETH payout returns, so total supply is already reduced while the token balances are not yet settled, and the quotient overstates the unit value. The attacker re-entered Sentiment from the exitPool ETH callback and had RiskEngine.isAccountHealthy price 221.214516056534546564 B-33WETH-33WBTC-33USDC at 3.5500730700050576 ETH instead of the 0.2201185612401734 ETH the same function returned outside reentrancy, a 16.1x inflation, which let AccountManager.borrow approve four undercollateralised borrows in the same transaction. The violated invariant is that a collateral price must not be derived from a Balancer pool's balances and supply while that pool is mid-update; the deployed oracle has no state in which it can detect that.

loss.notes: Gross depletion of Sentiment's four LToken lending pools in the anchor transaction, read from the AccountManager Borrow(account,owner,token,amount) events at log indices 37, 40, 43 and 46: 461,000 USDC.e out of LUSDC 0x0ddb1ea478f8ef0e22c7706d2903a41e94b1299b, 361,000 USDT out of LUSDT 0x4c8e1656e042a206eef7e8fcff99bac667e4623e, 81 WETH out of LWETH 0xb190214d5ebac7755899f2d96e519aa7a5776bec and 125,000 FRAX out of LFRAX 0x2e9963ae673a885b6bfeda2f80132ce28b784c40. Each pool also paid a 0.1 percent origination fee out of the same amount to the Sentiment treasury 0x92f473ef0cd07080824f5e6b0859ac49b3aeb215; the fee is included because it left the lending pool. The attacker's realised proceeds, forwarded from the exploit contract to the attacker EOA at log indices 110-113, were 0.51695721 WBTC, 29.973117081932212940 WETH, 538,399.328226 USDC.e and 360,000 USDT, about 968,971 USD at the same prices, the roughly 1M USD figure reported at the time; the gap to gross depletion is Aave flash-loan premiums, Balancer join and exit costs and the balances left behind in the borrowing account. The 50 WETH margin deposited into the Sentiment account before the borrows came from the Aave flash loan and was converted into 221.214516056534546564 BPT that stayed inside the Sentiment account as collateral, so it is not counted as depletion. Sentiment recovered the position on 2023-04-08 in transaction 0x4d9e9ad33412949def1b3246833e46440208142450f9916905a8f9d8e9a64cc9, where liquidator 0xf0885fc34fa3b36910d0f256d0fd862a4be79c16, funded by 0xc478f962e932bd8f4e45f9a66b5cbb972d8ac63e, repaid 464,272.338750 USDC.e, 363,579.746514 USDT, 81.674233642042944923 WETH and 125,901.406716158845171079 FRAX and took the account's collateral; per methodology that later recovery does not reduce gross victim depletion.

incidents.name: Minterest mUSDY flashLoan exchange-rate reentrancy
incidents.summary: The mUSDY market runs the ERC-3156 borrower callback while its own cash balance is still reduced by the flash-loaned amount, and the mToken exchange rate is computed from that cash balance. Supplying USDY back inside the callback therefore minted mUSDY at an inflated rate. The attacker repeated the cycle 24 times to build collateral it had not paid for and borrowed the WETH and mETH markets out against it.

loss.notes: Components are the attacker EOA’s net token gain in the single exploit transaction, which is a contract creation whose constructor runs the whole attack. The four later transactions in that EOA’s history only unwrap and swap the proceeds. The borrows backing the collateral were never repaid. DefiLlama observations are 127 and 103 seconds after the incident timestamp. Nothing was recovered.

incidents.name: Utopia predictable airdrop balance overwrite
incidents.summary: Utopia._airdrop overwrites rather than increments a predictably chosen address balance. A crafted pair skim overwrote the pair’s Utopia balance, allowing sync and tiny subsequent sales to drain WBNB reserves.

loss.notes: WBNB extracted from pair 0xfeef619a56fce9d003e20bf61393d18f62b0b2d5: 492.088605739133158123 in the anchor plus six later payouts totaling 3.657063239971340118, less the attacker’s 0.01 WBNB purchase input. Protocol fee conversions retained as MT for LP rewards are excluded. No separate value is assigned to overwritten or unsold Utopia balances; gas and subsequent transfers do not reduce gross loss. WBNB is valued at the timestamped BNB/USD sample.

incidents.name: Fortress Loans Chain price feed submit() without validator verification
incidents.summary: Chain.submit() accepts a caller-supplied price array with caller-supplied signatures and never rejects signers that hold no validator stake, so any address can set any feed value. In one transaction the attacker executed a queued governance proposal that made fFTS collateral, called submit() to set FTS/USD to 4e34, and borrowed every Fortress market dry against 5,000 fFTS minted from 100 FTS.

loss.notes: Every component is the net token movement of the exploit contract 0xcd337b920678cf35143322ab31ab8977c3463a45 in the single exploit transaction, plus its native BNB balance, which goes from 0 at block 17634662 to 1224.650634144094162737 at block 17634663. Attacker-side inputs are excluded: 100 FTS and 3.02030953619907 MAHA were paid in, and the 5,000 fFTS and 2,000,000,000 ARTH.usd received are protocol receipt tokens with no external market. DefiLlama observations lie within 65 seconds of the incident timestamp; the four stablecoins use par, whose largest deviation from the DefiLlama observation is 0.25 percent. Contemporary reporting put the loss near USD 3 million, which is above this exact onchain sum; the difference is valuation method, not additional transfers.

incidents.name: Hedgey Finance ClaimCampaigns unvalidated locker approval (Ethereum)
incidents.summary: ClaimCampaigns.createLockedCampaign did not validate the claimLockup.tokenLocker address, so a campaign created with an attacker-controlled locker left ClaimCampaigns holding a token allowance to that locker that survived cancelCampaign, letting the attacker spend the protocol's full token balance afterwards.

loss.notes: Loss is the main attacker campaign (0xded2b1a4 driving attack contract 0xc793113f) on Ethereum, measured as exact victim depletion of the ClaimCampaigns contract 0xbc452fdc. USDC: the contract's USDC balance went from 1,303,910.12 (1,303,910,120,000 base units) to 0; the drain transaction 0x2606d459 moved exactly that amount from ClaimCampaigns to the attacker EOA. In the anchor transaction the attacker's own 1,305,000 USDC flash-supplied to fund the campaign flows in and back out (net zero) and is an attacker-supplied input, not victim loss. NOBL (0x88b9f5c6): the attacker received exactly 48,019,408 NOBL from ClaimCampaigns (victim->attacker gross, with 0 NOBL sent back), then dumped it through DEX routers. NOBL is illiquid and was not spot-marked: valuation uses realised proceeds. The attacker's entire Ethereum haul was consolidated into a single 1,987,902.6082287668 DAI transfer to cash-out wallet 0xd84f48b7 in transaction 0x1c2fe7c2 (nonce 103). That net take decomposes as the 1,303,910.12 USDC (valued 1:1) plus 683,992.4882287668 DAI of NOBL sale proceeds (gross DAI received across the campaign was 2,038,902.61, of which ~51,000 DAI was the attacker's own spend acquiring ~684,313 seed NOBL, an excluded attacker input). This ~$1.99M matches Halborn's reported ~$2.1M Ethereum split. The same public vulnerability was independently exploited in separate transactions by other actors (0xf0cad3 drained 120,800 MASA, 0x462412 drained 22,393.28 BLOCK, 0xc0ffeebabe drained 72,688.46 ARC, 0xd1aff3 drained 1,957,142.85773 CO), each after the main campaign; those are distinct campaigns by distinct senders and are not counted here. Later recoveries/returns are not netted.

incidents.name: Internet Token LiquidityUnifier unvalidated V3 pool callback mint
incidents.summary: LiquidityUnifier.swapV3(token, pool) is permissionless and accepts any contract whose token0()/token1() return the reward token and the caller-chosen token; it never checks a Uniswap factory or registry. It stores the caller-supplied pool in currentPoolV3 and calls its swap(), and uniswapV3SwapCallback then mints INT to currentPoolV3 in an amount the caller controls, guarded only by msg.sender == currentPoolV3. The validateSupply modifier is defeated inside the same call by burning the minted INT through the Convertor and re-minting it after swapV3 returns. Any caller can therefore mint unbacked INT through the TOKEN_MINTER role the unifier holds and sell it into protocol-owned liquidity, breaking the invariant that INT is minted only against a genuine pool swap of the configured swapAmount.

loss.notes: Component 1 is the first exercise's depletion of the protocol-owned INT/WETH Uniswap V3 pool 0xdec6eadbd8ed3f655cba4bb4eeff6fb43b16969d. Components 2 and 3 are five later copycat transactions by other actors repeating the same swapV3 fake-pool mint before the TOKEN_MINTER role was revoked; they took WETH from the same pool and USDC from two Uniswap V4 USDC/INT pools. Unbacked INT kept by attackers (764,145,702.183763063166443405 INT by the first attacker, later burned) is dilution, not measured victim depletion. Copycat WETH is valued at the first-exercise quote; all merged transactions fall within 2,744 seconds.

incidents.name: ROE WBTC/USDC LP live-reserve collateral valuation
incidents.summary: ROE's custom WBTC/USDC LP oracle divided the pair's current externally priced reserves by current LP supply. It applied no time, donation or deviation bound, so a same-receipt reserve donation immediately raised every recursively minted roeLP collateral claim before the USDC borrow check. The violated invariant is that collateral value used to authorize borrowing must not be increased atomically by the borrower through a live reserve balance that is amplified across repeated claims on the same underlying inventory.

loss.notes: Immediately before the receipt, the ROE reserve aToken 0x68b26dcf21180d2a8de5a303f8cc5b14c8d99c4c owns exactly 2,953,841,283 raw UNI-V2 WBTC/USDC LP out of 5,771,992,996 supply. The pair reserves are 578,680,045 WBTC satoshis and 100,949,159,688 USDC micro-units. Integer-floor redemption therefore equals floor(2,953,841,283 * 578,680,045 / 5,771,992,996) = 296,141,905 WBTC satoshis and floor(2,953,841,283 * 100,949,159,688 / 5,771,992,996) = 51,661,149,896 USDC micro-units. Receipt logs 600-605 burn exactly that LP and emit exactly those two quantities; the reserve's LP balance becomes zero. The campaign has 50 borrow principals totalling 147,692,064,150 raw LP, 49 redeposits totalling 144,738,222,867 raw LP, and the final 2,953,841,283-raw burn. At receipt end the EOA has 147,692,064,169 raw variable LP debt and a 5,673,090.338021 roeUSDC claim, while the helper has a 144,738,222,868-raw roeLP claim and 5,673,090.338021 USDC debt. Both underlying reserve balances are zero immediately after the receipt and remain zero through block 25,882,427 while all four claim/debt balances only accrue, so the cross-claims are unbacked bad debt, not collectible consideration. The 5,673,090.338021-USDC Balancer funding, deposit, borrow and repayment cancel exactly. After the burn, 26,024.069170 of the just-received USDC is sent back to the pair and sync() is called; it is recycled victim inventory rather than external attacker consideration. A later same-receipt swap returns 0.66679001 WBTC and 14,345.053375 USDC, leaving the helper with 2.29462904 WBTC and 39,982.134101 USDC proceeds. Those proceeds are not substituted for gross victim depletion. Canonical WBTC reports 8 decimals and Circle USDC reports 6 decimals; DefiLlama's independently preceding observations value them at 17,417.95 USD and par, giving exact products 51,581.8489419475 USD and 51,661.149896 USD.

incidents.name: yETH weighted-stableswap solver invariant collapse
incidents.summary: Extreme imbalanced deposits drove the weighted-stableswap supply solver outside its valid domain until its product term collapsed to zero, yet the pool accepted the divergent result and over-minted yETH LP. The attacker repaired only the product through zero-value removal, used permissionless rate reconciliation to burn protocol-owned LP rather than their own, drained the LST pool, then re-entered the zero-supply bootstrap path and triggered an unchecked underflow to mint enough yETH to drain the yETH/WETH Curve pool.

loss.notes: Yearn's disclosure lists the eight pre-exploit LST balances in the yETH pool and 298.35 WETH in the downstream Curve pool; live balance checks show each LST balance reduced below 0.000000000000001 token units and the Curve pool reduced to 0.221058531986020280 WETH in the exploit block. Reputable reporting values the gross extraction at approximately $9 million. The later coordinated recovery of 857.49 pxETH is not subtracted from gross loss.

incidents.name: GatewayEVM arbitrary-call USDC allowance drain (Base leg)
incidents.summary: The attacker set IsArbitraryCall on GatewayZEVM.call, so ZetaClient zeroed the sender and the TSS signed a destination execute() that routed into _executeArbitraryCall, whose onCall/onRevert-only deny-list let a transferFrom selector through; the Base GatewayEVM proxy then pulled 110,342.28643 USDC from a team wallet's pre-existing gateway allowance to the attacker EOA.

loss.notes: Exact receipt accounting: one USDC Transfer of 110342286430 units from team wallet 0x8f1aa4dc8efdb3faa5060179e90ec3572ff86e38 to attacker EOA 0x00467f5921f1a343b96b9bf71ae7e9054ae72ea4 inside the TSS-signed execute(). This record covers the single largest destination leg only; the wider campaign drained about $333,868 across 9 TSS-signed executes on Ethereum, BSC, Base, and Arbitrum, consolidated to 139.01439 ETH. No attacker-supplied campaign inputs besides gas; victim funds moved via pre-existing ERC20 allowance, not from custody inside the gateway.

incidents.name: ATM expired-reward reserve-removal campaign
incidents.summary: Staking.burnExpiredReward was permissionless and converted any expired USDT-denominated reward into an ATM amount at the current pair reserves. It then called ATMToken.recycle, which transferred ATM directly from the ATM/USDT pair to Staking and synchronized the reduced ATM reserve.
