loss.notes: The lending pool's WHYPE reserve holder aWHYPE 0xcf4642ef89683d0299b59738b1cc3ac0177348ba held 425.521620381705945356 WHYPE before the borrow and 0 after; the attacker's 26.82 WHYPE spent buying the PRFI collateral is its own input and the 100 WHYPE Morpho flash loan is repaid, so gross loss is the reserve drain. Valued at the DefiLlama WHYPE price at the exploit timestamp.

incidents.name: Abracadabra (CauldronV4)
incidents.summary: CauldronV4 (yvcrvSTETH): rounding drift in userBorrowPart accounting exploited to zero out borrow shares.

loss.notes: Approximate gross MIM value reported by Abracadabra.

incidents.name: Asset-harvesting contract 0x19a2 unauthorised payer transferFrom
incidents.summary: The shared asset-harvesting contract 0x19a23ddaa47396335894229e0439d3d187d89ec9, which MEV bots on BSC hold live BUSDT allowances to, exposes two permissionless entry points. Selector 0xac3994ec records an order under a caller-supplied key and debits only msg.sender, so anyone can designate themselves as that order's privileged executor. Selector 0x1270d364 then reads the payer, recipient, token and amount out of calldata and performs token.transferFrom(payer, recipient, amount) after checking only that msg.sender matches the address stored with the order; nothing binds the payer to the order or requires the payer's consent. An attacker contract deployed 63 seconds earlier registered its own order and used it to move the entire BUSDT balance of bot 0x8c2d4ed92badb9b65f278efb8b440f4bc995ffe7, which had an unlimited allowance outstanding.

loss.notes: The component is the single unauthorised transferFrom in the exploit receipt, log index 5: 366,058.040206325661577467 BUSDT moved from bot 0x8c2d4ed92badb9b65f278efb8b440f4bc995ffe7 to attacker contract 0x3918e0d26b41134c006e8d2d7e3206a53b006108, which was the bot's whole BUSDT balance. The equal-sized 366,058.040206325661577467 BUSDT taken from the WBNB/BUSDT pair 0x16b9a82891338f9ba80e2d6970fdda79d1eb0dae in the same transaction was a flash swap and was repaid as 367,159.518762613502083719 BUSDT; that 1,101.478556287840506252 BUSDT financing fee does not reduce gross victim depletion, so the attacker's realised 364,956.561650037821071215 BUSDT is lower than the loss recorded here. No other address was drained in this transaction and the attacker EOA sent no further exploit transactions. BUSDT is valued at par; DefiLlama returns no historical quote for this token at the incident timestamp.

incidents.name: OpBorrowing liquidation clears shared LToken debt
incidents.summary: OPBorrowing and OpenLevV1 shared one LPool debt balance per borrower. During marginTrade(), attacker-controlled 1inch callback data opened a dust-collateral OPBorrowing position under the margin trader's address. OPBorrowing.liquidate() then treated the trader's full margin debt as that position's debt and called repayBorrowEndByOpenLev(), which wrote off the unpaid balance. The attacker closed the now debt-free margin trade in the next transaction.

loss.notes: The LPool's transaction-local Borrow event records 33.127662613057717773 WBNB sent for the margin trade. Its later RepayBorrow event records 0.014812739983287788 WBNB repaid, 33.112849873074429985 WBNB of bad debt, and the borrower's debt reset to zero. The bad-debt value is the exact lender depletion net of the attacker's same-transaction repayment; the inherited $234,000 estimate is unsupported by the onchain amount.

incidents.name: Hyperbridge HandlerV1 MMR verifier accepts out-of-range leaves
incidents.summary: HandlerV1.handlePostRequests copies caller-supplied leaf indices into its inlined MerkleMountainRange verifier, which never rejects leaves outside every peak. A proof with leafCount 1 and a forged leaf at index 1 reconstructs the genuine root from the proof node alone, so the unverified request is dispatched to the host. Forged TokenGateway requests released escrowed WETH, MANTA and CERE and reassigned the bridged-DOT admin, whose unlimited mints were dumped into DOT pools; forged HostManager requests withdrew host fee balances on Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum and BNB Chain.

loss.notes: Floor of exactly measured victim depletion: TokenGateway escrow and host fee balances released by forged requests, plus the counter-assets paid out of pre-existing bridged-DOT pools by swaps before each pool's first liquidity change. Later pool outflows (net 98.05 ETH on Base, 91.12 ETH on Arbitrum over the campaign) mix pre-existing and newly added liquidity and are excluded, as are the dilution of bridged-DOT holders, 14.93 yTRYB, 1527.25 CICADA and 2732.70 faketaxi of unpriced pool outflows, and sub-$20 LINK, VIRTUAL, GMX and EURC outflows. Hyperbridge's revised $2.5m figure includes DOT-denominated losses not measured here. ETH on L2s and native-ETH pools uses the Ethereum WETH price; all prices are taken at the anchor.

incidents.name: Yield Strategy live-balance donation
incidents.summary: Strategy.burn calculated pool-token output from the contract's live pool-token balance instead of its cached accounted balance. Direct donations therefore inflated withdrawals without increasing the attacker's strategy-share basis, allowing repeated mint/burn cycles to capture donated and pre-existing pool tokens.

loss.notes: Measured as exact net assets retained by the attacker contract from zero balances in the focal transaction. The six Yield strategy tokens are valued at their same-block burnDivested redemption: attacker balance multiplied by baseCached and divided by totalSupply, with integer flooring. Their base claims are 94,844.146598 and 32,853.597181 USDC.e; 7.260657701703898767 and 5.839509554563126601 WETH; and 7,530.973994243543558137 and 4,499.358746908109561687 DAI. The contract also retains 15.857377675310499790 DAI and 91.013962 USDC.e. Stablecoins use par and WETH uses the nearest DefiLlama ETH price before the incident.

incidents.name: Compound v2 UNI oracle guard stale-price bad debt
incidents.summary: Compound's immutable UniswapAnchoredView accepted Chainlink UNI updates only while they stayed within 15% of a 30-minute Uniswap v3 TWAP. A genuine rapid UNI rally moved the reporter outside that band, so validate() emitted PriceGuarded and retained the stale $8.34 price. The actor supplied stablecoin collateral, borrowed 232,890.987 UNI at that valuation across six transactions, and sold it at the higher market price; liquidations exhausted the collateral and left 28,699.848 UNI of bad debt.

loss.notes: The final liquidation transaction records accountBorrows of exactly 28,699.848014519304045859 UNI after the six campaign borrows and all economically useful collateral seizures. The borrower retains no cUNI and only non-economic cUSDC and cDAI dust. The quantity is valued at the $10.381361 UNI price accepted onchain by UniswapAnchoredView 24 seconds before that liquidation; subsequent interest and unrelated same-window borrower campaigns are excluded.

incidents.name: Taiko SGX attestation accepts DEBUG-mode enclaves
incidents.summary: Taiko's AutomataDcapV3Attestation checked an application enclave quote's MRENCLAVE and MRSIGNER but never its attributes, so a DEBUG-mode enclave passed SgxVerifier.registerInstance. The attacker re-signed the trusted Raiko enclave with the MRSIGNER key that had been committed to the public raiko repository, ran it in DEBUG mode, and registered instances in both the SGX-GETH and SGX-RETH verifiers. The debug-readable instance keys then signed forged proofs, the Inbox saved forged L2 checkpoints, and forged bridge messages drained ETH and ERC-20s from the L1 Bridge and ERC20Vault.

loss.notes: Exact L1 depletion of the Taiko Bridge (native ETH) and ERC20Vault (ERC-20 Transfer logs) caused by forged messages across 36 transactions, including 18 ETH taken as the processing fee by 0xc0ffeebabe while it front-ran the forged message 9000. Each asset is valued at its DefiLlama price nearest its first release. The reported DefiLlama figure is $1.7M (source-12). Recoveries are not deducted.

incidents.name: Messina router hop() recursive VAA re-emission (Opulous OPUL)
incidents.summary: The Messina router on Avalanche, the Wormhole emitter trusted by every destination bridge, re-publishes any verified VAA through hop() without checking its emitter, source/destination network or target chain. Attackers fed the router's own output VAAs back into hop() hundreds of times, turning single deposits into many distinct claimable VAAs that released OPUL and other escrowed tokens on Arbitrum, Ethereum, BSC, Base and Polygon.

loss.notes: Merged campaigns 2026-03-13/14 (Ethereum, BSC, Arbitrum), 03-24/25 (DBD, 0x53b8eba7), 03-30 (BUBBLE, 0x7e358874), 05-07 (Mog/BOBO, 0x6551de33) and 09-22 (BUBBLE/RLB/DEGEN, 0xe33112d9) against the same router implementation. Liquid escrowed assets are measured as escrow releases to the attacker set minus attacker deposits into the same escrow, at incident price. OPUL is an unbacked float on each chain and was dumped with large price impact, so it, BOBO, DBD and the September BUBBLE are valued only by realised DEX proceeds net of attacker purchases; roughly 80M OPUL sent to exchange deposit addresses or left unsold is not valued, so the figure is an onchain lower bound. Treasury fees are excluded and later recoveries are not deducted.

incidents.name: Elephant Status manipulable sweep pricing
incidents.summary: Permissionless sweep() sized and executed a zero-minimum-output Treasury-funded buyback from live PancakeSwap reserves, so the attacker skewed the BUSD/WBNB spot price, triggered the buyback against that price, reversed the trade, and retained the spread.

loss.notes: Net loss is the exact BUSD transfer from the attack helper to the attacker EOA after four flash-loan principals and fees were repaid; both attacker and helper started with zero BUSD and the helper ended with zero. The Treasury lost 193,627.110417113639371428 BUSD to the manipulated buyback, but the transaction also acquired and burned fee-on-transfer ELEPHANT and paid pool fees, so the vulnerability-attributable gross depletion cannot be isolated without a counterfactual price. The conservative onchain net is valued at par.

incidents.name: Router multicall self-target authorization bypass drives Safe modules
incidents.summary: Private DeFi Saver-style Router 0x4f0055926c839d1d960a82cbf84e2ee933958ebc exposes multicall(address,bytes[]) and treats any call whose target is the Router itself as authorized. Wrapping multicall(MODULE, [recipe]) inside multicall(ROUTER, [...]) runs the inner call with the Router as msg.sender. Safe module 0xea18b13d11f705a68f0954f637949e1eaa7ac4ca lists the Router as an executor, so it forwarded an attacker recipe into the victim Safe as a DELEGATECALL to RecipeExecutor. That recipe moved 2,900 aEthrsETH to the Uniswap V4 PoolManager for an MEV frontrunner. Copycats repeated it within 1,443 blocks against this Safe and three other Safes whose modules also trusted the Router, taking aEthrsETH, DUSD, USDC, PAXG and dust.

loss.notes: Gross depletion of the four victim Safes across 31 router-self-call transactions from block 25980525 to 25981968. Safe 0x40e93a52f6af9fcd3b476aedadd7feabd9f7aba8 (module 0xea18b13d) lost 2,965.999999999976730685 aEthrsETH in 17 transactions. Safe 0x6a1fac6b3466e29421f70d6eaa91a0de0f627ea2 (module 0xf73a5695) lost 86,631.946830531868921782 DUSD and 38,248.15816 USDC in one transaction. Safe 0xb8e12daf63314a9baa71b1e39baa4538637bf138 (module 0xd479bcc8) lost crvUSD, ASF, YND, ALCX, CVX and 0.000064083553162801 WETH (not valued) in three transactions. Safe 0xb725533606e9d0b4a07ac2b8bd477353aa8b509b (module 0xb8c74599) lost 0.701391963568975838 PAXG in ten transactions. All went to the Uniswap V4 PoolManager 0x000000000004444c5dc75cb358380d2e3de08a90. aEthrsETH is priced at the DefiLlama aEthrsETH quote. The first frontrunner kept 2,882.367408826118 rsETH and paid 17.632591173879632 rsETH to the builder; later recoveries are not deducted. The PoC reports ~7.8M USD for the first transaction only.

incidents.name: Tornado Cash Governance executes an unpinned proposal target
incidents.summary: Governance.execute(uint256) reads only proposal.target and re-checks Address.isContract(target) before target.delegatecall(executeProposal()). The Proposal struct stores an address and never binds the code that was voted on, so the deployed code cannot tell that the runtime at the approved address changed after the ballot closed. Configuration.sol states the intended invariant in the deployed source itself - VOTING_DELAY is documented as needed 'to prevent reorg attacks that replace the proposal' - but the implemented protection covers only reorgs, not SELFDESTRUCT plus CREATE2 redeployment at the same address. Proposal 20's target 0xc503893b3e3c0c6b909222b45f2a3a259a52752d carried a benign 1513-byte runtime (hash 0xf7caba6622c5dfc3a02619f85f224ed0fff459af31bdeaa586eb04828cd00149) from its creation at block 17249477 through block 17299105, was self-destructed to empty code at block 17299106, and held a different 5079-byte runtime (hash 0x6ae6d1594daf6781285e59fbe5a02e67b868acf133401847ec022a93c2cd3bce) from block 17299107 onwards. Thirty-two blocks later the Governance proxy delegatecalled that substituted runtime, which wrote 100 lockedBalance entries of 10,000e18 and one of 200,000e18 into Governance storage slot 59 - 1,200,000 TORN of voting weight that was never deposited - against roughly 70,000 legitimate votes. The violated invariant is that an executed proposal performs the action token holders approved; the boundary test finds no parameter value that restores it, because EXECUTION_DELAY, VOTING_PERIOD, QUORUM_VOTES and PROPOSAL_THRESHOLD constrain timing and weight, never the identity of the code at the approved address.

loss.notes: The quantity is exact and reconstructed from receipts, not from reporting. Reversing keccak256(abi.encode(address, 59)) over the 102 Governance storage slots written by the anchor transaction identifies 49 of the addresses whose lockedBalance was fabricated; those 49 addresses then withdrew from the TornadoVault 0x2f50508a8a3d323b91336fa3ea6ae50e55f32185 in three transactions (4,000 TORN in 0x65fa5b47, 6,000 TORN in 0xdf9dbfe1 and 473,000 TORN in 0x13e2b735), totalling exactly 483,000.000000000000000000 TORN of other users' locked deposits, all consolidated into 0x092123663804f8801b9b086b03b98d706f77bd59. Marking that quantity at the DefiLlama TORN spot price of USD 6.40 at the anchor timestamp would give USD 3.09 million and is not realisable: 483,000 TORN was roughly a tenth of circulating supply and the attacker's own dumping into thin DEX liquidity realised only 493.24082618920283 ETH (about USD 0.9 million at the ETH price of that day) for roughly 444,727 TORN, leaving 38,302.57 TORN transferred on unsold at block 17329628. The recorded USD figure is therefore the reported one, Halborn's USD 2,173,500 for the 483,000 TORN, which prices the stolen deposits at about USD 4.50, between the attacker's DEX realisation and the pre-incident spot. The 1,646.9 TORN that the anchor transaction moved from the staking contract into Governance is the relayer-penalty action that voters actually approved and is not counted. Nothing was recovered; the attacker later restored governance control but kept the TORN.

incidents.name: Gnosis Pay Zodiac Delay forged ERC-1271 module signature
incidents.summary: Gnosis Pay card Safes are guarded by Zodiac Delay modifiers whose enabled module is the account's owner Safe. The Delay authorises execTransactionFromModule either from an enabled module or from a module signature appended to calldata; for a contract signature (v = 0) Zodiac SignatureChecker._isValidContractSignature staticcalls signer.isValidSignature and compares bytes4(returnData) with 0x1626ba7e without checking the call's success. The owner Safe's ERC-1271 path (CompatibilityFallbackHandler -> checkSignatures) calls a contract owner named in the signature before checking that it is an owner and bubbles its revert data, so an attacker contract that reverts with 0x1626ba7e made any owner Safe appear to sign. The attacker queued transfers of every Safe's balance to itself through each Delay and executed them after the 180-second cooldown.

loss.notes: The canonical figure is the Gnosis Pay post-mortem's per-asset total taken by the attacker(s), USD 1,496,151 (GNO 641,159; EURe 453,175; USDC.e 399,121; SAFE 2,202; WETH 323; xDAI 135; USDC 28; USDT 7), excluding a further ~USD 300k it reports as rendered inaccessible; Gnosis later restored users, which does not reduce gross loss. The components are an exact onchain lower bound for the primary attacker EOA 0x81ba8a2b895d30280bca199c2ff75f3f058d4c6c only: Transfer logs crediting it in the 102 Delay.executeNextTx transactions of source-6 (82 sent by the EOA, 20 by its executor 0xf6a9f265012130d02fda1f39f74e9faf8388d2f6), each debiting a different card Safe behind a clone of Delay 0x4a97e65188a950dd4b0f21f9b5434daee0bbf9f5, total USD 541,172.81. EURe is counted once although the legacy wrapper 0xcb444e90d8198415266c6a2724b7900fb12fc56e mirrors each 0x420ca0f9 Transfer; two LI.FI USDC.e returns to the EOA (0x0f44354b..., 0x06191310...) are excluded. Other addresses that used the same forgery, including rescuers such as Safe 0xbb897a566146fdb959ddde80ce00c50b4f5be03f, are not attributed here.

incidents.name: WOOFi WooPPV2 sPMM self-posted price collapse
incidents.summary: WooPPV2 both quotes swaps and rewrites the oracle price it will quote against next. _calcQuoteAmountSellBase() computes newPrice = (1e18 - 2*coeff*price*baseAmount/priceDec/baseDec) * price / 1e18 and _sellBase() writes it back through Wooracle.postPrice() with no floor, cap or relative-move bound, while the same call's payout coefficient only subtracts coeff*price*baseAmount, i.e. half as much. A single permissionless swap() sized so that 2*coeff*price*baseAmount just under-runs 1e18 therefore still pays out about half of notional and leaves the posted WOO price at 9 (1e-8 USD units) instead of 56,608,180. _calcBaseAmountSellQuote() then divides the next quote amount by that collapsed price with no sanity check and paid 10,232,908.094389174718777777 WOO out of the pool for 0.926342 USDC.e.

loss.notes: The three components are WooPPV2 0xeff23b4be1091b53205e35f3afcd9c7182bf3062's exact net token depletion across the three exploit transactions, summed from their Transfer logs: -1369.87930679761355693 WETH, -4173698.205095947120305521 WOO and -1207805.530262 USDC.e. Attacker-supplied inputs are already netted out inside each transaction: every flash loan (10.5M USDC.e from Uniswap V3 pool 0xc31e54c7a869b9fcbecc14363cf510d1c41fa443, 2.7M WOO from LB pair 0xb87495219c432fc85161e4283dff131692a528bd) and the 5.09M WOO borrowed from Silo 0x5c2b80214c1961db06f69dd4128bcffc6423d44f is repaid in the same transaction, and the WOO the attacker sold into the pool is counted as an inflow. WETH is valued at the DefiLlama ETH price at the anchor timestamp. WOO is valued at realised proceeds rather than spot because the attacker's own selling moved the price: the 4173657.742464672345895972 WOO taken out was fully sold in five Trader Joe LBRouter transactions between 1709653444 and 1709654519 for 542.451683823751274736 ETH, sliding from 0.00013219905 to 0.00011924248 ETH per WOO, which at the same ETH price is 0.4930814467971356 USD per WOO against a DefiLlama spot of 0.565311. Spot-marking the WOO instead would give 8764293 USD, close to WOO Network's reported 8.75M. USDC.e is valued at par. Financing fees and the builder payment are not deducted.

incidents.name: SwapX arbitrary transferFrom on approval holders
incidents.summary: SwapX exposes selector 0x4f1f05bc, which takes the token owner as a caller-supplied argument and runs transferFrom against it into a pair the caller also chooses, with no check that the owner is the caller. Every wallet that had ever approved SwapX could therefore be drained by anyone, and the attacker swept 68 of them in a single transaction and swapped the proceeds to WBNB.

loss.notes: The attacker pulled a long list of approval holders in two transactions and routed each balance straight through a PancakeSwap pair, so the tokens never sat in the attacker’s hands at a markable price. Netting both transactions across the attacker EOA and its exploit contract leaves 739.641476234907877084 WBNB gained and 1,000,000 DND of the attacker’s own token spent, so the realised proceeds are used as the measure rather than a mark on the drained tokens, which were mostly thin BSC assets sold into their own pools. Contemporaneous reporting put the event near USD 1 million on a nominal basis; that figure is not reproducible from the realised flows and is not used. Nothing was recovered.

incidents.name: Gyroscope GYD L1 CCIP escrow arbitrary call on message receipt
incidents.summary: GydL1CCIPEscrow._ccipReceive transfers the bridged amount and then runs recipient.functionCall(data), with recipient and data taken from the L2 bridger's message. The attacker bridged 1 wei GYD from Arbitrum naming the GYD token as recipient and approve(attacker, max) as data. On delivery the escrow approved the attacker, who pulled the escrow's 6.1M GYD. The attacker then sold 0.82M GYD into Balancer pools on Ethereum and, after bridging part of it back out, on five L2s.

loss.notes: The escrow lost 6,099,337.38 GYD. The USD value is the attacker's realised proceeds from 823,930.68 GYD sold on six chains, because GYD lost its market once those sales drained liquidity (DefiLlama 0.9997 before, 0.7447 after). About 5.27M unsold GYD (4.58M still on Ethereum plus unsold L2 mints) is not valued, so this is a lower bound. The 1.19M GYD re-deposited to mint L2 GYD is attacker routing of stolen funds, not a recovery.

incidents.name: PegaBall
incidents.summary: buyGamesFrom self-funds purchases from the proxy balance instead of requiring msg.value, letting a vendor drain vendor/referrer cuts.

loss.notes: The exploit trace records 258 outward ETH transfers from the proxy: 0.290589 ETH to the attacker and 0.290589 ETH to the attack contract. Self-calls and DELEGATECALL frame values are excluded.

incidents.name: Civfund attacker-supplied pool callback
incidents.summary: An unrestricted CivTrade function accepted an attacker contract as a Uniswap V3 pool and temporarily authorized it as the mint-callback sender. The fake pool invoked the callback 31 times, using victims' existing allowances to drain nine assets.

loss.notes: Exact gross debits requested by the vulnerable contract's 31 transferFrom calls and reproduced by summing Transfer events from the 31 victim wallets. This includes the full victim debit for fee-on-transfer 0NE rather than only the amount received by the attacker. USDT and USDC are valued at par; all other assets use DefiLlama observations immediately before the transaction. The onchain result replaces the seed row's rounded $165,000 estimate. Later attacker transfers and swaps dispose of the same assets and are excluded.

incidents.name: Phoenix Finance missing delegateCallSwap authorization
incidents.summary: The main implementation exposed delegateCallSwap(bytes) without authorization and forwarded caller-supplied swap calldata to its configured swap module, so the attacker could route assets borrowed into the Phoenix proxy through an attacker-priced token pair.

loss.notes: Gross loss is the exact 10,258.326219 USDC transfer from the Phoenix money pool to the proxy in the exploit receipt. The attacker separately supplied 8,000 USDC to buyLeverage; after Phoenix's 8 USDC fee, 18,250.326219 USDC entered the attacker-priced pair and 18,142.669795 USDC returned to the attack contract. The attacker contract's transaction-level net was 10,132.669795 USDC after its 7,990 USDC flash-loan receipt and 8,000 USDC repayment. The commonly reported $100,000 figure is not used because it is not present in the selected transaction's onchain flows.

incidents.name: Polygon PoS MRC20 unbacked native issuance
incidents.summary: The genesis MRC20 runtime accepted an invalid zero-address authorization without enforcing the source balance, causing five unbacked native MATIC issuances before the emergency runtime replacement.

loss.notes: Gross loss is the five unbacked native-balance issuances recorded by MRC20 Transfer events from the zero address: 10,000 + 50,000 + 540,000 + 100,300.509906 + 101,301.009906 = 801,601.519812 MATIC. Each amount exactly equals the recipient's archive native-balance increase across its receipt block. These are protocol-created native units, not inventory outflows or later disposal proceeds. Component-specific prices are the closest preceding DefiLlama observations. The separately disclosed 500,000-MATIC Whitehat2 bounty and Polygon's later reimbursement are not part of the blackhat receipt boundary and are not netted.

incidents.name: FloorStaking stake/unstake supply accounting
incidents.summary: FloorStaking transferred a stake into its FLOOR balance before rebase() calculated balance minus circulating supply as distributable profit. An attacker could therefore have borrowed principal counted as reward, mint gFLOOR at the old index, trigger the resulting index increase during unstake(), and redeem at the new index for more FLOOR.

loss.notes: After repaying the FLOOR flash loan and swapping the 14,606.145072279 FLOOR surplus, the exploit receipt records exactly 40.146353823753349478 WETH leaving the DAO-owned FLOOR/WETH pool.

incidents.name: Reddio RedSonic Vault stETH double count via permissionless registerErc20
incidents.summary: The RedSonic Vault diamond prices its ETH share class from provider legs that read the vault's raw stETH balance, and anyone could register stETH as a separate share class whose assets are that same raw balance. The attacker registered stETH, bought nearly all rsvETH with flash-loaned ETH, deposited stETH to inflate rsvETH's backing without minting rsvETH, then redeemed rsvETH at the inflated rate and withdrew its stETH, draining the vault's native ETH.

loss.notes: Exact native-ETH depletion of the diamond in source-1 (balance before minus after). The attacker's deposited ETH and stETH are returned within the transaction and are not victim loss.

incidents.name: Abracadabra CauldronV4 cook() unhandled action clears the solvency check
incidents.summary: CauldronV4's cook() tracks a CookStatus memory struct across the action loop. ACTION_BORROW (5) sets status.needsSolvencyCheck = true, but the trailing else branch for an unrecognised action assigns status = returnStatus from the empty base _additionalCookAction(), overwriting the struct with zeroed defaults. Calling cook([5, 0], ...) therefore borrows MIM and then clears the flag, so the closing require(_isSolvent(msg.sender, exchangeRate)) never executes and the borrow needs no collateral. The attacker drained the free MIM balance of six deprecated cauldron clones sharing two master contracts in a single transaction.

loss.notes: One transaction. Six uncollateralised cook([5, 0]) borrows moved the whole free MIM balance of six cauldron clones out of DegenBox 0xd96f48665a1410c0cd669a88898eca36b9fc2cce to the attack contract as 1,793,755.863303087483120210 shares - 736,232.217688 from 0x46f54d43, 75,477.235212 from 0x289424ad, 612,313.552562 from 0xce450a23, 274,846.689470 from 0x40d95c4b, 85,411.627254 from 0x6bcd99d6 and 9,474.541117 from 0xc6d3b82f - which the contract withdrew as 1,793,766.133547645084844120 MIM. MIM is valued at par; DefiLlama's nearest observation, 85 s after the incident, is USD 1.00056. The attacker sold the MIM through the Curve MIM-3CRV pool and the 3pool into DAI, USDC and USDT and then into 395.059753040555107478 ETH; that realisation is smaller than the MIM taken because of pool slippage and is not the measured loss. The matching liability is bad debt left on the six cauldrons, which cannot be liquidated because it has no collateral. No recovery is netted out: 46 later transactions from the attacker EOA deposit the proceeds into Tornado Cash, and the Abracadabra DAO's subsequent open-market MIM buyback is treasury market support, not a return of the stolen assets.

incidents.name: CIVNFT unvalidated mint callback
incidents.summary: CIVNFT accepted an attacker contract as a purported Uniswap V3 pool, then trusted its mint callback and token-address responses. Nine calls used victims' existing allowances to transfer five assets from their wallets to the fake pool.

loss.notes: Exact gross transfers from nine victim wallets to the attacker helper across the nine defect-executing transactions. USDC is valued at par; the other assets use historical DefiLlama observations before the attacker began disposing of them. The seed row's $180,000 estimate is replaced because it is not reproduced by the onchain asset quantities and contemporaneous prices. Later transfers from the helper to the attacker EOA and swaps are movements or disposal of the same stolen assets and are not counted again.

incidents.name: DungeonSwap swap router pulls approved tokens for any caller-named user
incidents.summary: The unverified DungeonSwap router 0x544fde4e... exposes 0x4f1f05bc, which transferFroms the input token from a caller-supplied user address and swaps it along a caller-supplied path, sending the output to that user, with no check that the caller is the user or an authorised front end. Anyone could therefore spend every allowance granted to the router: attackers forced approved wallets' BUSD, USDT, USDC and other tokens into buys of DND or other tokens they then dumped. The first drain (29 wallets) came at block 26028397 and hundreds of copycat senders continued until October 2025.

loss.notes: Lower bound on victim input across 11,251 unauthorised router calls in 7,308 transactions by 457 senders against 6,474 wallets (blocks 26028397..63995459). Stablecoin legs are counted at par: victim stablecoin inputs, or the stablecoin output of a victim-token first hop. WBNB legs are counted only for the first-day campaign (blocks up to 26040000: 63.467677718180654806 WBNB at the anchor-time quote); 116.66 WBNB of later WBNB legs and 1,776 first hops whose input and output are neither WBNB nor a stablecoin (e.g. CAKE, ETH, zSEED routed directly) are not valued. Victims received the path's output tokens (mostly DND) at manipulated prices; that output is not netted.

incidents.name: TrustedVolumes
incidents.summary: RFQ proxy had permissionless registerAllowedOrderSigner and checked authorization against order.taker (attacker) instead of order.maker, draining the maker's approved balances.

loss.notes: The receipt records the resolver's exact WETH, USDT, WBTC, and USDC outflows. The USDC component is net of four raw USDC units paid back by the attacker-signed orders.

incidents.name: Poolz LockedDeal CreateMassPools integer overflow
incidents.summary: LockedDeal.CreateMassPools(address,uint64[],uint256[],address[]) charges the caller getArraySum(_StartAmount), and getArraySum accumulates the caller-supplied array with an unchecked sum = sum + _array[i] under Solidity 0.6.12. An amount array summing to 1 modulo 2**256 therefore transferred a single token unit in while CreatePool credited the attacker's pools with the full element values, and because the pools' _FinishTime was already past, WithdrawToken immediately paid out the contract's entire balance of each token.

loss.notes: Exact token depletion of LockedDeal 0x8bfaa473a899439d8e07bf86a8c6ce5de42fe54b on BSC, summed from the ERC20 Transfer logs whose sender is the contract across the five exploit transactions between blocks 26475367 and 26475466. Every component is a thin PancakeSwap listing that the attacker's own selling moved, so each is valued at realised proceeds, not spot: the per-token unitPriceUsd is the BNB the attacker EOA actually received when selling that token, at the DefiLlama BNB price of 311.7638042244487 at the anchor timestamp, divided by the quantity taken. Realised proceeds total 1328.5787180093985 BNB. PORTX realises zero because the attacker burned all of it to the zero address at block 26490195 after failing to sell it, and part of the KMON was never sold, so the total is a floor. The Ethereum and Polygon deployments of the same contract were drained in the same hour by the same attacker; those losses belong to their own records and are excluded here, which is why this figure is not PeckShield's ~$390,000 cross-chain estimate.

incidents.name: Curve CRV/ETH Vyper lock reentrancy
incidents.summary: Vyper 0.3.0 allocated the same named nonreentrant lock to different storage slots in different functions. The CRV/ETH pool's native-ETH callback therefore allowed cross-function reentrancy from remove_liquidity() into add_liquidity(), minting an invalid claim on pool reserves.

loss.notes: The two structured components are the attack helper's exact end-of-transaction proceeds after repaying its 10,000 WETH flash loan. The later 2,879.65 ETH whitehat extraction was returned to Curve and is excluded. Other Vyper-affected pools were attacked independently and are not included in this pool-specific loss.

incidents.name: NFT Trader 2022 swap contract counterparty reentrancy
incidents.summary: The 2022 NFT Trader swap contract settles the creator's ERC-721 leg before the counterparty leg and has no reentrancy guard, so the attacker re-entered from onERC721Received to repoint the open swap at an address that still held an approval and had that address's Bored Ape or Mutant Ape pulled on settlement. Same defect shape as the 2021 BatchSwap contract, but distinct deployed code with its own age.

loss.notes: 26 Bored Apes and 9 Mutant Apes, 35 distinct tokens, were pulled from approval-holding victims through this contract between blocks 18798295 and 18798739. Unit values are the median single-item marketplace fill for each collection over blocks 18790000-18804000, taken only from transactions carrying a Seaport OrderFulfilled or Blur execution event and measured as the payment received by the seller, with every campaign address excluded: BAYC 26.300 ETH from 34 sales, MAYC 5.190 ETH from 85 sales. Those medians are converted at the DefiLlama ETH price for the incident timestamp. The 143 tokens taken through the separate 2021 contract 0xc310e760778ecbca4c65b6c559874757a4c4ece0 are recorded under eip155:1:0x431341c6d41301b7db3b719ccaec8081adf71b707069ea27d71dcdd374d8e6fa and are not counted here. Recovery is excluded: Yuga Labs and Boring Security later paid a 120 ETH bounty and the exploiter returned 36 BAYC and 18 MAYC across both contracts.

incidents.name: Balancer boosted linear-pool rounding
incidents.summary: AaveLinearPool rounded a crafted bb-a-USDC-to-USDC swap output to zero while still changing the pool's BPT balance. After the attacker reduced virtual supply close to zero, this accounting change inflated bb-a-USDC's rate; the nested bb-a-USD pool cached that rate and exchanged the overvalued BPT for bb-a-DAI and bb-a-USDT.

loss.notes: BlockSec reports more than $2.12 million stolen across the related boosted-pool attacks on several networks. The structured components reproduce $367,786.81 of proceeds in the Ethereum code-age anchor transaction, including the pre-transaction aUSDC rate, and provide an onchain cross-check for the reported campaign estimate.

incidents.name: Audius Governance proxy re-initialization
incidents.summary: AudiusAdminUpgradeabilityProxy declares `address private proxyAdmin` in ordinary storage slot 0, while the delegated Governance logic inherits OpenZeppelin's Initializable, whose `bool private initialized` and `bool private initializing` are packed into byte 0 and byte 1 of the same slot 0. The Governance proxy's admin is its own address 0x4deca517d6817b6510798b7328f2314d3003abac, so byte 1 reads 0xab and `initializing` is permanently true. The `initializer` modifier's guard `require(initializing || isConstructor() || !initialized)` therefore always passes and, because `isTopLevelCall = !initializing` is false, never re-arms. Governance.initialize(address,uint256,uint256,uint256,uint16,address) stayed callable by anyone for the life of the deployed proxy; the attacker re-ran it to install himself as guardian, then submitted and evaluated his own proposal, which moved the community treasury's AUDIO balance out.

loss.notes: Proposal 85 moved exactly 18564497.819999999999735541 AUDIO from the Governance/community treasury 0x4deca517d6817b6510798b7328f2314d3003abac to the attacker helper in 0x4227bca8ed4b8915c7eec0e14ad3748a88c4371d4176e716e8007249b9980dc9 (log 0x2b). Twenty-seven seconds later the attacker swapped the entire position through the single Uniswap V2 AUDIO/WETH pair 0xc730ef0f4973da9cc0ab8ab291890d3e77f58f79 and received 704.177543861243828018 ETH in 0x82fc23992c7433fffad0e28a1b8d11211dc4377de83e88088d79f24f4a3f28b3. That one swap took AUDIO from a 0.3667 USD spot mark to a realised 0.0588 USD per token, so the realised ETH proceeds are used as the valuation, priced at the DefiLlama ETH observation nearest the sale. Spot-marking the 18.56M AUDIO would imply 6.8M USD, a price at which the quantity could not have been sold. Nothing was recovered. Gas and the attacker's earlier failed proposals do not adjust the depletion.

incidents.name: Equilibria transferable-share reward replay
incidents.summary: VaultEPendle did not update reward debt on share transfers and public getReward(account) let fresh receivers re-claim the same native rewards repeatedly.

loss.notes: Five successful reward-replay transactions plus one funding-only attempt form one episode. CALL-value outflows minus all campaign inflows, including recycled payouts and the standalone 0.664440216358314284 ETH topup, equal 13.599119865909616611 ETH. This matches vault balance depletion from 13.603353927190515249 to 0.004234061280898638 ETH over blocks 23203451–23204165. Net loss is used because pooled attacker inputs cannot be assigned individually to the residual balance. Gas, builder payments and later recoveries are not deductions. All ETH is valued at the first-exploit historical price; the campaign lasts under three hours.

incidents.name: Balance Protocol BTCB spot-poke unbacked mint and withdrawal
incidents.summary: Balance Protocol's permissionless BTCB price path accepted a manipulated price with no validation: the oracle wrapper and Spotter poke calls refreshed the stored price and filed it into Vat, and Vat.frob then authorized unbacked BLC debt minting and BTCB collateral withdrawal against the false spot. GemJoin and BlcJoin exits paid the attacker directly, and PancakeSwap and SmartRouter swaps realized the proceeds in USDT.

loss.notes: Exact pre-recovery victim depletion from pool payout legs in the three same-fault campaign transactions: 52833.890793109591603470 plus 708862.704903208386296283 USDT in the anchor, 14927279434726129096 plus 93633807309981979623697 plus 28496315975075951166290 wei across three pool payouts in the second transaction, and 2123087448775227454826 wei from the PancakeSwap pair in the third. The attacker supplied no campaign inputs besides gas: no BTCB entered GemJoin before the anchor withdrawal, so the full 10.737 BTCB exit is victim collateral. Sub-dollar dust transfers and the actors' later unrelated activity are excluded.

incidents.name: Balancer V2 composable stable pool rounding
incidents.summary: The Stable Pool exact-out path rounded the calculated input amount down instead of up. In low-liquidity, rate-scaled Composable Stable Pools, repeated crafted swaps amplified that error enough to manipulate the invariant, mint underpriced BPT, and extract reserves.

loss.notes: Balancer's official post-mortem reports $121.1 million in gross losses across Balancer-deployed pools on Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base, Optimism, and Polygon. The structured components reproduce $70.654 million removed from the two Ethereum pools used by the code-age anchor and provide an onchain cross-check. Recovery and protected-at-risk funds are tracked separately from gross exploit loss.

incidents.name: Beefy StrategySyrup unsettled-reward share pricing
incidents.summary: StrategySyrup.balanceOf() omitted accrued MasterChef and SmartChef rewards even though deposit() materialized them, while the vault minted shares from that pre-deposit balance before calling deposit(). The attacker could therefore deposit 50,000 CAKE at the stale low share price, trigger settlement of rewards earned by prior depositors, and immediately withdraw a pro-rata share of those rewards.

loss.notes: Gross loss is the exact excess CAKE redeemed from the vault: the helper deposited 50,000 CAKE, withdrew 79,913.717660761050982637 CAKE, and repaid the 50,000 CAKE Venus borrow. It then deposited the 29,913.717660761050982637 CAKE surplus back into the vault for 16,787.443968823239623346 new shares, preserving its claim and the existing holders' dilution rather than recovering their loss. Attacker-supplied BUSD and CTK and financing costs are excluded. CAKE is valued at DefiLlama's nearest price at or before the incident.

incidents.name: Channels Finance cCLP_BTCB_BUSD donated-balance exchange-rate manipulation
incidents.summary: The cCLP_BTCB_BUSD market derives its accounting from the spot underlying balance of the market contract, so an unpermissioned token donation moves its exchange rate. In the anchor transaction the attacker sent 53,410,306,284,612 wei of the PancakeSwap BTCB/BUSD LP token to the market and called the permissionless gulp(), which booked balanceOf(this) minus the MasterChef stake, 26,704,653,141,956 wei, into totalReserves; exchangeRateStored collapsed from 1,019,546,530,792,148,236,798,388 to 38,177,206,864,348,614,462, every cCLP collateral position became liquidatable, and the attacker liquidated the two remaining borrowers, seized all 26,193,658 cCLP and redeemed 26,193,656 of them, leaving totalSupply at 2 wei. In the follow-up transaction the same defect ran the other way: accrueInterest() stakes idle underlying into MasterChef, so a 2,026.818338424751118747 LP donation became market cash and the attacker's 2 wei of cCLP were revalued at 2,026.83 LP of collateral, which he used to borrow the entire cash of seven Channels markets.

loss.notes: Gross depletion is the seven borrow legs of the follow-up transaction 0x93372ce9c86a25f1477b0c3068e745b5b829d5b58025bb1ab234230d3473b776, taken from the Borrow events and the matching underlying Transfer logs out of cWBNB 0x860df3e99f6223d695ab51b2fb9eaa92fa903e8d, cBUSD 0xca797539f004c0f9c206678338f820ac38466d4b, cUSDT 0xba5b37100538cde248aaa4c92fb330fcf91f557c, cUSDC 0x33e68c922d19d74ce845546a5c12a66ea31385c4, cDAI 0x7d247295a6938587c581f5bb8cbd98a72388e530, cETH 0x11797d61fd4bff9728113601782d4444503093d7 and cBTC 0x7140a671da66c0bd411e3fc3b15c51c36dbb5ca3; each borrow drew that market's entire getCash() and none was repaid. Attacker-supplied inputs are excluded: the PancakeSwap V3 flash loans of 11.9 BTCB and 500,000 BUSD, the 2,026.818338424751118747 LP minted from them and donated to the cCLP market and later redeemed back out, the 2 CAKE seeded before the campaign, and the 53,410,306,284,612 wei LP donated in the anchor transaction. The eighth component is the cCLP market's own collateral pool at the moment of the anchor transaction, 26,705,653,142,656 wei of Cake-LP BTCB/BUSD seized from the two remaining borrowers and redeemed; at roughly 490 USD per LP token this is about 0.013 USD, so it is carried at zero rather than given a spurious price, and it does not affect the total. Gas and the PancakeSwap flash-loan fees are not deducted.

incidents.name: Sodium smart-account session-key validation bypass draining Lumi Finance users
incidents.summary: Sodium._validateSignature authorizes the ERC-4337 executeWithSodiumAuthSession path whenever the session-key address read out of the userOp's own callData (bytes 16..36) equals the signer address read out of the userOp's own signature blob, and never checks that address against the wallet's stored session records the way the execute branch does through isSessionOwner. checkValidSodiumSignature type 0x01 takes the signer from the signature itself and resolves it through SignatureChecker, so an attacker-deployed ERC-1271 contract that returns the magic value for any digest makes signer, session key and validation all attacker-controlled. validateUserOp then unconditionally runs _payPrefund, moving the victim wallet's ETH to the EntryPoint where the attacker is the bundler beneficiary, and _approvePaymasterToken, which asks the userOp-supplied paymaster for getTokenAllowanceCast and grants exactly the allowance the attacker's own paymaster requests. The attacker set callGasLimit to 0 so every execution phase reverted out of gas while the validation-phase prefunds and ERC20 approvals persisted, then drained the approved balances with transferFrom.

loss.notes: Quantities are the exact depletion of the victim Sodium smart accounts, reconstructed from every ERC20 Transfer whose sender carries the Sodium proxy runtime and whose recipient is one of the seven attacker addresses (3383 wallets, 5790 transfers, blocks 483390113-483407358) plus the sum of EntryPoint UserOperationEvent actualGasCost across the attacker's 113 defect-executing transactions (5449 wallets, 8657 user operations, 0.152366822290852271 ETH). Inbound WETH and stablecoins from the three Uniswap V3 pools are the attacker's own swap proceeds and are excluded so nothing is double counted. LUAUSD is valued at realised proceeds: the attacker sold the entire stolen 74480.723661281941687839 LUAUSD into Curve in two transactions for 48399.605758 USDT0, an effective 0.6493678878437041 per unit, because his own selling moved LUAUSD from 0.965 to 0.547 within the hour. The stolen 65964.433640948840615208 LUA is left unvalued: DefiLlama returns an unchanged 3.1248490646990934 quote for every timestamp around the incident and no quote at all afterwards, so that figure is a stale mark rather than a price at which this block could have been sold, and the attacker never realised more than 16000 LUA onchain. The recorded USD total is therefore a floor; published reporting of about 264000 USD marks the LUA leg at that stale quote.

incidents.name: FOX Colony EtherRouter meta-transaction resolver takeover
incidents.summary: The FOX Colony EtherRouter exposed executeMetaTransaction, which self-called with address(this).call and therefore passed DSAuth's src == address(this) trust check, so the attacker meta-signed setResolver to point the router at a malicious resolver deployed two blocks earlier, then called drain() through the hijacked resolver to sweep the full USDC balance and the FOX balance, swapping the FOX for WETH in the same transaction.

loss.notes: Exact receipt accounting: one Transfer of 132,704.591501 USDC from the router to the attacker EOA, plus 841086.343608217839604694 FOX (0xf929de51d91c77e42f5090069e0ad7a09e513c73) from the router into the attack contract and on into the pair, swapped in-tx for 1.949506469643782660 WETH paid to the attacker EOA. The WETH leg is priced at the 2026-05-13 CoinGecko daily close. The Blockaid-reported second $50k leg has no identified transaction and is not included. No attacker-supplied campaign inputs besides gas.

incidents.name: SAND Base OFT delegate-confused-deputy bridge drain
incidents.summary: OFTSand exposed an unrestricted approveAndCall callback whose first-argument check did not constrain the callback target, selector, or authority used by the callee. Calling the LayerZero Endpoint through OFTSand therefore made the Endpoint see the OFT itself as msg.sender and let an unprivileged caller replace the OFT's configuration delegate. This is an executed confused-deputy defect in the direct OFTSand runtime, not a compromised credential or an initially unsafe configured parameter.

loss.notes: Exact pre-recovery gross depletion is the sum of 15 SAND Transfer events from Ethereum OFT adapter 0xac531eb26ca1d21b85126de8fb87e80e09002dcf. Each receipt's OFTReceived event identifies LayerZero source EID 30184 (Base); the set starts 150 seconds after the Base takeover and ends at 2026-08-22T01:22:11Z. The exact raw sum is 14753431668978000000000000 wei-SAND. Nominal unbacked Base mint amounts, attacker swaps, and later unrelated withdrawals are excluded. DefiLlama's nearest high-confidence Ethereum SAND observation was $0.04648630455127788 at 2026-08-22T01:20:00Z, 131 seconds before campaign end.

incidents.name: Telcoin CloneableProxy re-initialisation
incidents.summary: Telcoin wallet CloneableProxies were created without their initializer being run, so the OpenZeppelin _initialized flag stayed clear and the master’s initialize(address,bytes) remained callable by anyone. The attacker re-initialised each unused wallet, pointing its beacon slot at a module of their own, and had the wallet delegatecall that module to transfer out its TEL.

loss.notes: The quantities are exact: netting the 22 transactions the attacker sent to its module between blocks 51546496 and 51553000 gives 3470866212.40 TEL and 37.080124317370778845 LINK moving out of Telcoin wallet proxies into attacker control. The USD figure is the reported one because marking that quantity at the pre-incident spot price is not realisable: TEL fell from 0.002358 to 0.0008175 within five minutes of the drain as the attacker sold, and 3.47 billion TEL at the pre-crash price would be about USD 8.2 million against a realised figure that contemporaneous reporting puts at USD 1.2 to 1.25 million. The components therefore carry quantity only and the USD total is the reported realisation. Nothing was recovered.

incidents.name: VerusBridge supplemental-export parser divergence
incidents.summary: VerusProof did not reject a cross-chain-export output carrying the supplemental flag. A crafted output that Verus treated as inactive supplemental data was therefore parsed on Ethereum as an active export whose attacker-chosen transfer hash authorized unbacked ETH, tBTC, and USDC payouts.

loss.notes: The exploit transaction itself transferred exactly 1,625.36688649 native ETH, 103.56766017 tBTC, and 147,658.836798 USDC from the bridge to the attacker-controlled receiver. The USD total values ETH and tBTC at the nearest pre-anchor DefiLlama prices and USDC at par. Subsequent recovery is separate from this exploit-time gross-loss measurement.

incidents.name: SubQuery Settings missing setter authorization
incidents.summary: Settings.setContractAddress() and setBatchAddress() lacked owner checks, so five transactions installed attacker-controlled critical-role addresses and used the resulting StateChannel, staking, rewards, token, and booster authority to drain Treasury funds, pooled stake, deployment boosters, and 272 approved wallets.

loss.notes: Exact stolen SQT is the sum of attacker-controlled recipients' net increases across the five loss receipts: 7,123.035017761666600000; 218,070,478.035174175990999309; 11,819,839.568823074202091517; 22,811,586.289378905375499424; and 129,364,800.151362385762131451 SQT. It excludes 359,614.732487847483438659 SQT of withdrawal fees retained by the protocol Treasury, which explains the difference from SubQuery's rounded 382,433,441 SQT gross-withdrawal figure. The latest CoinGecko observation before the anchor values the stolen amount at $220,502.84.

incidents.name: Fun.xyz retired CheckoutPool unauthenticated bridge()
incidents.summary: Fun.xyz's retired first-generation CheckoutPool at 0x13046f51 exposes bridge(address,BridgeParams) with no caller authorisation - that runtime holds no operator variable at all - so the only remaining constraint on bridgeParams.target and bridgeParams.callData is the bridge-target and chain-id allowlist, and setAllowAll(true) had disabled it. Any address could therefore make the pool perform an arbitrary external call, violating the invariant that only the protocol operator selects the call a CheckoutPool makes on a checkout's behalf. Because the retired pool was still an allowed operator on CheckoutPaymaster, the attacker aimed that call at activateAndCall, which invoked the live CheckoutPool's onlyPaymaster execute() for a checkout the attacker had self-registered through the permissionless deposit() with params.targetAmount 85,730 USDC.e against 1 USDC.e held, and the pool paid the 85,729 USDC.e difference out of _POOL_EXCESS_.

loss.notes: Gross depletion of the live CheckoutPool 0x1929347e, measured from its token balances and net of attacker-supplied deposits. Its USDC.e balance was 85,735.269319 before the campaign's first deposit at block 84290864 and zero after block 84292990; the attackers put 3.000000 USDC.e in through three deposit() calls and took 85,730.000000 out in the anchor transaction plus 8.269319 in the recurrence, so 85,735.269319 USDC.e of pre-campaign holdings were lost. _POOL_EXCESS_[USDC.e] fell 417,094.931356 -> 331,365.931356 across the anchor block, the protocol's own accounting of the 85,729 excess spent there. The recurrence at 84292990 by 0xc513e4f5 through contract 0x972c516a used the same defect and adds 24.490243 native USDC and 9.891240460827629941 WMATIC of net depletion. Stablecoins are valued at par, corroborated by DefiLlama observations of 1.0000018 and 0.9999971; WMATIC uses the DefiLlama mark at the recurrence. The seed inventory's 85,730 was the anchor transaction's gross transfer and did not net the attacker's own deposits or count the recurrence.

incidents.name: Aztec Connect RollupProcessorV3 numRealTxs settlement gap
incidents.summary: Decoder.decodeProof() proves whole 32-tx inner-rollup chunks while processDepositsAndWithdrawals() settles only numRealTxs txs, and numRealTxs sits outside the hashed header, so a deposit in a later slot of the deprecated permissionless RollupProcessorV3 was minted on L2 without its L1 deposit ever being debited.

loss.notes: Aztec's incident report gives the seven exact quantities and a $2.19 million incident-time aggregate. The six ERC-20 transfers reproduce in the exploit receipt; the ETH withdrawal reproduces in the call trace.

incidents.name: 1inch Fusion v1 Settlement calldata corruption (resolver drain)
incidents.summary: Settlement._settleOrder() used attacker-controlled interactionLength in unchecked Yul pointer arithmetic. A wrapped length moved the appended suffix backward in memory, overwrote the authenticated resolver field, and made the deprecated Fusion v1 contract call a third-party resolver against its standing token approvals.

loss.notes: The reported approximately $4.5 million is the gross TrustedVolumes drain. The selected transaction contains two exact 1,000,000 USDC transfers from the resolver, recorded here as a $2 million partial component. Decurity reports that nearly all funds were later returned and the attacker retained a negotiated bounty; recovery is not netted from exploit-time loss.

incidents.name: Univ3CollateralToken
incidents.summary: Univ3CollateralToken stored deposited Uni V3 positions under the vault minter and balanceOf(vault) valued that minter-wide list. One position deposited for vault 40 therefore supplied borrowing power to every vault owned by the same minter.

loss.notes: The receipt records 44,218.394393 USDC and 7,019.930123 USDC.e leaving the USDI reserves for the attack helper. The helper's later swaps and final WETH transfer are proceeds transformations and are excluded from the loss total.

incidents.name: RigoBlock Drago setMultipleAllowances missing owner check
incidents.summary: Drago v2 pools expose setMultipleAllowances(proxy, tokens, amounts) without the onlyOwner and whenApprovedProxy modifiers that guard setAllowance, so anyone can make a pool approve an arbitrary spender for its ERC-20 holdings. The attacker had the Pure Alpha Drago approve its contract for six tokens and then pulled and sold them; a second actor later used the same call on the byte-identical PayRue 1 Drago to take its aDAI.

loss.notes: Exact Drago debits: Pure Alpha 0x682e3e207b18555bc75c072233e7d9fd0c386b9a lost six tokens in source-2 (block 14224068), and PayRue 1 0x98901ce9c337c8663e49a8ba2bc36370990d5e6e lost 78.459636476125759114 aDAI (including interest accrued on transfer) in source-6. Source-2 was sent by generalized front-runner 0x7eb44bf215794d5a44d44b2d8d4a32da2a7a5aea, which replayed the attacker contract's public drain function; the attacker's own copy (0x3ea9d22cda4e34f8fb73b3a79f84be174f2af459d46322e6d5e7903259696bf8) reverted, and the proceeds still went to the attacker contract. Reported whitehat returns and the bounty do not reduce gross loss. Reported totals (SlowMist 160.86 ETH, DefiLlama 464,000 USD) are not reproduced by any Drago debit found; they appear to describe value at risk.

incidents.name: Ambient CrocSwapDex surplus-collateral accounting
incidents.summary: Flash-loaned WETH deposited as CrocSwapDex native surplus collateral, then a tick-by-tick walk of the ETH/USDC curve with a narrow mint-and-harvest let the attacker disburse more surplus than was deposited, exposing a surplus-collateral accounting flaw in the dex.

loss.notes: After the 50 WETH Balancer flash loan was repaid, the receipt records 33.721988711712491517 WETH and 55,913.808223 USDC leaving the attack helper as proceeds. The downstream USDC-to-WETH conversion and builder payments are excluded to avoid double counting.

incidents.name: LootBot xLoot staking redeem pays each duplicated NFT id in the input array
incidents.summary: LootBot Staking.redeem(uint256[] xloots) computes the reward in the view _redeemable by accruing each listed xLoot NFT's ETH per epoch, and only afterwards writes each id's nextRedeem marker. Repeated ids in the array are therefore each paid. The attacker redeemed with a single owned id repeated 10 to 1,984 times in seven direct calls on 2026-04-08. On 2026-04-15 it flash-borrowed 2.1 ETH from Balancer and sent it to the contract to open a new epoch. It then redeemed seven ids repeated about 155 times each, taking 6.21 ETH.

loss.notes: Campaign 1 (2026-04-08, blocks 24835237..24835508, seven direct redeem calls by 0xacdcd2e9): the contract paid 2.625696793184068608 ETH; each call listed one owned id n times, so the payout times (n-1)/n, 2.622144009704757525 ETH, is counted as excess. Campaign 2 (2026-04-15, source-2): contract ETH balance fell by 4.10983297318446132 ETH net of the attacker's own 2.1 ETH epoch deposit; the attack contract's single-copy entitlement for its seven ids, payout/155 = 0.040063438536673944 ETH, is deducted, leaving 4.069769534647787376 ETH. The Balancer flash loan is financing.

incidents.name: Aztec 2.0 escape-hatch verifier soundness failure
incidents.summary: The escape-hatch verifier the deprecated Aztec 2.0 RollupProcessor delegated proof checking to did not bind a note’s output owner to the party entitled to it, so a proof carrying an attacker-chosen outputOwner verified as sound. escapeHatch() forwarded the attacker’s proof, verify() returned true, and the rollup paid the requested withdrawals out of pooled funds without any further ownership check.

loss.notes: Three escape-hatch transactions from the same EOA drained the rollup: the ETH leg in the anchor transaction, then the DAI leg at block 25339169 and the renBTC leg at block 25339172. The rollup balance falls from 1158.759804206229645062 ETH to 0.759804206229645062 ETH, from 150095.695899720407042487 DAI to 95.695899720407042487 DAI, and from 0.46963295 renBTC to 0, and the attacker address holds exactly the difference afterwards. The residue was swept the next morning by a second actor, fresh EOA 0xb6f89d12ff9a9e394f40b701ac46428de0d1bea5, through two processRollup transactions whose proofs the same TurboVerifier and verification key accepted: 0.759804206229645062 ETH at block 25343196 and 95.695899720407042487 DAI at block 25343289, taking both balances to exactly zero. Those two legs are merged here as further components; ETH is valued at the DefiLlama observation 17 seconds after the ETH leg and DAI at par. Nothing was recovered; the contract’s ownership is renounced so it could not be paused.

incidents.name: ERC20TokenBank
incidents.summary: ExchangeBetweenPools.doExchange(uint256) is permissionless and sends the selected ERC20TokenBank balance through Curve with min_dy = 0. The attacker distorted the USDC/USDT yPool, invoked doExchange to force the bank's 119,023.523157 USDC through the manipulated price for 47.391213 USDT, then reversed the distortion and captured the difference.

loss.notes: Gross victim depletion is the exact USDC balance decrease of from_bank 0x9ab872a34139015da07ee905529a8842a6142971, from 119,023.523157 USDC immediately before the transaction to zero afterward. The manipulated exchange returned only 47.391213 USDT to to_bank 0x21a3dbee594a3419d6037d6d8cee0b1e10bf345c. The attacker's exact 111,500.389841 USDC proceeds are smaller because Curve execution and the 120,000 USDC flash-loan fee are attacker costs; they do not reduce gross victim depletion.

incidents.name: INKFinance
incidents.summary: INK payroll claimPayroll scaled the payout to the instantaneous treasury balance, so seeding the treasury with a flashloan before claiming drained excess USDT.

loss.notes: Exact USDT transferred to the attacker after subtracting the repaid flash loan.

incidents.name: ether.fi AtomicQueue unauthenticated solver
incidents.summary: AtomicQueue.solve takes the solver as a caller-supplied argument and pulls the want token from it via transferFrom without requiring solver == msg.sender. The attacker registered its own request with a worthless offer token and an atomicPrice equal to each victim's balance, then named third-party wallets holding standing liquidETH or USDC allowances to the queue as solvers, draining them. Copycats repeated it within two hours against sETHFI, weETHs, eEIGEN, liquidUSD and liquidElixir allowances.

loss.notes: Exact gross depletion of 62 third-party allowance holders across source-1 and eight later copycat transactions (source-7); worthless fake offer tokens credited to victims are not netted. Liquid assets use DefiLlama quotes; liquidElixir (no quote) uses realised proceeds of the last copycat's disposal, so the aggregate method is other. The first attacker's realised 15.4536 ETH from liquidETH does not set the liquidETH valuation.

incidents.name: MEV bot 0x0ad8 unprotected arbitrary call
incidents.summary: The bot exposed a public entry point that executed caller-supplied calldata with no access control, letting the attacker make it pull 91,638 USDC out of a companion contract that had approved it.

loss.notes: The exploit receipt records one USDC transfer of 91,638.112249 from companion contract 0x211b6a1137bf539b2750e02b9e525cf5757a35ae to the attacker.

incidents.name: ZED RUN GaslessReservoirEnabler whitelisted-token module allowance drain
incidents.summary: GaslessReservoirEnabler.erc20WithTransfersAndExecute is callable by anyone and runs module.call(data) for every ExecutionInfo whose module is on moduleWhitelist, with the calldata entirely caller-controlled. The same contract pulls users' ERC-20s with safeTransferFrom(_msgSender(), ...), so users hold standing allowances to it. Once the admin whitelisted the WETH token itself as a module, any caller could make the enabler call WETH.transferFrom(victim, attacker, amount) and spend every user's allowance, breaking the invariant that the enabler moves a user's tokens only on that user's own call or signed meta-transaction.

loss.notes: WETH is the sum of the anchor's 466 transferFrom pulls (8.719916012102510925) and the same attacker's second pass through the same path 21 blocks later (0.130437373635793407). ZED, a second whitelisted token module drained from 165 approvers through the same function, is valued at its realised proceeds: the helper sold it in the same transaction for 0.004146795847693404 WETH. The helper later forwarded exactly the sum of the three legs, 8.854500181585997736 WETH, to the attacker EOA.

incidents.name: Nimiq HTLC handler GSN execute verification bypass
incidents.summary: Nimiq's ERC20PermitHTLCHandler and ERC20MetaHTLCHandler are each their own OpenGSN forwarder, paymaster and recipient. Their forwarder execute() (onlyRelayHub) discards the signature, domain and type hash, skips checkOpen/checkRefund, and opens or closes an HTLC for request.from; signature, nonce and business checks live only in the handler's own preRelayedCall. RelayHub lets a staked relay name any paymaster, so a relay naming its own always-accept paymaster made the handlers pull a liquidity wallet's approved USDC, USDT0 and USDC.e into attacker-recipient HTLCs, and a later actor refunded other users' expired HTLCs to itself.

loss.notes: Campaign 1 (attacker 0x2258491525c21f334c5a2dc22ce55e55023fc45d, source-1): the liquidity wallet 0x24cb173ae221aea93369f34bdcf0ddb35b436773 loses its full balances, 26130.641710 USDC, 24332.489269 USDT0 and 0.661117 USDC.e; source-11 later redeems the three HTLCs to 0x4b0e8b2c38b0044405e24db481d00be7d5419e04 (payout of already-counted assets). Campaign 2 (0xfa20e2bd6cc9c41218d9811ffd984ae333fca618, source-7, about 48 minutes later): two relayed refund() calls through the same execute path send 27.781516 USDT0 and 4.541131 USDC from other users' expired HTLCs to that actor instead of their refund addresses. Component amounts sum both campaigns. realizedAt is the last campaign-2 transaction.

incidents.name: NFT Trader BatchSwap counterparty reentrancy
incidents.summary: BatchSwap.closeSwapIntent() settles the creator's side of a swap with an ERC-721 safeTransferFrom before the counterparty side, and has no reentrancy guard. The attacker re-entered from onERC721Received and called editCounterPart() to point the open swap at any address that still held an ERC-721 approval to the contract, so settlement then pulled that address's token to the attacker.

loss.notes: 143 distinct NFTs were pulled from approval-holding victims through this contract between blocks 18797420 and 18799856. Only the 12 BAYC and 13 MAYC are valued. Unit values are the median single-item marketplace fill for each collection over blocks 18790000-18804000, taken only from transactions carrying a Seaport OrderFulfilled or Blur execution event and measured as the payment received by the seller, with every campaign address excluded: BAYC 26.300 ETH from 34 sales, MAYC 5.190 ETH from 85 sales. Those medians are converted at the DefiLlama ETH price for the incident timestamp. The remaining 118 NFTs across 25 collections (World of Women, Hashmasks, HERO, VeeFriends, 0N1, HAPE, OCMonk, CloneX, PartyBears, Azuki, Doodles and others) are not valued, so the figure is a conservative floor; press coverage of the whole NFT Trader event reports close to USD 3 million across both exploited swap contracts. The 26 BAYC and 9 MAYC taken through the separate contract 0x13d8faf4a690f5ae52e2d2c52938d1167057b9af are recorded under eip155:1:0x906d06acd236c48a8c8708d7dc50d968b8faad7c7c393e7c01549adf4922b180 and are not counted here. Recovery is excluded: Yuga Labs and Boring Security later paid a 120 ETH bounty and the main exploiter returned 36 BAYC and 18 MAYC.

incidents.name: Compounder StrategyDAICurve permissionless deposit manipulation
incidents.summary: StrategyDAICurve exposed a permissionless deposit() that converted its entire loose DAI balance and added the resulting yDAI to Curve with every minimum-output amount set to zero. The attacker imbalanced Curve, routed 40,000 DAI into the strategy through Compounder's share-accounting flow, and forced this unslippaged deposit before reversing the Curve trades for a net DAI profit.

loss.notes: The successful transaction ends with an exact 27,146.693493638241032728 DAI transfer to the attacker EOA. This is the attacker's net revenue from the composed Compounder and Curve sequence, valued at DAI's one-dollar par value.

incidents.name: OMNI404 transfer treats small amounts as ERC-721 ids and pays a full unit per Uniswap V3 exact-output swap
incidents.summary: O404.transfer(to, valueOrId) treats any value up to maxTotalSupplyERC721 (50) as an ERC-721 id and, if the caller owns that id, moves a full 1e18 ERC-20 unit plus the NFT. A Uniswap V3 pool pays swap output with transfer(recipient, amountOut). The attacker flash-borrowed O404 from the O404/WETH pool and repaid it through id transfers, leaving the pool owning ids 1..21. It then swapped exact outputs of id-many wei, receiving 1e18 O404 per id for about 2 wei of WETH, and sold the O404 back for the pool's WETH, repeating across four transactions.

loss.notes: Net WETH depletion of the O404/WETH Uniswap V3 pool 0xb3f613b9bc84ddb29d78fa4685b01d98412bba0b across the attacker's run() (source-1, 2.427003380901677080) and three drain() calls in the same block (source-2..4: 0.368159024646616381, 0.148862125724857290, 0.080539588011933639), net of the attacker's WETH inputs; the Balancer flash loan is financing.

incidents.name: GMX v1 GLP reentrancy short-price manipulation
incidents.summary: PositionManager.executeDecreaseOrder wraps order execution in enableLeverage/disableLeverage and refunds native ETH to the order account, which can be a contract; the refund re-enters mid-flow while leverage is enabled, letting the attacker open Vault shorts that drive shortsTracker.globalShortAveragePrices far below spot. GlpManager.getAum prices GLP from that reentrancy-manipulable global-short average with no manipulation resistance, so GLP minted before and redeemed after the manipulation over-withdraws the Vault's reserves.

loss.notes: The measured loss is the net decrease of the GMX Vault's nine external reserve assets during the drain transaction 0x03182d3f (source-2), 274 seconds after the anchor. Per-asset net = Vault Transfer-out minus Transfer-in in that receipt: USDC out 18,291,966,230,478 minus in 8,538,567,619,570 = 9,753,398,610,908 base units; FRAX out 28,958,626,304,231,692,487,914,531 minus in 18,410,000,000,000,000,000,000,000 = 10,548,626,304,231,692,487,914,531; the other seven assets have no same-transaction Vault inflow. The attacker's own staked GLP token (0x45096e7a, fsGLP) transfers in and out of the Vault in equal amount (67,266,389,486,834,066,844,513,960) and nets to zero, so it is excluded. The earlier anchor rehearsal 0x1f00d added 3,001 USDC to the Vault and withdrew 0.009963368148593124 WETH, a net gain to the Vault, so it contributes no victim loss and is not netted against the drain. Volatile assets (WBTC, WETH, LINK, UNI) use DefiLlama historical prices within ten seconds before the drain; the five stable assets use par. The attacker later returned roughly 40.5M of the proceeds to GMX under a 10% white-hat bounty settlement; per methodology that recovery does not reduce gross victim depletion and is not netted here.

incidents.name: Limit Break Payment Processor V2 forwarded-calldata offset sender spoof
incidents.summary: Payment Processor V2 copies a forwarded call's trade data from the caller-supplied ABI offset but sizes the copy as if the offset were canonical. Sending offset 0 through a permissionless trusted forwarder shifts the copy, drops the forwarder-appended real sender and lets attacker bytes become the ERC-2771 sender, so the attacker could act as any wallet that had approved Payment Processor: accepting its own zero-price offers for victims' NFTs and making victims buy worthless listings with approved WETH and stablecoins.

loss.notes: Exact victim ERC-20 debits from spoofed buy-listing calls on Ethereum, Base, Polygon, Arbitrum (sibling V2 deployments) and ApeChain (PP V3, identical modifier, same actors and forwarder 0xb48d6af77c5e3b99876ea71b38e9c814ba5b1c8e), totalling $1,665,921.59 at DefiLlama prices of each asset's first drain. The stolen NFTs (at least 84612 ERC721 items and 77264 ERC1155 units from 12769 Ethereum wallets, plus the other-chain events counted in source-3) are unvalued, so this amount is a lower bound; SlowMist reports about $2.8M. Scan ends: Ethereum block 26078818, Base 51922870, Polygon 94620091, Arbitrum 509846310, BNB 124606568, OP 157518303, ApeChain 50588304; later drains are not included.

incidents.name: Trusted-forwarder open relay approval drain
incidents.summary: Forwarder 0x26bbc304699d31b5b3accfa83320a1a396da01f9 accepted an arbitrary claimed sender, appended that address to caller-supplied calldata, and called an arbitrary target without authenticating a signature or caller. The attacker claimed to be each approval holder and routed through a receiver that trusted this forwarder, causing its spending helper and the shared AllowanceTarget to transfer approved aUSDT, USDT and stETH balances.

loss.notes: The receipt shows the drain of 85,744.811604 aUSDT, 69,140.278477 USDT and 32.517352764402807668 stETH from seven approval holders. The aUSDT was redeemed and the stETH was liquidated with the rest of the basket; the attack contract then transferred exactly 229,030.971300 USDT to the attacker EOA. This exact realised-proceeds net measurement avoids imposing a spot price on the stETH disposal. Gas is not deducted and no recovery is netted.

incidents.name: DeFi Plaza single-sided removeLiquidity rounds reserve to zero
incidents.summary: DeFiPlaza.removeLiquidity pays X*(1-F) of one token with F=(1-R)^16 computed in truncating 0.64 fixed point and no bound on the burnt LP fraction R. For R above roughly 0.94, F truncates to 0 and the entire reserve is paid out, breaking the product invariant it is meant to preserve; swap() then prices against a zero input reserve and pays the whole output reserve for 1 wei, so a flash-loaned LP majority emptied all 16 reserves.

loss.notes: Exact net depletion of the pool's 16 reserves in the single exploit transaction: every reserve fell from its block-20240538 balance to 1 base unit (USDT to 0). Attacker swap and addMultiple inputs were returned within the same transaction and are netted out, so the components are LP-owned assets only. Valued at the last DefiLlama points before the exploit (source-7, 227-289 s earlier); DFP2 has sparse points, so it uses the pre-exploit quote at 1720180509 (source-9) rather than the 1720185404 point taken after the drain, when DFP2 later fell to 0.006. The profit went to an MEV frontrunner copying the original attacker's pending transaction; later recoveries, if any, are not deducted.

incidents.name: BvaultsStrategy convertDustToEarned unprotected swap
incidents.summary: BvaultsStrategy.convertDustToEarned() is callable by anyone and swaps the strategy’s holdings through PancakeSwap with no minimum-output argument and no slippage bound. The attacker flash-loaned the BUSD/ALPACA pool out of balance, called the function so the strategy sold 768,358.95 BUSD into the skewed pool for 513.35 ALPACA, and took the difference when the pool re-balanced.

loss.notes: The strategy 0x21125d94cfe886e7179c8d2fe8c1ea8d57c73e0e pays out 768358.953227757555088466 BUSD in the single exploit transaction and receives 513.348353791467415682 ALPACA for it, worth USD 97.39 at the DefiLlama ALPACA price for the incident timestamp. The component records the BUSD that left; loss.usd.amount is the net shortfall after crediting that ALPACA, which is why loss.kind is net-loss. The attacker EOA keeps 760889.017097225537647455 BUSD; the difference is the flash-loan fee paid to the pool out of the drained funds. Nothing was recovered.

incidents.name: Planet Finance borrow discount treats freshly borrowed principal as accrued interest
incidents.summary: PlanetDiscountDelegate.changeUserBorrowDiscount treats the growth of a borrower's stored balance since the last snapshot as interest and subtracts a discount share of it from the recorded debt, while GToken.borrowFresh raises the principal without refreshing that snapshot. After staking GAMMA to reach a 5% discount tier and supplying USDT collateral, the attacker alternated gUSDT borrow() with the public updateUserDiscount(). The discount was applied to new principal 76 times, cutting its recorded debt by 10,183.70 USDT before it repaid and redeemed.

loss.notes: Net USDT depletion of the gUSDT market 0x045e2df638ebec29130dd3be61161cba5f00a9c8 in the single exploit transaction, which nets the attacker's own collateral supply and repayment and equals the summed discountGiven of the 76 BorrowDiscountAccrued events to within 1e-12 USDT. The attacker received 10,124.78 USDT; the rest went to swap and flash-loan fees.

incidents.name: Huma credit approval bypass
incidents.summary: Permissionless requestCredit() created unapproved Requested credit lines, then permissionless refreshAccount() promoted them directly to drawable GoodStanding state without Evaluation Agent approval; a later drawdown emptied three pools.

loss.notes: The loss transaction transfers exactly 82,315.571143 native USDC and 19,074.730401 bridged USDC.e from the three pools to the attacker helper, which forwards the same quantities to the attacker EOA. Both assets are valued at par.

incidents.name: Idols NFT self-transfer reward double-credit
incidents.summary: IdolMain._beforeTokenTransfer settles stETH rewards twice for the same holder when the sender and the receiver are the same address. It first calls _claimEthRewards(_from), which pays balanceOf(_from) * (rewardPerGod - claimedSnapshots[_from]) and writes claimedSnapshots[_from] = rewardPerGod, and then, because the sender will hold one fewer token, executes delete claimedSnapshots[_from] whenever balanceOf(_from) == 1. It then evaluates the receiver branch, where balanceOf(_to) > 0 still holds, and calls _claimEthRewards(_to) against a snapshot that has just been zeroed, paying the whole cumulative rewardPerGod again. Calling safeTransferFrom(self, self, tokenId) in a loop therefore mints one full rewardPerGod payout per iteration while the token never leaves the caller. The onlyAllowedContracts(_to) guard, which relies on Address.isContract, does not stop it because the loop runs inside the exploit contract's constructor, when its code size is still zero.

loss.notes: Exact victim depletion: the sum of every stETH Transfer log emitted with IdolMain 0x439cac149b935ae1d726569800972e1669d17094 as sender to an attacker-controlled address between blocks 21624128 and 21626433, 107.685747932188918815 stETH over 51 transactions. A further 0.114227 stETH left IdolMain to four unrelated addresses in the same window and is excluded as ordinary user claims. None of the extracted amount was the attacker's entitlement: each exploit contract received its Idol immediately beforehand, which set claimedSnapshots[contract] = rewardPerGod, so its legitimate pending reward was zero. stETH is deeply liquid and was not sold through a thin market, so it is marked at the DefiLlama stETH price for the campaign-end timestamp rather than at realised proceeds. Gas is not deducted; the attacker kept the Idol NFTs, which are not part of this measurement.

incidents.name: DBXen burnBatch ERC-2771 sender split
incidents.summary: Called through its trusted ERC-2771 forwarder, DBXen.burnBatch credits accCycleBatchesBurned to _msgSender() but burns XEN from msg.sender, so the XEN onTokenBurned callback sets lastActiveCycle for the forwarder instead of the user. The user's burned batches then stay unsettled against a stale cycle, and claimFees pays that user a share of the accrued protocol fees computed from cycle-0 rewards. The attacker drained the fee pool on Ethereum and, 75 minutes later, the BNB Chain deployment.

loss.notes: Native fee-pool payouts minus the protocol fees the exploit transactions paid in. DXN minted to the attackers by claimRewards is supply inflation, not depleted victim assets, and is excluded.
