incidents.name: Ajna ERC20Pool liquidation accounting campaign
incidents.summary: Two Ajna ERC20Pool master lineages permitted a campaign-controlled borrower to compose drawDebt/addQuoteToken/kick with bucketTake/removeCollateral/take/settle/repay so that liquidation accounting released scarce quote assets without matching debt repayment. The violated invariant is that collateral or quote released during an auction must remain covered by repaid debt or equivalent scarce consideration. Eleven immutable pool clones were affected in one coordinated campaign. The legacy and newer masters have different runtimes but implement the same failure; the legacy lineage first reached in the campaign supplies its canonical curve knot while the later newer-lineage recurrence remains reviewed supporting evidence.

loss.notes: The 11 pool components are kept separate so lineage attribution remains machine-readable. Legacy master 0x05bb: cbETH/WETH 48.880994783447236415 WETH, wstETH/WETH 44.618985982526959274 WETH, rETH/WETH 5.151922446056045673 WETH, WETH/USDC 23,059.288839 USDC, sDAI/USDC 11,784.029677 USDC, WBTC/DAI 28,601.317832590344872652 DAI, and rETH/DAI 31,979.823008843540407093 DAI; exact USD subtotal 338,821.76619691822682552330043072. Newer master 0x4b3b: sUSDe/DAI 161,183.378480172531808886 DAI, mwstETH/wstETH 34.841843097892057306 wstETH, syrupUSDC/USDC 114,340.133355 USDC, and sDAI/USDC 14,244.041987 USDC; exact USD subtotal 395,283.24861868069118902436312289563392853470902444. Their exact sum is 734,105.01481559891801454766355361563392853470902444 USD. Archive balances reproduce every component. Campaign-created collateral positions and the small retained cbETH, wstETH, rETH, WBTC, sDAI, sUSDe, mwstETH-share and syrupUSDC quantities are attacker-supplied consideration, not additional victim loss. The cbETH continuation returned 0.026228701460587952 WETH to its pool and removed the remaining 0.000204277342017555 cbETH, so that return is netted from the earlier WETH outflow. The later syrup recurrence deposited 27,661.722202 USDC and withdrew 51,672.758035 USDC for 24,011.035833 USDC additional loss. Two unrelated transactions inside bounded archive windows withdrew 0.510962 USDC from the legacy sDAI pool and 2.478109933470371768 DAI from the WBTC pool; both are source-9 and excluded. No Ajna-pool return appears in the three campaign EOAs' later successful transactions through block 25,875,486. Stablecoins are at par. WETH prices are the closest preceding Chainlink ETH/USD answers for the three legacy WETH components. The new wstETH component uses the preceding 2,436.91552334 USD ETH answer and the pool-prestate wstETH stEthPerToken value 1.242726238226704561, yielding 3,028.41886119657925883287995374 USD per wstETH.

incidents.name: iEarn yUSDT hard-coded iUSDC accounting mismatch
incidents.summary: The immutable yUSDT runtime hard-coded Fulcrum's iUSDC market while treating assetBalanceOf() as USDT in its pool-value calculation. The attacker minted iUSDC to the vault, inflating the USDT-denominated share price, then used deposit and withdraw calls to create unbacked yUSDT and extract assets through the Curve yPool; the next block repeated the same defect against a sibling yUSDT deployment connected to the BUSD pool.

loss.notes: The USD total is the attacker cluster's exact net holdings after both defect executions, settlement and consolidation: six stablecoins valued at par plus 507.550988138411541129 WETH valued at the Chainlink ETH/USD answer of $1,920.14 updated at timestamp 1681365347. It excludes all repaid flash-loan principal. Gross victim depletion is not used because the campaign routes assets through two yUSDT deployments, Curve pools, Aave and an attacker helper, making the independently observable net proceeds the cleaner quantity.

incidents.name: Royal1155LDA amount-blind batch bookkeeping inflating a royalties claim 100x
incidents.summary: Royal1155LDA._beforeTokenTransfer loops over the ERC-1155 ids array and never reads the parallel amounts array, so it credits the recipient's shadow per-tier balance _BALANCES_[tierId][to] with exactly one unit per array entry regardless of how many units the ERC-1155 transfer actually moves. Its sender-side branch is additionally skipped whenever _IS_OWNED_TOKENS_BACKFILL_COMPLETE_ is false and the sender's shadow balance has already reached zero, so the same id can be listed many times without reverting. A safeBatchTransferFrom listing LDA id 42<<128|424242 one hundred times with one hundred zero amounts therefore left tierBalanceOf(42, receiver) at 100 against a tier supply of 1, and Royalties, which pro-rates a tier's deposited USDC by tierBalanceOf, paid a claim 100 times the attacker's own 2638.089539 USDC royalty deposit and emptied the contract.

loss.notes: The Royalties proxy 0xfe16ee78828672e86cf8e42d8a5119ab79877ec7 held 261170.864398 USDC of undistributed royalties at block 89018050 and 0.000037 USDC at block 89018051, so 261170.864361 USDC of other holders' funds left it. The 2638.089539 USDC the attacker deposited into the same tier in the same transaction was flash-borrowed from the QuickSwap USDC/WMATIC pair 0x6e7a5fafcec6bb1e78bae2a1f0b612012bf14827 and is an attacker-supplied input, so it is not counted; the 7.938083 USDC flash-loan fee likewise does not reduce gross depletion. The attacker's own net take was 263808.9539 minus 2646.027622 = 261162.926278 USDC, which is the figure the seed row carried as 261163.

incidents.name: kTAF liquidation seize rounding
incidents.summary: Repeated tiny liquidations rounded the seized kTAF collateral up, allowing more collateral to be redeemed than the DAI repaid was worth.

loss.notes: The exploit receipt records an exact 8,187.514103413431539366 DAI transfer from the attack contract to the attacker after the 4,000 DAI Balancer flash loan was repaid.

incidents.name: StepHeroNFTs referral-claim reentrancy
incidents.summary: claimReferral(address) sent the caller's accrued BNB referral commission before reducing its recorded balance, so the attack contract's receive hook could reenter and claim the same self-referral commission repeatedly.

loss.notes: Gross loss is the exact native BNB balance decrease of the StepHeroNFTs contract in the exploit transaction: it received 1,000 BNB through buyAsset() and paid 1,138 BNB through the reentrant claimReferral() calls. The attack contract retained 137.9 BNB after paying a separate 0.1 BNB Pancake V3 flash-loan fee; financing cost does not reduce victim depletion. BNB is valued at DefiLlama's nearest price at or before the incident.

incidents.name: BankrollNetworkStack self-funded buyFor inflation
incidents.summary: buyFor() accepted the pool itself as the beneficiary. WBNB.transferFrom(pool, pool, amount) was balance-neutral, but purchaseTokens() still minted internal stake and allocated virtual fees. Repeating that self-funded buy inflated dividends owed to the attacker's real stake, which sell() and withdraw() paid from the pool's WBNB reserve.

loss.notes: The exploit receipt records 16,000 WBNB entering BankrollNetworkStack and 16,412.459593848661728154 WBNB leaving it. The exact transaction-local reserve depletion is therefore 412.459593848661728154 WBNB; the attacker's 404.459593848661728154 WBNB receipt is lower because 8 WBNB repaid the flash-loan fee. DefiLlama observed BNB at $580.89 at timestamp 1727023800, 58 seconds before the exploit.

incidents.name: Unidentified proxy 0x6f7a unauthorized balance routing
incidents.summary: Proxy selector 0xbfd479c4 processed arbitrary token amounts with no caller authorization or ownership check, letting anyone route the victim's live balances into a liquidity path.

loss.notes: The exploit receipt records exactly 4,236.940422340651762428 DAI and 2,295.632629412184755149 FEI leaving the victim. Their stablecoin-par sum measures the victim's gross asset loss and excludes the attacker's downstream AMM arbitrage, avoiding double counting.

incidents.name: MainPool public calcStepIncome()
incidents.summary: MainPool.calcStepIncome(id, amount, step) was callable by anyone with arbitrary arguments and credited the caller's withdrawable income directly, so the attacker joined the game and then wrote itself an income entry it withdrew as ETH.

loss.notes: The attack trace shows the helper depositing 15 ETH into MainPool and MainPool paying it 36.0999999999999999 ETH. MainPool's balance therefore fell by exactly 21.0999999999999999 ETH, valued at DefiLlama's pre-incident ETH price of $2,297.41606930621. A separate 3 ETH ticket purchase was attacker input to another contract and is not victim loss.

incidents.name: Ribbon Gamma Oracle unrestricted setAssetPricer
incidents.summary: Oracle.setAssetPricer in Ribbon's Gamma fork is declared external with no owner restriction and only guards the replacement case, so any caller can install an arbitrary pricer contract for an asset that has no pricer yet. The attacker registered pricers he controlled for stETH, AAVE, LINK and PAXG, used the equally unrestricted Whitelist.whitelistCollateral and whitelistProduct to create four oToken series against them, then pushed expiry prices inflated by 1e10 and redeemed a dust position for almost the entire collateral held in the shared MarginPool.

loss.notes: Components are the net token movement of the Gamma MarginPool 0x3c212a044760de5a529b3ba59363ddeccc2210be across the eight campaign transactions in source-5: the pool receives 0.068 WETH, 0.083 wstETH, 100 USDC and 0.0028 WBTC of attacker collateral when the four oToken series are minted in 0x9b686c9d95, and pays out 323.748462037559855726 WETH, 371.753847784297541009 wstETH, 192,612.423528 USDC and 2.75850126 WBTC across the six redeem transactions; the attacker inputs are netted out. The assets left the pool on 2025-12-12, six days after the anchor, which loss.realizedAt records and which the valuation timestamps use; at the anchor timestamp the same quantities would be USD 2,808,028.08. Published figures of USD 2.3-2.7 million are Aevo's vault-level accounting after the announced 19 percent withdrawal haircut and are not netted out here. DefiLlama observations lie within 31 seconds of the valuation timestamp; USDC uses par, 0.03 percent above the DefiLlama observation.

incidents.name: Dolomite legacy exchange callFunction approval drain
incidents.summary: The retired Ethereum Dolomite exchange contract exposes callFunction(), which performs an arbitrary external call on behalf of the contract. Its only protection is a noEntry reentrancy flag that the caller can clear by entering through the unguarded SoloMargin operate path, after which anyone can make the contract call transferFrom on any token. The attacker used it to pull USDC, WETH and DAI out of every wallet that still held a stale approval to the contract.

loss.notes: Eleven transactions from the attacker EOA call the exchange contract between blocks 19477009 and 19477249; netting ERC-20 transfers across all eleven gives exactly these three tokens, with the attacker helper contract 0x0da9fcc650e2109e09344fd571bb78091b781f06 receiving essentially all of it and a few wei reaching 0x02c57952e2e406a9a9af2dff2c280c59df9a8b8b. Losses fall on the individual approval-granting wallets, not on protocol-held funds. Contemporaneous reporting put the loss near USD 1.8 million. Nothing was recovered.

incidents.name: pNetwork Burner convertAndBurn slippage sandwich
incidents.summary: Burner.convertAndBurn() is permissionless and swaps the contract's accumulated USDT/WBTC into PNT through Uniswap V2 with a zero minimum-output, so the whole conversion could be sandwiched by pre-buying and re-selling PNT in the same transaction.

loss.notes: After the 70 WETH Balancer flash loan was repaid, the call trace records the helper unwrapping and transferring exactly 1.726285094628080033 ETH to the attacker EOA. Transaction gas is excluded.

incidents.name: HedgePay staking forceExit pays out the stake without clearing the staked balance
incidents.summary: The HedgePay HPAY staking proxy's implementation lets any staker call forceExit() to receive its full staked balance, but forceExit never decreases that balance or totalSupply, so the same stake can be withdrawn again. On 2025-12-22 a staker account paid out once through forceExit and again through withdraw eight blocks later; on 2026-02-25 an attacker staked 1.17M flash-borrowed HPAY and called forceExit 50 times, draining 57.5M HPAY of other stakers' deposits and selling it for 26.01 BNB.

loss.notes: Gross depletion of the staking proxy's HPAY beyond the exploiting accounts' own stakes. Campaign 1 (2025-12-22, sweeper 0x07eb2a01 operating the EIP-7702-delegated 2022 staker account 0xf2552dd6): forceExit paid 25,475.22865342 HPAY and withdraw then paid 25,475.228653419999999999 HPAY again; only the second payout is counted, valued at the HPAY/BTCB pair spot reserves times the DefiLlama BTCB price (no HPAY feed). Campaign 2 (2026-02-25): proxy HPAY 58,649,389.75968834 -> 1,124,071.708415473546212768, i.e. 50 forceExit payouts of 1,173,986.082679038090893617 minus the attacker's single post-tax stake of the same amount; the attacker sold the proceeds via HPAY/BTCB and BTCB/WBNB for 26.014224201105944931 WBNB, valued at the DefiLlama WBNB price as realised proceeds. HPAY transfer taxes to fee addresses and the flash loan are not netted.

incidents.name: Thetanuts zero-supply residual-asset share pricing
incidents.summary: deposit() used a one-to-one initialization rate whenever totalSupply was zero even though the vault retained WBTC, so the attacker minted all new shares with a two-satoshi seed and a 4.68 WBTC deposit, then redeemed those shares for the deposit plus the unowned residual balance.

loss.notes: Gross loss is the exact pre-existing WBTC captured from the vault. The helper deposited 4.68000002 WBTC, withdrew 4.83177164 WBTC, repaid the separate 10 WBTC flash loan, and transferred the 0.15177162 WBTC difference to the attacker EOA. This transaction-level amount supersedes the larger reported estimates that are not supported by its token flows. WBTC is valued at DefiLlama's nearest price at or before the incident.

incidents.name: Unifi UP reward manager accepts a caller-supplied fake pool for LP reward eligibility and reward math
incidents.summary: The unverified Unifi UP reward manager 0x5d8aa155 treats any contract that calls mintUP(self) as a pool once its token0() returns WBNB, and claimUP(pool, a, b) sizes the payout from balanceOf and totalSupply read from that same address. The attacker's contract, whose runtime differs from every Unifi pool, minted UP with 0.001 flash-borrowed BNB, then claimed the manager's whole 0.559 UP reward reserve by reporting a huge LP balance. It redeemed the UP at the UPRedeemer for 5.86 BNB.

loss.notes: The manager's pre-exploit UP reward reserve, less 1 wei left behind; the 0.000092563800 UP net minted from the attacker's own 0.001 BNB in the same transaction is excluded. Valued at the transaction's own redemption rate, 5.860110743711839863 BNB for 0.559209321435491586 UP (10.479279 BNB per UP), times the DefiLlama WBNB price.

incidents.name: Ocean BPool single-sided join-exit math drain
incidents.summary: Ocean BPool joinswapExternAmountIn prices pool-share minting from a base-token-only deposit while SideStaking mirrors the leg with datatokens and matching shares, and exitswapPoolAmountIn redeems through calcSingleOutGivenPoolIn so the same shares buy back more base token than the join paid for. The attacker flash-swapped mOCEAN and cycled single-sided joins and exits across eight SideStaking-managed clones, extracting a net 127,861.01 mOCEAN after repaying the flash swap.

loss.notes: The mOCEAN quantity is the exact onchain exit to the attacker EOA inside the anchor; the $11.9K figure is the reported contemporaneous-pricing estimate over a memecoin-paired token. Flash-swapped principal was repaid in-transaction and only the net extraction is counted.

incidents.name: Futureswap exchange position asset wraparound
incidents.summary: The exchange implementation's position accounting behind changePosition(int256,int256,int256) fabricated collateral. Two helper accounts first opened longs of 0.1 and 0.324678582642240534 WETH, exactly cancelling the exchange's -0.424678582642240534 WETH net asset, a third added 0.001 WETH and a fourth opened a 68 WETH short. The first helper's stored long then read back as 324,518,553,658,423,603,970,963,131,354,509 asset units, which is 2^108 minus 3.12e18 - the unsigned image of a small negative asset - with the mirror-image negative written onto the exchange's own pool position. A follow-up changePosition whose deltaAsset was zero settled against that fabricated position and paid the exchange's entire 894,992.852305 USDC.e balance to the attacker. No parameter value makes a position balance wrap, so the defect is in the deployed implementation, not in configuration.

loss.notes: Exact gross depletion of the exchange proxy 0xf7ca7384cc6619866749955065f17bedd3ed80bc, taken as its balanceOf deltas across the single exploit block: USDC.e 197,436.748947 to 0 and WETH 99.85267275162134 to 32.278351334263576. Balance deltas already net out the 500,000 USDC.e the attacker deposited through the four position openings, so no attacker-supplied input is counted. The attacker EOA realised 394,742.852305 USDC.e, which is this depletion converted through the exchange's own Uniswap V3 hedge less the 250 USDC.e Aave flash-loan premium; the depletion figure is the victim-side measurement and is used here. Both assets are deeply liquid on Arbitrum and were not moved by the attacker's own selling, so a timestamped price is appropriate; the WETH unit price is DefiLlama's observation nearest the anchor, returned with its own sample timestamp 1768033862, and is recorded here at the anchor timestamp; DefiLlama records $395,000 for this incident, which is the attacker's realised USDC leg alone.

incidents.name: SWAPP Staking unchecked cToken transferFrom deposit credit
incidents.summary: SWAPP's Staking.deposit calls transferFrom on the deposited token without checking its boolean result and credits the caller's staking balance regardless, while emergencyWithdraw pays that balance out for any non-stablecoin token. Compound cTokens signal a failed transferFrom by returning false instead of reverting, so the attacker deposited the Staking contract's entire cUSDC balance without owning any cUSDC, had it credited, and immediately emergency-withdrew the contract's real cUSDC, which backed users' USDC stablecoin deposits.

loss.notes: Exact gross depletion of the Staking contract's cUSDC in the single anchor transaction: receipt log 0x13c transfers 128657759164064 base units (1286577.59164064 cUSDC) from Staking to the attack contract, taking Staking's cUSDC balance from exactly that amount at block 22957532 to zero; no attacker input is involved because the matching deposit transferred nothing. The unit price is cUSDC.exchangeRateStored() at block 22957532 (250283795288235, i.e. 0.0250283795288235 USDC per cUSDC) with USDC at par; the stored rate omits 333 blocks of unaccrued interest, so the value is a marginal floor. A later deposit on 2025-12-22 credited another 57250164371717 cUSDC without a transfer but found no cUSDC left to withdraw, so it adds no loss.

incidents.name: Thetanuts
incidents.summary: Thetanuts IndexVault.mint() computes each required component-vault transfer with truncating integer division and accepts zero amounts. After claiming flash-borrowed index shares reduced totalSupply to three, the attacker made 37 sub-supply mints whose component transfers all rounded to zero, reminted the shares needed to repay Aave, and kept the five component-vault balances.

loss.notes: The exploit receipt measures exact net proceeds of 105,471.499078 USDC plus 33,593.775337 residual AVAXUSD, BNBUSD, and MATICUSD component-vault shares. Gross IndexVault depletion was also exact: 49,716.431047 BTCUSD, 23,955.277333 ETHUSD, and those three residual balances. The attacker disposed of the BTCUSD and ETHUSD shares through initWithdraw to obtain the USDC; the USD total uses those realised proceeds and conservatively excludes the unvalued residual shares. The approximately $2.1 million cited for the incident was value at risk, not realised loss, because a whitehat rescued approximately $2 million.

incidents.name: Futureswap governance in-transaction snapshot flash-loan vote
incidents.summary: Futureswap's Ethereum governance implementation takes the FST voting snapshot inside createProposal - it calls FST.snapshot() in the proposer's own transaction - and accepts votes weighted by balanceOfAt(voter, thatSnapshot) in the same transaction. Because ERC20Snapshot records the balance held at snapshot time, FST borrowed through a Uniswap V2 flash swap counted as voting power and was repaid in the same transaction, clearing the ~10%-of-supply pass threshold that the proposer's own 12,166.89 FST could not. The passed proposal made the governance executor grant the attacker wallet access in the Registry, and the attacker drained the Futureswap Wallet's 79.41 WETH and 315,981.63 USDC. A second actor repeated the same flash vote in January 2026 to take ownership of the executor and drained further Futureswap holdings on Ethereum and, through a cross-chain ownership message, on Avalanche.

loss.notes: Gross victim depletion across two merged campaigns of the same flash-vote defect. Campaign 1 (0xcd7c839c..., 2025-12-16, $550,740.77): the Futureswap Wallet 0xd1ed35a3ee043683a1833509de8f2c1a0d8777b7 lost its entire 79.405596790744422188 WETH (unwrapped and forwarded as ETH) and its entire 315,981.629985453558859560 FSDPT, redeemed for 315,981.62972 USDC paid to the attacker. Campaign 2 (0x81801a4e..., 2026-01-10, $52,969.63): Ethereum stETH and WETH from Futureswap holding contracts 0x173181d00c9af20497fe692b7ecbb62aeab801b9 and 0x9fc1c67246f8c047d72760b4d29ef7247026db9a, 0.49991228 ETH from messenger 0xb36ea7b5ec29afc1b05fe22b5420e4faae149caf, 0.524163232103428489 WETH extracted from the FST/WETH Uniswap V2 pair by selling 1e12 FST minted through the captured executor, and Avalanche USDC, WAVAX and JOE from three Futureswap contracts after a cross-chain transferOwnership. Excluded: the 31,826.29 DAI the second attacker received on Ethereum (bridge proceeds of the Avalanche USDC, not additional loss), attacker-paid messaging fees and flash-swap fees, and FST holder dilution. Reports cite about $500k (Verichains, campaign 1) and $830k (Cryptopolitan, basis unstated).

incidents.name: DHC award contract repeatable claim
incidents.summary: The DHC award implementation behind proxy 0xe2a047aadbac51b0116af1ce91ebdae4b4202094 pays a claim (selector 0x43609f36) of a fixed 10% of an award's reward from the shared proxy DHC balance without marking the award as spent. A dust re-participation (selector 0xe3db9b54, amount 2 wei) makes the same claimed award claimable again, so anyone who creates and funds one award can claim it repeatedly. The attacker made 333 claims on five self-created awards (328 of them re-claims) and drained the proxy's pooled DHC.

loss.notes: Quantity is the award proxy's DHC balanceOf drop across block 120055460 (568371.829157042339390458 at block 120055459 to 1.082368461773454472 after transaction index 5). That equals the proxy's 333 outbound DHC transfers (770986.4460311507701734 DHC) minus the attacker's 333 inbound deposits (202615.699242570204261 DHC), within 23586 wei of reflection rounding, so attacker inputs are excluded. The dump moved the thin DHC/USDT price, so the drained DHC is valued at the attacker's realised USDT: gross sales of 32723.708074671970382493 + 48532.096783683429190177 + 576.0010148635625929 USDT from pair 0x4b92a34aa2beec3fcdffeb5251c1654ee004e5f4 and 19.210835043410999985 USDT from 60 DHC routed through WBNB, less the attacker's own 10000 USDT seed purchase of DHC, equal exactly the 71851.016708262373165555 USDT forwarded to the attacker EOA. The 10000 USDT DODO flash loan was repaid in the same transaction. USDT is valued at par. The figure is net of DHC transfer taxes and referral cuts paid out of the drained DHC, so it is conservative. DefiLlama has no DHC price.

incidents.name: Alkemi Earn self-liquidation collateral inflation
incidents.summary: AlkemiEarn.liquidateBorrow() let a borrower liquidate their own position with the borrowed asset also serving as the collateral asset, crediting more supply than the repayment consumed, so a flash-loaned supply/borrow/self-liquidate/withdraw sequence walked out with more ETH than was deposited.

loss.notes: The trace records 89.5395 ETH supplied or repaid to Alkemi and 132.99345 ETH borrowed or withdrawn, for an exact protocol net loss of 43.45395 ETH.

incidents.name: VerifierExit exit-proof verification always returning true
incidents.summary: ZKSwap 1.0's VerifierExit implementation 0xd12f4d8329584f36aed67f807f42d9a02beb9534 accepts every exit proof: each verifyExitProof frame in the campaign - one in the anchor, fifteen in the later batch transaction 0x5488f6bb - returns true after exactly 1,496 gas and makes no elliptic-curve precompile call, so no pairing check is performed on the 708-byte proof argument. Once the rollup was in Exodus Mode the ZKSwap L1 contract 0x8eca806aecc86ce90da803b080ca4e3a9b8097ad therefore credited the attacker's forged exits against the frozen state root and released the bridge's balances on withdrawal. The invariant violated is that an exit may only be credited for a balance actually committed in the frozen rollup state.

loss.notes: Reconstructed from receipts rather than taken from the reported headline. Netting every ERC20 Transfer of the ZKSwap L1 contract 0x8eca806aecc86ce90da803b080ca4e3a9b8097ad between blocks 22882059 and 22885419, plus its single outgoing internal transfer of 362.365589999999975424 ETH in 0x79fbdfad..., gives the 31 components listed. Three fabricated ZKS tokens (0xf0628ce987b7cf5d3687e1a7656fe37b556742de, 0x9017e2c072fea689b0201224f9ec6eccdbf6623b, 0x281e0115d1c613f59f5a90486551d65436e1241d) were deposited into the bridge in the same transactions that drained real assets, 26,000, 16,000 and 100,000,000,000 units respectively; they net exactly to zero and are excluded as attacker-supplied inputs. gZKS and the real ZKS token 0xe4815ae53b124e7263f08dcdbbb757d41ed658c6 are the project's own tokens and have no DefiLlama price series, and the wrapped-QTUM ERC20 has none either; those three carry quantity only, so the USD total is a lower bound on the full depletion. The priced components sum to 4,867,767.04 USD, which corroborates the 5 million USD figure Blockaid reported. Nothing was recovered.

incidents.name: DoinGud marketplace acceptOffer zero-amount replay
incidents.summary: The DoinGud marketplace facet's acceptOffer(offerer, tokenId, price, amount) pays the full offer price out of the diamond's USDC escrow even when amount is 0, transferring no NFT and leaving the offer record in place, and it does not stop the offerer from accepting its own offer. The attacker funded one self-offer with flash-swapped USDC and accepted it twice with amount 0, receiving the price twice and draining other users' escrowed USDC.

loss.notes: Gross depletion of the diamond's pre-existing USDC.e escrow (third-party deposits accumulated from 2021 to 2023): the balance falls from 35486.935717 at block 94170780 to 0 after the exploit. The attacker's own flash-swapped deposit of the same amount (log 3) is returned by the first accept (log 6) and is not loss. The attacker's net 35380.154566 USDC.e is lower by the 106.781151 USDC.e flash-swap fee paid to the pair, which does not reduce victim depletion.

incidents.name: BonfireSwap router transfer() pulls BONFIRE from any approved holder
incidents.summary: BonfireSwap.transfer(to, amountAIn, beneficiary, deadline) and loggedTransfer call BONFIRE.transferFrom(to, pancakePair, amountAIn). There is no check that msg.sender is `to`, so the router spends any holder's standing router allowance for any caller. The function then calls skimPools(beneficiary), which pays the pair's excess BONFIRE to the caller-chosen beneficiary. The attacker named 65 approved holders as `to` and itself as beneficiary. It emptied their BONFIRE balances into the pair, skimmed the tokens back and sold them through the router for 66.08 BNB.

loss.notes: The loss is the 65 victims' whole BONFIRE balances before the exploit, 6022302608127.130500287 BONFIRE (9 decimals). All 65 balances are 0 after source-1. BONFIRE's 10% transfer fee is not deducted: it came out of the victims' balances. The unit value is the attacker's disposal in the same transaction. Two router sell() calls debited 5084276867162.854999227 BONFIRE and returned 66.080052256436953636 WBNB, which the router unwrapped to the attack contract. BNB is valued at DefiLlama WBNB 714.764306662756 USD (source-7), giving 9.28975e-9 USD per BONFIRE. That is below DefiLlama's pre-exploit BONFIRE quote of 9.6255e-9 (source-8), so the dump moved the price. The victims' depletion is worth 78.2715 BNB at that rate; the attacker's realised BNB was 66.08. Later abuses of the same function are de minimis and not added: 0x3ae217b0 pulled 146609.934596658 and 66339.006546790 BONFIRE (logged) from 0x284a931f in 0xf1e58aed... and 0xc0e37d95... (blocks 122183344/122184014), and 0x1fc3f1bd pulled 0.545202767 BONFIRE from 0x9f8f224a in 0xd6d06f57... (block 124310589). Together they are under 0.00001 BNB at the same unit value.

incidents.name: Float Hypervisors mint and redeem shares at the pool's instantaneous tick
incidents.summary: Float Protocol's two Visor-style Hypervisors on the FLOAT/WETH Uniswap V3 pool price deposits and total holdings with the pool's current tick. Their only guard is a DepositProxy ratio check against those same manipulable holdings. Swapping the pool, depositing through the whitelisted DepositProxy, swapping back and withdrawing returns more value than was deposited. 0x492d2552 did this against Hypervisor B on 2026-07-30. 0xaea29218 repeated it against both Hypervisors on 2026-09-01.

loss.notes: Attackers' gross realised extraction, a lower bound on the Hypervisor holders' loss. In source-1, 0x492d2552 received 5.502794615000686908 WETH net (unwrapped to ETH; 5.499404026050304823 ETH then went to builder 0x6c42a0b5, which does not reduce the loss) at ETH 1921.1729153052704. In source-2, 0xaea29218 received 10.706591043820923462 ETH net at ETH 2447.2727076168653. The Hypervisors' measured depletion is larger: source-1 took 7.975817164335609226 WETH from Hypervisor B while leaving 2,568.549500696945334661 more FLOAT, and source-2 took 5,003.835636638384594363 FLOAT and 1.637791718201924993 WETH from Hypervisor A and 37,021.255010587666626779 FLOAT and 1.556302565234474972 WETH from Hypervisor B. At the pre-exploit DefiLlama FLOAT quote (0.4937, then 0.6501) that is about 41.9k USD, but the attackers' disposal moved the FLOAT price, so realised proceeds are used. The PoC reports ~$28K for source-2 only.

incidents.name: Truebit TRU bonding-curve purchase-price overflow
incidents.summary: The pre-0.8 bonding-curve implementation performed an unchecked addition of two large purchase-price numerator terms. A crafted TRU purchase overflowed that sum and rounded the required ETH payment to zero, allowing effectively free minting followed by redemption against the pool's ETH reserve.

loss.notes: CertiK reports approximately $26.6 million from the anchor transaction, whose trace pays 8,535.363576519732789359 ETH to the primary attacker, followed by approximately $224,000 extracted by a second attacker using the same defective purchase path. The rounded $26.8 million campaign total includes both exploiters.

incidents.name: Enjin CryptoItems ERC-1538 registry adapter initialize manager takeover
incidents.summary: The two Enjin ERC-1538 adapter registries route every registered adapter selector through their own fallback, including the adapter template's initialize(uint256). Called directly on a registry, that initializer runs in registry storage, where its once-only guard slot was never set and its owner slot is the registry's pending-manager slot. Any caller could therefore make itself pending manager and accept management. The attacker took over both registries and pointed the item-adapter transfer selectors at its own code. It then pulled ERC-1155 items from holders without approval and melted them, draining 6.58M ENJ of backing from the platform reserve.

loss.notes: Gross reserve depletion across 595 attacker transactions (blocks 25834071-25834993). Stolen items were melted for 6,518,518.5545533333333333 ENJ paid to the attack contract, plus 61,108.67468 ENJ the reserve paid to 22 other recipients inside the same melt calls (not deducted). The anchor transaction alone melted 5,231,353 ENJ to the attacker. Value of stolen items that were not melted is not measured. The attacker's later ENJ swaps do not set the valuation.

incidents.name: USM FUM defund split-invariance
incidents.summary: USM.defund() prices a FUM redemption off the mean of the current and post-redemption sell price and contracts adjShrinkFactor per call, so redeeming one position in 64 slices paid strictly more ETH than one call - a pure rounding/split-invariance flaw with identical oracle reads throughout the trace.

loss.notes: Gross loss is the exact USM balance decrease in the exploit transaction after excluding the flash-loan round trip. The latest CoinGecko ETH observation before the transaction values it at $135,809.90.

incidents.name: TimeBridge cross-contract signature-domain collision
incidents.summary: TimeToken's mint authorization hash omitted the target contract, so validator-approved payloads from the CGU bridge were also valid mint authorizations on the BNB Chain TIME contract.

loss.notes: Gross victim depletion is the TIME/WBNB pair's two receipt-level WBNB outflows: 49.148868512713910253 + 47.055759351281121339 = 96.204627863995031592 WBNB, with no WBNB input to the pair in either selected sale receipt. The corresponding 50,000 and 469,000 TIME pair inputs equal the preceding mints in full. Those tokens were created from the zero address rather than removed from bridge inventory, so the 519,000 TIME inflation is causal evidence but not an additional loss component. Archive balances reconcile after excluding third-party transactions in the same blocks: 59.066548624489445285 + 0.089715987592328670 - 49.148868512713910253 = 10.007396099367863702 WBNB, and 48.324075110012389377 + 0.147530569832458028 - 47.055759351281121339 = 1.415846328563726066 WBNB. The imported approximately $872,000 figure valued the nominal mint before slippage; it is replaced by exact LP depletion using a separate preceding BNB price for each sale. Later recoveries are not netted.

incidents.name: Lixir forged-permit vault drain
incidents.summary: Lixir vault-token permit accepted a dummy signature as long as ecrecover returned any nonzero address, so a forged permit granted allowance to drain every holder's shares.

loss.notes: Gross victim outflows in the exploit trace and final attack-helper transfers. The 2.603255642603989317 ETH total includes the attacker's 2.588255642603989317 ETH receipt and 0.015 ETH builder payment. Stablecoins are valued at par; LIX is valued from the pre-exploit Uniswap V3 LIX/WETH pool state and the nearest pre-exploit ETH/USD observation.

incidents.name: Goose Finance StrategyGooseEgg prices deposits before folding harvested EGG into wantLockedTotal
incidents.summary: StrategyGooseEgg._deposit mints shares as amount * sharesTotal / wantLockedTotal and only then calls _farm(), which adds the strategy's whole idle EGG balance to wantLockedTotal. _withdraw calls MasterChef.withdraw, which harvests pending EGG rewards into the strategy as idle EGG. With flash-swapped EGG, the attacker ran two VaultChef deposit/withdraw rounds: each withdraw harvested rewards, and the next deposit bought shares at the stale denominator before those rewards were counted. It then sold 2.66M extracted EGG for 13.04 WBNB.

loss.notes: EGG extracted from the vault beyond the attacker's deposits, measured as the attacker's net EGG sales into the EGG/BUSD pair 0x19e7cbecdd23a16dfa5573df54d98f7caae03019 (1,327,968.604 EGG) and the EGG/WBNB pair 0xd1b59d11316e87c3a0a069e80f590ba35cd8d8d3 (1,328,058.875 EGG) after the flash swaps were settled. The attacker received 13.042529647721630412 WBNB in total, valued at the DefiLlama WBNB price as realised proceeds.

incidents.name: EtherFreakers capture pays out before settling the target, transfer hook re-dissipates stale energy
incidents.summary: In EtherFreakers.attack(), a successful capture sends the target's full energy to the defender and then transfers the NFT; the ERC-721 _beforeTokenTransfer hook recomputes the target's energy from its not-yet-updated balance and dissipates 0.1% of that already-paid energy into the global freakerIndex. The index therefore grows without ETH backing. Attackers minted fresh Freakers, charged them with flash-loaned ETH, looped captures between their own tokens to inflate the index, and discharged more ETH than they put in, draining the contract's 17.87 ETH over two campaigns.

loss.notes: Net ETH paid out by the EtherFreakers contract across the 23 successful campaign transactions (3 by 0x7ef9ac48, 20 by 0xbe9ef50f), i.e. discharges minus the attackers' own birth and charge payments into the contract. The total equals the contract's balance drop from 17.876119787873554828 ETH (block 24602559) to 0.007904525048744983 ETH (block 24614227). Valued at WETH prices at each campaign's first transaction; flash loans are excluded.

incidents.name: Projekt Reward Vault unbacked purchase-delta allocations
incidents.summary: The reward vault's permissionless trackPurchase(buyer) treated a buyer's token-balance increase as purchase value and credited withdrawable ETH without authenticating ETH spent, a genuine purchase, or unique economic activity. Reversible balance movements could therefore create unbacked allocations that massWithdraw paid from the vault.

loss.notes: The single atomic transaction contains 13 successful native-ETH payments from vault 0x574fc478bc45ce144105fa44d98b4b2e4bd442cb to the attack contract. Their exact trace sum is 301.704684684555317704 ETH, reducing the vault from its transaction pre-state balance of 400.662319764705062341 ETH to 98.957635080149744637 ETH. The attack contract then paid a 1 ETH tip and swept exactly 300.704684684555317704 ETH to the profit wallet. The tip and transaction costs do not reduce gross victim depletion. No second campaign transaction or recovery was identified.

incidents.name: Amnext prize strategy draws winners from a blockhash seed known to the completer
incidents.summary: Amnext's PoolTogether-V3-fork MultipleWinners strategy lets anyone call completeAward(), which takes its seed from RNGBlockhash.randomNumber(); on first read that returns uint256(blockhash(block.number - 1)), a value every sender knows before its transaction executes. After no award had been completed since June 2022, about 436M AMC of staking yield sat in the AMCStakingPrizePool. The attacker deposited 46.06M AMC for 60.2% of tickets and called startAward, then sent completeAward in exactly the block after one of the only 3 of 367 eligible blockhashes that made all 10 draws land on its contract. It received 330.45M AMC of prize tickets, withdrew instantly and sold the AMC for 154.017 WBNB.

loss.notes: Stolen asset: the 10 x 33044833.892968331314898145 AMC of prize tickets awarded to the attacker contract (Awarded events), which it redeemed and sold in the same transaction. The contract withdrew 376508794.385313827402796135 tickets (its 46060455.455630514253814685 deposit plus the prize), paid a 4605160.587738330854694255 AMC exit fee to the pool owner, and sold the remaining 371903633.797575496548101880 AMC into PancakeSwap pair 0x01738bfbb67875417543fad4fe408299d31ea757 for 154.016960821795457015 WBNB. That sale doubled the pair's AMC reserve (463.05M to 834.95M) and cut the realised price to 0.000311 USD against a 0.000562 USD pre-sale spot, so the AMC is valued at the attacker's average realised proceeds: 154.016960821795457015 WBNB x 751.59899299391 USD (DefiLlama, source-7) / 371903633.797575496548101880 AMC, applied pro rata to the prize part. The attacker's own deposit (AMC bought for 31.4 BNB in txs from nonces 0, 1 and 4) and its exit fee are attacker inputs and are excluded. So is the 10% manager fee (36716482.10329814590544238 tickets minted to owner 0xd3ae60193ece30926f3a69351749e04afa3001a2), which the fork's award() takes on every prize. No fair-share offset is applied: the attacker's whole award rested on the draw it chose. A fair draw over the same balances would have given its just-in-time 60.2% ticket share an expected ~61% of the prize, so the predictable seed alone accounts for at least ~39% of this loss. The full sale proceeds of 115758.99 USD, which SlowMist and TenArmor report as about 116.1k USD, include the attacker's returned principal.

incidents.name: Goldfinch legacy Pool unauthenticated collectInterestRepayment
incidents.summary: Pool.collectInterestRepayment(address from, uint amount) is declared `external whenNotPaused` with no caller restriction, so any address can make the deprecated 2020 Goldfinch Pool call USDC.transferFrom(from, pool, amount) against any account that still holds a standing approval to the Pool, and then credit the pulled amount to sharePrice as `sharePrice += amount * mantissa / totalShares`. The Pool held only 28.05 shares, so the attacker deposited 1,000 USDC to own 99.997% of totalShares, pulled the entire 340,567.004224 USDC USDC balance of legacy depositor 0x526c7665c5dd9cd7102c6d42d407a0d9dc1e431d into the Pool through that function, and redeemed the inflated share price with 37 withdraw(uint256) calls capped by the 10,000 USDC transactionLimit.

loss.notes: Exact pre-recovery depletion of the single victim: the ERC-20 Transfer netting of the anchor receipt shows 0x526c7665c5dd9cd7102c6d42d407a0d9dc1e431d at -340,567.004224 USDC, which is the amount argument of the one collectInterestRepayment call. Of that, 330,999.000000 USDC reached the attacker EOA, 9,567.004224 USDC stayed stranded in the deprecated Pool because the attacker's shares ran out, and 1.000000 USDC paid the Uniswap V3 flash fee. The attacker's own 1,000 USDC deposit was flash-borrowed from the USDC/WETH pool 0x88e6a0c2ddd26feeb64f039a2c41296fcb3f5640 and repaid inside the transaction, so it is not victim loss; the flash fee is not netted off gross depletion. Valued at par.

incidents.name: DxSale Legacy Locker repeat-unlock drain
incidents.summary: DxLockLPDep.unlockToken() used an if instead of a maturity requirement and never cleared the recorded amount after transfer. A caller with one valid lock could therefore invoke it before maturity and repeatedly withdraw the same allocation from the contract's shared LP-token balance.

loss.notes: BlockSec reports approximately $7.3 million drained across the multi-transaction campaign and more than 1,400 LP positions. The anchored transaction is one representative 500-call repeat-withdrawal leg.

incidents.name: Flamincome USDT Strategy donatable Convex NAV
incidents.summary: Flamincome's USDT Strategy prices VaultYUSDT shares from balanceOfY(), whose delegatecalled implementation deposited() adds Convex BaseRewardPool.balanceOf(Strategy) times the USDP/3CRV metapool get_virtual_price() to its Aave and idle USDT. Convex stakeFor lets anyone credit that balance, and virtual price values each LP at par although USDP was deeply depegged. The attacker deposited 17.94M flash-loaned USDT into VaultYUSDT, minted cheap USDP/3CRV LP, staked 691,647.8 LP for the Strategy to inflate its NAV, and withdrew all shares for 503,115 USDT more than it deposited, paid from real Aave USDT backing.

loss.notes: Net loss is the attacker's realized USDT extraction, net of every attacker input. The Strategy's real backing (aUSDT + USDT) fell 595,787.542728 USDT across the transaction: it paid 18,439,013.669987 USDT to the exploit contract and 92,658.360150 USDT withdrawal fee to the Flamincome Aragon Agent (governance) and received the attacker's 17,935,898.4858 USDT vault deposit; the remaining 14 USDT was an honest pre-inflation VaultX redemption of market-bought xUSDT. The attacker's excess receipt over its deposit was 503,115.185187 USDT, of which 157,212.5152 USDT was spent acquiring the 691,647.799229 usdp3CRV LP that stakeFor credited to the Strategy. That LP is an attacker-supplied input retained by the victim; the team unwound it within three hours into 721,614.516498 USDP, a token whose onchain prices in and before the exploit ranged from 0.011 3CRV (metapool spot at block 25990442) to about 0.21 USDT (small Uniswap V4 fill), so its USD value cannot be fixed and gross victim depletion cannot be separated from it. The 345,902.669987 USDT attacker profit is therefore reported as net loss; it is a lower bound on depositor loss whenever the retained LP was worth less than 249,870.88 USD (the LP cost plus the fee kept by governance). A later depositor, 0x3d920c35a92f9a224d2918568647c8f9789bee2a, redeemed 1,433,072.621231 USDT at the still-inflated NAV in transaction 0x1533ae36ed8cefcea13dea730a73d2c24f5780d4c719f4714f4c095b75d67383; that redistribution among depositors is not added.

incidents.name: Lien Finance
incidents.summary: BondMakerCollateralizedEth validated only the aggregate number of exception matches when exchanging bond groups, so repeated exception IDs could bypass per-bond multiset integrity and mint unbacked bonds. GeneralizedDotc and DecentralizedOTC then priced permissionlessly registered, attacker-crafted bond structures without validating their backing or economic shape, letting those bonds pull 542,144.628604 USDC from an LP allowance.

loss.notes: Exact pre-recovery victim depletion in the anchor receipt. Three USDC Transfer logs move 532,070.026484, 74.602120, and 10,000 USDC from LP 0xa961684a3a654fb2cca8f8991226c0cefc514d80 to the attack orchestrator, totaling 542,144.628604 USDC; a final transfer sweeps that exact amount to the attacker EOA. Stablecoin-par valuation excludes later recoveries and does not count attacker-supplied inputs.

incidents.name: sMYX dividend token transfer creates unbacked profit-per-share while shrinking recorded supply
incidents.summary: The unverified 2020 sMYX dividend contract 0x40432844506f3a51c266ecabad2beb23cad27f66 raises its profit-per-share accumulator by the transferred amount divided by total supply on every transfer, without any MYX inflow. Because of a reversed subtraction helper it also lowers the recorded supply by the transferred amount, so each transfer mints a larger unbacked dividend. The attacker flash-borrowed 3 WETH, bought MYX, and took a dominant sMYX position split across two contracts. It then alternated transfers between them with withdraw() calls and exited, draining 6.68M MYX of other holders' deposits.

loss.notes: sMYX's net MYX depletion in the exploit transaction, net of the attacker's own buy-in. MYX's transfer tax burned 1,049,377.107 MYX and sent 1,049,377.107 MYX to the MYX contract on the way out, and the remaining 4,576,539.435 MYX were sold into the MYX/WETH pair 0xe5437565cba444f33f40215afecc92e38e2d1ba9, whose net WETH depletion of 1.692074431746939187 is the realised value of the whole drained amount (a lower bound on holders' loss). The 0.009 WETH flash-swap fee is financing and not netted.

incidents.name: Notional V1 Escrow uint128 truncation in free-collateral ETH conversion
incidents.summary: Notional V1 Escrow.convertBalancesToETH (ExchangeRate._convertToETH) casts abs(balance) to uint128 without a bound check, so a net currency balance of -2^128 converts to 0 ETH. Via public ERC1155Trade.safeTransferFrom fCash pair mints the attacker made one account owe exactly 2^128 DAI fCash while passing the free-collateral check, used the unbacked 2^128-1 receiver leg as collateral to mint matured DAI/USDC claims sized to the escrow balances, then settled and withdrew all DAI and USDC from the escrow.

loss.notes: Exact escrow depletion in source-3: the Escrow proxy's entire DAI and USDC balances. The attacker supplied no tokens (source-1 moves no ERC-20). WETH and WBTC held by the escrow were not taken by the attacker. A third-party liquidation at block 25900571 is excluded (liquidator paid USDC for WETH collateral).

incidents.name: GebProxyActions quitSystem callable directly for library-owned SAFEs
incidents.summary: GebProxyActions is a shared library meant to be DELEGATECALLed from each user's DSProxy. Its quitSystem(manager, safe, dst) has no authentication and forwards to GebSafeManager.quitSystem, which only checks that msg.sender owns the SAFE. SAFEs 3, 5, 8 and 18 were opened with the library itself as owner in October 2020. Calling quitSystem directly on the library therefore passed the ownership check. In the post-shutdown system the attacker processed each SAFE, moved its free ETH-A collateral into its own SAFE, and exited 5.94 ETH.

loss.notes: Free ETH-A collateral of SAFEs 3, 5, 8 and 18 after GlobalSettlement.processSAFE settled their RAI debt, exited through the ETH-A CollateralJoin as WETH and unwrapped by the attacker. Before the exploit the SAFEs held 2, 1.5, 0.7 and 2.5 ETH-A of locked collateral. A later direct quitSystem on SAFE 8 by 0x982deb98 (0xa452ecb59f35c03e8838ccc20161c6f9e9ab0b9b28bab7a338507bc496605142) found it already drained.

incidents.name: Balancer V1 BPool single-join rounding drain
incidents.summary: BPool.joinswapPoolAmountOut reverse-computes the single-asset input for a requested BPT output in 18-decimal fixed-point math with no minimum effective input, minimum pool balance, or relative-error check. After flash-loan-funded swaps compress one reserve to dust, the required input rounds down to one base unit while the full BPT amount is minted; the attacker repeated the join and exited pro-rata across eleven Balancer V1 pools within four hours.

loss.notes: Exact pool depletion: for each of the 27 exploit transactions, every pool token's balanceOf(pool) at the block before minus at the block of the transaction, summed per token across the 11 drained BPools (all runtime hash 0x974df1c33872ba8aab782be5117ff348802441590f84ed7701d734bb9c21683e). Flash-loan legs wash inside each transaction and so cancel in the block-boundary deltas. Tokens are priced at the DefiLlama observation nearest before the campaign end; the two Uniswap V2 LP tokens are valued as their share of pair reserves (TWA has no price series, so that pair is taken as twice its WETH side) and wSTA carries no USD value for lack of a price series. SlowMist reported $234,000 for the campaign without publishing a basis.

incidents.name: OMPxContract treasury-inventory mispricing
incidents.summary: getBuyBackPrice divides the contract's ETH reserve by token.totalSupply() even though the contract itself held ~79% of that supply as unsold inventory, so purchase() sold that inventory for a fraction of the reserve share it entitles the buyer to and buyBack() immediately redeemed it at the full per-supply price, letting a flash-loaned purchase/buyBack loop drain the reserve.

loss.notes: The exact amount is the victim contract's net ETH outflow across seven purchase/buyBack rounds in the exploit trace. It excludes the attacker's flash-loan principal and transaction gas.

incidents.name: NovaBox uninitialised dividend checkpoints
incidents.summary: NovaBox adds new dual ETH/NOVA depositors to the dividend list without initialising their dividend checkpoints, and its extcodesize guard is bypassed from a constructor, so a fresh depositor could immediately withdraw and collect the whole stale historical ETH dividend.

loss.notes: Gross loss is the 56.942794338375078272 ETH paid above the attacker's 427.5 ETH campaign input. NovaBox's larger 65.022544338375078272 ETH balance decrease also includes 8.07975 ETH in transaction-generated owner fees sourced from that input, so those fees are not victim loss. The latest CoinGecko ETH observation before the transaction values the stolen ETH at $93,470.33.

incidents.name: UController.newOrganization adopts another organization's Reputation
incidents.summary: DAOstack's shared UController owns the Reputation, native token and Avatar of every organization registered with it. Its newOrganization(avatar) is permissionless: it adopts whatever nativeReputation and nativeToken the supplied avatar reports and registers the caller as a full-permission scheme. It never checks that the Reputation already belongs to another organization. The attacker registered a fake avatar that reported Genesis Alpha's real Reputation and minted itself 20,000 REP through the UController, about 67% of the new supply. It then passed a SchemeRegistrar proposal installing itself as a scheme on the real Genesis Alpha avatar, and had the UController send the avatar's 4.025 ETH.

loss.notes: The Genesis Alpha avatar's entire ETH balance (4.025 ETH at block 26059089, 0 at 26059090), sent to the attacker contract by UController.sendEther. A copycat, 0x9240fa3939a2… (block 26059353), used the same newOrganization path with its own fake avatar and moved only dust GEN and WETH, under 1 USD; it is not valued.

incidents.name: Laundromat free-deposit ring withdrawal
incidents.summary: Laundromat's deposit function did not enforce its configured payment, allowing the attacker to fill the remaining participant slots with chosen keys, satisfy the ring-signature withdrawal flow, and withdraw 1 ETH without depositing it.

loss.notes: The exploit trace records exactly 1 ETH leaving Laundromat for the attack contract. It is valued at the nearest pre-exploit CoinGecko observation.

incidents.name: OrderFactory permissionless createOrderForBuyer drains buyer escrow
incidents.summary: The unverified 2017 order factory's order-creation entry point (selector 0xbde886fc) checks only that the named buyer has an active request (getState(buyer) == 1). Any caller can create an order for any buyer with an attacker-chosen seller. The factory then moves the buyer's whole Account System ETH balance into a new order proxy and records the attacker as seller, and the proxy's seller-gated abort(address) sends that ETH wherever the caller says. From 2017 to 2018 only the platform operator EOA called this entry point. In September 2026 an attacker helper contract drained the platform's dormant buyer balances.

loss.notes: The loss is the buyers' pre-existing escrow: Account System ETH outflows minus the attacker's own deposit(address) top-ups, which were credited to buyers and swept back out. Component 1 is the first attacker's campaign, five transactions in block 25933639 (tx indices 2-6) against Account System 0xfcf3d97c6db4c3bf6020a2b99af074b595bda163, which lost 24.523408005580266342 ETH. It also includes index 7 against the byte-different sibling deployment (factory 0xf682e1279976178aa2c4d3c00bd73bbcfd81fc26, Account System 0xcccbeac80848dfb620b5ca4e5e8bc877361dbc0a), which lost 0.18 ETH. Index 8 paid 24.70340800558027 ETH to the attacker EOA. Component 2 is a later actor (0xfc3facd6 via 0x2a9a23bb) repeating the path at block 25937470, which took the last 0.011 ETH. Both Account System balances were then 0.
